journey.prep:
1. First and the most important thing is to always keep a smile on your face. Be confident in whatever

you answer (even if you are telling the wrong answer

2. Pay attention to the PPT conducted by the company. Note down some of the points if you want to, as

it might be helpful in asking questions in the interview.

3. Know your resume really really well. You should be aware of each and everything that you've

written on your resume, be it the projects, tools or anything. Do not lie about anything as the
interviewer will easily know that you're not aware of the concept. While explaining about a project,
if it is a group project, first explain the whole project then tell them specifically about your role in it.
Try not to mention anything that you're not aware of or comfortable with, as the interviewer might
start grilling you on that.
--- PAGE 3 ---

4. Do not panic if some people are called for their 2nd or 3rd interview round and you've not even

given your 1st round. Also do not worry if there are 3 rounds of interviews for some people and only
2 for some. It might happen that you will be called for your 2nd round just 15-20 minutes after
finishing your 1st round, be ready for that as well:)

5. Start your placement preparation in advance, do not wait for the last months as you will not have

time to cover up so many concepts once the companies start coming. Practice DSA daily on
whichever platform you prefer like Leetcode, CodeChef, etc. You should be aware of all the data
structures. Also have in depth knowledge of your primary language.

6. Refer GFG, Brainstellar for puzzles, InterviewBit, javatpoint, GFG for revising your OOPS, OS,

DBMS concepts, IndiaBix for aptitude. Prepare for aptitude really well, do not take it lightly as most
of the companies have aptitude, verbal reasoning as a part of their assessment.

7. Coming to the HR questions, just google HR interview questions and you will get a list. Prepare

sample answers for these questions in advance. These are more like the personal response questions,
just remember not to brag about yourself, be humble and answer these questions. Do not tell them
about your higher education plans even if you have one :)

8. Prepare some questions for the interviewer to ask in the interview beforehand. Have some basic

knowledge of the company, what it does, recent news about the company, values of the company, etc.

9. The interviewers don't expect you to tell the correct answers for every question, they just want to

know your approach and how you go about solving the problem, they analyze you on your problem
solving skills. If you do not recall the answer, tell them politely, sometimes they might give you
some hints. Do not be in a hurry to answer the questions, take a pause, think about the answer
properly and then answer.

10. The placement season is a very stressful phase, so do not take stress as it might affect your health and

in turn affect your preparation. Instead of burdening yourself with the rejection you faced in one
company, think where you can improve and start preparing yourself for the next company that visits.

11. Always have a positive mindset and believe in yourself. Whatever you think, comes back to you!

All the best!
Feel free to contact me on LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/in/aakanksha-dhawale-807023237/

Interviews:

1. Tech Round - 1

2. Tech Round - 2

1.
Online Assessment Round
The test link was sent on the registered email id of the candidates. There were a total of 22 questions - 1
DSA question, 1 API question, and 20 MCQs.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/lexicographically-largest-subsequence-containing-all-distinct-characters-onl
y-once/ was the coding question.
The REST API question for me was the 1st question from https://thejoboverflow.com/p/p1439/
The MCQs included questions related to basic geometry, probability, profit & loss, speed of trains, grammar,
comprehension, etc.
This round was for 100 mins.

2. Tech Round - 1[47 candidates were selected for this round]

The round started with the interviewer asking the most basic question - "Walk me through your resume." I
was asked about 2 of my projects which I explained to the interviewer in detail. He also asked me about the
Kavach Hackathon that was to be held in August 2023, since I had mentioned about that in my resume
because I was selected for the Final Round. Next, he asked about the four pillars of OOPS which I explained
to him by giving examples. He asked me to further elaborate on Polymorphism and told me to write the
pseudo code for method overloading and overriding using an example, but he then cross questioned me
about what I wrote is correct or what I explained for method overloading is actually method overriding and
vice versa. Be firm with your answer, they might just want to check your knowledge by saying the opposite
of what you've written. Next I was asked 2 SQL queries. Then came the coding questions,
--- PAGE 2 ---
1st was to print the star pattern
*
**
***
****
*****
(You can practice various types of pattern printing questions that are available on GFG).
2nd question was to find the missing element from N natural numbers. Then he asked me about stacks and
queues, their working. He then turned towards some HR type questions, like my hobbies, the last book I
read, where do I see myself in 5 years. With this the interview ended and he asked me if I had any questions
for him, I asked him 2.
This round went on for like 40-45 minutes. In this round the interviewer asked me HR questions too, but for
some people the first round was completely DSA based and more technical questions. So, the round
completely depends on which interviewer you get.

3. Tech Round - 2

The round started with the interviewer introducing himself. He was a core Java developer with 17 years of
experience in programming. Then started the questions related to the skills I had mentioned in my resume,
like MongoDB, MySQL, their advantages and disadvantages over one another, joins in DBMS. Next he
asked me what Bootstrap is and how I used it in my project, the advantage of using Bootstrap with the latest
JS frameworks (Bootstrap provides prebuilt components which can be readily used and they're responsive to
the screen size). Then he also asked me the difference between GET, PUT, POST methods, what Media
Query is in CSS. Next he gave me some Java code snippets and told me to find the output (for this you
should know the difference between the access modifiers in Java, String methods like equals, Stack
memory & Heap memory in Java and how objects and variables are created in them). Then for the DSA
questions, 1st question was to find the sum of the 3 digit numbers in a given array, 2nd was to count the
number of words in a given string (take care of the edge cases like if there's a space at the end of the
sentence). Also he asked me about the projects that I had mentioned in my resume. With this the second
round ended, and he asked me if I had any questions for him, so I asked him about the Oracle FlexCube,
what it is and how it works, since they had mentioned about it in their PPT.
This round went on for almost an hour.
At the end, 17 students were shortlisted for the job.

journey.prep:
Technical Tips:

• Solve a lot of DSA problems. Especially fundamental topics like Stack, Queue, Linked

List, Trees, Graphs are non-negotiable. Master these first. If you have enough time after
being comfortable with these topics, you could try and go over advanced topics like DP.

• Be familiar with Computer Science Theory like OOPS, Networking, DBMS and specific

theory of the programming language you use. If you have done some development, you
need to be familiar with its theory as well. Try to anticipate what questions could be
asked. Don't spend an ungodly amount of time on it, just go through an online crash
course or a questionnaire, it should be more than enough.

• Projects. You should be able to talk comfortably about your projects for about 10

minutes. Prepare what you are going to say beforehand and rehearse it. It constitutes a
--- PAGE 5 ---
major bulk of the interview so make sure you give enough time to it. Similar to the
previous point, try to anticipate what questions the interviewer would ask and prepare
appropriate solutions.
Interview tips:

• Be yourself.

• Before the interview try to meditate. During the interview remain calm and relaxed.

• Take pauses. Let your thoughts marinate in your head and frame sentences before

answering. Do not try to answer quickly even to questions that seem simple as you may
make a mistake in doing so. Watch this video: https://youtu.be/11EnMmH9qh4

• Always make sure you understand the question before answering, especially coding

questions. I made a similar mistake in my second interview as I mentioned above. Repeat
the question as you interpret it back to the interviewer and make sure both of you are on
the same page. Then proceed to thinking about the solution.

• Be quite stoic in your interview. Don't be too happy if you get the answer, nor too

disturbed if you don't. Take it one question at a time. Control what you can and don't
worry too much about what you cannot.

• Keep a smiling face and be very polite. More often than not people mirror each other's

body language. Sit straight and keep your spine erect. This also boosts confidence.
journey.howSecured:
The placement process was divided into the following rounds:

• A preliminary coding round that consisted of 3 questions. One Easy, 2 Medium. I was

able to completely solve the first 2 problems and partially solve the last one. This was
enough to get qualified for the interview rounds.

• Technical Round 1

• Technical Round 2

• Professional Fitness Round

• HR Round

1. Technical Interview Round 1[21 Candidates appeared in this round]

The round began with the interviewer going through my resume. He asked me to give a detailed
description of the projects that I had mentioned on my resume, which I proceeded to give. He
then asked me about any challenges I faced in my projects. This took about 10-12 minutes.
He then asked me to code the famous fibonacci question. I coded up 2 solutions for the problem
and explained it in detail to him. He seemed pretty satisfied with my explanation. He then asked
me the difference between stack and queue data structures. He demanded I give an
example/application of stack and queue. This phase of the interview took 2-3 minutes.
This was followed by a series of technical questions on various computer science topics that I
had mentioned on my resume. He asked me about OOPS, polymorphism, access modifiers and
code reusability. He requested me to demonstrate these concepts. He further quizzed me about
Computer Networks, the OSI model. I was able to answer all of his questions. This part of the
interview took another 5 minutes or so.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The interviewer then proceeded to ask me a quiz question. The question is as follows: You are
given a cake and a knife. You are allowed to cut the cake 3 times only. You need to make sure that
the cake is cut in 8 pieces. I gave him the following solution: Cut the cake once, stack the 2
pieces on top of each other. Repeat this process 3 times. 1 > 2, 2 > 4, 4 > 8. He said this was a
valid solution but it would ruin the cream on the cake. A better solution would be to cut the cake
once from the top, and slice it twice through its height, resulting in 8 pieces with 3 cuts. I
admitted that his solution was better. Towards the end, we had established a decent camaraderie
and we both were smiling.
Finally, he asked me if I had any questions for him. I requested him to tell me about any project
of his, and what impact it had on an organizational level. I mentioned to him that I was really
passionate about this stuff, and therefore would love to know about it. He replied that he was not
really allowed to talk in detail about his projects but he assured me that the smallest piece of
code that one writes has an enormous impact on the organization. I was quite happy with his
response and the interview ended. It took about 20-22 minutes in total and I was selected in the
next round.

2. Technical Interview Round 2[18 Candidates appeared in this round]

In this round, the interviewer first began with a brief introduction with himself. He then asked
me to introduce myself. After my introduction, he told me to explain the projects on my resume.
After the explanation, he asked me questions about the projects. He asked me about my role in
these projects, how I collaborated with my teammates, the programming languages we used, the
API's we used, the frameworks used by us, etc. This phase of the interview lasted about 15
minutes.
The interviewer then proceeded to ask me a series of DSA questions. The following were the
questions:

• You are working at Amazon and your task is to deliver a series of packages. You are given

3 things about a delivery: The coordinates of the delivery address(x-coordinate and
y-coordinate) and the price you would get on the delivery of the package. Input is a 2d
array: [[x1,y1,p1], [x2,y2,p2], …..], with each nested array representing a delivery. The
output is a sorted input array, with the array being sorted according to the price to
distance ratio of each delivery.

• You are given an array. You need to sort the array according to the frequency of each

element in that array.

• Mirror a binary tree.

• Top view of a binary tree. You are viewing the binary tree from the top. You need to sum

all the elements that you would observe in the same line. For example if we start from the
root node, if we go to the left child and then to the subsequent right child, we would
observe the 2 nodes in the same line.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Example:
5
2 4
6
Imagine the above binary tree. In the above tree, 5, 2, 4 would be visible in the same line
if one were to view from the top.
The first 3 questions I was able to solve pretty easily. The interviewer seemed quite satisfied with
my solutions. The last question I faltered in. I did not understand the question clearly and thought
that it was a BFS question. I coded up the solution but it was not a valid one. I asked the
interviewer to explain the question to me once again, which he did again quite carefully. But,
shortly after he told me that we were out of time and he encouraged me to think about the
solution post interview.
He asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him the same question which I had asked in
the previous interview. He was quite happy that I asked him about his projects and proceeded to
explain his projects in heavy detail. While he was speaking, subconsciously I was thinking about
the problem while simultaneously listening to him and worked up the solution mentally. Once he
was done, he asked if I could briefly attempt the solution to that problem. I explained to him the
approach and he was quite pleased with it, and told me that it was the right one.
The entire interview took about 40 minutes.

3. Professional Fitness Round

This interview began in a similar fashion as the previous interview. I was asked to introduce
myself and right after asked to explain my projects in heavy detail. The interviewer then
proceeded to ask me questions on the projects that included why certain APIs were used, and
what their purpose was. I was able to answer all his questions and the interviewer was quite
pleased with my answers. This phase took about 20 minutes.
Following was a quiz question:
You are given 2 buckets of water: one is 3 liters and the other is 5 liters. We need 4 liters of water
and cannot measure the level of water in buckets while they are partially filled.
--- PAGE 4 ---
A better explanation: https://codingnconcepts.com/puzzle/the-water-jug-riddle/
This puzzle was from a famous Die Hard movie and I was aware of this solution. I told the
interviewer that I have seen this in a movie. He smiled and challenged me to solve it immediately
which I did.
After this was a series of HR type questions. He asked me if I had an offer from abroad versus an
offer in India on my favorite tech project, which one would I choose. He asked me why I had
done a course on Financial Markets. He asked me what I wanted to accomplish in the next 5-10
years. I was able to give satisfactory responses to each question.
Similar to the first interview I managed to establish a decent rapport with the interviewer. He was
quite formal with me in the beginning but at the end he was quite comfortable discussing things
with me. I thanked him for his time and the interview ended. This round lasted for 45 minutes.

4. HR Round

This round consisted of standard HR questions, thankfully which I had gone over in my
preparation. It started with the interviewer asking for my introduction followed by these
questions:

• Why Deutsche Bank? Describe Deutsche Bank in one word.

• Describe your 2 strengths and weaknesses

• Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years?

This was followed by objective questions like family background, did I have a passport or not,
etc. This interview took 15 minutes.

Name: Aayush Sheth
Position: Jr Analyst - Analytical Verification
Stipend: Rs 30 k, CTC = 13 lacs
Category: Super Dream
My Linkedin : https://www.linkedin.com/in/aayush-sheth-aa7488200/

Hi friend! The placement season is of the most important aspect of engineering life. Kindly please
start gearing up for it. The soon the better . Placements are 70% hard work and 30% luck.

First Round:
70 MCQ, 30 Aptitude and 40 Technical MCQ
40 MCQ where about 35 questions were of Java and Python. 5 were of SQL.
The first round is conducted in college and is strictly monitored and proctored.
Kindly prepare the concepts and details before hand, you can refer to gfg, sanfoundry and other
sources. All the questions asked in technical were original since I had spent the previous day
practicing from various sites online. Most of the questions asked to predict the output or were of
generators and decorators. A few basic questions were asked as well however they were only 6-7 of
35.
Keep practicing SQL queries on your side. Practice "Wild Cards, Joins, Inbuilt functions like AVG,
SUM"
Kindly be thorough with OOPS in python and java, static, private in java/python and collections as
well. There is negative marking as well, be aware of it.
Aptitude was like India Bix, RS Aggarwal quantitative aptitude book as well. I shall recommend that
book for study.
Try to attempt about 40-50 questions confidently.
Second Round:
ISS does not share the shortlist all together. They first share of 12-13 people then they share of next
5 after 10-15 mins. My name was not in any of the lists. Felt like ISS is over let's target next firm. I
was waiting near 410 to meet my mentor regarding final year project discussion.
Suddenly after 15 mins I received multiple calls from TPC's and was notified of my selection.
Kindly be patient and "DON'T LEAVE" before they say so.
Coming to the round the questions asked:
The interviews were taken online for Analytical Verification Role, by a person having 15+ years of
work ex. The questions asked were -

1) Introduce yourself

2) He sent me a sql code in notepad on email (creation and insertions of values in table) and

asked me a few basic things on the same.

3) He asked me to join two tables, find average of salary and implement a condition as well. So

basically, it had 3 "SQL Things" in one statement (AVG, JOIN, HAVING)

4) He then sent me a csv file and asked me to use pandas and perform basic functionalities.

5) Basic Functionalities like correlation, head(), tail()

6) Some concepts like "Label Encoder" were also discussed.

After which he discussed my resume and projects. Later he asked me how many members were in
my family and what does my dad do etc ..

HR Round
HR reviewed my resume, asked me why ISS and other typical HR questions,
A point to note is she asked me into depth about my internships and projects.

Feel free to contact me !!

The selection process consisted a total of 4 rounds: OA + 2 Technical + HR.
The OA consisted of 12 MCQ-type questions on core concepts such as OOPS, DBMS, and even some Java
based questions. The MCQs in and of themselves should not be difficult given you have paid some amount
of attention in the college lectures. Some quick brushup from GFG, Interviewbit would do the job just fine
for the MCQs.
Next the coding question: this was a variation of leetcode medium question:
https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/
The twist was that instead of 1s and Os, there were 4 different characters(a,b,c,d). I was able to pass all test
cases with a simple BFS approach, as I had done this question previously.

1. Technical 1 [ 49 candidates selected for Tech 1]

The interview started with the usual question: "Tell me about yourself." My suggestion would be to
prepare a good response to this question, unlike me. He then turned to my resume, from which the
interviewer asked me about my projects. Be sure you are thoroughly aware of the things you have done in
ALL of your projects. Don't mention the projects you are unsure about, or haven't done much work on. He
asked me quite a few questions about my 'favourite project". After this, he turned to some DSA questions.
The difficulty of these was not too high, would say about easy-medium in leetcode. Solving medium
questions on leetcode would get you through these. He also asked me a very simple SQL query to "find the
3rd greatest salary from emp table". After this, he asked me some core concept questions on OOPS, DBMS.
This round lasted for about 40-45 minutes.

2. Technical 2 [Around 20-30 candidates]

Started, with the same "Tell me about yourself" question, followed by "What do you know about
MSCI?" After this, the interviewer told me to write code to find the index of the first occurring "1" in a
sorted array of 1s and Os. I first answered with a simple linear search, and then after asking to optimize it, a
binary search. She then proceeded with my resume and asked which language I preferred to code in and
why. After which she asked me some questions about my summer internship and why wouldn't I be
continuing with the same company. Finally, she gave a logical reasoning question to solve, on a sheet of
paper. These types of questions can be found on GFG, interviewbit, etc very easily.
Lasted for about 30-35 minutes.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. HR [ 15-20 candidates ]

This was a very chilled-out round. The interviewer asked me some standard HR questions:

1. Tell me about yourself

2. Tell me what you know about MSCI

3. What's your family background

4. Strengths and weaknesses

5. Hard work or Smart Work?

6. Why would you be a good candidate for MSCI

7. Where do you see yourself in 5 years?

8. Hobbies and interests

She then inquired if I had any questions for her, to which I asked a couple,

1. What do you look for in a candidate to be suitable for MSCI

2. How do you find MSCI workwise?

Lasted for about 30 minutes.
Selected a total of 8 Candidates

a. Technical Round 1
b. Technical Round 2 + HR

1. Aptitude Test [229 students (174 BTech + 55 MCA) appeared for this round]

This was an online aptitude test conducted on MeritTrac's Online Assessment Engine -
PARIKSHA. The test consisted of 60 questions, with 20 questions each in the verbal, analytical,
and quantitative sections, with no negative marking. The time limit was 60 minutes so timing is
the key here. There was a cutoff for this test which was not known to us.
38 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Pre-Placement Talk

This round started at 10 am. We were briefed about the company, including its values, various
programs, and significant milestones. In the end, we were given the opportunity to ask
questions. Make sure to ask questions (good ones) to get noticed. I had made a question in two
parts which I had thought to ask one in PPT and other part in Interviews. Question Was "Could
you please elaborate on the specific security measures and protocols that Nomura has in place
to safeguard client data and financial transactionsạ
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Technical Round 1(30 - 35 minutes)

During my interview at around 11:50 am, I began by introducing myself and expressing Bill
Gates as my role model, citing his entrepreneurial spirit and philanthropy as my inspiration. The
interviewer then thoroughly reviewed my resume and engaged in discussions about my
projects, particularly focusing on the technologies used. Notably, in one project utilizing
DynamoDB, he inquired about the choice over SQL and MongoDB. My passion for the projects
led him to ask why I hadn't considered open-sourcing one of them. He showed interest in the
details of all my projects, even asking if there was a working model. Additionally, he inquired
about a non-tech internship had completed.
To test my knowledge and interest in the company, he asked what I knew about Nomura. I used
the opportunity to inquire about the company's security measures, continuing a question I had
posed during the pre-placement talk. The interviewer concluded by providing positive feedback,
considering me a strong candidate with creative potential.
15 students got shortlisted for the next round, and 13 were waitlisted. The waitlisted candidates
were called for an additional review round out of which 3 students moved to the final round (not
sure what was asked in the review round). Finally, 18 students moved to the final round.

3. Technical Round 2 + HR (45 - 50 minutes)

My interview was scheduled to be two separate rounds, an HR round, and a technical round.
However, due to time constraints, the two rounds were merged into a single round, which
started around 4 pm. The panel consisted of two members, one from the HR team and another
from the Tech team.
The interview commenced with questions about my proficiency in programming languages. I
mentioned SQL and Python. They presented a simple SQL task where I had to count the total
number of males and females in a given column (Gender). Though initially nervous, I explained
a more complex approach using multiple select statements and Union. With their helpful hint
about using the GROUP BY function, I quickly grasped the simpler solution.
The technical questions continued, focusing on SQL. They asked me to write a query to replace
male with female and vice versa. Later, they inquired about joins and window functions, and the
discussion went on to my projects, which seemed to captivate their interest. We spent around
half an hour discussing my projects in detail.
The panel then challenged me with some puzzles to solve, followed by questions about my
tech-related learning beyond the college curriculum. They specifically asked about Blockchain
and whether I had worked on any projects related to it. The conversation then transitioned to HR
--- PAGE 3 ---
questions, including why I chose Nomura, why they should select me, a time when I performed
at my best, and how I would handle a team.
The entire interview lasted about an hour, providing a comprehensive evaluation of my technical
skills, projects, and ability to handle HR-related questions.
I was able to answer almost all of the questions, but I was unsure whether I would get selected
or not as it was my first offline interview. Finally, the results were announced at 6 pm, and 11
students (10 BTech + 1 MCA) were selected and I was one of them.

After being the only one rejected by Deutsche Bank and in the last round of MSCI and 11 other
companies, EDS visited us on the 17th of August.
There were a total of 5 rounds. PPT and the first two rounds were conducted on the same day in online
mode, while the other rounds were conducted in offline mode. Students were not allowed to apply for both
Data and SDE roles; only the first round was common for both.
All the students who applied appeared for the test.

1. Aptitude Round - 17 August 2023, 7:00 PM

This round was held online and was entirely based on aptitude. Practicing Indiabix questions will help you
pass this round.
This round was approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour long.
Around 70 students applied for the SDE role, but only 25 qualified for the next round.

2. Coding Round - 17 August 2023, 8:30 PM

For this round, there were two sections. The first section had coding questions, and the second had
SQL-related questions. The coding questions were easy to medium-level LeetCode questions.
This round was approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour long.
Only 15 students qualified for the next round.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Technical Round 1 - 22 August 2023, 2:00 PM

Interviewed by the EDS Technical Lead of the Web Department
In this round, we had to give interviews in pairs, and both of us had to give answers to the same questions.
Based on your answers, you will be evaluated.
Interviewers will decide with whom you will be paired. It is based on your resume and the similar interests
mentioned in it.
The interview started with our introduction. There were 2 interviewers; they provided us with a sheet of
paper and asked us the following questions one by one, the same for both and at the same time:

1. A very simple question about an array

2. How to center a div?

3. Create a JSON from an object

4. Convert the above JSON and store it

5. An SQL join query

The questions were relatively easy, and I was able to answer all the questions. For question 4, I asked them
if I could modify JSON so it could be efficiently stored. They allowed me to modify it.
For the final question, they were not satisfied with both of our answers, as they needed an efficient query.
This round lasted for 1 to 1.5 hours.
At the end, I asked him a question. "Suppose a framework that is being used in one of your projects gets
deprecated and is no longer supported. How do you handle this situation?" To which he answered, we use
Dockers, and in that Docker we can keep the framework of any version, and it will continue to work until we
change or remove it ourselves. I was a little confused with the answer, but he was right: the framework will
continue to be used as long as it is inside the docker and is unchanged.
Only 7 students qualified for the next round.

4. Techno-HR Round 1 - 22 August 2023, 6:00 PM

Interviewed by the EDS co-founder, CEO, and CTO
My interview was really late, and it was conducted online via Zoom call. The interview started with my
introduction, then he went through my resume and asked me a few questions based on my projects. Then we
discussed some of our experience working on different technologies, as I worked on both Android and the
Web. He asked me a question related to SQL, and I was able to give an answer. He then asked me if I was
comfortable working on React Native, as previously I built apps with Flutter and Java but not with React
Native. I said it would be fine. I will get the opportunity to add another skill to my knowledge set. It was a
friendly conversation.
This round lasted for about 1 to 1.5 hours.
At the end, I asked him a question. "Consider a framework that you are currently using, let's say React
Native. You mentioned that you use it for your application, but we also have Flutter. Let's say in the future,
Flutter or any other framework gives 2x performance compared to React Native. In that case, will you
switch your framework? This will also include the fact that current employees will have to learn the new
technology and the time required to migrate or rewrite the entire codebase in a new language or framework.
How will you handle this?" He answered to this question by saying that if the new framework gives us 2x
performance, then we will definitely switch to it. The performance of an application matters the most, and
we want to deliver the best performance to our users. I was satisfied with the answer.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Only 1 student qualified for the final round.

5. Techno-HR Round 11 - 22 August 2023, 7:30 PM

Interviewed by the EDS Chief Architect
While waiting for the result, I was surprised to know that there would be another HR round that I had to
face. After getting rejected in the HR rounds again and again, I knew this was my final test.
This interview was also conducted online via Zoom call. Again, the interview started with my introduction,
and we discussed some of my projects and started talking about the new technologies. The interviewer was
very chill.
This round lasted for about half an hour.
At the end, I asked him a question. Honestly, I do not remember what I asked.
After about an hour, they announced the result, and finally I got selected :)
Some Tips:
After getting rejected again and again because of my lack of communication skills and preparing again and
again, this interview was very easy for me.

• Make sure that you have good communication skills; if not, practice more and more.

• Solve Indiabix questions; do not take the aptitude test lightly, as I did, and it cost me 3 companies.

• Practice Leetcode questions daily, and the technical interviews will be very easy for you.

• It is up to you to ask questions at the end; do not ask too many questions.

• Always go through the company's website before the interview.

Feel free to ask me any doubts on my LinkedIn account.
All the best for your placements :)
And of course, you must not give up!

arrival time =  [0,0,0,0] no of queues = 2, Answer = [1,1,2,2]

1. Digital Interview (26 - 31 July)

2. Technical Test (5 August)

3. Group Discussion (7 August, 8:30 - 9:30 AM )

4. Personal Interview (7 August, 10:30 AM onwards)

5. Leadership/HR Interview (7 August)

Note: Make sure to make good notes from the pre-placement talk. You will be able to understand the
company's profile, work-culture and value system which will be proven useful in the process.

1. Digital Interview (Online) - All the applied students appeared for this round

This round was conducted using the HireVue Digital Interview platform. A video will narrate you the
question. Then you will get 30 seconds to 1 minute to prepare and think. Finally, you will have to answer the
question in maximum 3 minutes in only one attempt. Again, next question will be narrated through a video.
And so, there were a total of 6 questions.

The questions:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Tip: Be honest and give genuine answers. Do not get your answers from the internet. Be well-dressed and
give this round in a proper environment. Respond in a way that a real interviewer is sitting in front of you
because this hirevue round is manually checked, not by using AI.

2. Technical Test - 107 candidates were shortlisted for this round

Platform: Microsoft forms
Time: 30 minutes
Format: 25 MCQs
Topics Covered: DSA, SQL, Aptitude, Programming language

Tip: Don't get stuck on a question for long time. Time management is important.

3. Group Discussion - 71 students appeared for this round

There were 7 groups, each consisting of around 10 students. This round was conducted offline but the
communication medium was Microsoft teams. You are supposed to use earphones.

My experience: There were 10 students and 2 Baker Hughes Hiring team member in my panel. My GD Topic
was "ChatGPT: Pros and Cons". The GD lasted for 25 minutes. I spoke approximately 4 times, and with each
opportunity I had, I made sure to address the current status of the discussion and also added new points.
Because I added several new points my name was mentioned frequently by other students when they wanted
to add-on to my point. This kept me visible throughout the GD. 2 students were shortlisted from my group.

Tip: Adding new points to the discussion must be relevant and in context. Do not add irrelevant points just for
the sake of saying something, even few strong meaningful points gain more weightage. Do not interrupt
someone on purpose. If two students try to start a conversation at the same time (This happens quite often in a
GD, so make sure to plan out in advance what you will do in such a case) then one must politely address the
situation and ask the other to continue and may politely say that "I would like to go next after hearing your
viewpoint" or something on the similar lines. Last but not the least, have a warm smile on your face

4. Technical Interview - 28 people were interviewed in this round.

There were 3 panels set up, each panel consisting of 2 people. This round began at 10:30 am.

My experience: I had a little cold and fever that day. So, the first thing I did after entering the room was to
reduce the air conditioner cooling :/ The interviews usually go for an hour, so its better to request for the same
politely in the beginning itself if you are not well. This basically was a resume-based round. They can even
fetch out a single word from your resume and grill you on that. They first asked me to explain all the projects
mentioned in my resume. 3 projects were on Data Analytics and Machine Learning and 2 projects were on
Web development. After my brief explanation of all the projects, the next 45 minutes were questions all about
DATA. The questions ranged from Data base management system to Data analytics.
Some example question being:

1. How would you use a stationary shopkeeper's data to gain useful insights to increase his/her revenue? I had

to explain the step-by-step procedure and also mention the technical tools that will be needed to fulfil the
same.

2. How does the random forest algorithm work?

3. How do you use machine learning for classification-based problems?

4. Difference between Authentication and Authorization in context of Data base management system.

I personally have great interest in data and had explored this domain much more than what is covered in
college academics. Hence, I was able to answer all the data related questions and the interviewer was satisfied.
Then the other interviewer asked me altogether few different kind of questions. First question being, "What is
the length of the rope present on the sides of Worli Sea link bridge?". This was not a guestimate; she needed a
proper mathematical approach. This could basically be solved using the concepts of engineering mechanics
studied in the first year of engineering. I stated some terms related to tension along the rope length, rope
material, force, length of the bridge and gave a rough layout of my approach but I was afraid of concluding
my answer with an absurd number, so I just said "I will have to revise on this to get to the right number". Then
the second question was "How will you reduce the number of potholes in Mumbai?". Luckily, I had recently
watched a startup on shark tank that worked on the similar cause. I mentioned about the startup and how they
are approaching this problem and their solution.
I was also asked if given a project of some domain I am currently unaware of, will I be able to do it? What if
your friends at work are given some familiar and exciting domain project and you are stuck on some different
project? To this I answered that as a fresher what I can bring to the table is a problem-solving mindset and
good human principles. Technologies keeps on changing and updating itself very frequently, so I will be never
afraid of something unknown and give my level best to learn and complete the task assigned to me. And rather
than comparing ourselves with others, we must focus on giving our 100% and becoming better every day.
At the end, they asked me if I had any questions for them, I asked about their role in Baker Hughes and how
long have they been working at Baker Hughes. One of them was a Data Architect (hence he had asked all the
data-related question) with around 15 years of experience and the other was a Product Manager.

Tip: Do not lie on your resume. Make a good 1-page resume covering everything you know and things you
have achieved.

5. Leadership Round - 15 candidates appeared for this round

After my technical interview, I had a 10-minute break and was directly send to the conference room for the
final round with a senior director of Baker Hughes. He was associated with Baker Hughes for around 20 years.
After I introduced myself, the interview did not even feel like an interview. It was a very friendly interview,
and no typical HR questions were asked. I had spent the two years of engineering entrance exam preparation
without any coaching assistance, practicing only self-study with the help of free resources available on the
internet. He was quite impressed by that and asked me details of that journey. I talked about Sudha Murthy,
my hobbies. One question he asked me was; If I walk into your class and ask your batchmates about how you
are as a person, then what will they say? Primarily this round assesses you as a human and your thought
process.

Tip: Be honest and genuine. Do not fake anything. And again, have a warm smile on your face

All my offline rounds (GD + technical round + leadership round) had very short breaks in between and were
over by 12:30 pm. Results were out around 6pm in the evening and 8 students were shortlisted. I was one of
them!

Trust your preparation and be yourself.
Give your best and don't worry about the result.

Feel free to contact me on LinkedIn if needed. Best of luck!

journey.prep:
1. Read the JD thoroughly. Always try to align your resume with the skills required(Though it doesn't matter

if your resume is technical or non-technical for this role). Do talk with your seniors in the same domain. Try
to gather as much information as you can. I also talked with a couple of my CA friends about this role and
how to prepare for the same.

2. Read your resume and be completely honest in your answers. The interviewers are experienced enough to

gauge your understanding of the stuff put up in the resume. Make sure you know each and every word you
put on your resume.

3. Even if you have a basic understanding of finance and risk terms it would be okay. you should be able to

deviate your interview based on your top skills. Also learn about the role and try to do any course if you
have some time before the interview day. It will greatly help you.

4. Do prepare 1-2 good questions to ask at the end of the interview. But do keep in mind don't ask too many

open-ended questions because they too don't want to feel that they are being interviewed.

5. Learn from the mistakes you have made in the past interviews and work on them.

6. Ensure that you speak in a coherent and calm manner to sound formal. The interviewers want to know

what you've got for them to consider you. Make the most of your time.

7. Do prepare for the HR questions too thoroughly because we had a couple of cases where they took their

HR round but were not short-listed and trust me that's the worst feeling when you can see the finish line but
you were not able to make it.

8. Also read about JP Morgan and Chase values and what they do and if asked on the same, say what you

know or remember.

9. Also have a firm and crystal clear mindset. Your clarity of thoughts would have a great impact on your

overall interview. Have a humble and sharp attitude while interviewing in front of the panelists.

10. Lastly, all the best for your interviews. If you need any help you know where to find me(Obv LinkedIn).

Placement process can be very stressful so make sure you keep yourself positive around all situations.
Non-tech interviews are easier to crack but trust me rather than the skills or your resume achievements they
just want to see how you are as a person.
journey.howSecured:
1. Resume Screening

The actual process of JPMC started with the 1st company itself (Application date: 8th July). They asked to
apply for the role in Gform as well as their portal. In this round screening was done based on the resumes.
Therefore, It is important to have a strong, if not excellent, resume that includes your skills,
extracurricular activities, GPA, projects, internships, and other relevant information. The resume
was a talking point during my interviews.
11th July shortlisted candidates names were released.
82 Students were shortlisted.

2. Online Aptitude Test(12th July)

There was an extra round this time. It was an aptitude test which had 29 questions and we had 45 mins. Most
of the questions were on CAT Quantitative analysis. Make sure to practice those beforehand and also try to
use more and more tricks to save time in the exam. Also the questions are almost Quant/ CAT level.
Results of this round were a bit delayed. Results were declared on 18th July.
28 Students were shortlisted.
There was a PPT for the selected candidates(On Zoom). Be active during these rounds, make notes about
companies requirements, tech stack being used, any specific condition and skills they are looking for, make
sure to ask good questions. (But it doesn't affect much)

3. Business Round 1(26 Students appeared- 2 got selected for different company)

The interviews started around 10.00 -10.30 am. The interviewer went through my resume simultaneously
and asked me questions related to my internships, positions of responsibilities, extra curricular activities in
--- PAGE 2 ---
detail. Therefore, ensure that you are completely thorough with every single word mentioned in your
resume. Few questions that I recall are:

1. Thad mentioned Design thinking as one of my courseworks so she asked phases of Design thinking

2. Then she asked which language I am proficient in? (Java) So she asked why Java and why not

Python? She just wanted to know what I thought before deciding on anything.

3. Then she asked me to explain one of my projects in depth. Also she asked me how I could monetize

this project.

4. Then she went on asking me situational questions like as I was team leader in one of the hackathon

which we won. Like what were the challenges I faced, how I solved them. Also like if 2 team players
are not performing to fullest what will I do? If there is conflict in the team what will I do?

5. Then she asked me about my weaknesses and how I improved on them?

6. Then she asked me why finance and why non-tech?

7. She asked me do I have any idea or opinion on current global scenario of international markets? I did

had some idea but sooner I did hit a deadend because I wasn't aware of a recent incident in depth.

8. She asked me about risk management in general, what is risk and what are it's stages and phases etc.

9. Then at last she asked me do I have any questions for her? (Response: Nothing as such specific but

still I do wanna know what's the one piece of advice would you like to give me if I want to succeed
in this role if I get selected)
The interview lasted for about 35-40 minutes, however, for some it was only 15-20 minutes.
> 15 students were shortlisted for the second interview

4. Business Round 2 (15 Students appeared for this round)

This was same as the first round but some of my friends had a panelist which was pure technical so do
prepare for both scenarios. There were 2 interviewers. They asked me questions related risk and types of
risks and risk management in general. It is important to note that if you're unable to answer any question,
just acknowledge that you don't know. Then one of the panelist asked me to take any one project which I
like and start explaining it in and out and how you thought about this project how you worked on it and how
you convinced your mentor to work on this project. He gave me hypothetical situation that if my mentor is
not aligned with my views then how will I convince him/her? Then if I had conflict in my team how will I
resolve it? Then if I was given a project of which I had no idea then will I take that project and given ample
time will I do it? (Yes provided I had to do it anyhow) Then he asked me if you had an option of doing alone
or with team what will i choose?(Obv team over myself because if same task can be done within 2-3 months
then why not) Then he asked but teams have conflicts why would you want conflict if you simply can avoid
by doing yourself? So this is how he was trying to make me fall in this trap of questions. So do have a firm
belief about things as well as try to make your point and stick to it. This was done deliberately by the
interviewer to see how my I will react in these situations. So stay calm and make your point clear.
Finally, they'll ask if you have any questions for them(I asked the same question which I asked in Round 1).
This interview lasted for about 20-30 minutes.

3. HR Round (7 Students appeared for this round)

Almost immediately after the 2nd interview I was called for the HR Round. This was a very casual
conversational type round wherein you will be generally asked about location preference, if I was
comfortable working late nights. Why JPMC and why this risk management role? Why should we hire you
and not the 28 others that we interviewed? Then at last do I had any questions for them?(To which I replied
that nothing as such relevant because I had been asking questions in these last 2 rounds and I am pretty
--- PAGE 3 ---
much clear about the company as well as this role). So it doesn't matter what you ask or not it's just a basic
courtesy to ask a question but it is not a deciding factor for your selection.
5 Students were offered the Job.

journey.howSecured:
Durvesh Chaudhari
ETRX

Company - Oracle

Job Profile - Associate Application Developer

Offer Type - Placement Only

CTC - 19.18 LPA (14.5 Base + ESOP + PF/PPF + Gratuity)

Location - Mumbai / Pune / Bangalore / Chennai

❖ Placement Process -

1. Online Assessment Round (Coding and Aptitude) -

In total, there were 22 questions during the round, comprising 10 quantitative, 10 verbal, 1 medium
difficulty coding, and 1 easy API question. The quantitative and verbal questions were straightforward,
and the round lasted for 100 minutes.

Coding Question - Lexicographically Largest Subsequence
API Question - REST API: Asteroid Orbit

2. Interviews -

• Technical Round - 1

In this round, I was among the 49 students selected, and the interview focused solely on evaluating
our resumes. The session lasted for about 40 minutes, and it kicked off with the classic "Tell me
about Yourself" question. I had prepared extensively for this question to steer the interview in the
direction I wanted. The interviewer then proceeded to read my resume and asked specific questions
about all the projects I had listed.

As Python was my primary language, the interviewer inquired about the differences between tuples
and lists, and also asked me about Python's dynamically typed nature. I confidently answered these
questions, which seemed to satisfy the interviewer.

Next, the interviewer delved into Database Management Systems (DBMS) topics and asked about
indexing and ACID properties. I provided satisfactory responses to these queries.

Following that, the interviewer presented a coding question, asking me to swap two variables
without using a third variable. I quickly came up with a solution using the addition and subtraction
method, and the interviewer seemed pleased with my answer. However, the interviewer then
proposed an alternative approach involving multiplication and division, and asked me to analyse
which one was better. I pointed out the potential error risks in the division-based approach,
reaffirming the superiority of my initial solution.

Afterwards, the interviewer challenged me with a medium difficulty question Rotate Array. He also
asked me different types of Tree Traversal techniques.

Given my background in Computer Networks, the interviewer asked me to state the different layers
in the TCP/IP protocol, which I answered accurately. Additionally, because of my Electronics
background, the interviewer inquired about the difference between a Microprocessor and a
Microcontroller. Although I must admit I wasn't fully prepared for this question, I provided a
partially correct answer. However, the interviewer corrected me, and we engaged in a constructive
discussion about the topic. Later he asked me a puzzle - 9 balls.

At the end of the round, 28 students, including myself, were shortlisted for the next stage of the
selection process.

• Technical Round 2 -

During this round, which lasted for approximately 30 to 35 minutes, the interviewer started by
asking me to introduce myself. Since I had mentioned that I took a Foundational course in
Programming and Data Science from IITM, the interviewer inquired whether I was still continuing
the course and what I had learned from it. They then asked me to explain Normal Distribution
without using any technical terms and with a simple example, as if I were explaining it to a ten-
year-old. Similarly, I was asked to explain Queue and Priority Queue using non-technical language
and examples.
After that, the interviewer asked about the time complexity of inserting, popping, and accessing an
element in both the Queue and Priority Queue data structures. Following this, they asked me with a
medium difficulty DSA question: finding the Kth largest number in an unsorted array. Initially, I
provided a brute force approach by suggesting to sort the array. The interviewer acknowledged that
it was correct but encouraged me to optimize the solution. I then proceeded to solve the question
using a Priority Queue and even wrote the code for it on paper.
Finally, the interviewer asked me if I have any question for them and ended the interviewer.

• HR Interview Round -

This interview lasted for around 20 minutes. During the interview process, we were split into two
groups and conducted interviews on different floors. As the day was coming to an end, some
students, did not have the HR round scheduled. On my floor 6-7 students were selected for this
round.
In this round, there were two interviewers, and although it was supposed to be an HR interview, one
of the interviewers surprised me by asking about procedures in Database Management Systems
(DBMS). I wasn't familiar with this concept, I admitted that and I tried turning it into a constructive
discussion. The interviewer was kind enough to explain the concept to me.
The same interviewer then asked me to explain Doubly Linked List with an example. I provided an
explanation to the best of my knowledge, and the interview proceeded smoothly. The other
interviewer focused on HR-related questions, inquiring about my family background and my future
plans for the next 5 or 10 years. Additionally, they questioned why I didn't use Java as my primary
programming language, even though I had studied it in my 5th semester. I confidently explained
that due to the IITM course, Python became my first programming language, and I became
comfortable with it. However, I reassured them that I was proficient in Java as well and could easily
switch between languages based on the requirements. I made sure to convince them that language
was not a barrier for me, and I was adaptable and competent in both Python and Java.
Then he asked me if I have any questions for him.
Finally, 17 students were selected.

❖ Tips -

1. Interviews will always start by asking to introduce yourself. So, prepare well for this question.

2. Know your resume well and do not add anything that you don't know about.

3. Be clear and confident while answering to the questions.

4. Communication is the key. Don't just answer. Try to build a conversation with interviewer.

5. Knowing Java is not necessity. But make sure to convince them that you are flexible to change the

language if needed.

6. When asked a dsa question, start by giving them a brute force. While solving keep communicating

what you are thinking and your approach to solve the question. Then after brute force, give them an
optimised approach. Give them a dry run of your code by running few test cases.

7. If you don't know the answer, admit it and try to get into a discussion and show them that you are

interested in learning.

8. Practice few easy for building base, and majorly medium questions on leetcode.

Feel free to connect on LinkedIn.
All the Best!!

journey.prep:
• Aptitude Test: Indiabix and similar websites can be helpful to get you started with the type of

questions. But the difficulty level is higher on the test and hence you should solve more questions at
approximately CAT level. And also being mindful of the time for each section is crucial.

• For guesstimates and other case studies, one of the best channels to get started with is 'Case

Interviews Cracked'. For more preparation you should ideally practice with your friends and switch
between interviewer and interviewee. And also give feedback after each session to understand your
weaknesses. Pick up some questions from the internet and try making the session as close to the real
thing as possible.

• Resume: You need to know everything that's on your resume and you need to be thorough with it.

This is very essential.

• Try finding out the most common HR type questions and have answers ready for the same. Having at

least a basic frame of what you want to say will help you remember when you actually have to
answer them.

• Most of the interview regarding guesstimates and case studies is mainly based on how well you're

structured and how well you can explore the given question. The calculations matter less than your
approach, so if you think your number may be wrong, just mention it to the interviewer and proceed
further. So, keep practicing and you'll get the hang of the basic frameworks for each type and you
can infer more knowledge as you go further in the question.

• The people taking the interview were very relaxed and it was comfortable to talk to them while

giving the interview. If you do start to think you're stuck or you're panicking, just tell them that you
want a minute or two and calm down and proceed at your own pace.

• One last important thing is to pay attention during the pre-placement talk and understand what the

company does and research more about the company on your own time. Questions about how much
you know about the company always come up in any interview for any company.
You can approach and contact me on LinkedIn at any time. I'd be happy to answer all your questions.
All the best for your placements!!

1. Aptitude Round: ~100 Students

The first round consisted of an Aptitude Test of 60 mins where it was divided into Attention to Detail,
Quantitative, Data Interpretation, Logical Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Abstract Reasoning. All the
sections were timed and you could only attempt each section once and no navigation between the sections
while a particular section was being solved was allowed.
The questions were at a higher level than normal aptitude tests have. Indiabix will not be enough to prepare
for these. There was no negative marking.
37 Students were selected for interview rounds.

2. Interview Round 1: (~30 mins)

The interview process started by the interviewer asking me how I was doing and to tell me about myself.
Then he asked me about why do you want to do consultancy, tell me how you are a team player(as I had
mentioned this on my resume). Next he asked me about a solution for my father's business that has helped
the company (I mentioned to him that my father has a business and I have had exposure to the business
side). He also asked about my plans for higher studies. Next he proceeded with a guesstimate "Calculate the
number of planes in Indian airspace at any given moment". At the end of the interview I asked him a couple
of questions about the company and about the skills to learn if I do get selected.
22 people were shortlisted further.

3. Interview Round 2: (~25 mins)

The interview started just 15 mins after I was done with round 1. The interviewer introduced themselves and
what they do in the company. First question asked to me was what was my motivation to do consulting.
Further she asked why GEP and also why consulting. Then she asked what I thought the role of a consultant
is. Then she asked me what procurement and supply chain means (as I had mentioned previously when
talking about the company). She then asked me about the project I had mentioned in the resume and
following that she asked to list challenges faced, solutions found and the outcome realized during the term of
the project. Then we moved on to a guesstimate "Calculate the total number of people traveling in a day
from Mumbai to Delhi on Indigo flights". I went on with guesstimate while confirming my steps with the
--- PAGE 2 ---
interviewer and finished until she was satisfied with the answer. Lastly she asked me why I wanted to go
into a non tech domain.
About 8 people were shortlisted further.

4. Interview Round 3: (~25 mins)

The interview was conducted in the TPO office. The interviewer started with him introducing himself and
then asked to introduce myself to him. He started by asking about my project and some details around it. He
then asked me a puzzle about the Two wires problem. Then he asked me about what I knew about GEP.
Then he moved on to a profitability question "Your client is a travel agency and they have been seeing less
profits than the industry average. Analyze the issue.' I approached the question as a usual profitability
question and used the basic framework. After discussing multiple sectors and factors, I was stuck with what
the actual issue that the company was facing. He then proceeded to give the actual answer to what was the
issue and what could be the reason it was happening.
Finally, 4 people were offered the job. (All from S.P.I.T.)

answer them.

• Most of the interview regarding guesstimates and case studies is mainly based on how well you're

structured and how well you can explore the given question. The calculations matter less than your
approach, so if you think your number may be wrong, just mention it to the interviewer and proceed
further. So, keep practicing and you'll get the hang of the basic frameworks for each type and you
can infer more knowledge as you go further in the question.

• The people taking the interview were very relaxed and it was comfortable to talk to them while

giving the interview. If you do start to think you're stuck or you're panicking, just tell them that you
want a minute or two and calm down and proceed at your own pace.

• One last important thing is to pay attention during the pre-placement talk and understand what the

company does and research more about the company on your own time. Questions about how much
you know about the company always come up in any interview for any company.
You can approach and contact me on LinkedIn at any time. I'd be happy to answer all your questions.
All the best for your placements!!

This round was conducted on 24th July in college. A total of 116 students gave this test. This test had
4 questions divided in two sections and each section had a time limit of 30 mins and has two questions
each. Only c++ allowed to write code.

Section A:

1. https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-number-of-flips-to-make-the-binary-string-alternating/

2. A class was given and we have to write a function in class to find average of numbers passed in

the function :-
Condition :- a) if the length of numbers are <=3 then find average and print
b) if length >3 then find average of latest 3 elements
Eg. :-
Input -
5 //output 5
15 //output 10 (avg(5,10))
10 // output 10 (avg(5,15,10))
5 // output 10 (avg(15,10,5))
9 // output 8 (avg(10,5,9))
So on… (size is not defined)

Section B:

3. Given n. print the union of prime numbers less than n and Fibonacci numbers less than n.

Eg - n=10
Prime numbers :- 2 3 5 7
Fibonacci :- 0 1 1 2 3 5 8
Output :- 0 1 2 3 5 7 8

4. Question was on DP. Given an array of position of houses and you have to arrange 4 people in

such a way that at most distance between adjacent people should not be more than m. find the no.
of ways for such arrangement.

I did both questions in section 1 and one question in section 2. A total of 15 students qualified for the
next round.

2. Technical Interview (Offline) (about 1hr 15 min) (25th July)

This round was conducted in their andheri office.  There were two interviewers. The interview was
mainly focused on basics of C++. And some DSA questions. Make sure to clear each concept in c++
right from clas ses to STL. They asked about o ops and then polymorphism . They asked me to write
down code for every example. Then they asked me about inherit ance and its types. What will be the
size of an empty class, which functions are present in class by default, virtual class, etc.

Then they came towards data structures and asked me to write code to implement stack using queue. I
firstly got confused and told that I will use array t o implement stack but they want implementation
using queue only. I thought for a while and gave one approach using queue. They seemed to be satisfied
by that approach.

Then they grilled me on pointers.  Asked me many tricky questions on pointers. Use of malloc, calloc,
new and delete. I was also given one DSA based question which was implementation of queue. Lastly,
they asked me about sorting. I did not prepare for this question. Though I told them about different
sorting techniques. Then one interviewer told me to write code for merge or quick sort. I got fumbled
first but then I explained the basic approach of merge sort which I recalled. But still he told me to write
function for that approach and asked me time complexity for that function. I wrote basic definition of
recursive function in merge sort and luckily, he seemed quite happy with that and told me if I had any
questions for them.

3. HR Round (10-15 mins)

After technical round they told me to sit for a while, after 2 mins they called me for HR round. It was
very quick round for me. Asked me to introduce myself, my family background, why I chose c++ over
any other language, plans for master s, and its done.  There was no any tricky question for me lik e
strengths or weaknesses OR situation-based questions.

After this they told me to leav e and my interview is done. I thought that I was not selected But the
result came later in evening and I was one in the selected candidates. Toal 3 students selected after HR
interview.

1. Digital Interview (26 - 31 August)

2. Technical Test (5 August)

3. Group Discussion (7 August 7:30 - 9:30 AM)

4. Personal Interview (7 August 10:30 AM onwards)

5. Leadership Interview (7 August)

1. Digital Interview (Online)

The digital interviews were conducted on the Hire Vue platform. Following are the questions that
were asked

1. Explain why my background and experience will be a good fit for this job?

2. Why did you decide on your degree program?

3. What do you want to gain from this internship?

4. How did I organize my time if I was given multiple priorities?

5. Tell me about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome

that?

6. If there's something more we need to know about you?

Each question has 30 sec to prepare and a maximum of 3 mins to answer 1 attempt only per
question.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Be assured in your response, without hesitation or filler words. Maintain fluency while speaking.
Only a limited number of students were not chosen. 107 students were selected for the next
round.

2. Technical Test (20 Questions 30 Minutes) 107 students gave the technical test

The technical test was administered via the Microsoft Forms platform. It comprised 20
multiple-choice questions (MCQs) that focused on topics such as data structures (predominantly
trees/graphs), the time complexity of provided code snippets, several aptitude questions
primarily centered around probability, as well as a few questions related to Al/ML and sorting
algorithms. 71 students were shortlisted for further process.

3. Group Discussion (15 minutes)

A total of 71 students were organized into groups of 10 or 11 each. Each group deliberated on
diverse topics assigned to their respective panels. The topics encompassed discussions like
Electric Vehicles vs. Hybrid Vehicles, The Future of Electric Vehicles, Reasons for the Decline
of Digital Education, and several other subjects related to these themes. Use of the internet was
not allowed, only 2 minutes were given to prepare once the topic of GD was disclosed.
In the group discussion, I managed to contribute once despite facing two interruptions, I
encouraged others to share their views. In the end, when asked to summarize, I ensured a fluent
and concise delivery. The conclusion I provided aimed to encapsulate the key discussion points
effectively.
From every group, 4 students were selected for further rounds.
Tips for Effective Group Discussions:

• Active Listening: Pay attention to others while they speak. This shows respect and

enables you to respond thoughtfully.

• Clear Expression: Speak clearly and confidently. Express your thoughts concisely to

avoid confusion.

• Valuable Contributions: Add value to the discussion by offering unique insights,

examples, or counterarguments that enhance the conversation.
--- PAGE 3 ---

• Respectful Interaction: Treat every participant's viewpoint with respect, even if you

disagree. Avoid interrupting or dominating the conversation.

• Time Management: Keep track of time to ensure everyone gets an opportunity to speak.

Avoid lingering on a single point for too long.

• Balanced Participation: Encourage quieter members to contribute and ensure that the

discussion is inclusive.

• Summarization: Towards the end, provide a brief summary of the key points discussed to

conclude the conversation effectively.
28 students were shortlisted for further process.

4. Technical Interview (Personal Interview : 1 hour)

The session began with a self-introduction. I shared that I had recently begun focusing on
problem-solving, three months prior to the placements. When queried about my choice of timing
for mastering data structures, I clarified that my primary focus lay in development. I highlighted
my accomplishments in various hackathons as well. Subsequently, I was prompted to list and rate
my skills. Questions related to my projects followed, including discussions on algorithm choices,
my preference for React over other frameworks, my contributions, and encountered challenges. I
fielded inquiries about the technical skills I had outlined earlier, involving CSS concepts like the
distinctions between div and span, margin and padding differences, methods for centering a div
tag, and the utility of display flex. JavaScript queries came next, covering topics like the
differences between let, const, and var, as well as the transformation of JSX to JS. Delving
deeper into frontend development, I explained the operational flow of a React application. Later,
leveraging my "problem solver" skill, I was presented with a puzzle involving a man living on
the 7th floor, https://www.puzzlesandriddles.com/LateralThinking13.html which I answered
convincingly. The interviewers were pleased with my response. The technical segment continued
with questions on data structures and algorithms, including linked list operations, stack
functionalities, and binary search tree construction. I confidently addressed each query. I had one
of my projects on encryption algorithms, so I was also asked questions related to end to end
encryption of whatsapp and a few questions related to certain scenarios. Towards the conclusion,
I discussed my strengths and weaknesses. I concluded the interview by inquiring about the
--- PAGE 4 ---
company's resilience during economic downturns, their specific domains within Baker Hughes,
and the organization's commendable achievement in reducing carbon emissions by 31%.
The exchange was thorough and comprehensive, reflecting my adeptness in both
problem-solving and technical domains.
15 students were shortlisted for HR round

5. HR Interview (Leadership Interview: 45 minutes)

The interview followed a Techno-HR format, involving a pair of interviewers. Commencing with
a personal touch, they inquired about my day's experiences. Subsequently, they delved into the
topic of the Group Discussion, probing the points I had raised. Project-related inquiries ensued,
with a focus on their implementation details and the challenges encountered. Of particular
interest were my victorious project from a hackathon and my contribution to the official
undergraduate college website. They keenly explored the hurdles faced during their
development. Discussions encompassed my strengths and areas for improvement, along with my
approach if entrusted with enhancing the college community. Leadership skills and hobbies were
also topics of exploration. My roles as PR Head for IPL Auction and in the realm of Fine Arts
with MUDRA drew their curiosity, leading to in-depth conversations. I was requested to
elucidate technical terms cited on my resume, demonstrating my familiarity with each. The
interview transitioned into my artistic influences and inspirations driving UI/UX design. When
listing my top qualities, I endeavored to align them with the company's values, encapsulating
growth, collaboration, leadership, and care.
Concluding the interview, they invited my questions, where I probed the organization's stance on
work-life balance and reduction of carbon emission. This sparked a meaningful discussion on the
organization's efforts to reduce carbon emissions, encapsulating a dynamic exchange of ideas.
Finally 8 students were selected
Invaluable Insights:

• Practice patience; my interview occurred five hours after the shortlist announcement, but

my HR interview followed just five minutes after the Technical Interview.
--- PAGE 5 ---

• Familiarize yourself with puzzles and riddles as they could be employed to evaluate your

problem-solving acumen.

• Thoroughly grasp the contents of your resume.

• Revisit Computer Science fundamentals, particularly OOPS concepts and Data Structure

algorithms.

• Devote time to comprehending DBMS concepts, with special emphasis on normalization,

Joins, Keys, and ER diagram notations.

• Ensure a comprehensive understanding of the company's core values.

• Remember that it's acceptable to admit unfamiliarity with an answer; avoid guessing and

providing incorrect information.

• Fortune does hold significance in the placement process, yet don't allow intrusive

thoughts to steer you off course.
ALL THE BEST !!! Feel free to contact me for any queries !
