Day 1:

• Coding Test

Day 2:

• Technical Round 1

• Technical Round 2

• HR Round

1.
Coding Test [182 Candidates appeared]
Firstly there was a pre-placement talk conducted by PhonePe discussing the various aspects of the company
which was then followed by a coding test.
It was a 90 minute pure coding test consisting of 4 questions.

1. This was a medium/hard string question. We were given a main string (say, m) and two other strings

(say, s1 and s2). Now, we had to create a resulting string such that it is a concatenation of any
number of s1 and any number of s2 (in any order) as long as a character in the resulting string
appears at most as many times as it appears in m. Initially I thought this was a greedy approach using
word frequencies but it seemed more difficult than that so I moved on to the next question. Later I
came back to the question and applied a recursive approach to consider all permutations. As a result I
was able to pass most of the test cases. I wanted to apply the DP approach but I had run out of time
so I was only able to do it partially.

2. This was a hard graph question. The question was also really long so I can't recall it. Eventually I

understood what the question was asking but it would've taken a long time and still I wasn't sure so I
skipped it completely and moved to the questions which I at least had some idea about.

3. This was also a hard tree question. It looked like a greedy question. I thought about an approach but

to me it seemed risky given the time constraints so I moved onto the next question.
--- PAGE 2 ---

4. This was a medium level tree question. You were given a tree, there is a robber at the root node and

each leaf node of the tree consists of a bank. The goal is for the robber to be able to rob as many
banks as possible. However there are also police stations which can appear at any node. Now, we are
given a parameter (say, m) such that the robber can rob any bank as long as the path from the root
node to that bank does not consist of m consecutive police stations. We had to find the maximum
number of banks that could be robbed. This question was easier than the others. I applied a direct
DFS approach along with the necessary conditions. I was able to solve this one.
Finally, 14 candidates were selected for the next round. It looks like the cut off was at least 1 question fully
solved and maybe one partially solved.
Tip: During the test, read each question first and start with those questions which you have an intuition
about.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 14 Candidates appeared]

The round started with the interviewer asking for my introduction and then gave his own introduction. He
also asked me to briefly explain the recent projects I worked on. After explaining, he asked some basic
questions about it, nothing too serious. Next he started with the dsa questions.

1. You are given an array of Characters(only B and F) and a frog positioned at the starting index. The

frog has to reach the ending position. B indicates a backward jump and F indicates a forward jump.
Sample input: FROG | FBBBBFFBBFFB | END
You have to find a minimum threshold jump distance (say, d) such that if the frog lands on an F tile
then it can make a forward jump of at most d (i.e jump length can be between 1 and d, inclusive)
tiles and if it lands on a B tile, it can make a backward jump of at most d tiles. The goal is to find a
minimum threshold jump distance d such that the frog can reach the end.
Firstly, the interviewer made sure that I understood the question. So, after he was finished
explaining, I gave him my understanding of the PS.
I started with the logic, about how the frog can reach the end position. He also gave me a sample test
case to test my approach. Eventually, I told him that since forward jumps are only helpful in this
question, we have to find the distances between consecutive forward jumps. And the maximum
distance between any two consecutives F's is the distance which we will have to cover using a jump
so that would be the answer. After giving this logic, I still thought about the edge cases to see if it
fails. I explained my logic as to why it is necessary to take the maximum. After this he asked me to
write a pseudo code for my approach and then using a sample test case we checked if it works.
Finally he agreed on the approach and moved to the next question.

2. Next was a leetcode question: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncrossed-lines/. This is similar to the

longest common subsequence question.
--- PAGE 3 ---
I started with the brute recursive approach. However, he said that it has exponential complexity so I
added the DP approach to remove redundant computations. However, he wanted the On 2)
approach so I gave him the bottom-up iterative approach. He asked me to give the pseudo code and
told me to first write the DP equations. Since it was a 2D DP problem, he told me to draw the DP
matrix and gave me a sample test case to do a complete dry run. Then he asked me that if we want to
print the matching string then how can we add code for that. I told him we can perform a second pass
doing a backtracking from the bottom right cell in the matrix and reaching the top-left left using the
DP relation. However, he was looking for a solution in a single pass and asked me if that was
possible. I told him that it would not be possible in a single pass. He then asked me about the worst
case time complexity of printing the matched string. I told him it would be O(s1.length + s2.length)
in case there are no matching characters.
I asked him a few questions about his position and work at PhonePe. He then also gave me a scenario about
how one would go about testing and reviewing code they have written. The round ended with a couple more
questions.

3. Technical Round 2[9 Candidates appeared]

The round directly started with a dsa question.
You are given a 2D matrix containing positive and negative integers. You have to find a strictly increasing
sequence of cells such that from the current cell you can move to any cell in the same row or any cell in
the same column. This looked like a DFS + DP problem, so firstly I explained my approach and they
also told me to write the c++ code as well. They also gave me sample cases to test my approach. The
complexity of the solution was O(n) so they told me to improve it. I gave a few other approaches but
they said it was not a significant improvement. They were looking for something with an On') or
O(n'logn) complexity.
This problem took some time but I kept explaining my approaches. They also gave me some hints on how
to proceed. Finally, I was able to optimize it further and come up with an O(n'logn) solution using binary
search and sorting. They told me to write production level cpp code after which the interview ended.

3. HR Round [6 Candidates appeared ]

The round was comparatively pretty chill. He firstly asked me what was my experience with the coding test.
What was the difficulty level and so on. Then he asked for my introduction and then moved onto my
resume. He first asked me about my projects. What was the motivation for the project, what were the
problems we faced, how did we solve them, how much were we able to complete, tech stack used, etc. He
also gave me a few scenarios like how I would distribute work in a team and also asked about any
experience I had where I did not like working on a project because of some problems with a colleague or a
teacher, etc.
After this he went on to my internship. He asked about what product we were building, what was my team
like, what was my contribution as a backend dev, how did we do code reviews, etc. I thoroughly explained
the whole process we followed and also the product I had worked on. He asked whether we used a sql/nosql
DB and why. He asked for my opinion as to why we chose a Nosql DB, and what problems did it solve.
--- PAGE 4 ---
Then he asked what according to me are my 5 strengths/weaknesses and also what are the 5 things I would
improve about myself.
After this he asked me what is the app I frequently use, I said reddit. He then asked questions about how,
according to me, does reddit deal with latency issues and how does it make sure that updates are done in real
time. Since, I did not exactly know how reddit handles all this, I gave him a rough idea of what I think it
might be using. I told him about distributed computing and databases which could be used to deal with
latency and also using cache queues for real time updates. I also explained strong and eventual consistency
and their application in different systems in order to maintain consistent data. He then asked whether I know
about CDNs. I said yes and then explained in brief what they are and their applications. He then gave his
views and experience on the topic.
After that he asked if I had any questions for him. I asked him questions about how phonepe executes an
idea from start to final deployment. I asked about his experience as a former cpp developer. The interview
ended after a couple more questions.
Overall, the HR round was kind of like a discussion about my resume and technology in general along with
a few behavioral questions. The interviewer was also quite friendly.
Finally, 4 candidates received an offer.

Tips:

1. PhonePe interviews are mostly DSA based so make sure to focus more on that. Study the working

and time complexities of all important data structures and algorithms.

2. During the technical interview, make sure to think out loud. It is important that you communicate

your ideas and approaches to the interviewer, since they are interested in your thought process and
logic building. If they know what direction you are thinking in, they can also provide appropriate
hints.

3. When given a dsa question, firstly explain your own understanding of the problem so the interviewer

can make sure you have got it right and also ask for constraints before coming up with a logic.

4. Do not lie on the resume or during an interview and be confident in what you know. Make sure you

have an in-depth knowledge of everything you have put on your resume.

5. Practice by giving mock technical and hr interviews.

6. Study the important concepts of OS, CCN, DBMS, OOPS along with a knowledge of system design

concepts.
All the Best!!

Each round is an elimination round.

1. Resume Screening

2. Aptitude Test (Online)

3. Group Discussion (Group size 10)

4. Interview Round 1

5. Interview Round 2

6. HR Round

ROUND 1: Resume Screening

Not much to say about this round just general tips with regards to resume:

• Make single column resume using Latex (might as well use other one but this is the standard one)

• Do add your photo when it comes to submitting resume to JPMC

• Check your resume score using- https://resumeworded.com/score.php

70 students were shortlisted for the aptitude test.

ROUND 2: Online Assessment

45 Questions (No negative marking) - 45 minutes

1. Section 1 - Corporate finance and Financial Accounting (10 questions)

2. Section 2 - Market Awareness (10 questions)

General questions related to RBI, SEBI, policies, etc..

3. Section 3 - Quantitative Aptitude (15 questions)

Mostly Probability, Profit & Loss, Worker/Water tank problem, etc.. (all are standard ones)

4. Section 4 - English Usage (10 Questions)

59 students were shortlisted after the round.
Preparation: https://www.indiabix.com/
--- PAGE 2 ---

ROUND 3: Group Discussion

Topic: Current Trends in banking system in India and across the globe
Divided into groups of 10 candidates each. The GD topic was given a day prior but the groups were allotted
just before the round started.
The given topic was just the theme for the GD. During the GD they gave topics one by one and asked to
discuss the same. First it started with UPI in the current banking system, fall of Silicon valley Bank (SVB),
emerging of Neobanks (each one of us had to suggest one topic and they chose one of it... this was the one I
suggested and was taken up) and finally general market discussion.

Tips:

1. Have adequate entries and good points as your performance here determines when your interview

will be scheduled. Better you perform, the earlier your next round, higher are the chances.

2. Support your views with numbers and/or examples.

ROUND 4: Interview 1

Duration: 35-40 min (was shorter for other candidates)
My interview began with the classic question, "why a non-tech role?
Then he went on to ask what has been the market trend off late in India and then across the world. So I told
him about the general trend in Asian markets (Japan, South Korea and China) and US markets. As I
mentioned regarding US increasing interest rates, he asked me how that works. Then he moved on to ask
about the failure of SVB. Other things he asked in current affairs where 2008 Subprime crisis, recent Merger
and Acquisition, reason for fall in US market price yesterday and finally yesterday's sensex and Nifty
closing (see this for sure before the interview)
Then he moved to the financial statements - definition, questions on basics (understand these inside out as
they are very very very important), EBIT, EBITDA, SLR, Equity, Debt, Enterprise value, etc..
Last part of the interview was puzzles and mental math.

Tips:

1. Puzzles: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzles/

2. Can practice mental math here if you want https://www.mathtrainer.io/ (I haven't used it but it's

good)

3. The interview is mostly driven by your answer in the previous question so be careful while

answering and drive the interview accordingly

4. Be thorough with financial statements.

ROUND 5: Interview 2

Duration: 15-20 min
He started by asking "walk me sequentially through your resume" and he made sure I cannot see it :) ... so
be thorough with your resume.
This was more straightforward than the previous one as it mainly focused on basics and in-depth knowledge
of financial statements and other concepts like financial ratios.
He also asked me regarding valuation methods (make sure to do this) which I didn't know and told him.

1. Round 1: Online Assessment

In this round, we were asked to give a test on the hackerearth platform. It consisted of 2 coding questions
and 20 multiple choice questions (10 QA and 10 English). The MCQs were fairly easy. My first coding
question was DSA based, Good Subsequences. This was a Dynamic Programming based question and
was a difficult one. The other was a REST API (3rd question) based question where we had to write a JS
code to fetch data of countries from the given API. This question was easy to solve. Most of the people
who got selected had solved both of these questions, so aim to complete both of them.

2. Technical Round 1(35-40 minutes)

This round consisted of 49 students who were selected from the test. We were first given a pre placement
talk after which the interviews started. The interviewing panel consisted of 2 individuals. They started by
asking me to introduce myself. They made sure that the environment was very friendly and made sure
that I was not nervous. They asked me questions purely based on my resume. They started with my
projects and how I had contributed to them. Simple questions like what is redux, which version of node
did I use were asked. They also asked me about Git commands and if I knew what SVN is (Version
Control). After that they moved onto RDBMS, asked me which I would prefer while making a project.
Then they asked me which type of DB would be best suited for Instagram. I also had mentioned a
hackathon on my resume so they asked me about my contribution to it. Then they moved to DSA. I was
asked the missing number problem. After this I was asked which is the best sorting algorithm for a
partially sorted array, to which I replied Insertion sort and I was asked to code the same. The last
question was about tree traversals. I was asked to write the pseudo code for Level Order Traversal which
I did and the interview ended there.
After Round 1, I was the first to be called for Round 2 and it happened immediately after the previous
round.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Technical Round 2(30 minutes)

This round was shorter than the previous round. Again, this round started with the interviewer asking me
to introduce myself. I had mentioned that I play chess so we had a short conversation about that. All the
interviewers were very friendly and made sure that I was comfortable. There was only 1 person in the
panel this time. He asked me about the CNN algorithm, since I had used it in one of my projects. Then
he moved on to DSA. Again, I was asked Tree traversals, BFS/DFS and how all of them work. The next
question was Dutch National Flag. I had previously solved this question on leetcode. He had framed a
story: There is a school annual day and students, teachers and parents are all invited. There is a line of
chairs arranged and everyone randomly sits in any of the chairs. I have to sort them in such a way that all
students sit together, all teachers sit together and so do the parents. He gave me 5 minutes to think about
this question. He made me realize that I can do better than merge sort. First I gave him the counting
approach which was correct but he wasn't satisfied with it. So I used a 2 pointer approach by swapping,
which was what he wanted. He asked me if I knew the name of the problem since it is very famous, but I
was unaware about it. The interview ended here.
HR round was not conducted for me and many other students, but this does not eliminate you from the
process. A total of 17 people were selected after the whole process was completed.

discussion with the interviewers.

seemed quite experienced. He first asked me about the difference between Graphs and Trees.

know it, so I told him the same. Then he gave me one coding question- Given an array of strings,
find the pairs of anagrams in the array. I explained to him my approach of sorting every string

You will have a high chance of clearing the first 2 rounds if you solve both the coding questions

1) If you're new to SQL, it's a good idea to start by mastering the basics. You can do this by using

resources like SQLBolt, which provides interactive lessons to help you understand SQL concepts
step by step.

2) Once you have a grasp of the basics, move on to practice platforms like HackerRank. These

platforms offer various SQL challenges and problems to solve.

3) To further challenge yourself and expand your SQL expertise, consider working through a set of 50

SQL questions on platforms like LeetCode. These questions are designed to test your
problem-solving abilities and deepen your understanding of SQL concepts.

4) Enhance your learning by working on real-world projects related to data analysis or data science.

Applying SQL in projects allows you to practically utilize your skills, improve logical thinking, and
understand how SQL fits into larger data-driven processes.

5) Develop your critical thinking and puzzle-solving skills by engaging with puzzles from sources like

GeeksforGeeks and Brainstellar. These platforms offer a variety of challenges that can sharpen
your problem-solving abilities.

6) Boost your confidence and refine your communication skills through mock interviews. Participating

in mock interviews helps you identify areas for improvement, work on your delivery, and build the
stamina needed for actual interviews.

7) Remember, mock interviews are opportunities to make mistakes and learn from them. Each mistake

you address in a mock interview is a chance to refine your responses and strategies, ensuring you're
better prepared for the real placement interview.

8) If you have any questions or need guidance, feel free to connect with me on LinkedIn. My provided

LinkedIn ID is available for you to seek help and advice as you navigate through your preparation
and placement process.
ALL THE BEST !!!

The placement process involved three rounds, preceded by a pre-placement talk and resume shortlisting. The
pre-placement talk allowed candidates to ask questions and learn about the company. After the resume
shortlisting, 113 students proceeded to further rounds.

1. Round 1 (SQL Round) [ 40 students appeared for this round ]

The interview session lasted for approximately 30 minutes. It began with me introducing myself and making
sure to present myself well while mentioning my strengths. Following that, I was prompted to assess my
proficiency in SQL on a scale of 1 to 5. I rated myself a 4, reserving 1 point for potential improvement.
Subsequently, I was presented with an employee database schema and tasked with executing straightforward
queries. These queries encompassed tasks such as sorting, identifying unique values, and gradually
increased in complexity with each subsequent question. The SQL-related questions posed during the
interview were of intermediate difficulty and spanned various concepts including aggregate functions,
joins, and the 'group by' clause etc Furthermore, the interview included several theoretical questions
pertaining to DBMS theory, encompassing topics such as data types, DDL, DML, cross join,
distinctions between cross join and right join, and the applications of partition keys. I provided accurate
responses to these questions, leading to a discussion about the projects listed on my resume. Given the role's
focus on data, I highlighted relevant projects on data analysis, data engineering, and machine learning
domain. This served to underscore my keen interest in the realm of data. Just so you know, the interview was
done online using the Gmeet platform and I was asked to share my screen and write queries on Notepad.
Total 10 students were shortlisted for further rounds.

2. Round 2 Problem Solving Round] [ 10 students appeared for this round]

The interview extended for about an hour and was conducted by the Product Lead at WorkIndia. Unlike
past years interview experiences, I wasn't asked any guesstimate questions. The interview began with me
introducing myself once again. To demonstrate my keen interest in the data field, I mentioned that I had
undertaken projects in different domains such as data engineering, data science, and data analysis. I was
--- PAGE 2 ---
then asked several questions related to my projects. Following this, the interviewer inquired about the
app I used most frequently on my mobile. I replied that it was WhatsApp. He followed up by asking
about the latest feature I had observed on WhatsApp, to which I answered "WhatsApp Digital
Payments." This shift in the interview's direction led to discussions about product-related scenarios,
essentially testing my ability to approach and assess features. We delved into topics such as evaluating
feature success through data analysis, particularly in the context of WhatsApp Digital Payments. The
conversation covered various cases, including entering a market with strong competitors, tracking
feature success over time, and comparisons with other competitors. The interviewer used these
questions to gauge my logical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and my approach to conducting
data analysis and product feature analysis. Continuing with the interview, I was presented with an
Instagram database schema. My task was to write queries for tracking user engagement with
different features on Instagram. These queries were quite challenging and tested my
understanding of self joins, subqueries, and timestamp-related queries. After correctly addressing
them, I was given a puzzle to solve. I managed to solve it accurately, and the interviewer probed into my
approach for arriving at the solution. Throughout the interview, the interviewer consistently assessed my
thought processes and approaches in solving various cases and questions. It was crucial to effectively
communicate each approach to ensure clarity. In essence, the interview highlighted the importance of
demonstrating clear approaches and problem-solving techniques, especially in the context of analyzing
product features. Later in the interview, I was given the chance to ask the interviewer any questions I
had. This moment provides an opportunity to set yourself apart from other candidates. Instead of asking
common questions, it's important to conduct research about the company's work. By posing distinctive
questions, you can make a memorable impression. Inquiring about unique and different aspects
demonstrates your genuine interest in the company. Further 3 students were selected for the final round
including me.

3. Round 3 (Culture Fit Round) [ 3 students appeared for this round]

The round commenced at 6:30 pm in the evening and spanned around 45 to 50 minutes. The interviewer,
a co-founder and alumnus of SPIT, began by introducing himself. I followed suit with my introduction,
but he interjected, advising me to avoid delivering a rehearsed response. I then took the opportunity to
discuss my internship experience, which I hadn't covered in my initial introduction. As our conversation
progressed, the interview retained a relaxed atmosphere. It appeared that the focus was on gauging my
compatibility with the company's culture. He inquired about my decision to pursue a career as a data
scientist after enrolling in electronics engineering. This line of questioning led to further queries on the
same theme. The interviewer delved into topics like my strengths and weaknesses, my motivation for
joining WorkIndia, and whether I would consider joining the company for a salary of only 6 lakhs. He
also sought explanations for why I believed I was the suitable fit for the role and what unique qualities I
possessed. While the interviewer sets a casual tone, it's essential to recognize that the evaluation begins
from the outset of the interview. Towards the conclusion of the session, I once again had the opportunity
to pose questions. Just as I had done in the previous round, I utilized this chance to ask well-researched,
distinctive questions about the company. This final interaction serves to create a lasting impression and
reflects a genuine interest in the organization. Total 2 students were selected and offered the I + P offer
from WorkIndia for the Product Analyst/ Business Analyst/ Data Scientist role.
--- PAGE 3 ---

For the placement process, three rounds were conducted. There was a resume shortlisting round before any
of the actual rounds happened. 112 students were shortlisted after the resume round.

1. Round 1: SQL Round

Around 40 students had applied for the role of a data analyst. Round 1 was the SQL round. I was
interviewed by a panel of two full timers. The questions were straightforward and ranged from very easy to
hard leetcode SQL queries. The interviewers increased the level of questions after each correct answer. I
was asked 4 questions in this round. The first question was a simple where query. The second question was
a simple join query. The third question was that of sorting the table. I gave two approaches for the third
question. The first approach had a small error so I was asked to find the error and rectify it. The second
approach was correct. The fourth question was a follow-up question of the third one and it was a complex
query so the interviewer asked me to explain the approach and not write it down. After which the
interviewer explained the correct logic for this question. The interview went on for 30 minutes.

2. Round 2: SQL + Guestimates

The second round was a longer round. It went on for about an hour. 10 students were shortlisted for this
round. I was asked to introduce myself again. Then a google spreadsheet was shared with me which
contained the schema for two tables followed by 7 questions. I was given 15 minutes to solve those 7
questions. Level of the questions was medium and hard leetcode queries. I was able to solve 5 questions
and started with the 6th one but time was up. After that the interviewer asked me to find an error and rectify
it which I had made in the first query. He then asked me the approach for the other two queries which I
hadn't solved. I was able to answer one but I didn't know the approach to the second one so I told him.
We then moved on to guestimates. The first question that was asked was to estimate the number of bank
accounts present for a particular bank. The second question was to estimate the number of tea cups
consumed in Delhi throughout the month. The third question was to estimate the number of people living in
a housing society. I gave a straightforward answer for this one where I took the average family size per
household multiplied by the average houses on a floor multiplied by the number of floors. However the
interviewer wanted me to take into account the varying sizes of household and asked me to think
--- PAGE 2 ---
accordingly. I proceeded by assuming that each house on a floor houses a different number of people based
on the size of the house. He then asked if I has any questions for them.

3. Round 3: HR/Culture Fit

This round was a 30 minute round. 4 students were shortlisted for this round. The interviewer was an SPIT
alumni. He started off by introducing himself. Then he asked for my introduction. He then shared his
college experience and some valuable insights. He asked me the same questions regarding my college
experience till date. Then he asked me about my extracurricular activities and the committees I was a part
of. He asked me my highest point of life till date and to give reasons for the same. Then he asked me my
lowest point and we had a little chat about that. Finally he asked me if I had any questions for him.
2 students were given the job including me. Keep in mind that the interviewer tests you right from the
beginning as soon as he starts chatting with you about his college life etc. Don't get carried away and end
up saying something you don't mean to. This round mainly checks your behavior with other colleagues and
your ability to communicate properly with utmost clarity.

1. First Round [82 students appeared for the test]

The test was conducted on Google Forms in the form of MCQs in the college. There were 70 questions which
had to be solved in 90 minutes. And please note that there was negative marking of 0.25 as well.
Questions: 40 technical and 30 aptitude based.
Technical: 18 Java, 17 Python and 5 MySQL (The questions for Java and python included output -based
questions and abit of theory as well and for MySQL, queries were given as option)
Aptitude: It included bar-graph, pi-chart, age problem, distance problems and the basic aptitude problems.

In the technical part, concepts related to enum and singleton , collections, oops were also asked for Java and
for python questions related to tuple, lists, dictionary were asked . So, try learning the basic concepts of both
the languages as sometimes it will help in solving the easy and straightforward questions of both the languages
as well. For practice, GFG, interviewbit and other websites would be useful.
For MySQL, knowing about joins, group by having clause and subqueries would be useful. Now, for the
technical part, most of the questions were output based questions where the code's picture was giv en and
output was asked.
For the aptitude part, indiabix is one of the useful resources. Practice aptitude questions as it will help you in
solving them quickly during the main test.
If possible, rather than guessing right from start, try solving questions  whose answer you are sure about as
there is negative marking.
The questions in the test were of mixed difficulty and required solving as well. So, it is better to have a practice
in advance.
Also, one approach that I used was to allot time for each section so I could give maximum time to the section
in which I was most confident.

2. Technical Round [23 students were selected for this round]

The interviews were conducted the same day as the test. There were two rounds of interviews: Technical and
HR round. The interview was conducted by two people. Also, this interview mainly dependent on the first
preference you filled while the form for this  company was floated. Like mine was software engineer as the
first preference. And for me, this round lasted for about 45 min to 50 mins.
The interview started with my introduction where I had mentioned my projects so I explained about it in short
as well. Then, they started straightaway with the interview. One thing which I felt was that the interviews
easily understood how much confident we were in any concept. So, they would ask in depth for the ones which
we knew but not in depth as well.
They started by asking my major programming language which was Java and they asked about the 4 pillars
of OOPS and with the words they were satisfied and they moved on to upcasting and downcasting in Java.
And this is the question which I was asked in every interview which I appeared so ensure you know that. The
basic concept is which methods and variables are acces sible if we make object of parent class and use child
class constructor and vice versa.
Then a basic java program was asked to me which was to count distinc t words in a string which can be done
using HashMap. This led to a follow-up question of if I want to insert elements in insertion order which would
be used and it would be linkedHashMap and why not TreeMap So, a good knowledge of Collections is a must
if your major programming language is Java. Then a common question to me and candidate before me was
asked which was if you have a list of objects of employees which has the department and salary stored in it,
how will you calculate average salary per department. So, one of the approaches was that using two hashmaps,
it can be done where one would store the number of employees per department and another would store the
total salary of the employees of that department. And then basic questions related to Java were asked so have
solid points to answer when asked any questions.
This was then followed by MySQL and MongDB related questions as I had mentioned both in resume. The
difference between NoSQL and RDBMS. The generation of unique ID in MongoDB document and w hether
it can be updated, type of nosql database mongodb is, difference between collection and document. Basic
queries of how MongoDB works like and how connection is done. For MySQL, they were interested in how
to connect mysql with Java which can be done by downloading JDBC driver and also know how whole process
takes place like for connection like the components in connection query which contains the username,
password and all. For query, a simple group by having clause query was asked and the order of e xecution of
select, group by, having, where was asked. Also, a major discussion went on the topic of difference between
unique not null key and primary key and whether null can be used multiple times in unique key or it cannot
be considered even once. So, regarding these questions, make a note in your book as due to the interview
pressure, one might get them wrong. Also, if they feel that we know the answer but are confused regarding
the same, they would give small hints.
And then they asked whether about REST API and the methods of rest and how is the request of get and put
works.
The interview ended with they asking whether I had any questions so I asked them regarding the tech stacks
and the latest projects they were working on. It was altogether a very  good interactive interview which felt
more like a discussion. And incase if you don't know any concept or answer, tell them honestly so they can
move on with next question.

3. HR Round [7 students were selected for this round]

In this round basic HR quest ions were asked after I gave my introduction which was less technical and I
mentioned about my education as they had told me what all they want to know about me in my
introduction. Apart from that, they asked whether I would like to pursue higher studies and why not. They
asked me about my preference between working full stack and only backend. It was then followed by what
would I choose between working on different programming languages or different databases irrespective
of the language. In my resume, I had mentioned about my minor course of management from SPJIMR, so
they were interested to know about that. And the basic question of why ISS was asked. It ended with me
asking few questions about the company.
It was comparatively a short interview but a goo d experience. General piece of advice would be that for
this round, don't mug up any answer but keep in mind what all points you would say if any kind of
questions are asked.

At the end, all 7 students were selected.

the answers as well and then make yours, don't mug it up but try and have points clear.

7. Always build your solution step by step and communicate with the interviewer what you are

thinking. Don't show him that you know the answer even if you do, he wants to test your
thinking, not your ability to remember. He may not always need the answer to a puzzle
question, he just wants to see how you approach a problem and your logic-building.
Feel free to contact me on LinkedIn!
ALL THE BEST!

journey.howSecured:
Each round is an elimination round. Round 2 was on the 13th of July
2023(online) and the rest of the rounds took place on the 21st of July 2023(offline).
List of rounds:

1. Resume Screening

2. Aptitude Test

3. Group Discussion

4. Interview Round 1

5. Interview Round 2

6. HR Round

ROUND 1: Resume Screening

o In this round, the company scanned all the resumes and sent the shortlist to college. My
suggestion would be to keep 2 copies of resume in hand, one to be attached while sending
to company and second carried on campus.
o Always use a Latex resume to be sent in online screening tests.
o Keep your resume very clear and to the point. Do not put anything that you are not aware
of or are dicey. Make sure that it contains key words related to banking and finance.
70 students were shortlisted for the aptitude test.

ROUND 2: Aptitude Test (70 applicants)

o This round was completely online, that is it was not mandatory to stay on campus while
attempting the test.
o There was a window of 30 minutes (1p.m to 1.30 pm) to log in to the test. The round
comprised 45 questions for 45 minutes, 10 on Market Awareness (Questions on current
affairs), 10 on Corporate Finance (Basics of Accounting and Financial Ratios), 15 on
Quantitative Aptitude and 10 on Verbal Reasoning.
o The questions on Verbal and market awareness were easy and quants and finance between
easy to moderate. Overall, it was moderate exam. The catch here was the time limit per
question.
Out of 70, 59 students were shortlisted for the round.

ROUND 3: Group discussion (59 students)

o Every year the company keeps a banking workshop, but for my batch they had kept group
discussion. Initially the topic was not disclosed.
o I had prepared on various topics, like diversity, inclusion, G20 mission, technology. Make
sure to be ready in case topic is not disclosed.
o 2 days before the interview, late night we received the topic "Current trends in banking
system in India and across the globe."
o The discussion lasted for 20-25min in groups on 10. There were 2 interviewers present who
were giving inputs and giving us topics to talk on. Be active and respond politely. Make
sure to add new and innovative points so that panellists notice you. Keep yourself updated
with recent market news.
o We were allowed to carry mobile phones and refer the points we have noted down, but it
may not be the case for your batch. So be ready to speak without reference.
o There are some ground rules for group discussion, make sure you always follow them.
From my panel, 5 of us were sent for next round and from 59 students in total 35 students were
shortlisted.

ROUND 4: Interview Round 1

o The shortlisted candidates were divided into 8 panels, each had 1 or 2 members from the
recruitment team.
o The round began with very normal conversation; they try to calm you down. My
interviewer asked me to introduce myself. By that time, he was scanning through my
resume. He caught on the minors in management course from SPJIMR. He started asking
me how exactly the selection is done, what were the topics covered. After 10-15 min he
moved on to the finance questions.
o Initially, he asked me what is accounting and what was my understanding on it. I explained
him in detail 3 financial statements. He then moved on to asking how the statements were
linked to each other. The next question came that how was revenue recognized. At this point
I got confused so I asked him to elaborate a bit. I then answered the concept of accrual and
cash basis. I also explained him revenue recognition criteria.
o He saw in my resume a project that I had done in core finance which interested him very
much. There was a detailed round of questioning that took place on the project. He also
gave me suggestions to improve it further. Overall, this project was the key which helped
me in further rounds.
o We then moved on to the puzzles and quick maths. He asked me a probability puzzle from
GFG which I could not recollect at that moment.  I told him how much I could recall and
then he gave me a few hints as well. After 5-7 min of trying, I gave up and told him I am
unable to solve. For this question use of paper allowed. He then asked 67 ✕ 73 mentally to
which I gave him the approach and the correct answer. Note that none of the mental maths
such as squares, square root question allows the use of calculator.
o At the end, the interviewer asked me my future plans. He was very blunt in asking are you
planning to give CAT this year to which I answered no.
o The interview lasted for more than 45min.
o In any of the questions, be it quick maths, puzzles, or finance, do not pause for 1-2 min.
Rather walk him through your approach and simultaneously keep calculating. It is your
attitude to attempt the questions rather than the answer.
o Make sure to be very through with core financial concepts and basics.
o After this round, we lost track of how many applicants were shortlisted for the next rounds
as the rest of the rounds were conducted in parallel.

I was shortlisted was both, CIB, and CR roles, so my interviews were going on in parallel.
However, for the CIB role my round 2 was not taken and I was sent directly for HR Round.
Only 2 candidates out of the selected ones had this opportunity to go directly by skipping one
round.

ROUND 5: HR Round

o This was the final round. I was greeted at the beginning by a panel only one lady. It started
with how are you, how was your day.
o The she moved on to my family background and asked me a few questions on it. I
mentioned that my father works in a CA firm, so she asked my why not CA then, why
MBA. This was a partial trick question because she wanted to see how I justified my reason
for choosing a particular career field.
o She then asked me to talk about something which was not there my resume. Fortunately, I
had not put my college projects in the resume, so I spoke in details about the Sem 4, Sem
6 and current major project. Mention any significant progress that you have made in this
project. I mentioned filing a patent on the project.
o She then asked me why JPMC and what I expected from the role. I was asked 2-3 times
why I wanted to work in Investment Banking and not in Corporate Risk. I talked about my
passion and liking. She also asked me why I did not try for Fintech.
o In the end, I was asked whether I had any questions. I asked her 2 questions. (Keep a few
questions ready beforehand)
o The round lasted for 15 - 20 min.
In total, 13 students were selected for the internship.

Important Points to Note:
 This link has all the resources I used for the preparation.
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Nwf3VM4tBb92TxsgUxDtghXyLeSLHU_v/view?usp=s
haring   (Please open on laptop / desktop)
 It is a pure non-technical finance role and we as engineering students come from a very
strong technical background, so they do not expect you to know a lot about finance and
accounting (do not take this lightly). However, having a few courses such as Accounting
Fundamentals, Corporate Finance from CFI would help you stand out from others. It
personally helped me a lot so I highly recommend you to do this course or any other
equivalent course. Apart from CFI, you may refer to Investopedia.
 Study the current affairs such as merger and acquisition deals, Market trends and IPO
launches from Economic Times. Read the past 1month news in detail. Make sure you are
aware about topics like SENSEX, NIFTY, GDP. They just want to check how aware you
are of things going on in the domain that you aspire to work in.
 While solving the mental math questions and puzzles keep explaining your approach, do
not pause for more than a minute if in case required for calculations. It is okay not to get
the correct answer, but the attempt carries brownie points.
 The interviewers try to test your personality in every interview, so work on your
communication skills, and confidence and never go blank for any question, if you don't
know the answer just explain your thought process. Keep smiling throughout and always
maintain eye contact with the panellists.
 Be very honest while creating your resume and while giving the interview. Do not give
them any chance to grill over something that you've mentioned on the resume and is not
true. Be thorough with your resume. Prepare detailed answers on every section of your
resume. Start from introduction, move on to the education. If you have taken up minors, be
ready to answer that as well. Create a sample answer format for projects, internships,
achievements and even certificate sections. I will attach a few common questions that can
possibly be asked on resume sections.
 Do not wait for the placement season to commence to start your preparations. Believe me,
you will not get any time once the season starts, so be prepared well in advance. I myself
had started preparing a year ago, and this was the point that the interviewers liked a lot.
 Be prepared for questions like, "Where do you see yourself in 5 years?", "Do you have any
plans for higher studies?" or "Why won't you consider MBA as an option as it would add
more value to your resume?" while answering such questions do not mention your higher
studies plans although you may have one. I will also try to attach as many HR Questions
as possible.
 Placement season is extremely stressful, so stay physically, mentally and emotionally
strong during the process. Do not believe any rumours regarding the companies not arriving
the campus, the TPO will officially keep sending updates regarding the companies and the
roles offered.
 Feel free to reach out to the seniors in case of any doubts regarding the placement process
or any role-specific questions, we are here for y'all. Also, in case of any doubts for the CIB
or CR roles, you can definitely reach out to me or connect on LinkedIn.
 Lastly, stay calm and composed during the process. Be enthusiastic while answering the
questions. The company is always looking forward to work with people who are passionate
and active, so make sure you deliver that. Do not panic!
All The Best Guys!
You've Got This :))

Keep two points i and j on the head of two linked list. If i and j nodes are equal then add it into the new linked list or else move the pointer whose value of node is smaller. The interviewer asked me the Time complexity of the approach 3rd Question: There is a highway which is 1 directional only, No overtaking is allowed. No accidents are gonna happen. journey.prep:
• Practice DSA regularly

• Have a good knowledge of OOPS, DBMS, SQL and any of the following languages (Java, Python,

C++). I would prefer Java, since most of companies require java but its not compulsory

• I haven't heard anyone being asked concepts of OS and CCN much. For these 2 subjects some

standard questions are enough

• For aptitude questions, puzzles prepare from Indiabix, GFG. That's sufficient

• Prepare a nice introduction for yourself and practice it. If you give a nice introduction that sets a nice

tone for the rest of interview

• Know your resume very well, especially projects you mentioned. Take help of your friends or gpt

and prepare as many questions as possible that you could be asked in your interview and prepare
accordingly. Also prepare some introduction ready for each project whenever asked to give an
overview of the project. Introduction should be just 5-6 lines regarding your project like why did you
do it? What it is? What are the features? And finally the tech stack. Keep the answers as simple as
simple. If you use big words in your answers and you don't have an idea about them then the
interviewer can cross question it, so keep the answer simple so he also understands it easily.

• Whenever asked any question if you know then answer it in the easiest way possible. If you don't

know any answer then tell it honestly, or if you know it slightly then tell how much you know. Don't
be quiet. Don't give answers in just one word. If you are asked a certain concept, then it's better to
explain it with an example, this shows the interviewer you haven't only mugged the answer but you
genuinely know it.

• If you are asked a DSA question then discuss your approach with the interviewer, don't stay quiet.

Let the interviewer know how you come up with the solution. They are more interested in how you
think rather than the answer. And if possible first give a brute force solution and then optimize it
further.

• Be relaxed in your interview. Most of the interviewers are friendly and help you. Ask questions

whenever you are stuck. Prepare some questions that you will ask the interviewer at the end of the
interview.

• Do a background check of the company before going into the interview. Generally the companies

values, what it does, what are it's some popular products/services, any recent achievement/news
regarding that company

• And lastly, don't worry too much about the result. Focus more on preparation. This is only a start of a

new phase in life, you have an entire race ahead of yourself. Even if you are rejected in any
--- PAGE 6 ---
interview, don't get frustrated. Go home, eat dinner, do something relaxing and take a good sleep.
Instead of whining about why I didn't get selected, focus on what went wrong and try to improve
that next time. This was my 6th interview, so let me tell you the placement process is very tiring and
stressful. But don't give up hope, there's no point in that because companies will keep coming. Our
TPO is doing a pretty good job, compared to other colleges.

• And luck does play an important role in the process to be honest, sometimes you see people less

capable than you get selected, but luck isn't in our hands, what is, is hard work. So focus on
preparation. Learn from your mistakes instead of being sad and look forward.

• Maintain a positive demeanor and always wear a smile. Project confidence in your responses, even

when addressing incorrect answers.
References:
DSA - Striver SDE Sheet, Coding-Decoded SDE sheet, Love Babbar SDE sheet. Any one of them you can
follow
DBMS, OOPS - GFG, Javatpoint, Interviewbit are sufficient. Search for top 50 interview questions and
prepare accordingly
SQL - For theory you can refer to GFG, javatpoint. For practicing queries I would suggest hackerrank.
Mostly focus of joins, group by, sub-query, limit
OS, CCN - some some standard questions from GFG
Puzzles - Indiabix, GFG
Wishing you all the best for your placements and for your future, everyone!

were selected for only 1 role, though in the end it didn't matter for which role you were selected, depending
on how you performed in the interview you were selected for a role)

Round 2: Technical Interview-1

For most candidates, the duration of the round was 40-60 minutes.
There was no fixed pattern of questions asked in the interview. Some were asked about the projects in their
resume while some were asked coding questions or sal queries, or totally out of box questions
--- PAGE 4 ---
Let me share my experience:
My interviewer's name was Priyam Sinha. So first I was asked to introduce myself. Then he asked me to
explain one of the projects which was a fitness website. Then since my other 2 projects were related to
machine learning he asked me whether I am more focused on ML, to which I answered that's not the case
and I am still exploring various domains and am currently planning to work on cloud computing for my
final year project. We discussed it for around 5 mins then he asked me questions related to Heap Data
Structure like what is heap, what does it work, what are its uses, what are its types etc. they were general
questions and i answered most of them correctly. Then he moved on to dsa. I was asked 2 questions on dsa:

1. https://leetcode.com/problems/amount-of-time-for-binary-tree-to-be-infected/description/

2. https://leetcode.com/problems/search-in-rotated-sorted-array/

example. I was also asked to tell the time and space complexity for the program.
For the second question the required time complexity by the interviewer was O(log(n)). I was only told to
explain the approach and write the if-else conditions required in the program.
This was it. He asked whether I had any questions to which I asked about his role and what companies he
has worked with prior to IDfy (I searched about him on LinkedIn, so I framed my questions accordingly)

Round 3: Technical Interview-2

For most candidates, the duration of the round is 60-70 minutes.

basically swapped. The interviewer asks whether this question was asked to you in first interview(*answer
honestly since they have a report of the previous round.
Let me share my experience:
This time my interviewer's name was Niranjan. He first asked me what questions were asked to me in my
last interview. Then he gave me 2 standard puzzles:

1. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-1-how-to-measure-45-minutes-using-two-identical-wires/

2. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-farmer-goat-wolf-cabbage/

questions related to CNN(convolutional neural network) which is a type of deep neural network. Questions

feature maps. I actually didn't have a very good idea of what it was, but I said what I knew. There was a
mention of numpy and open cv libraries in my project so he wrote a code and asked me what the output
would be. I didn't know about it so I answered honestly and said I don't know and for the projects I referred
to different documents and research papers and did accordingly so never actually learned python. (To be
honest at this point in my interview I thought I wasn't going to get selected). Then he asked me to write a

code for a lift/elevator (you heard right a **lift**). He first asked about what will be the inputs, then after
discussing what will the inputs he told to write the code. At this point my mind was going crazy but still I
wrote some code. Then he gave me different scenarios/edge-cases and asked me to think how will you solve
it. I thought and suggested my methods to which he countered everytime with a different edge-case.
Basically the point of this question was to test my thinking skill. Then he told me to write the code for this
question we would require 2 writing board and that he also can't write the code. Then he asked me how to
measure how much it had rained in mumbai on any particular day. We discussed this for some minutes and I
wasn't able to answer this properly. Then he asked me some mcqs that were there in the test and asked me to
write the code for one of the questions. Then he told me to write a pseudo code of implementation of a stack

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
• Practice DSA regularly

• Have a good knowledge of OOPS, DBMS, SQL and any of the following languages (Java, Python,

C++). I would prefer Java, since most of companies require java but its not compulsory

• I haven't heard anyone being asked concepts of OS and CCN much. For these 2 subjects some

standard questions are enough

• For aptitude questions, puzzles prepare from Indiabix, GFG. That's sufficient

• Prepare a nice introduction for yourself and practice it. If you give a nice introduction that sets a nice

tone for the rest of interview

• Know your resume very well, especially projects you mentioned. Take help of your friends or gpt

and prepare as many questions as possible that you could be asked in your interview and prepare
accordingly. Also prepare some introduction ready for each project whenever asked to give an
overview of the project. Introduction should be just 5-6 lines regarding your project like why did you
do it? What it is? What are the features? And finally the tech stack. Keep the answers as simple as
simple. If you use big words in your answers and you don't have an idea about them then the
interviewer can cross question it, so keep the answer simple so he also understands it easily.

• Whenever asked any question if you know then answer it in the easiest way possible. If you don't

know any answer then tell it honestly, or if you know it slightly then tell how much you know. Don't
be quiet. Don't give answers in just one word. If you are asked a certain concept, then it's better to
explain it with an example, this shows the interviewer you haven't only mugged the answer but you
genuinely know it.

• If you are asked a DSA question then discuss your approach with the interviewer, don't stay quiet.

Let the interviewer know how you come up with the solution. They are more interested in how you
think rather than the answer. And if possible first give a brute force solution and then optimize it
further.

• Be relaxed in your interview. Most of the interviewers are friendly and help you. Ask questions

whenever you are stuck. Prepare some questions that you will ask the interviewer at the end of the
interview.

• Do a background check of the company before going into the interview. Generally the companies

values, what it does, what are it's some popular products/services, any recent achievement/news
regarding that company

• And lastly, don't worry too much about the result. Focus more on preparation. This is only a start of a

new phase in life, you have an entire race ahead of yourself. Even if you are rejected in any
--- PAGE 6 ---
interview, don't get frustrated. Go home, eat dinner, do something relaxing and take a good sleep.
Instead of whining about why I didn't get selected, focus on what went wrong and try to improve
that next time. This was my 6th interview, so let me tell you the placement process is very tiring and
stressful. But don't give up hope, there's no point in that because companies will keep coming. Our
TPO is doing a pretty good job, compared to other colleges.

• And luck does play an important role in the process to be honest, sometimes you see people less

capable than you get selected, but luck isn't in our hands, what is, is hard work. So focus on
preparation. Learn from your mistakes instead of being sad and look forward.

• Maintain a positive demeanor and always wear a smile. Project confidence in your responses, even

when addressing incorrect answers.

DSA - Striver

If you have built projects using JS it would be a piece of cake and the entire test could be completed in 30 mins max. Accuracy matters over here for clearing the cutoff.

2. Machine Coding Round [ 11 shortlisted 7 appeared ]

It was conducted in Batches offline in the BrowserStack office in Oberoi Commerz 2. Due to the limited number of students they had confined a single batch for SPIT. The PS for the machine coding round is shared below:

This problem requires you to implement a log-watching solution (similar to the tail -f command in
UNIX). However, the log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as your server code). The
log file is in append-only mode.
You need to implement the following:

● A server-side program to monitor the given log file and stream updates as they happen using

Socket. IO for real-time communication. This will run on the same machine as the log file. You
can use any programming language for the server.

● A web-based client (accessible via a URL like http://localhost/log) that displays updates in the

file in real-time, without requiring a page refresh. The page should load once and keep
updating. On initial load, the user should see the last 10 lines of the file.
Problem Constraints:

● The server must push updates to clients in real-time using Socket. IO.

● The log file could be several GBs. How do you optimize retrieving the last 10 lines?

● The server should not retransmit the entire file every time; it should only send updates.

● The server must handle multiple clients simultaneously.

● The web page should not stay in a loading state after the first load and should not reload

thereafter.

● You may not use off-the-shelf external libraries or tools to read the file or provide tail-like

functionalities (except Socket. IO for real-time updates).
You'll be evaluated on code quality, testability, modularity, and handling of corner cases.

The Machine coding round began at 10:30 AM and we were given roughly 2 hrs to build the backend server. You may find the solutions online, but an optimal solution that caters to the edge cases of the invigilator is preferred. You are not allowed to use any AI agents or LLMs or  medium articles during this round, our invigilator was right beside us. You may refer to the documentation for development. You can interact with the invigilator during the round. Primary goal is to develop the solution using Socket. IO , I preferred NODE for the backend and socket implementation to display logs realtime with a confined Buffer to prevent parsing the logs.
The invigilator would test it on multiple edge cases, like real time parsing, multiple browser compatibility with realtime logs and order in which they appear or cases where '\n' appears while parsing logs. If it passes all the cases and you are able to explain your code really well then you would be moved forward to the next round.

I was quickly moved to behavioral questions like how will I tackle Deadlines, How will I deal with my teammate who differs in an opinion. It was the most fun director round.

journey.prep:
Panelists' preferences and questioning styles can differ, so I suggest getting ready for a wide range of
questions. These might relate to your resume, the job role, or even general situational queries. Keep in
mind that these interviewers were once engineering students themselves, just like we are now. They
possess extensive knowledge about technology, so it's best to avoid trying to deceive them or providing
incomplete answers. They'll likely recognize it.

Around 14-15 students were shortlisted for the next round

4. Interview Round 2

The second round consisted of a technical assessment with two panelists. Af ter their introductions,
they immediately launched into questioning without asking me for an introduction. One panelist
initiated the session by inquiring about my preference for JPMC and what motivated me to pursue the
role. Additionally, they inquired ab out the CEO and CFO of JPMC, to which I could only respond
with the CEO's name.
The second panelist then delved into technical matters. Initially, they inquired about the technologies
I had mentioned in one of my projects, such as Cloud Services and AI to ols. They wanted to know
why I chose these technologies and their significance within the project. The discussion shifted to my
Machine Learning project, where I provided a brief explanation. Subsequently, the focus shifted to
Object-Oriented Programming ( OOPS) concepts, where I was prompted to present code examples
illustrating the four pillars of OOPS.
The technical assessment then turned to a SQL query task, where I was asked to formulate a query to
retrieve the second -highest salary from an employee ta ble. The panelist circled back to my resume,
noticing that I had mentioned Flask as my preferred backend framework. They requested that I create
an HTML form, explaining that upon clicking a button, the entered details should be stored in a
database using Flask. I proceeded to write the complete code, elaborating on each step and clarifying
the code's functionality. The panelist seemed satisfied with my approach and concluded their technical
inquiries.

Towards the conclusion, the other panelist inquired about my strengths and weaknesses, and how these
traits would impact my work at JPMC. With these questions answered, my second interview came to

an end. They also provided an opportunity for me to ask questions. I inquired about their tech stack
and whether t hey regularly adopt new versions or tools.  The entire technical assessment lasted
approximately one hour.

Useful Tips-

For technical round like these, you need to understand what role the company is offering and prepare
accordingly. There wasn't any DSA involved but it might have been the case if the role was SDE. So,
prepare according to the role. Bu t, nevertheless, always know what you've included in your resume
and be ready to answer those questions.

7 students were shortlisted for 3rd round

5. Interview Round 3 (HR Round)

Following the second round , the transition to the HR round was swift. The atmosphere during this
discussion was quite informal, and the questions posed were of a general nature. The topics included
my reasons for selecting the CR role and specifically JPMC as the pref erred choice. Additionally, I
was asked to clarify why I was seeking an internship at JPMC, considering that other companies like
PhonePe were offering internships coupled with pre-placement offers (I+P) at our college.

The HR representative also inquired about my comprehension of the role's responsibilities and whether
I would be comfortable with potential day shifts or night shifts if required. This round reached its
conclusion within a mere 10 minutes.

At the end, 5 students were offered the internship with me being one of them.

Useful Tips:

1. Carefully go through the job description (JD). Match your resume with the needed skills, whether it's

technical or non-technical. Talk to seniors in the same field and gather information. Consulting friends
in related domains, like financially sounded friends in my case, can be helpful too.

2. Familiarize yourself with your resume and give honest answers. Interviewers can sense your

understanding of what you've mentioned. Know every detail on your resume.

3. Basic knowledge of finance and risk terms suffices. Lead the interview w ith your strongest skills. If

possible, take a small course before the interview for better preparation.

4. Prepare a few thoughtful questions to ask at the end. Avoid too many open -ended questions, as you

don't want the interviewers to feel interviewed.

5. Learn from past interview mistakes and improve upon them.

6. Speak confidently and coherently to come across as formal. Use your time effectively to showcase

your strengths.

7. Be well-prepared for HR questions. A strong HR round is crucial for moving forward.

8. Familiarize yourself with J.P. Morgan and Chase's values and activities. If asked, share what you know.

9. Approach the interview with a clear mindset. Your clarity of thought and humble, sharp demeanor

matter.

Best of luck for your interviews! Stay positive during the placement process. Interviews are as much as
they are about you as a person as they are about skills or achievements. If any queries, you can easliy find
me on LinkedIn.

1. Resume Screening

The commencement of the JPMC selection process began with the company itself, with applications
being accepted starting from July 8th. Applicants were required to submit their applications through
both Google form and the company's portal. During this stage, the evaluation was primarily based on
the content of the resumes submitted.

As a result, having a strong, or even better, an excellent resume was crucial. Such a resume should
encompass your skills, extracurricular activities, GPA, projects, internships, and other pertinent
information. Notably, the content of the resume play s a significant role in the subsequent interview
rounds.

On July 11th, the names of candidates who made it through the initial screening were released,
indicating their progression to the next phase of the selection process.

82 students for this role were shortlisted for next round.

The online aptitude round consisted of a total of 30 questions, and candidates were given 45 minutes
to complete this section.  The test  also had a compo nent of negative marking (2 marks for correct
answer, -1 for wrong answer). The questions primarily covered topics such as logical reasoning,
quantitative analysis, and verbal reasoning. It is advis able to prepare for these types of questions in
advance and consider employing time-saving techniques and shortcuts during the actual test.

Only 28 students were shortlisted after this roun d. (26 students appeared for next round as 2
others got placed in MSCI)

company's prerequisites, the technology stack in use, any specific criteria, and the desired skill set they
are seeking. It's recommended to ask insightful questions to demonstrate your interest and
understanding.

started by asking me to introduce myself. Afterward, he shared his own introduction and proceeded to
inquire about my hometown, family, and educational background. He then delved into role -specific
questions, asking about various types of risks, specifically credit risk, and my understanding of risk
management.
Following this, he presented situational scenarios and asked for my perspective on how to handle them.
He also inquired about my location preferences and whether I would be comfortable with specific time
shifts. Towards the end, he asked me to specify which divisio n I would prefer to work in, as JPMC
was offering roles in middle office, risk reporting, and project risk management for the Corporate Risk
position.
As the interview came to a close, he gave me the chance to ask any questions I might have. The entire
interview lasted about 20-25 minutes.

journey.prep:
● Practice, practice and practice. Begin your placement preparation early, as waitinguntil the last few months won't leave you enough time to cover all the necessaryconcepts. Dedicate time daily to practice Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) onplatforms like LeetCode or GFG, give contests and have a strong grasp of your

primary programming language. Alongside, compare these algorithms you've usedin your projects.

● To be honest, I started seriously concentrating on DSA only around 2-3 monthsbefore my placements(which I still regret). However, if you're in a similar situation,don't panic. Put in dedicated and consistent effort, even if you have limited time forpreparation. Practice like hell and stay committed in the days leading up to yourplacements.

For the placement process, a total of 3 rounds were conducted. 1 MCQ round and 2 walk-in interviews were organized.

1. Round 1:  Online MCQ Test

Approximately 170 students from B.Tech and 55 students from MCA appeared for the test. The test was based on Verbal, Quantitative and analytical reasoning. 60 questions (20 from each section ) were to be attempted in a time frame of 60 minutes. The marks of this round weren't revealed. I think I got most of the Verbal and analytical problems correct and was left out with some 6-7 questions of Quantitative section. The problems were similar to those which come in competitive exams like NTSE. I would suggest trying to complete the verbal section as fast as possible as quantitative questions take up more time than others. 27 students from B.Tech and 11 from MCA made it to the interviews and I was one of them.

2. Round 2: Interview-1

Following the pre-placement talk, the interviews for the shortlisted students were scheduled within the college campus. The VP of the company ( who also presented the pre-placement talk ) was my interviewer for the first round. With a formal exchange of greetings, the interviewer asked for my resume and asked me to introduce myself as he went through my resume. After I properly introduced myself, I was asked some questions on one of my projects like a rough data flow of my project, why did I choose the problem statement etc. He then suggested an extension to my project and asked my views upon how I would implement it. He then out of the blue asked me to write any piece of code of python on paper and asked me to explain it to him. I used one of my functions that was used in my project. After this , he asked me to write the logic of a calendar application without using existing libraries from where I could directly import the interface. To this I answered by mapping the starting day( this can be calculated by odd days) to the number and using % operator to achieve a cyclicity of 7 days while keeping in mind the edge cases like a leap year, 30\31 days of a month etc. The interviewer seemed quite satisfied with my approach. He then asked me about a time when I had to balance multiple priorities at once to which I answered relevently. At the end he asked me 2 puzzles, one of them was an easy variation of Tower of Hanoi and a Water Jug problem. I was able to answer the first one quickly but the second one was a bit difficult for me as there were 3 jugs and no wastage of water was allowed. The problem was that we have 3 containers of capacity 10L, 6L, and 7L out of which 10L one was empty and the other were filled. Without wasting water or external supply we had to measure 9L. I started to solve it and while solving i was discussing my approach with the interviewer. He told me that I was on the right track but after a couple of minutes of solving the problem, I was stopped due to time constraints. He then asked me if I had questions for him and I asked him the questions that I had in my mind.
All in all this round was majorly focused about how I approach problems and my ideation. However, asking other students, their experiences were different, some were asked OOPS, SQL and named algorithms too. So it totally depended upon the interviewer.
11 People from B.Tech and 3 or 4 MCA were selected for the next round . However there was a review round also where 8 Btech and 5 MCA students were given another chance to again get interviewed and get selected for the next round. This took place maybe because the company was not sure whether to select these students for the next round. A total of 3 students made it to the next round from the review round.

3. Round 3: Interview-2

This interview had 2 panelists. After handing over my resume, I was asked to give my introduction. One of the interviewers was quite impressed with one of the projects saying that the problem statement was very unique. The interviewers carefully went through everything on the resume and asked every little detail of each project to which I answered best to my knowledge. The interview went pretty smooth as I answered pretty much everything confidently. One of the panelists said that he did not want to ask any tech questions to me as most of my projects were front end extensive and maybe the interviewers had a command over SQL, so I guess that's the reason I wasn't asked one. 11 students were finally selected for the programme.
