Sakshi Khanna
TE ETRX
KPMG

Round 1: Aptitude Test.

This test contained 45 questions to be solved in 55 minutes. The questions were
based on Logical reasoning, Quants, Data Interpretation & Verbal. I found the
questions to be of medium difficulty level on an average.
After this round, around 54 students were shortlisted.

Round 2: Group Discussion

We were divided into panels of 10 to 7 people. My panel had all good speakers &
hence no one could be confident about making through this round. Our topic was
"Importance of Media in the society". Since it was an easy topic, all 10 made very
valid points. The GD lasted for 10 mins & each of us got only one chance to speak.
Later all of us were asked to conclude one by one. In the end, 5 of us from my
panel were selected & these were the ones who were articulate, spoke fluently &
did not fumble in between. In this GD, we felt that communication & presentation
skills were given more weightage.
After this round, in all 32 students made it to the next one.

Round 3: Personal Interview + HR

This round, atleast for me, was totally non technical, as I expected. It was the
most smooth interview I ever gave. I started with a brief introduction about
myself & since I had mentioned all my Positions of Responsibility in it, most of my
interview surrounded that. They were specifically intrigued by my position of
Chairperson of the Industry Relations Cell & they asked a lot of questions on what
I learnt from the industry leaders I had invited, what I learnt about the industry,
etc. There were some questions asked on my project too.

The HR then asked me if I had any backlogs, checked if my marks were 60% &
above throughout. Asked which all companies I had applied for previously, etc.
Later they asked me if I had any questions for them.
After this interview, a total of 19 candidates were shortlisted for the final round.

Round 4: Interview with KPMG's Director

My Round 3 round got over at 2:30pm, post which I was expecting a shortlist. We
thought that the last round would just be a check on the culture fit, however, this
round turned out to be the most difficult. It started at 6pm & went on till 10pm. I
was interviewed by the Director, Associate Director & Manager of KPMG. I was
the first one to be interviewed again. The Director asked me about the subjects I
had studied in sem 5 & 6. I named them & after that he started asking me
questions on one of the subjects, CCN. Some questions were actually on topics
that weren't taught to us. I answered what all I could, but for some I did say, "I am
sorry Sir, I am unaware  of this". I honestly felt like the interview had slipped out
of my hand. However, I picked up again once they started asking me questions on
my project & extra curricular activities. The project I had mentioned on my
resume was on Data Analytics so I was asked a few questions on that. Then
looking at the mention of my extra curricular activities in Entrepreneurship, I was
asked why I wanted to join KPMG & not become an Entrepreneur. I was also
asked to mention 3 traits of an Entrepreneur. Post which I was asked some
situational questions that were about  team work & ethics. I was also asked where
I see myself in the next 5 years. This second half of my interview went really well
& I was very well prepared to answer questions based on my resume & situations.
However, a lot of cross questioning took place in this round.
After my round was done, I realized that others were also quizzed on their
subjects as well & most couldn't answer. Some were also asked questions like
explain the mechanism behind the landing of Chandrayan, etc.
A common conclusion we drew from this that they purposely wanted to put us in
uncomfortable situations & check how we still manage to take things forward.
After this round, 7 students were finally selected for this role.

Tips & Facts:

#About KPMG's process:

1. I personally loved how KPMG conducted the whole process not because I got

placed, but because it was extremely fair, giving an equal chance to everyone. Not
to name any other firms, but what a lot of them did was that they conducted
round 1 of the first few people & immediately sent them for subsequent rounds,
while others were still waiting for their first round to start. With KPMG, they let a
round finish for all candidates at once, got into a room, discussed & then gave the
shortlist for the next round. This resulted in them waiting until 11pm in the
college, but they put an effort into giving an equal & fair opportunity to all
candidates. This literally speaks volumes about the ethics of a firm.

2. The harsh truth is that at the end, people who got selected at KPMG were the

once that demonstrated great communication skills & had a strong extra caricular
profile. Their job role eventually also revolves around that. Things like your
branch, CGPA, techstack, etc didn't matter at all. This firm values people skills like
no other.

#About Placements in general:

1. Aptitude Rounds are honestly very luck based. Most people end up not making

through this round unfortunately, even though they fully fit the job role.

2. For GDs, making relevant points is important. However, speaking up & your

communication & articulation matters more. Most people end up staying quiet
because of the pressure, never do that. Try giving personal examples on the topic.
Also remember the difference between GDs & Debates. Be as polite & as humble
as you can.

3. Most interviews are based on your resume & resume alone. Hence do not

mention anything in your resume that you aren't confident about. It's okay if your
resume doesn't have high level projects. But make sure that whichever you are
mentioning, you should be able to explain them & handle questions on them.
Same goes for any PORs/courses etc.

4. Our batch is getting placed at a very weird time. The non tech opportunities we

saw our seniors getting, half of them didn't turn up. Honestly, you shouldn't look
at the previous year's statistics & consider that you will get the same
opportunities. It can be better for your turn (I hope so) or even worse. You can't
predict such things. Look at every opportunity as your last & give your best.

5. Preparation for non tech especially actually starts from your first year itself.

You need to build a profile throughout the 3 years that adds a lot of talking points
in your interview besides your projects & subjects because that is something that
they'll find in every candidate's resume. What they will not find in everyone's
resume are leadership skills, participation in National level competitions, etc.
Being an active participant in things on an around you is very important in my
opinion for non tech profiles atleast.

6. You are reading my interview experience today for KPMG because I was lucky

that the interview went smooth. By this I mean, in most cases, you have same
skills that a certain other candidate also possesses. However, you still don't make
it & other candidate does because he got an easy interviewer who did not grill a
lot while your interview panelist was the opposite & you were asked a lot of tricky
questions that maybe the candidate who got selected also wouldn't know. These
things do happen. It's a lot based on your luck. However, I would recommend you
to also talk to the people who did not get selected to know what went wrong in
their interview so you also know what to avoid, if that thing is in your control.

Prepare as much as you can. Rejections happen, but in the long run, you'll know
that it's for the better good. Godspeed!

• I know this might sound cliche but do not ever think that you cannot achieve something,

self doubt kills. I lost my hope to get into DB when a month prior to placement I got the
mail that I was selected for JPMC CFG and focused primarily on web development. So
when my CFG actually got over on July 9 I had minimal days to revise my DSA concepts
as we got the news that DB was visiting the campus on July 15. I did not have the hope
that I could even clear the first round because I thought my peers were very well
prepared. But on that day I could solve 2 questions which gave me confidence that I
might get selected for the interview.

• Get your DSA skills strong. Practice questions on leetcode, gfg, codeforces anything you

like but start preparing way before the placements, in fact start doing dsa and cp from 2nd
year itself. Solving questions in the coding round requires practice which cannot be
gained overnight. I personally started doing leetcode and strivers sheet from my second
year which helped me clear the first round even if I did not do intensively 1 month before
my placements.

• Do CCN, OOPS, Java core concepts(if you have java mentioned), CCN, OS, DBMS,

SQL (Be well prepared even before the placement season starts as you may never know
when you will get selected for the interview. I had to prepare in just 5 days because I did
not have time for core subjects during june month

• Standard DSA questions are asked in the interview, start by giving the brute force and

then move to the optimal solution, this will give you time to formulate your thoughts and
give the solution with clarity.

• Do practice puzzles DB likes to ask them. Search top 20 puzzles on gig.

• Be well versed with your resume (projects and internship if any). You should know what

you have written and don't mention technologies or skills for making your resume rich.
Be honest.
--- PAGE 4 ---

• You have done an internship or not, your peers' resume looks much better- do not think

anything of that sort. I myself don't have an internship. As a fresher no one expects a lot
of things on your resume.

• Research in depth about the company- values, ethics, what services it provides, their

CEO, you should be able to answer anything. Ask questions at the end of every interview
(go only with the usual ones if you cannot think of any!).

• An interview is just like a discussion between two people and how better you can sell

yourself. Try connecting your strong points(hackathons, coding, web development) when
a question is asked and highlight them as much as possible.

• For the questions that you may not know the answer to, tell the interviewer that you do

not know this topic. It is better to say this rather than beating around the bush and giving
an unsatisfactory answer. Do not let such questions affect the rest of the interview.

There was one coding round and 4 interview rounds conducted. The coding round was conducted
on July 15, 2023 and the interview rounds were conducted on 26 July, 2023. The whole process
was going to be offline but only the coding round was conducted offline and the offline
interviews which were scheduled to be conducted on 20 july were postponed due to rains and the
interviews were then conducted online on 26 july.

1. Coding Round (90 mins)

The coding round was conducted on hackerearth platform. We had to go to the college to
give the test. There were 3 coding questions of 20,50,50 marks. They were two pointers,
priority queue, dp respectively. The test's duration was 90 minutes. I solved 20 marks and
one 50 marks question. 26 students were selected for interviews. But 6 students got placed
elsewhere hence got out of the interviews.

2. Technical Interview 1 (45 mins)

The interview started with the interviewer's favorite question, "Introduce yourself." The
interviewer reviewed my resume and asked about my achievements and projects. Next he
wanted to see one of the projects mentioned on my resume which was a Django project and
asked me to open the website and also told me to explain the code in the vs code. After this,
he moved on to data structures and asked me which data structures I knew about. Difference
between arrays and linked lists. What are the different sorting algorithms you know? Which
is the best among them? The best average and worst time complexity of insertion sort. What
is the requirement of binary search? What are the different layers in the OSI model? What is
the difference between router and switch? He moved on to DBMS and asked me SQL
queries. Moved on to oops concepts- difference between abstraction and encapsulation.
Difference between java overriding and overloading. Is overriding static polymorphism?
What are the different access modifiers in java? Furthermore, he asked about the various
--- PAGE 2 ---
access modifiers in Java and whether a private class can be inherited, and if so, which access
modifiers are allowed for the child class. The interviewer then wanted to move on to actual
coding- so I have an array with positive and negative numbers in it and you have to pair up
positive numbers from it such that when you add them up then the corresponding negative
number should be present in the array. The interviewer was impressed with my reasoning and
quick responses and decided to end the interview here. I then asked him a couple of
questions.
18 students were selected from 20 students.

3. Technical Interview 2 (45 mins)

The interview started with the usual "introduce yourself." The interviewer asked about my
two favorite projects from the resume, and we had a good discussion about them. Then, he
asked about the Code for Good hackathon and wanted an explanation about it. Moving on to
coding questions, he asked about Huffman coding, to which I honestly admitted that I didn't
know the algorithm. He then asked about minimum spanning trees and explained Kruskal's
algorithm. Next, he asked me to find the middle element in a linked list. He then gave me
some questions to solve in my IDE. One of which was→ Consider a circular array and find a
subarray of size k with maximum. In the DBMS section, he asked about different
normalization forms and asked about serializable schedules. He then asked me questions on
java and oops concepts. How can we achieve abstraction? What is interface and abstract
classes, state the differences. Can an interface be private? Or any of its methods? Difference
between static and final keywords? Can static methods be overridden? The interviewer
presented a puzzle involving three switches and three bulbs, which is a famous one from
GFG.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-7-3-bulbs-and-3-switches/
Now he had no further questions for me as I had answered everything. He asked me if I knew
about guesstimates. I acknowledged that I was aware of them but unsure about how to
approach them. He proceeded to give me a question, asking me to determine the number of
cars in the evening in Andheri. I attempted to approach it, but unfortunately, I couldn't figure
it out so he guided me on how to approach it. Towards the end, he asked if I had any
questions, and I asked a few. Around 13 students were selected for the profit round.

4. Professional fitness round (30 minutes)

The interviewer directly asked situational and behavioral questions. For example, how would
I react if a project I worked on had issues with the model, and everyone blamed me? If the
issue escalated to the manager, how would I handle it? If you are put into a team which has a
completely different tech stack what will you do? If for this reason your team lacks behind
because you were taking time to complete it how will you take responsibility for it? If a
member of your team now complains about it how will you react? etc. They also asked about
--- PAGE 3 ---
my strengths and why I wanted to join Deutsche Bank. They inquired if I would reject an
offer from another banking company for DB. Finally, they asked if I had any questions. In the
end, 10 students were selected for the HR round.

5. Hr round (30 minutes)

This was a standard HR Round. Tell me something about yourself? Minimal questions were
asked on DB Values and ethics. What is the biggest challenge you faced till now? Gave me
situational questions on how you would handle the situation if your team contains lazy
people who are not contributing to the project. Now your manager is upset with all of you.
How will you handle it? This went pretty well so he decided to end it and asked me if I had
any questions?
Verdict: Selected :) All 10 students were selected

journey.howSecured:
The entire process consisted of five rounds spanning over a period of 1-2 weeks .

Rounds Date
Digital Interview 26 - 28 July
Technical Test 5th August
Group Discussion 7th AugustPersonal Interview
Leadership Interview

1. Digital Interview

It was a 15-minute Digital Interview on HireVue, with 6 basic HR questions about my background, choiceof Btech, weaknesses, internship expectations, and more. You have to record your answers and submitthem. The emphasis was on genuine responses, avoiding plagiarism and AI tools. After review by the HRteam, 107 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Technical TestThe next round was a Technical Test. It consisted of a 30-minute MCQ test on Microsoft Forms, focusingon Computer Science fundamentals and aptitude. The questions were centered around DBMS, DSA(Trees ,Graphs, sorting algorithms) , code snippets as well as quantitative aptitude. The difficulty levelranged from easy to medium. 70 students were shortlisted for the next round, which was the GroupDiscussion.

3. Group DiscussionGroup discussion was conducted virtually on microsoft teams but in college. Each group consisted ofaround 10 participants . Different topics were assigned to different groups . My group was assigned witha topic 'Generative AI'. 2 minutes were given to think about the topic and 10 minutes were given for the

discussion. Approximately 3 Students per group were selected for the next round i.e. personal interview. Total 28 students qualified for the personal interview.

4. Personal interviewThere were two interviewers. The opening question was "Tell me about yourself." I provided a briefintroduction, after which they proceeded to inquire about details from my resume. They began by askingabout each of the projects listed on my resume. I had four projects in total: one centered around theMERN Stack, another involving vanilla JavaScript, a third one implemented using JAVA and MYSQL, andthe final project being related to IoT .Ensure you have a thorough understanding of your resume beforeattending an interview as questions can cover a wide range of topics related to your resume.

Regarding the MERN project, I was asked about the authentication flow, JWT tokens, and the format ofJWT. They also asked about Firebase, which was part of my IoT project. A few students were asked towrite a code for reversing a linked list.
Next, they tested my knowledge of CCN (OSI layers), OS (linux commands) . During my introduction, Imentioned that Java is my primary programming language, hence they asked me to rate my Javaproficiency on a scale of 1 to 10 (answering between 8 and 8.5 is a good response for such questions). They also posed several questions on Object-Oriented Programming (OOPS), including questions aboutconstructors, their purpose, abstract classes, abstract methods, difference between interfaces andabstract classes.
In addition to technical questions, they also asked a few HR questions in between like strengths andweaknesses, why I want this job ? and questions related to teamwork. They also asked me about what Iknow about Baker Hughes . It's important to be prepared for questions about the company's values asthey do ask about them. Cracking this interview is easy if you are familiar with every small thing writtenon your resume. I passed this interview and reached the final round.

4. Leadership InterviewThis was essentially an HR round with a few technical questions. It was conducted with the SeniorDirector. The interviewer asked about my GD topic and my perspectives on it. As the topic was'Generative AI', she also questioned me about the various types of AI tools I am familiar with. Additionally, she presented a situation-based scenario and asked for my input and suggestions. Thetechnical questions were based on my resume. I was questioned about DBMS and database tools. Furthermore, she asked me about how communication takes place between two computers, to which Iexplained using the OSI model.

Afterward, she asked if I had any questions. It's important to ask at least one question at this stage. Ichose to ask about the types of roles I would be involved in. Confidence is key, so remember to maintaina smile on your face. Roughly 10-12 students made it to this round, and out of them, 8 students wereselected for the internship.
Few Tips :

● The placement process can be stressful, but it's important to maintain a positive attitude. Remember that everyone eventually secures a placement. Just be patient and have faith thatyou'll achieve what's destined for you. Before Baker Hughes, I hadn't been shortlisted for anyinterviews in the initial 10-12 companies. The Baker Hughes interview was my first one. So,always be prepared for every opportunity.

● Luck plays a very important role so work hard and wait for your chance.

● For the technical test, brush up your cs fundamentals. Practice coding (on leetcode) andaptitude (from indiabix, prepinsta). If you are an EXTC student ,make the most of Open Electivesubjects like DSA, DBMS, and DA .

● During a group discussion, make an effort to initiate and conclude the discussion. If you aren'tgiven the chance to start, ensure to present your points as early as you can. Don't wait forsomeone else to offer you the opportunity to speak, as that might not happen. If you remainsilent, it's over for you . Even if you contribute just two-three meaningful points, it can make adifference.

● For personal interviews, maintain confidence. Don't lie on your resume. Having knowledge of allpoints mentioned on your resume will help you clear the personal interview more easily. If youdon't remember anything , don't panic , the interviewer will help you to recall.

● Follow all the instructions given by the company and TPO. For any questions feel free to contactme on my LinkedIn : Shashank Jagtap

All the best !

Then she asked me how will you send an output generated by a java program to MySQL database. I

guess). A DSA question was asked, Given a sorted array, give the first and last occurrence of a
number.
Any questions for the interviewer. With this the round got over.

Round 2 - Technical Interview (30 to 40 mins)

What programming language do you use. What is a linked list. Show me the internal implementation

OOPS questions were asked. Method overloading vs overriding. Then a puzzle was asked. Don't

Round 3 - HR round

Pretty chill round. Questions like strengths and weaknesses. Family background. How were the
previous 2 interviews. Do you know about the company? Full form of company. Situational questions
like if one of the teammates does not perform well, what will u do? Be honest and confident.

journey.prep:
You don't need to solve all questions to get shortlisted. So, read all questions properly and

then focus on the ones which you are sure you can do.

Technical Interview - Round 1 (15 Shortlisted):

Introduce yourself.
Question 1: Initial capital, max number of projects which can be done, arrays of capital required
by each project and profit generated by each project. Find maximum money possible.
Approach:

• Sort all projects according to capital required (Store capital[index] and index for every

project)

• Declare a Priority Queue -> Comparator : profit[i] - capital[i] -> (Descending order)

• Run a for loop: 0 to k-1

• Add all feasible projects (capital required < current capital) to a Priority Queue

only if profit [1] > capital[1]

• Pop the top and add it to answer.

• Time Complexity: O(nlogn + k)

• Space Complexity: O(n)

Question 2: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncrossed-lines/
I gave a DP solution after a Recursive solution. Then, I wrote the whole code on paper.
I could easily solve both questions. Initially, I was not sure whether I had to maximize the net
capital or the obtained profit so, I clarified it before approaching the solution. Almost everyone
who could solve all questions (2 or 3) asked to them were shortlisted for the next round. This
round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Understand the question properly, clarify the constraints, discuss approach (My interviewer

expected me to speak out what I was thinking and how I was approaching the problem), dry run,
write code.
--- PAGE 3 ---

Technical Interview - Round 2 (9 Shortlisted):

General Questions like hobbies, goals, aspirations to start the conversation.
Question 1: A matrix of numbers is given. From each cell, you can jump to any cell in the same
row or in the same column which is strictly greater than the current number. Find the longest
possible path.
Approach:

• Sort all cell values in descending order (Store x and y coordinates for each cell)

• Initialize a rows[r] and cols[c] array to store the max path in each row and column

respectively

• Traverse through the sorted list

• For each element, check max path available, add 1 to it and update the same in

rows and cols arrays

• Time Complexity: O(n*m*log(n*m))

• Space Complexity: O(n*m)

I gave a On*m*(ntm)) solution and then came up with the optimal solution after a hint. I wrote
the whole code after explaining the approach.
Question 2: Solve a Sudoku
An obvious solution would be Backtracking. However, the interviewer asked for a better
solution. He insisted on thinking about maybe a new data structure.
He was simply looking for how you approach such problems. No code was expected, it was only
a discussion. This round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Explain what you are thinking. Sometimes, they are just looking for how you approach a

problem. Be very patient while explaining your approach. They might try to confuse you to
check how confident you are about your approach. The best thing to do is to take a test case and
dry run.
Hiring Manager - Round 3(6 Shortlisted):
(No DSA, purely Resume-based, behavioral, and abstract problem solving round)
Started with how the test was and the previous interviews. Then he started asking questions on
my projects.

1. What, Why and How was the project built? Your contribution (for group projects), Did

the project serve the purpose? What more could have been done?

2. Why this field / role ?

--- PAGE 4 ---

3. Frontend or Backend? Why is that? > Backend -> He had mentioned about the difficulty

of handling multiple services at the backend in the PPT. So what do you think is difficult
in the backend?

4. App used frequently - Instagram - Explain how only the stories of the people you follow

are shown to you from millions of stories. Explain how the story bar is designed. How are
advertisements added to it?

5. On basis of my previous answers, I was asked whether I would build a startup in Finance

or Tech if was provided with the required money
This round started with explaining each and every detail written on the Resume. The interviewer
will ask follow up questions based on your answers. Your overall understanding of your projects,
passion for technology, future goals, how you approach unseen problems, how you deal with
counter opinions is tested throughout the interview. This round lasted for more than an hour.

Tips: Structure your answer and then speak, prepare technical as well as business aspects of your

projects. Be Very Honest during the interview. Do NOT lie on your resume.
> 4 candidates received offers (3 - I+FTE and 1 - I)
Be ready with good questions for the interviewers. They spend a considerable time answering
them. I do believe they value the intent and interest shown through the questions.
Stay Calm, Give your best and Enjoy the Process. Best Of Luck!
(Feel free to contact me in case of any queries)

Time: 1hr 30mins

1. Given: Box of characters, Two names. Find maximum length of name combination that

can be formed without reusing any character from the box.
Approach:

• Find Frequency of characters in the box, in the name_1 and the name 2

• Run a loop where i is the number of times the name_1 can be taken from the box.

For every i, find the maximum number of times (val) the name 2 can be taken.
Length = i*name_1 + val*name_ 2. Check for the maximum value of Length.

• Time Complexity: O(n)

2. Robber at root vertex. Banks at terminal nodes. Police stations at nodes indicated by

another array. Robbers cannot go on a path with m consecutive police stations. Find
number of banks the robber can rob
Approach: DFS

3. Multiple Islands given, Flights Routes between islands with profit on each route given.

Max number of routes allowed for each island is given, Find max profit.
Approach: Sort all routes according to profit. Take a route only if it is feasible.

4. I don't remember the question. It was something like a number of employees connected

over a network. Multiple queries given, take min/ max distance for each query where
distance is shortest path between any two connections.
--- PAGE 2 ---
I could solve the first question completely and the second and third partially. I was rushing
through the questions to pass as many test cases as possible. Because of this, even though I had
reached the solution of the first question within 10 minutes, I made many silly errors and was
able to pass all test cases after spending a lot of time. Because of this, I could not focus on other
questions. Many peeps did not read the easier question and wasted their time attempting to solve
the harder questions.

Tips: You don't need to solve all questions to get shortlisted. So, read all questions properly and

then focus on the ones which you are sure you can do.

Technical Interview - Round 1 (15 Shortlisted):

Introduce yourself.
Question 1: Initial capital, max number of projects which can be done, arrays of capital required
by each project and profit generated by each project. Find maximum money possible.
Approach:

• Sort all projects according to capital required (Store capital[index] and index for every

project)

• Declare a Priority Queue -> Comparator : profit[i] - capital[i] -> (Descending order)

• Run a for loop: 0 to k-1

• Add all feasible projects (capital required < current capital) to a Priority Queue

only if profit [1] > capital[1]

• Pop the top and add it to answer.

• Time Complexity: O(nlogn + k)

• Space Complexity: O(n)

Question 2: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncrossed-lines/
I gave a DP solution after a Recursive solution. Then, I wrote the whole code on paper.
I could easily solve both questions. Initially, I was not sure whether I had to maximize the net
capital or the obtained profit so, I clarified it before approaching the solution. Almost everyone
who could solve all questions (2 or 3) asked to them were shortlisted for the next round. This
round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Understand the question properly, clarify the constraints, discuss approach (My interviewer

expected me to speak out what I was thinking and how I was approaching the problem), dry run,
write code.
--- PAGE 3 ---

Technical Interview - Round 2 (9 Shortlisted):

General Questions like hobbies, goals, aspirations to start the conversation.
Question 1: A matrix of numbers is given. From each cell, you can jump to any cell in the same
row or in the same column which is strictly greater than the current number. Find the longest
possible path.
Approach:

• Sort all cell values in descending order (Store x and y coordinates for each cell)

• Initialize a rows[r] and cols[c] array to store the max path in each row and column

respectively

• Traverse through the sorted list

• For each element, check max path available, add 1 to it and update the same in

rows and cols arrays

• Time Complexity: O(n*m*log(n*m))

• Space Complexity: O(n*m)

I gave a On*m*(ntm)) solution and then came up with the optimal solution after a hint. I wrote
the whole code after explaining the approach.
Question 2: Solve a Sudoku
An obvious solution would be Backtracking. However, the interviewer asked for a better
solution. He insisted on thinking about maybe a new data structure.
He was simply looking for how you approach such problems. No code was expected, it was only
a discussion. This round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Explain what you are thinking. Sometimes, they are just looking for how you approach a

problem. Be very patient while explaining your approach. They might try to confuse you to
check how confident you are about your approach. The best thing to do is to take a test case and
dry run.
Hiring Manager - Round 3(6 Shortlisted):
(No DSA, purely Resume-based, behavioral, and abstract problem solving round)
Started with how the test was and the previous interviews. Then he started asking questions on
my projects.

1. What, Why and How was the project built? Your contribution (for group projects), Did

the project serve the purpose? What more could have been done?

2. Why this field / role ?

--- PAGE 4 ---

3. Frontend or Backend? Why is that? > Backend -> He had mentioned about the difficulty

of handling multiple services at the backend in the PPT. So what do you think is difficult
in the backend?

4. App used frequently - Instagram - Explain how only the stories of the people you follow

are shown to you from millions of stories. Explain how the story bar is designed. How are
advertisements added to it?

5. On basis of my previous answers, I was asked whether I would build a startup in Finance

or Tech if was provided with the required money
This round started with explaining each and every detail written on the Resume. The interviewer
will ask follow up questions based on your answers. Your overall understanding of your projects,
passion for technology, future goals, how you approach unseen problems, how you deal with
counter opinions is tested throughout the interview. This round lasted for more than an hour.

Tips: Structure your answer and then speak, prepare technical as well as business aspects of your

projects. Be Very Honest during the interview. Do NOT lie on your resume.
> 4 candidates received offers (3 - I+FTE and 1 - I)
Be ready with good questions for the interviewers. They spend a considerable time answering
them. I do believe they value the intent and interest shown through the questions.
Stay Calm, Give your best and Enjoy the Process. Best Of Luck!
(Feel free to contact me in case of any queries)

1. Aptitude Round

2. Group Discussion

3. Technical + HR Round 1 (Interview with Technical Head + HR manager)

4. Technical + HR Round 2 (Interview with KPMG's Director and Partner)

Round 1: Aptitude Round (55 mins)

The assessment was conducted in online mode on HirePro platform. There were 45 Questions in total which were
split into 15 questions per sections which included Analytical Reasoning, Quantitative, Verbal Ability. There was
no time limit per section. Overall, I found the questions to be of medium difficulty level.
After this round, 54 candidates were shortlisted.
I would recommend the following playlist for the Quantitative aptitude section as many folks find it to be tricky.
Link- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnc9ojITRg4&list=PLpyc33gOcbV A4qXMoQ5vmhefTruk5t9lt
There are many questions available on Indiabix for practice. I also referred RS Agarwal book.

Round 2: Group Discussion (2 mins ideation time + 10 mins GD + 1 min to conclude)

We were divided into panels of 8 -10 candidates. My panel had all the good speakers and hence everyone was
skeptical about making through this round. Our topic was "Role of Media in Society". We were given 2 m ins
time for articulating our thoughts so as it was a very common topic I quickly jotted down the points on paper. As
media encompasses a lot of sectors and every individual uses it differently so I kind of mentioned about it. I also
mentioned how media can be regulated so that it doesn't negatively impact the society and also about the positive
side of it. I made sure that I support my points with valid real -life examples and statistics (for eg. I mentioned
about Twitter and how it overcame the issue of fa ke profiles.) As GD is not just about communication, its also
about listening to the fellow panelist s and acknowledging them. After 10 mins of healthy GD, we were given 1
min per panelist to conclude wherein we were expected to of  course give a conclusion and mention whether we
were for or against the particular topic.
After this round, in all 32 students made it to the next round. From my panel 5 candidates were shortlisted.
Few tips from my side:

1. Make sure you participate in mock GDs conducted by the training team of TPO before the placement

season as it will give you an experience and also the realization of your weak points based on the feedback
of the GD evaluator and self-introspection. More you will participate better you will get at it. As reading
books and communication was an integral part of my day-to-day life and my experience of heading couple
of student organizations parallelly helped to ace this round.

2. In GD, communication skills definitely matter no doubts but it should be backed with valid points and

wholesome perspective on the given topic. If you have less understanding about the topic so just maintain
your calm and listen to few points of your panelists and try to come up with something rather by staying
quiet.

3. Most of the folks just focus on putting their points but not on listening and maintaining a positive body

language and they incur demerits. Most of the time you will be listening and just don't get into a debate.
Be polite and maintain the decorum.

4. If you have any doubts related to the given topic, make sure you ask the evaluator regarding the same and

then start off with ideation.

Round 3: Technical + HR Round 1 (20 mins approx)

This round was completely resume based. They asked me to give a brief introduction about myself after which I
was asked to explain my projects one by one. I made sure that I maintain a proper flow while explaining my
projects. The flow is as follows:

• Introduction + Motivation behind the specific project

• Need and practical implementation

• Explanation of the tech stack used with proper reasoning. (I prefer to use pen and paper in order explain

the project with the help of block diagrams, ER diagrams wherever required.)

• Explanation of the output in great detail by mentioning all the features and functions.

• Any additional features you can add to improvise the project basically the future scope.

Interviewer seemed impressed by the explanation but he did ask me some follow up questions in between my
explanation. He was more oriented towards cloud computing. He asked me basic  questions related to AWS and
also the pandas as well as pytesseract library of python which I used for OCR. He then took interest in data
visualization and asked me about how did I go about making dashboards and further he gave me some random
real-life situations and asked me to provide the technical implementation details with overall time frames. As two
of my projects revolved around data engineering it definitely gave me a slight edge I feel.
After this the HR person stepped in and she asked me to she d some light on my contributions in TPO and
Entrepreneurship Cell. As I was parallelly heading three student bodies so she  also asked about my motivation
behind being this active and taking various initiatives in the college and also  couple of questions on  time
management. She also asked me on why did I apply for this role? Couple of questions on KPMG and this marked
the end of the interview. I knew that I had aced this round as well.
After this round, around 19 candidates made it to the next round.

Round 4: Technical + HR round 2 (1-hour approx)

This round was taken by the director and partner of KPMG. This was unlike the standard HR round where  I
wasn't asked very basic and standard questions  but they focused more upon my exposure towards business and
entrepreneurship and whether I could deploy and use my technical as well soft skills in order to cater the client's
requirements. They started off with appreciating my overall resume, they asked me that why am I not starting up
my own venture considering the kind of network  and relevant exposure in entrepreneurship  that I had . They
conveyed that they were 99% convinced that I would drop this offer for my future startup  and my task was to
convince them that I won't do that. So, I mentioned about our placement policy, SPTBI as well as how I can use
my entrepreneurial mindset and business exposure for KPMG. After few exchanges on the similar lines, they
moved on to cloud and gave me a situation where a client wants to use AWS but wants to spend minimal amount
on it, so which services will be my recommendation  followed by an explanation of the entire architecture using
those services with an estimate amount for the entire setup.  There was also a question on why  AWS is the most
preferred cloud in India?  After this they asked me whether I had some plans for higher education and if no then
what's the reason? Obviously, considering the shorter picture I said no and I gave them couple of genuine reasons
to support my decision. But I conveyed that if KPMG gives me an opportunity for higher study, I will definitely
consider and if not then I will prefer distance learning courses over an offline degree  if my future role demands
management expertise. Prepare well for such standard questions beforehand.
Refer this link for standard HR Questions with answers which I had prepared -
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ukWKckgkcs99Ww5S5OI9diirGgHwgP9e/view?usp=sharing
They asked me about New Education Policy and how it can be improvised and put in action. As I prefer to stay
updated with current affairs so this was something I had red  before and given a thought upon so I explained the
policy and my thought process and they were satisfied with it. Then they were open for questions? So, I asked
them about the overall internship structure for us and few  questions on the  different roles and opportunities  as
well.
Finally, 7 candidates were selected for an I+P opportunity at KPMG.

Few points about placements in general:

1. Honestly, the first round is pretty random for all companies as a lot of folks end up solving all the questions

but only a few fortunate ones end up getting shortlisted. So, if you aren't able to clear the first round
definitely keep practicing but don't get demotivated as eventually you will end up getting shortlisted but
till then make sure you are covered with all the topics and equipped with relevant skills in your arsenal.

2. I always focused on overall development and was never biased towards anything . Through my projects

and by solving dsa problems I had gained the necessary technical skills  as well as aptitude  and my
leadership experience came through my positions of responsibilities. I would encourage you guys to also
focus on these two aspects and take part in national level competitions  beforehand, be a part of some
student body which will make your profile wholesome. I had seen that there are lot of folks having
redundant profiles, you got to bring something new to the table. Especially a firm like KPMG expects you
to have that differentiating mindset.

3. Embrace failures and remember that these experiences are  just making you intellect ually as well as

mentally strong for the new chapter of your life that lies ahead of placements. Placement season definitely
made me mentally strong and at the same time it boosted my confidence and made me a lot humbler as
well. You will also notice many positive shifts in your personality. Trust the process, give your best.

I would like to end by highlighting this verse -
He who is satisfied with gain which comes of its own accord, who is free from duality and does not envy, who
is steady in both success and failure, is never entangled, although performing actions.

The entire process was online.

Round 1: Resume Shortlisting

Round 1. Resume Shortlisting: 50+ candidates appeared for this round
I registered on the Superset Portal for the company and submitted my resume. The company shortlisted 10
candidates for the next round, although the criteria for shortlisting were not specified. I assume it was based
on Java proficiency and internship experience. During the registration process, they inquired about any past
internships, with a particular emphasis on the Fintech domain.
Round 2. Online Assessment: 10 candidates appeared for this round
We were required to report to the college at 8:30 am for the online assessment. However, no one from the
company was present for supervision. Instead, TPCs were there to oversee the process. The test comprised
two segments: Quantitative Analysis and Verbal Reasoning.
For Quantitative Analysis, we had 25 minutes to answer 18 questions. These questions involved calculations
related to averages, percentages, ratios, Profit and Loss, and shares, based on the information provided in the
table.
The Verbal Reasoning section had a duration of 19 minutes with 30 questions. All the questions were
centered around comprehension.
Round 3. Online Interview: 3 candidates appeared for this round
I had a Techno HR interview that lasted for 20 minutes, conducted by three panelists - one from HR and the
other two from a technical background. The main aim of this interview was to assess the candidate's
confidence and communication skills. The atmosphere during the interview was relaxed, and an essential tip
--- PAGE 2 ---
is to discuss topics in which you feel confident. Essentially, you are the one steering the interview, and the
panelists are keen on evaluating your authenticity and eagerness to learn. During the interview, it was
emphasized to share details about past internship experiences, which proved to be immensely helpful in
securing the selection. I was the sole candidate selected for the position.

Following the aptitude round, 9 to 10 candidates were selected to proceed to the interview

Tech/Business Round 1:
The interviews were scheduled for 21st July and were divided into tech/business segments.
During the first round, lasting 25 to 30 minutes, the interviewer made me feel comfortable by
asking about my day and where I live. He then introduced himself and requested a brief
introduction from me. He paid close attention to my introduction, asking questions about the
projects I had mentioned. Subsequently, he provided an overview of the role, and the interview
commenced.
--- PAGE 2 ---
In the technical part of the interview, he inquired about one of my previous projects, including its
purpose, tech stack, and discussions on potential improvements. Additionally, he asked about
the application's download metrics and whether I received any negative reviews. Furthermore,
he challenged me to write a Python code for a full-stack application that segregates a given list
of numbers into positive decimal, positive natural, negative decimal, and negative natural
numbers. I successfully implemented the backend code and explained how the frontend could
be built using Flask or Django. The interviewer seemed satisfied with my responses.
Despite coming from an electronics background, he asked me why I was interested in a tech
job. Besides technical questions, he also posed a few inquiries about Tableau and Excel.
Moreover, there were some HR-related questions, such as my opinions on pursuing a master's
degree and current global news. Finally, he offered me the opportunity to ask any questions I
nad.
Following the interviews, three candidates were shortlisted to proceed to the next stage.
Tech/Business Round 2:
In the subsequent round, the interviewer began with a brief introduction, followed by a detailed
review of my resume. The questions primarily focused on Data Structures and Algorithms
(DSA), including differences between arrays and linked lists, real-world uses of stacks, linked
lists, graphs, priority queues, and object-oriented programming (OOP). Additionally, he
presented mental math problems like 67*99 and puzzles such as finding a defective coin among
10 using a weight balance in minimal attempts. He also asked about the angle between the hour
and minute hands of a clock given a specific time (e.g., 12:40). SQL questions were also posed,
particularly about pattern searching.
I answered all questions correctly and felt the interviewer was somewhat different in his
demeanor, as he didn't maintain consistent eye contact. However, I suspected it might have
been a deliberate test.
The process didn't involve further shortlisting, and it concluded with an HR round.

HR Round:

During the HR round, the interviewer introduced herself and requested a self-introduction from
me. She inquired about my interest in JPMC, particularly in the fintech role, and why I chose this
over a purely technical role. Additionally, she asked me about aspects not mentioned in my
resume, my thoughts on pursuing a master's degree, positive aspects of JPMC, and details
about my role as a lead in the Google Developers Students Club. Interestingly, she also asked
about my reasons for not considering working at Google, including whether it was due to Google
not visiting our campus.
**Important Tips**:
--- PAGE 3 ---

1. Stay active and alert during interviews as questions may be repeated, increasing the chance

of encountering familiar queries.

2. Maintain confidence and a positive attitude throughout the interviews, presenting yourself as

a suitable fit for the company.

3. Five minutes before the interview, stop preparing for any specific topic and clear your mind to

avoid potential fumbling.

4. Enhance your communication skills, including speaking, writing, and thinking in English.

Prepare answers for all potential resume and HR questions, maintaining a book to record
questions and their corresponding responses for effective revision.

5. While I was mainly asked technical questions, some of my friends encountered

finance-related inquiries. So stay prepared.

6. It's beneficial to be well-versed in DSA, SQL, and Computer Science fundamentals.

By following these tips and adequately preparing for technical challenges, you can increase
your chances of success in the interview process. Good luck!

journey.prep:
1. While prepping for test try solving leetcode easy and medium questions, and practice daily.

2. While prepping for interviews go through interview bit, javatpoint and gfg for oops, java, ccn,

os etc.

3. For hr questions, p ractice the most asked questions and prepare a struct ure for them, look at

the answers as well and then make yours, don't mug it up but try and have points clear.

4. While giving the test try to first go with the simplest approach that you can think of, sometimes

we think to complex but the question is very straight forward.

5. Try to solve the questions partially at least, because that also gets counted.

6. While giving the interview listen to the question and then give your answer/approach as what

matters is you are thinking, don't sit quietly.

7. Be confident and positive during the interview, if you don't know something say you that you

don't. Do not beat around the bush the interviewers tend to hate that.

8. Be as specific as you can while answering.

9. While making the resume only include the things you know about, do not write it to fill up the

space, mention about you projects in detail. The resume should be single columned and try to
use a simple template.

10. Get in touch with your seniors and ask them to guide you, give mock interviews.

c. Professional Fitness
d. Hr

1.     Coding Test

This round was of 90 minutes on Hacker rank Platform. 3 questions were given with a points
distribution of 20-50-50.

1. The first question was a simple array question. https://leetcode.com/problems/boats-

to-save-people/description/ I solved this by first sorting the array in ascending order
and then using two pointers approach.

2. Second question was a scheduling problem, where a number of counters were given

and array containing in-time of customers, we have to give out time of each customer
when the amount of time taken to process each request was 1 unit. I wasn't able to
figure it out but simple array approach would have been enough to solve it.

3. This was a dp question, where we were give a N*M matrix and each cell consisted of

a price we have to pick only one cell per row and find the total price that is closest to
the given price. I used memorization and solved it by selecting each cell of the row
and finding the one with minimum difference between given price and total price
calculated.
I was able to solve two questions. Solving two questions was enough to get to next round.

2. Technical Round 1

This was the first round. Total 27 students participated in this round. This round was a basic
one for me. First, I was asked to introduce myself, then interviewer asked me basic questions
about Data structures, different types, difference between array- linked list, application of
stack queue. Then he asked me to explain binary search to him as if he is a person who has no
technical knowledge. Then I was asked to name OSI layer models, what is router, basic java
questions, scheduling algorithms, in the end he asked me a coding question, where I had
given an array of elements, and I had to find if there exists an element that is negative of the
sum of any two elements of array. I had to find this for each pair possible from the give array.
First, I explained him brute force approach to loop through then I explained optimized
hashmap approach. Later on, I coded the solution and then I asked him questions about his
recent project and experience. The interview ended in 45 mins. 18 students were selected
after round 1.

3. Technical Round 2

This round was more based on my project and development perspective. The interviewer
asked me to explain the recent project on my resume. Then he moved onto asking ML
questions as the project I explained was based on ML. He asked me about accuracy and what
if it was 100%, answer was that model will overfit, then he asked me to explain the BERT
model as I used it for the project and difference between SVM and BERT, then we had a long
conversation about outliers and how to prevent a model from overfitting. Then he moved on
to asking questions like how data flow works between frontend and backend, how we test
apis, what is MVC architecture, then he asked me what are the responsibilities of a leader,
asked me a situational question if the team is lagging behind the expected schedule and you
can only deliver 8 requirements out of 12 what will you do, I told him my approach, then he
explained agile methodology and how situation should be delt with. Then he asked me if I
have any questions and I asked him a cliché question he said everyone's asking the same, ask
something different I asked he how he will handle a conflict in his team as a leader. This
interview was 1 hour long. Out of 18, 14 were shortlisted.

3. Professional Fitness

This round was more based on the professional point of you . I was first asked to introduce
myself. Then he asked me why computer engineering, who's my role model and why, do you
want to go for further studies, which company or product I like, I told  him how Zomato has
grate UI etc, the how lockdown impacted me, what do I do for fun, and then I asked him about
the recent projects in data a nalytics that DB is working on, this was  a quick 10 mins round.
After this 11 people were shortlisted.

4. HR

This round started with my introduction, then he asked me about my ongoing internship, then
my projects, why db, what are the values that I bel ieve in, my strengths and weaknesses, do I
have passport, voterId then asked me i f any of my family mem ber are a part of db  and at the
end I asked him about the work culture at db and the interview ended in about 20 minutes.

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
1. While prepping for test try solving leetcode easy and medium questions, and practice daily.

2. While prepping for interviews go through interview bit, javatpoint and gfg for oops, java, ccn,

os etc.

3. For hr questions, p ractice the most asked questions and prepare a struct ure for them, look at

the answers as well and then make yours, don't mug it up but try and have points clear.

4. While giving the test try to first go with the simplest approach that you can think of, sometimes

we think to complex but the question is very straight forward.

5. Try to solve the questions partially at least, because that also gets counted.

6. While giving the interview listen to the question and then give your answer/approach as what

matters is you are thinking, don't sit quietly.

7. Be confident and positive during the interview, if you don't know something say you that you

don't. Do not beat around the bush the interviewers tend to hate that.

8. Be as specific as you can while answering.

9. While making the resume only include the things you know about, do not write it to fill up the

space, mention about you projects in detail. The resume should be single columned and try to
use a simple template.

10. Get in touch with your seniors and ask them to guide you, give mock interviews.

1. Coding Round (90 mins)

This round was conducted in college. There were 3 coding questions (20, 50, 50). I solved two
(20, 50) fully and one (50) partially.

2. Technical Interview 1 (45 mins)

This round started with my introduction. He saw my resume and saw my github and asked me to
explain one of my git repos. Next he asked basics, what are data structure, why do we need them
etc, difference between linked list and array (structurally and functionally). He asked a few
questions on linked list (find middle element, delete nth last element) He then asked about
different searching techniques (linear & binary), their time and space complexity, different
sorting algorithms, their complexities.
He next asked about java concepts like polymorphism, overloading, overriding with examples
and access modifiers in java. He asked if private methods can be inherited, he then asked what
can be the access modifiers of overridden methods in child class. I said that child class needs to
have equal or broader access than parent class and not be more restrictive than parent class to
which he asked if I am sure. I said yes and so he asked me to google it later and said he too
would google it.
Then he asked a tweaked version of the famous two sum problem. I gave the brute force
solution, then optimised one with hashset, which he was not satisfied with so I gave another two
pointer optimised approach with the time complexity of all methods. He asked me to code the
pseudo code on my local editor. He was satisfied with my answer. I asked him a few questions
and the interview ended.

3. Technical Interview 2 (1hr)

work in depth.
The interviewer asked about each of my project in depth. My first project used ML so we

my model, could the accuracy be 100%? If yes, how. If no, why not etc. He asked in depth about
the internal working of my second project, the behaviour of my website and about APIS. He also
asked about MVC. He grilled a lot about minute details but also was helpful.
--- PAGE 2 ---
He then asked me DBMS concepts and a few SQL queries. We then discussed databases and case
scenarios when to use which and concepts about different types of databases. He then asked a dsa
question. It was tweak of a leetcode problem
(https://leetcode.com/problems/search-in-rotated-sorted-array/). I gave the brute force solution

solution on my IDE. He was satisfied with my answer.

averted a crisis etc.
I asked him 2 questions about which we discussed for quite some time and the interview ended
on a very positive note.

convincing answer. For example - apart from monetary compensation, a company provides
experience and growth which at DB would be more fruitful than at some other company. Never

1. Aptitude Test

2. Pre - Placement Talk

3. Interview Rounds

a. Technical Round 1
b. Technical Round 2 + HR

1.     Aptitude Test  [229 students (174 BTech + 55 MCA) appeared for this round]

This was an online aptitude test conducted on MeritTrac's Online Assessment Engine - PARIKSHA. The test
comprised of 60 questions, with 20 questions each in the verbal, analytical, and quantitative sections, with no
negative marking. The time limit was  60 minutes so timing is the key here. There was a cutoff for this test
which was not known to us.
38 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Pre-Placement Talk

This round was supposed to start at 9:30 am , but due to some delay it  got deferred to around 10 am. We
were briefed about the company,  including its values, various programs, and significant milestones. In the
end, we were given the opportunity to ask questions. Make sure to ask questions (good ones) to get noticed.

3. Technical Round 1 (30 - 35 minutes)

My interview was scheduled at 10:30 am, but again it got delayed and began around 11 am. This round
was entirely resume based. The interviewer  did not ask for my intro and directly started by asking my
branch and whether we had any CS related subjects in our curriculum to which I replied that we had them
in our open electives/minor course in CS which I had pursued. Then, he asked me about the extra-curricular
activities section in my resume, what I did during my volunteering experience etc. Then he came to the

projects section, and asked me in -depth questions about one of my projects, which was essentially a
desktop-based application using Java and MySQL. He gave me a pen and paper and told me to draw a
basic UI of the entire process to check my basic understanding of the project. Then he asked me some
situation-based questions on my project like how would your app handle the situation if the user tries to
write special characters in the name section. After that, he gave me some workplace -based situations,
which were: what if your manager tells you to work on a particular topic, and he asks your colleague to
work on the same topic too, h ow would you approach this situation. The second question was, what if
there is a particular topic on which your idea clashes with your manager's idea, what would you do in this
case. These questions were basically to check my collaboration skills and how well I can work with others.
In the end, he asked me if I had questions for him to which I asked him 2 questions. I wasn't asked any
tech questions in this round, but few others were asked some questions on data structures, SQL, puzzles
etc, it depends from panelist to panelist (there were about 10 of them).

15 students got shortlisted for the next round, and 13 were waitlisted.  The waitlisted candidates were
called for an additional review round out of which 3 students moved to the final round (not sure what was
asked in the review round). Finally, 18 students moved to the final round.

3. Technical Round 2 + HR ( 45 - 50 minutes)

Ideally there was supposed to be a separate HR round, but due to the time crunch, it was merged into 1
single round. My turn came at around 3 pm. This time, I was being interviewed by a panel of 3 including
the Vice President, and 1 member each from the HR and Tech teams. The interview began by a basic "Tell
me about yourself" question. Be careful of what you mention in your int ro as questions are asked on the
basis of that. Then the interviewer asked me some in-depth questions on SQL AND DBMS like what it is,
What are analytical functions, write an SQL query to print the salaries whose frequency is >5 in the
database and whether a group by clause would be relevant in this case. Then he drew a table on a paper
and asked me the output if right outer join or inner join was applied.  After that, he asked me about the
various ways to delete( drop, truncate, delete ), their definition, which is faster, and whether we can "undo"
the truncate command.
After that he came to the projects section, surprisingly the panel started asking about one of the electronics
project which I had mentioned  (I wasn't expecting it) , they wanted to know the b asic overview, our
approach, and since I had mentioned that we were filing a patent for our project, they were curious to know
the entire process, the novelty, whether any such product was already present in the market, future scope,
etc. Then, I was asked again about the Java project, about the techstack and database used, where is OOPS
being implemented in my code,  and then they asked me to explain a bit about what was going on in the
backend, and 1 situation-based question. He asked me whether this project would work on Linux, to which
I replied yes as Java is a platform -independent language. He then asked the reason behind it, I told him
that it is because of JVM, then he asked me to draw a diagram showing the relationship between the 3
components of th e Java architec ture.  After that, he asked me my approach to a basic data structures
problem(https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-anagram/description/) .
In the end, I was asked a HR question as to why I want to work with Nomura. After that, the VP asked me
if I had any questions for him to which I asked him a question and a follow -up question based on his
answer.

I was able to answer almost all of the questions, but I was unsure whether I would get selected or not as it
was my first offline interview. Finally, the results were announced at 6 pm, and 11 students (10 B Tech +
1 MCA) were selected and I was one of them.
