journey.howSecured:
1. Digital Interview (26 - 31 July)

2. Technical Test (5 August)

3. Group Discussion (7 August, 8:30 - 9:30 AM)

4. Personal Interview (7 August, 10:30 AM onwards)

5. Leadership Interview (7 August)

1.
DI - Digital Interview (Online) - All the applied students appeared for this round
This round was conducted using the Hire Vue Digital Interview platform. You will be given a set number of
questions to answer within a time limit. You will be given a limited amount of time (in out case 30s-1min) to
prepare and formulate your answer and around 3 min to present your answer. It was completely online and
you can give it anytime suitable for you within the deadline mentioned.
A link will be mailed to you with the redirect to the Hire Vue website and further instructions will be provided
accordingly. In our case, the following were the questions:

1. Why did you choose this degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

--- PAGE 2 ---
This round tested our communication skills, our fluency, and our honesty. Make sure you read a few tips and
research about the interviews given on such platforms before giving your interview. Putting down some of
the resources that I referred to before my Digital Interview.
Pre-Recorded Interview Tips:

1. Dress Professionally

2. Wear headphones and Mic

3. Make sure no background noises or distractions

4. Speak Clearly and Concisely, and Avoid rushing

5. Smile, be positive, look interested, and maintain good body posture

6. Look into the WebCam, not the Screen. You can also blur your video if you are uncomfortable.

7. Prepare answers to the most common questions

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cl9- xVQ800
Note: Do not use ChatGPT, any AI tool, or even read any scripted answers (You can refer some model
answers and use STAR type of methodologies, but make sure it's unique to you and not any generalized
answer). These all recorded interviews are scanned individually and manually by the hiring team. During our
time, such students were immediately rejected and reported to the TPO. So, make sure you BE HONEST,
CONFIDENT, and TRUTHFUL. They volue this the most!

2. Technical Test - Around 100 candidates were shortlisted for this round

The technical exam was conducted using the Microsoft Forms platform. It included 25 MCQs about DSA,
the time complexity of provided code snippets, several aptitude questions (basic), SQL, relational schema,
and a few questions about AI/ML and sorting algorithms. 71 students were chosen for further consideration
after this.
Tips for this round:

1. Practice some basic question types related to Aptitude questions from Indiabix or GFG.

2. Revise all sorting algorithms, their time complexities, and comparisons.

3. Study all data structures and algorithms clearly and try to take some quizzes or practice tests related to

their MCQS.

4. Understand how to calculate the time complexity of a given code snippet and practice it.

--- PAGE 3 ---

3. Group Discussion - 71 students appeared for this round

In this round, all 71 students were divided into groups of 10 each, and a GD panel was assigned. It was
scheduled for early morning 7:30 am. Each group was allotted rooms to sit and proceed with the GD. Our
group was the first panel and it was supposed to start at 8 am. But due to internet connectivity problems and
issues, it began around 8:45 am. Our group topic was - Generative Al: Boon or Bane? We were given 5
minutes for preparation and 10-12 minutes to present the GD.
During the GD, I tried to make a good start but was interrupted, so I gave the other person a chance and
respectfully continued the discussion. I placed one point across in the GD and stressed on the importance of
upskilling and adapting to the AI. Lastly, I made sure that I conclude the GD and gave a brief summary of all
the points that were discussed. I made certain that my delivery was clear and straightforward. My conclusion
was to adequately summarize the important discussion points.
The topics were mostly common ranging from Al, ChatGPT, EV and its evolution and adaptability in India
and its existence, etc. The topics differed somewhat but the central theme was either Al or EV.
After this round, around 4 students from each group were shortlisted.
Tips for GD:

1. Go through the current most hot topics in technology. Refer to the most asked GD questions and

topics through searching. I referred to this link

2. Have a pen and paper ready. As soon as you get the topic, jot down all the points that you can think

about and can talk about in the GD. This will help you focus more on the GD than on collecting your
thoughts during the discussion. Also write the points discussed throughout the GD to make an
impactful, apt, concise, and precise conclusion to the conversation.

3. Be o starter or finisher. Creates an impact on the panel and gives the feeling of a person who takes

the initiative

4. In case, it's not possible, follow up on the conversation and put forward valid points. Make sure the

points that you put are unique and not just paraphrased statements of each other's statements.

5. Try to steer the conversation into a new perspective if you think it's saturating. This will improve the

quality as well as quantity of the conversation and make you stand out from the crowd

6. Don't talk very much or very little. Be apt and clear in your thoughts and speaking.

7. Be confident und be open to understanding other people's perspectives. Make sure you are not

interrupting anyone and giving everybody a chance to speak their minds.

8. If you want to disagree to a point, say politely and put forward an argument.

Remember - This is a GD, not a Debate!

9. If you agree and want to add more to that, do so. That is one of the best ways to insert yourself into

the conversation.

10. Keep smiling and cheerful throughout the conversation and make sure you look fully indulged and

listening to the other people.
Note: If you are not well experienced and have not participated much in GD, go to our IPO or
communication skills professor and ask to conduct Mock GD sessions. This will help you boost your
confidence and give you an idea about your drawbacks. I had got a similar topic in my GD which I had
prepared in a Mock GD. This helped me to confidently put forward my views and ideas without hesitation.
--- PAGE 4 ---

4. Technical Interview - 28 people were interviewed in this round.

There were 3 panels set up, each panel consisting of 2 people. Each panel was equally assigned 7 candidates
which were carefully divided for each panel using their resumes (I suppose). This round began at 10:30 am.
My panel was taking very long interviews. I waited a long time before my interview, at least 5 hours. Some
of the early interviewed people had gone through their next round as well and we were stuck with even the
first round yet to be done. Finally, my interview call came at around 3:30 pm.
My interview started with the constant - Tell me something about yourself/Introduce yourself a question.
While I was answering this question, the interviewers went through my resume and highlighted some of the
points. I supposed that they would stress out on those. One interviewee was on a laptop and the other one had
pen and paper to ask questions. During my introductions, I strongly stressed on my interest and knowledge in
the field of cybersecurity.
So, the first question came through about - Can you explain to me the meaning of inquisitive (Since I had
mentioned it in my intro)? I gave an apt answer about the meaning. Next, the interviewer asked - What is
XSS? I was a bit surprised as I did not expect to get a question on cybersecurity as I did not experience any
such scenario in the earlier interviews. However, I knew all about this and I answered this question
confidently. Next, the interviewers followed with some questions on Linux commands and gave me scenarios
to ask about optimized commands to give the required output. I was able to answer those questions well.
Then the interviewer asked about my internship experience as a Cybersecurity Intern and I elaborated more
on it. Followingly, they asked me how would I proceed to do penetration testing on an E-commerce website
like Amazon (As the interviewer himself was working on an e-commerce website project). I gave all my
process and the vulnerable endpoints that I will scan and he seemed somewhat satisfied with my answer.
Next, the other interviewer read through my profile. He asked me about some of the tools that I had
mentioned related to cybersecurity and hacking.
Next, he asked me whether I wanted some more questions and my interest was more in Networking or Web
App Development. I gave my strong hold of Networking and he asked me further questions related to that.
The questions were about the OSI model, its layers, protocols in each layer, and all the other intricacies. I
stumbled and fumbled a bit on a subnetting question but he guided me through as my approach was clear but
the final answer wasn't accurate. Apart from that, the complete interview was great.
The interviewer also asked about the Minor Degree Management course that I was pursuing at SPJIMR and
how I managed my time throughout the course. What was my daily routine and what recreational activities
do you do and manage my time for that too? Lastly, the interviewer asked me about - Why should we hire
you? In my answer, I focused on my inquisitive nature and elaborated on how I am open to new opportunities
and challenges.
I asked them a question about the work culture and cybersecurity team of Baker Hughes and its details. They
provided me with a very good gist about their team. This concludes the interview. It took place for at least 45
minutes.
I thoroughly enjoyed the interview as it was my first time in on-campus placements where the interview
comprised of what I was interested in and had in-depth knowledge about. It was a really exciting and
insightful experience.
--- PAGE 5 ---

5. Leadership Round - 15 candidates appeared for this round

Immediately after the Technical round, I was asked to present 2 copies of my resume for the next round. I
was instructed to be ready and enter the room to interview after 5 minutes. The panel consisted of 2
interviewers. It was more like a Techno-HR interview.
As soon as I entered the room, I was greeted by the interviewers and I also greeted them. The first question
was - Can you give me a run-through of your resume without glancing at it? I had a complete map of it so I
started off and continued very smoothly. I gave a run through my education, work experience, projects,
achievements, languages, skills, tools, and some leadership role experience. This took at least 15-20 minutes
with all the discussion which followed after each point that I presented.
After this, the interviewer asked me about my hobbies. I told them that I was very much interested in sports
like cricket, volleyball, tennis, table tennis and actively followed F1. I also told about my interest in Music,
singing and that I play the Flute. He asked me - What do you understand by a Hobby? I told them that a
hobby is a task and when I do it, I feel immense pleasure and happiness and satisfaction. He further continued
on asking me questions about F1 as I showed my interest in it. He asked me about which team has done the
fastest pitstop and what was the time. I exactly knew the answer, so I confidently told - Redbull, 1.9secs.
However, the man asked if I was sure and even told me that I am wrong. But I was very sure about my
answer so I told him that I am very confident about it. (PS: Stay on your answer, this shows that you are
confident and will not stumble if counter-questioned). A few more guesstimates type questions on F1
followed namely - What is the weight of an F1 car? How many parts does an F1 car consist of? Here they
check your analytical skills and your approach toward problem-solving.
Next, the interviewer asked questions about some of the terms I had mentioned in my Resume related to IRP,
BCP, and DRP. I explained my understanding and there were some cross questions on it. On answering some
of the questions, the other interviewer, gave a grin and told - "Your answers are not very right, but I like your
confidence!"
. This was a bit weird comment but I liked to take the positive of it :).
They also asked about the Barclays Data Stellar Hackathon, why were you in the Top5, what was your
project and problem statement and about the overall experience. I answered by presenting my part in the
project related to security and told them that it was a main differentiating factor for the qualification in the
Top 5 teams. They seemed very satisfied with the answer. We were slowly going toward the HR questions.
She asked me what was my role as a TPO and what did I do in my position. There was also a question about
why did I leave TPO and do I wish to join it again. I answered that politely with a positive answer and
outlook. Nevertheless, the panel moved on as it became a bit uncomfortable (PS: Be patient if you face
something similar and try to be as honest and positive as possible)
Finally, the panel asked me how would team members look at me if I was a part of the hackathon team. I
answered this by being blatantly honest and completely in full control of my words as it was defining answer
for my personality. Followingly, I was asked about a failure and how did I overcome it. So, I gave an
anecdote about my cricket experience and how I came through this situation and stood strong once again. The
panel then finally asked me to link this answer to any professional or technical aspect of my life where I felt
so. So I compared it to the race of placements where I had prepped my whole year in cybersecurity while the
crowd was focusing on DSA and Web Development.
--- PAGE 6 ---
This was the final question. Then I asked about the growth opportunities that Baker Hughes provides to all its
employees and interns. The lady gave a very insightful answer to this question and I was very convinced that
the company had a great work culture and positive atmosphere with great growth opportunities.
This interview was also around 45 min - 1 hour long.
Finally, & students were selected in Baker Hughes. I was one of them!
This complete day was a very tiring journey that tested everything from initial patience, Technical skills,
knowledge, personality, and even your thinking.

Stipend: Rs 60,000/month ( 6 months Internship + Performance based PPO)
Placement Process Timeline:
15th July, 2023 - Resume Screening (Online Uploading of Resume)
17th July, 2023 - PPT, followed by Screening Test
19th July, 2023 - Offline Technical (2) + HR(1) Interviews held in College
Screening Test Round (Online)
This round was divided in 4 categories:-

• 4 MCQs on CS Fundamentals + Basic DS - Consisted of qs related to Infix/ Postfix

Notation.

• 4 MCQs on SQL - Touch upon basics of DBMS and SQL (W3Schools would be enough).

• 4 MCQs on specific Java Related Qs.

• 1 Coding Qs - Modification of

(https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/) instead of 1's and 0's
there were 4 alphabets a,b,c,d.
Offline Technical Round 1(40 minutes)
The interview started off directly with the interviewer asking me questions regarding the projects
I had listed. He was keen on knowing more about the techstacks, database softwares and tools
involved in the making of the project.
Next he switched to asking me questions about SQL and databases. He asked me indexing in
general, non-clustering indexing (I wasn't sure of the ans, so I broke down the word into two
parts, explained them individually), sharding, normalization techniques (specifically 3NF),
rollback and commit, and the difference between Truncate and Delete. He specifically asked if
truncating means losing data from the database completely. So I confidently told him yes,
however truncating signifies that the data is still present in the logs and can be retrieved.
He asked me questions on OOPs concepts, Encapsulation and Abstraction, and asked me to give
an example (he specifically mentioned something apart from the Car eg)
Lastly he asked me for a DSA qs- given a range limit (3) and a String, I have to find if there are
any duplicates in any contiguous substring of specified range limit. I started off with a
Brute-force approach of TC O(N^2) and eventually led up to an implementation with Hashmap
in ON) time. He asked me for an estimate of how many barbers do you think might be across
--- PAGE 2 ---
Mumbai. So I broke down to think about the number of barbers in my area and scaling up, but
then also listed three factors that I felt the number of barbers depended upon and gave him a
rough estimate of 100-120 (he was expecting more).
I asked him questions about MSCI, about the work they listed on the ppt, and he gave me an
insight on the restrictions too that employees have while working on teams involving Indexing
specifically.
Offline Technical Round 2(25 minutes)
I had a more senior interviewer for this round and he asked me to tell about myself. I had a ML
project on Latent Dirichlet Algorithm, so he asked me to explain the complete working of it on
paper, which I managed to do by drawing out diagrams. I had a project on a Travel Itinerary API
specification, which he was interested to know the JSON format in which I returned my Itinerary
object and even the logic of day-wise allocation of the places. Overall, it was an in-depth logic
analysis of each project. He even asked me to actually write down the JSON return object format
and any data structures I used for the same. It ended with me asking him about MSCI being
classified as a product-based or service-based company and his team and its current areas of
working. He was generous to give a detailed insight for the same.
HR Round (20 minutes)
The interviewer made me feel really comfortable. She asked me about my previous interviews,
(try asking and remember your interviewer names, it shows you're socially active), my domains
of interest. What are my strengths and weaknesses (try to mention something you're actively
working on). Like for this question, I mentioned to her that it was hard initially in project teams
to find someone you can relate to because everyone approaches the project with a different level
of priority towards a project, but with active communication, I have been trying to bridge the gap
and finding midway to achieve progress in my contribution to the project. Next she asked me
where do I see myself 5 years down the line and am I a team member or solo player. Be vocal
about preferences, if given a choice, ranging from location to interested domain. Lastly she asked
me about my family and their current job profiles.
Tips for the interview:-

• Be vocal. If something goes wrong, just acknowledge it.

• Be transparent to a degree where you know that the transparency isn't backfiring you.

• Be confident in your approach to DSA and even HR rounds.

ALL THE BEST!

journey.prep:
If you read this far (or skipped to the bottom), here are some tips that I followed (apart from the standard 'be
confident' and 'don't panic' stuff)

• Everytime I sat on the interview chair, the first thing on my mind was to follow the "SSS" strategy.

• SSS: Smile Slightly, Speak Slowly, Straight Back

• Treat the interviewer as your friend. Think as if this is a conversation and not an interview. You will

enjoy it and not stress unnecessarily.

• Make sure you know the name of the interviewer who took your interview. At times the next

interviewer asks ke pichla interview kisne liya and you not knowing it might create a bad impression.

• Show the interviewer that you are Smart & a Fast Learner.

• Fast Learner: For eg. If the job requires Python, you don't need to show that you know

python. You need to show that even when you don't know Python, learning it will be very
easy for you.

• Smart: For Eg. Even if you do not know a DSA question or a logical question, you are

thinking about it and giving it a shot. Nahi aaya toh thike but dimaag lagane ka try toh kar
rahe ho to get an answer.

• In the end if the interviewer asks if you have a question, it is much appreciated if you can take some

generalized topic from the interview itself and ask a question from it. That way it wont look scripted
and you would seem a curious person.

Test duration was 90 mins.

• DBMS/SQL (identify incorrect query, common queries etc)

• OOPS (basic concepts)

• The Coding question was related to DFS.

• It was similar to the 'number of islands' question on leetcode with some minor modifications.

(Number of Islands - LeetCode)
49 students cleared the OA.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Technical Interview 1 [49 students appeared]

Started with the interviewer checking out my resume.
He then directly jumped me on my projects and asked me to explain one of them.
Pro Tip 1: Prepare beforehand about all your project's explanations. Have 3-4 points ready so that
you know what to speak when asked to explain your projects.
I explained my project, he cross questioned on why I used this particular tech stack.
Pro Tip 2: Don't just say the tech stack I used is better/faster blah blah. They want honest answers.
Tell them one advantage and tell them that you were more familiar with it than the other stack so you
used it. Generalize this approach of answering similar questions. HONESTY op.
He further asked me JavaScript & React.js questions, since I had a project made entirely with JavaScript and
one included React. I had used/heard some terms he asked me to explain, and some I had never heard of.
Pro Tip 3:
if(don't know the answer) ‹
while(heard of it but not able to recollect) {
cout < "Please give me a hint to recollect";
cout < "Nope, I haven't encountered this / heard of this";
He further asked me about my internship experiences. He took a bullet point "increased website loading
speed by xyz%", and asked me to explain how.
Pro Tip 4: 'Doing your resume' means preparing explanations for every single bullet point you have
written. No one is 100% honest about every single word on their resume. It is okay to lie a bit,
provided you have a backup ready. Prepare these beforehand so that you do not get trapped during
the interview, and LIMIT THE LIES.
He further asked me a DSA question. It was an even easier version of Valid Parentheses - LeetCode
I knew the question well, yet I asked him to verify my answer on some test cases.
Pro Tip 5: The first part of solving a question is to UNDERSTAND it. Take your time to understand
the question, take 1-2 sample test cases and verify the output with the interviewer, then proceed to
solve it.
I told him a brute-force approach. While dry-running, I told him the 'stack' approach, and explained to him
the reason why I am using a stack, and what I will do at every step. I took the given test case, and dry run the
approach to get the answer. I then modified the same test case to make him believe that this approach would
cover all possible cases. He was contended by my explanation and dry run, he didn't ask me to code.
The entire interview lasted for around 30 mins. 20 mins for the resume and 10 mins for the DSA question.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Technical Interview 2 [27 students appeared]
After waiting for almost 3 hours.. pheww.. I finally had my Tech Round 2. The interviewer (who was also
the VP of MSCI, which I didn't know then), took my resume and asked me to introduce myself.
Pro Tip 6: Prepare a sweet and short (40-50 sec) introduction. "What you say is important, but
"How" you say it will set the tone of the interview. Try to stand out while answering this.
He then took one of my projects and asked me to explain it. This was the same project I explained in Round

1. He asked very detailed questions such as how did I extract stuff from the database, where and how did I

store images etc. I was able to answer most of the questions, but got confused with one question. Took about
20 mins.
Pro Tip 7: Refer "Pro Tip 1'. Haa again.. I can not stress more on how important it is. If you are not
able to answer questions on your own project, that is a big red flag for the interviewer.
He then asked me a SQL question. "Suppose you have a table with millions or billions of rows, how would
you optimize searching for a particular entryằi
'. I didn't know the answer and I knew there must be a method
which I haven't studied. But unhe dikhana toh padega na ke you are capable of ideating and applying brains
to come up with a solution. I thought and tried it logically, and discussed it with him. He told me the solution
which is "Indexing". MSCI ne ye question last year bhi pucha tha jo meko ekdum se yaad ayaa.. Thanks to
the Interview Experience of my seniors (and TPO ofc). I cross-questioned to him, if this is similar to
hashmaps in C++ where you find by indexing in O(1). Vo kuch toh bole ispe and I definitely understood it
very clearly. Took about 5 mins.
Pro Tip 8: Ab pata nahi hai matlab ye nahi ke humehsa mana kardo. This question was logical, so try
to think about it first, and discuss it. Phir soch soch ke nahi aaya toh bolo IDK. You can also cross
question when he tells you the answer, but aisa lagna chahiye tumne dimaag lagaya isiliye you are
asking and not just for the sake.
He then gave me a DSA question. It was same as Linked List Cycle - LeetCode
I had solved this question kaafi pehele, but did not remember the optimal approach. Started with brute force
which I could think on the spot. (Traverse and change value to -1, if encountered -1 again then loop, or no
loop). I asked questions to him to clarify stuff, for eg. if I could modify the values of LinkedList etc. Then
meko slow-fast pointer wala approach strike hua while solving and discussing, which I told him and he was
happy with it and didn't ask me to code. Took about 10 mins.
Pro Tip 9: Ask questions to the interviewer when he gives you the problem. Take a test case and ask
ke ye sahi hai na, aise hi hoga na. Edge cases bhi puchlo. Let him think ke you are curious to solve it.
He then moved to the next DSA question. It was same as Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array - LeetCode
Sorted array sunte hi I thought of Binary Search. I took a test case and implemented it. He told me ke isse
kaise hoga try karke dekho, I tried so hard and got so far, but in the end BS se nahi hua. Wasted 10 mins on
it and then explained to him ke BS se kyu nahi hoga solve and it was silly 'sorted array' sunke hi BS use
kıya.
I asked for a hint, he told me swap karke try karo, I gave him a solution but he was quick to pick that it wont
work on another test case. Aur 10 mins gaye isme.
--- PAGE 4 ---
I feel he didn't explain the entire question properly. At this point he said that it is okay if you can throw the
duplicates at the end of the array.
I asked for another hint, he told me to use the 2 pointer approach, and then try to swap. I thought for a while,
then called him back and dry ran a test case. I connected it with the approach I was telling him earlier jisko
vo mana kiya tha. He understood what I was thinking, and finally I showed him the proper solution. This
took nearly 15 mins. The whole Q2 took nearly 30 mins.
Pro Tip 10: Ask for hints if needed. Converse with the interviewer. Vo bahot time se interview le raha
hoga toh usko bore mat hone do.
He asked me if I had questions, I asked him a question related to databases and how MSCI uses them.

4. HR Interview [15 students appeared]

Immediately after Tech Round 2, I was called for the HR round. The HR connected online over MS Teams.
He introduced himself (one of the lines included him saying that he is not a 'tech guy'). He then asked me
the "Tell me about yourself' question. He asked the following questions:
'Explain me about your project"
Since he was not a tech guy, I only explained the working of a project and did not go into technical details
since he prolly wouldnt understand that and I would bore him. That's exactly what he wanted to test.
"Has there been a situation where you were doing a project and you thought of giving up midway? What did
you do?"
I explained my IIT internship experience where something similar happened. In the end I didn't give up and
finished the project. That 'never give up' attitude was what he was expecting.
Explain a team project and how the team members contributed
I explained my semester mini project where I lead the team of 3. I told him that I understood the skills of
every person and then delegated work accordingly. I went way too honest with him while answering the
contributions wala part which I wont type since baaki 2 log bhi padh sakte hai ye.
"What did you do 2 years during the c*vid lockdown?"
I included everything from studying 12 hrs a day for JEE.. yes :), to learning new skills in free time after
JEE, to enjoying watching aviation videos, that being my interest. I showed him diversity, and didnt get
stuck on one thing.
"Do you have any questions for me?"
I asked about the work culture at MSCI. He was happy to answer that since he said that he had received a lot
of standard technical questions earlier despite him saying that he was not a tech guy. The interview ended up
with him asking me my preferred job location:)
Finally 8 students got the offer.
--- PAGE 5 ---

2] Quantitative Aptitude- 12 Questions- Easy to Moderate

My first question was "Introduce yourself". Then they asked me extensively about my Projects.
NOTE: Make sure you know each and every word of your Resume. Most of the Tech interview rounds are
resume based. So make sure you prepare well.

journey.prep:
1. The first and most important step to cracking any Interview is DSA Prep. Maximum

companies will have their first round as the Coding Round, so if you don't have a strong
hold over DSA, there is no point in preparing for the further rounds.

2. Start your DSA preparation early and make sure you participate in contests on

Hackerrank, Leetcode. This will give you the environment to think under the time
pressure, which will hugely help you in Online Assessments. You can also time your
solutions for practice.

3. Refer to the Top 150 Qs list on Leetcode:

https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-interview-150/
And for difficult topics like Dynamic Programming and Graphs, refer to Striver's A-Z
Sheet:
https://takeuforward.org/strivers-a2z-dsa-course/strivers-a2z-dsa-course-sheet-2/
Watch the solution videos of the initial questions and then solve problems of the topic by
yourself.

4. Most Qs are an alteration of some typical concepts that you need to be aware of. You

can practice these standard questions multiple times, so that the logic is memorized.
Some of these typical questions are:
https://eetcode.com/problems/two-sum/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-increasing-subsequence/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-common-subsequence/description/
--- PAGE 5 ---
https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-subarray/description/

5. You can start revising the computer fundamentals subjects(OOPS, DBMS, OS), one

month before the placements begin. Revising from resources on GFG, InterviewBit will
be sufficient. Make sure that you are confident about these subjects as they show that you
have a strong understanding of the concepts.
Some resources:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-dbms/?ref=lbp
https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/
https://www.javatpoint.com/oops-interview-questions
https://www.interviewbit.com/oops-interview-questions/

6. Knowing how to solve at least medium level SQL Queries is very important in

interviews. Have a clear idea of the use of JOINS and aggregate functions. For
practicing SQL Queries, you can use: https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/
SQL Queries:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sql-query-interview-questions/
https://www.interviewbit.com/sql-query-interview-questions/

7. Don't run behind increasing the number of questions you have solved on leetcode/any

platform. Quality> Quantity. The more quality questions you solve, the more your
understanding increases. Interviewers will test your understanding.

8. Communicate with your interviewers to let them know your train of thought while

approaching a question. They want to judge how you come to the solution, rather than
only the solution.

9. Be thorough with the content of your projects. Only mention projects that you have

complete knowledge about.

10. Prepare the answers to standard HR questions in advance, so that it saves you the

thinking time in front of the interviewer.

11. Be confident and mindful throughout your interviews. Try to ask the interviewers their

names and remember them. Try to involve the interviewers in your thought process.
Feel free to reach out: https://www.linkedin.com/in/awani-khodwe-64762422b/
ALL THE BEST!!! :)

Interviews:

1. Technical Round 1

2. Technical Round 2

3. HR Round

1.
Online Assessment [ Around 290 candidates appeared for this round]
The online assessment was held on the Hackerrank platform with a duration of 75 mins. There
were 3 Questions in the test, as follows:
Q1: We are given an array of integers. We had to find the maximum length of the array for each
element, where the height of the current element is the maximum. We had to return the
maximum length for each element.
For eg. [3, 1, 2, 4, 7, 3]
So for the 1st element, 3, 3 has the maximum height till we reach 4 at index 3. I.e. 3 is the tallest
in the array 3, 1, 2. So the maximum length will be 3. Similarly for element 7, it's the tallest in
the entire array, so for that element the answer will be 6.
I implemented this using two pointers left and right, and calculated the maximum size for every
element. This resulted in a T.C. of O(N). However, I was able to pass 13/15 test cases here.
The optimized approach would have been using a Monotonic Stack, ON). The question used the
same concept as: https://leetcode.com/problems/trapping-rain-water/description
https://leetcode.com/problems/largest-rectangle-in-histogram/description/
--- PAGE 2 ---
Q2: Given two arrays of strings of equal size. For each string in the array at the same index, we
had to say if the strings were almost equal. Almost equal strings are those which have the same
length and the difference between the frequency of each character should be <= 3.
For Eg. s1 = [''abcb", "fgfh"], s2 = ['aacc", "bfd"]
I used a hashmap to solve this. For the strings, the freq of each character of both the strings was
stored. Then, the difference was calculated and the output was stored as YES or NO for the
satisfying conditions.
This was an easy question and with the implementation of the hashmap, I could solve all test
cases.
Q3:This was an SQL Query. Three tables were given. I don't exactly remember the question.
There were many things that needed to be calculated from the three tables by using the
appropriate JOIN. Aggregate functions like COUNT, SUM were also required. GROUP BY and
ORDER BY statements were required as well.
I wasn't able to crack the complete answer, so I couldn't submit this.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 49 candidates were shortlisted, 46 appeared ]

This round went on for 30 mins.
I was asked to introduce myself and after that, the interviewer proceeded with questions about
my resume. He asked about one of the projects which I had implemented in a Hackathon. I was
able to answer in detail about this as well as one more project. He asked me in detail about why I
chose the particular tech stack and asked me to implement the database structure of one of my
projects. He asked me what SQL and NoSQL databases are and asked me the structure of the
database in MongoDB and how I would store and display multiple addresses corresponding to
the same user. I answered by showing the JSON format of MongoDB Documents, and that I
would display all the addresses using the map function.
He then asked me to implement the following scenario using any programming language: There
is a fruit basket and the customer can enter 1 fruit (its name and quantity = 1). At the end he
wanted me to display the total quantity of each fruit in the basket. Firstly, I gave a solution using
unordered map in C++, and explained to him how unordered map will be efficient for this
approach. He then wanted me to implement this using some self designed structure. I got the hint
of the OOPs based approach, and explained to him the use of Class FruitBasket, its attributes and
creation of an object corresponding to each fruit name. Detailed explanation wasn't required
here.
I was further asked an SQL Query: There is an Employee Table(EmpID, EmpName, DeptID)
and the Department Table(DeptID, DeptName). I was asked to find the number of employees
corresponding to each department. This was fairly a simple SQL query and I wrote it down using
the JOIN and GROUP BY operations would give the correct result. He further added by asking
--- PAGE 3 ---
to represent the departments which have no employees as well. For this, I suggested using the
LEFT JOIN. He was satisfied with the answer and didn't ask me to write it down.
At the end, I asked him about the use of Generative Al being used by MSCI recently, which I
read in a news article. I asked about how MSCI is introducing Al into their technologies.

3. Technical Round 2 [ Around 25-30 candidates were shortlisted for this round ]

This went on for 30 mins as well.
The interviewer again asked me to introduce myself. Then, she asked me about the same project
I was asked in Round 1. I gave a detailed explanation of my contributions to the project. She then
asked me an OOPs question. There is a Library and we have to implement the various operations
of Borrowing a book, Returning a book and so on. I gave the solution using a Class Library and
the operations as methods. But she told me to implement separate classes for Books and Users.
So I wrote the pseudocode down and formed objects of Class Books and Users and implemented
the borrowing and returning operations inside the books class. She was satisfied with this
approach. She then asked me to explain Inheritance in OOPs.
Further, she moved on to ask me to implement the Queue Data Structure. I wrote the code down
using an array, and a rear and front pointer. I implemented the push and pop operations of the
queue. She gave me a sample test case to dry run the code. I could successfully do it.
Then, she asked me why I had used MySQL for a particular project. I answered it by explaining
the ease of representation in SQL in the form of tables. She followed up by asking me if I would
be able to use MongoDB instead for relational data, and how would the structure change. I
answered with a yes, and how MongoDB would represent the data in one single document for
certain entities rather than separate tables
She moved on to some HR questions. She asked me where I see myself in 5 years. Then she
asked me about my role models in personal and professional lives, and what inspires me to
pursue tech.
At the end I asked her about the huge amount of data that MSCI is handling, and what are the
measures taken for the security and management of the data.

4. HR Round [16 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

This was a typical HR Round.
The questions that were asked were:

1. Introduce yourself while not highlighting your tech achievements.

2. Why did you decide to pursue tech?

3. What are your hobbies?

--- PAGE 4 ---

4. What would you do to resolve conflicts in a team? And have you faced any such conflict?

5. Asked me about my family background, and if any family members were/are a part of

MSCI

6. Preference of location

7. Why I wish to work in a financial services company even though I have a Tech

background
At the end, I asked her about the roadmap for freshers in MSCI, and if MSCI initiates any special
programmes for freshers. I also asked her about the best thing about the culture at MSCI.
Finally, 6 Students got the offer.

journey.howSecured:
1. Aptitude and Technical Test [90 mins]:

The first round was a comprehensive test that included aptitude, technical multiple-choice questions
(MCQS), and coding. It was divided into 7 sections, and the total duration was 90 minutes. One coding
question was provided, and 30 aptitude questions had to be completed within 30 minutes. The aptitude
section was timed and non-navigable, meaning you can navigate between questions but once you exited this
section, you couldn't return to it.
The remaining sections covered subjects like Data Structures (DS), Database Management Systems
(DBMS), Computer Networks (CCN), and Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs). Unlike the aptitude
section, these technical sections were untimed and fully navigable, allowing candidates to move between
questions as needed.

• Coding: 1 coding question:

Evan needs to collect the maximum number of fruits from a garden matrix by moving up to K steps,
starting from a given position, and can move to adjacent cells only once per visit. The goal is to
return the maximum fruits collected in K steps.
Answer: Use Depth-First Search DFS) with backtracking to explore all possible paths and track the
maximum fruits collected.

• Aptitude: 30 timed questions based on logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, and verbal ability.

• Technical Sections: MCQs on DS, DBMS, CCN, and OOPs. The questions tested fundamental

concepts in each subject.
Number of students shortlisted: After this round, 31 candidates were shortlisted.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Technical + HR Interview 30-40 mins :

This round had two panels, one panel focusing more on your resume and the other delving into Data
Structures and Algorithms (DSA). It was essential to be well-versed with your resume and to have a good
understanding of core subjects like DBMS, OOPs, and DSA.
Interview Experience:
I started by introducing myself and explaining one of my projects. The interviewers went in-depth, asking
me why I had chosen MongoDB instead of MySQL, leading to a discussion about the differences between
SQL and NoSQL databases.
They first asked me about some React related questions like What is Virtual DOM.
Since Python was my primary language, they asked me about the difference between lists and tuples.
As I had mentioned C and Java in my resume, they asked a question from C about the difference between
pointers and references.
Lastly, they presented me with a puzzle to solve, which I was unable to answer, but I asked the interviewer
to explain the approach. This shows that you are open to learning and not just there for the interview.
Next, they asked me about my family background and about a leadership role I had in one of my internship
projects, specifically how I divided the work among my teammates. They also asked how I would handle a
situation with a tight deadline, and that was it.
Overall it was an easy round. You just need to be confident when explaining your projects and concepts and
stay calm and speak your approach during the puzzle-solving portion, as they're often looking to see your
thought process.

3. HR (With VP) |10-15 mins]:

The final round was a 10-15 minute interview with the VP.
It was more of a conversation to assess your mindset and goals.
Interview Experience:
He began by asking how my day was and whether I understood how things work in a corporate
environment. He then asked about my strengths, giving me the choice between development, data science,
and cloud. I told him that while I'm open to exploring various domains, my first choice would be data
science.
He asked if I had any questions for him, and that concluded the interview.
This was the final round and 10 students including me were offered the job.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Preparation Tips:

• Aptitude: Focus on practicing timed tests with a variety of problems. Indiabix can be sufficient for

preparing and answering the aptitude questions.

• Technical: Make sure you have a solid grasp of DSA, DBMS, and OOPs concepts. Practicing

common DSA problems on platforms like LeetCode and GeeksforGeeks can help.

• Resume: Mention relevant projects and technical skills clearly. Be thorough with everything you

have mentioned in your resume.

1. Online Assessment

Q1. For each index in the array find the  maximum length of a subarray
containing that index where the element at that index is greater than or equal
to all other elements present in the subarray.

(The question had some story about students and their confidence but this is
the logical part that was supposed to be done)

Solution: Find the index of the next greater element to the left and to the
right of each index and then that subarray would be the maximum length
subarray. This can be done using stack and two arrays to store the index of
the next greater element, with the first traversal from left to right and the
second traversal from right to left.

Q2. For multiple key value pairs find the minimum value associated with each
key. The keys would be from 1 to n. Also return -1 if any key from 1 to n is not
present.

(The question had some story but this was the logical part to be done)

Solution: Simply use an array of size n to get the desired result.

Q3. It was a complex SQL query. There are quite a few functions available in
MySQL for strings, numbers, date and time, if statements etc. and knowing
some of them was necessary to solve this question. For example CONCAT(),
IF(),IFNULL() etc. It also required the use of aggregate functions and joins.

2. Technical Round 1

First, I was asked to introduce myself and then based on my introduction she
continued to ask me questions. She asked me about all my projects in detail
and I was able to answer her questions. Then she proceeded to ask questions
on threads and multi -threading. It would be better if you know how to use
threads in at least one programming language. Then she asked me to design
a schema for a ticket booking system and had a few questions based on that.
Next, she gave me two SQL queries. The first one was a simple join query and
the second one was a combination of join and aggregate functions. Then she
asked me five DSA questions which were very easy and standard questions.

- Sum of all digits in a number

- Sum of all elements in an array

- Find the missing number in the array

- Maximum length of valid parenthesis substring (containing round, square

and curly brackets)

- Longest Palindromic Substring (Not Subsequence!!!)

https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-palindromic-
substring/description/

I started with the most naïve solution of generating all substrings and
checking if they are palindrome or not. The time complexity for this would
be O(n 3) and she was not happy with it so she asked me for a better
approach.

I gave her a better solution with O(n2) time complexity which was the best
approach that I knew and she accepted it.

But this problem can be solved in O(n) using Manacher's Algorithm. I was
not aware of this approach. You can find it in the links below.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/manachers-algorithm-linear-time-
longest-palindromic-substring-part-1/

https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/manachers-algorithm-linear-time-
longest-palindromic-substring-part-2/

longest-palindromic-substring-part-3/

longest-palindromic-substring-part-4/

3. Technical Round 2

projects. Two of my projects were from a hackathon so he asked me to explain
them in detail and then asked a few questions on it.

He then asked questions on DBMS: -

- Explain ACID properties

- Explain various keys.

- What is Normalization?

- What is indexing and its types?

- Explain different types of joins.

- Types of databases apart from SQL and No SQL.

He then asked me a SQL query where I had a Students Table containing
student details and Exam Table which contained student_id, subject and
marks. My task was to find those students who have not appeared for any
exam. First, I gave a subquery approach by fi nding the DISTINCT student_id
in the Exam Table in the inner query and then using the NOT IN operator in
the outer query to get the result. But he asked me for a different approach as
subqueries are not optimal. So, I gave another approach using joins. So , by
doing Student left join on Exam all the students who did not give any exam
will have all their Exam Table's column values as NULL and then you can select
those students by adding a where condition.

After that he asked me a question where I had to find and pick a task with
shortest duration. Every second a new task would come with a certain
duration. You can pick a new task after you finish an ongoing task. The
solution to this was using a Min Heap which would store the incoming tasks
and help to retrieve the task with shortest duration efficiently.

4. HR round

This was a very typical HR round and it is important to stay calm and answer
appropriately. The following questions were asked to me: -

- Detailed introduction and family background.

- Why should we hire you?

- Give me one situation where you took calculated risk and one where you

took the risk without any calculation.

- What do you know about MSCI.

- Do you know MSCI's values

- Where do you see yourself in 5 years

- Where do you see yourself in 10 years

There were a few of more questions but I cannot recall them. It was a very
fast paced round. It is important that you sit straight, maintain proper eye
contact, and do not fumble while answering. Sometimes she asked some
random questions which were totally off topic. I believe she wanted to see if
I panic or not. It is important that you chose your words properly.

Important Points: -

• You must know what MSCI does. I was asked this question in every round.

• Keep a note of your interviewers in each round as you might be asked who

interviewed you in previous rounds.

• The interviewers from MSCI will never introduce themselves so make sure

you ask the interviewer their name.

• Have your introduction ready as you will need it in every round.

• Your resume is very important and make sure the font is readable maybe

follow a standard template.  Do not add something that you are not
confident about or is redundant.

• Do not put copied projects or common and standard projects on your

resume. Have some unique projects and having projects from a hackathon
would be even better. Avoid projects like  blog website, stock screening,
expense tracker, e-commerce etc.

• OS and DBMS concepts are very important so make sure you read and

understand them well.

• Have a good understanding of SQL queries and how they execute. Learn to

build the logic for a query and try building the solution step by step to make
it easy.

• All they expect is for you to be able to answer the contents of your resume

and questions on fundamentals.

1. Round 1: Resume Shortlisting (All students above 6 CGPA were shortlisted)

Also take care to fill the Deloitte 's form properly on their website which includes candidate basic
information and submission of resume.

2. Round 2: Online test

Test Duration: 1 Hour
Platform: HirePro (We can take the test from home.)
Test information: 3 Sections (Aptitude, Reasoning, Verbal skills, 2 Coding Questions)
Each section was having definite time (no switching between sections), MCQ's were mostly easy and
solvable.
Coding Questions:
Question 1: This question is based on the concept of input validation and string processing. It asks
to determine whether the input is an integer or a string. If the input consists only of digits, output
"integer"; otherwise, output "string".

Question 2: Write a function that takes an array of numbers and returns the sum of all positive numbers
that can be divided only by 2, 3, or 5. These numbers should reduce to 1 when divided by these primes
repeatedly.

3. Round 3: Online Interview (Technical + HR: 30 min) [35 Students]

One day before the interview, we were assigned specific time slots for our interviews, each lasting 30
minutes. My interview was scheduled from 10:30 to 11:00 AM.
My interview began with an introduction where I talked about myself, highlighting my projects, the
technology stack I used, competitions I participated in and extracurricular activities. I also mentioned
my interest in chess, which prompted the interviewer to ask me a few questions about it.

After that, the interviewer asked me about my projects, starting with my data analysis project. She
requested a detailed explanation of the project and the technology stack I used. Following that, she
inquired about group project I worked on, which was based on the MERN stack. I mentioned that my
focus within the group was specifically on JWT, WebSocket, and Zustand. She then asked me to
explain the architecture of this project and the workings of  JWT in detail, which I was able to articulate
clearly. Then the interviewer asked about the challenges I faced during the project and whether there
were any conflicts among group members while working on it.
Then the interviewer inquired about how I managed my time to work on these projects alongside my
exams and major projects. Additionally, she wanted to know about my strengths and weaknesses. She
also sought my approach to learning a new technology in detai l. Finally, she wanted to know what
recent technology I had used, which one was my favorite, and the reasons behind my choice.
The final part of the interview involved her asking if I had any questions. I took this opportunity to
inquire about the culture at Deloitte and the specifics of the job description.
I had only one interview, while some students attended two. In the evening, the results were announced,
and 15 students were selected for the opportunity, and I was one of them.

Important tips:

• Be confident.

• Familiarize yourself with your resume so you can explain your projects and every detail you've

included.

• Some candidates were asked basic DSA questions, OOPS concepts, as well as DBMS and SQL

queries.

• Practice DSA regularly.

• Participate in mock interviews to improve your skills.

ALL THE BEST!

Destiny had other plans today
), I sat near TPO waiting for my interview round which was

faced with so many interviews till now, I was not at all nervous, I kinda had an idea of what the
interviewer was gonna ask me based on responses received by previous people. I went in with a smile,
sat down, there was only one panelist being the head of assurance & data quality, having 20+ years of

scratch with a real life example and application of my project, then he asked me about my internship
experience.

depth so solving this question was a piece of cake, I solved it in under 2 mins and ig he was surprised
somewhat, then he moved on to a Pandas group by function (value_counts), I was solving it but the
provided laptop had 15% battery so I told him that the laptop battery is quite low and that if i can go
outside and fetch charger for it. He said yes, and I brought back a charger but due to brand mismatch, it
didn't fit and then he joked saying you have limited time now to solve it and we shared a genuine laugh
on this and I solved the question.

--- PAGE 3 ---

a few questions about how ISS sources its Data, what type of projects he currently is working on and if I
got selected for this role, what would be that one piece of advice he would give me. The interview ended
on a very positive note.
(I was tensed ki interview went only for like 15 mins, will I even be selected as I was also one of the
last guys, but everything happens for a reason and within 20mins of the interview ending, I got a call
saying my HR was scheduled in some time:))

3. [HR Round] [17 shortlisted, 12 Selected]

But for me the case was different, my HR lasted for around 45 mins.
The HR round was taken by the MD of ISS (India region) and HR head (Asia Pacific Region). I was
greeted and was asked to hand in my resume. The HR comforted me by asking if I had anything as the
round started at 7pm to which I replied yes. At first she asked me if I knew their names, to which I
confidently replied Yes and told them their names. (For this, attending PPT with focus is very very
crucial). They were happy that I knew their names and joked about me getting selected solely on this :)
She liked that I was attentive enough to know their names.
They then asked me for my intro, then HR asked me for my internship project (As HR had asked,
hence I explained in layman terms excluding the TECH part out of it), then we had a brief discussion
on my family background, she asked details about my parents education, what my father does, what my
mother does, it was more of an informal chatting session (so much that I told her about my mom's yt
cooking channel and she note the name down
Then the MD of ISS asked me about the role offered, what part of it attracted me? He specifically
asked me to give info about what parts were mentioned in the JD (be sure to go through Job Description
before your interviews as you got to have clarity about the job profile and firm you are applying for). I
answered all this questions, correlating my answers with ISS values (to score brownie points
He then asked me that there would come a moment in future where you would be satisfied with the tasks
you are performing and that what would be the amount of time that I would take to move on to next
profile/ role (basically asking me the no. of years i would take to switch roles/ switch firm). I don't know
what Aristotle got in me & I answered philosophically by saying that the no. of years doesn't matter,
what matters is the quantity and most importantly the quality of projects that I get to work on. (he
seemed happy, which ultimately boosted my confidence)
The HR then asked me about traveling as I stay at Thane and goregaon is as you know far away...to
which I replied that I have been traveling to and fro from azad nagar to thane for 2.5 years and goregaon
would be the same. She then started explaining to me about the employee benefits @ ISS and work
culture, while also stating that If I'm selected for the role, I would be locked for the firm. (at this point i
had a strong feeling that I was selected for ISS & was bringing it home, but everything's
unpredictable and you gotta be calm until the final list is released). As many people were yet to give
the HR round, they told us to go home and the final list would be released before midnight. The
interview ended with me asking them for advice about this role (if I'm selected) and a general feedback
of the interview. This one too ended on a really positive note.
At the end 12 People were selected (including me) and were offered the Job!!

Aptitude Test

• 10 Questions on Finance and Accounting

• 10 Questions on Market Awareness

• 15 Questions on Aptitude

Finance and accounting Section has Questions related to various financial ratios
and financial statements
Market Awareness questions were related to current affairs ie both financial and non-

ratios and proportions etc.
VARC: Questions were asked based on a given Comprehension, Fill in the blank's questions
and sentence error correction questions

I would recommend practicing a lot of aptitude questions beforehand and focus on time
management while attempting the questions. Think beforehand about which section will you
attempt first and allocate time accordingly.

Group Discussion
Following the aptitude test, 73 students were Shortlisted for the GD. The topic for the GD
was announced beforehand it was "India-the 5th largest economy". As you know the topic
beforehand prepare thoroughly and write good points. Make sure to include statistical
metrices related to the topic.
Groups of 12 were made and we discussed for about 20 min make sure to make 2-3 entries
and also listen to what others are saying. If possible, add on to their points as well

Interview Rounds 1 and 2
Around 31 students were shortlisted after the GD. Following are the questions which were
asked to me (not exhaustive):

1) Explanation of the three financial statements and how are they related

2) About recent M&A's and their deal structure

3) Nifty and Sensex closing and how the value of Sensex is calculated

4) About brent crude oil price, INR To dollar exchange rate, 10 gm 24 karat gold price

5) About WACC and how it is calculated whether cost of equity will be more or cost of

debt and why?

6) About enterprise value and how it is calculated they will give some numbers and ask

you to calculate the enterprise value

7) As I had mentioned about Beta in one of my projects. I was asked what is beta how it

is calculated and they gave me two companies and asked me about beta w.r.t those
companies

8) Again, they asked me to write the three financial statements line items. Then they told

that if we increase the depreciation by x amount as compared to previous year and
assume a suitable tax rate, what will be the affect on the three financial statements.

9) About minority interest

10)  About what is cash conversion cycle?

11) Many puzzles and mental ability questions were also asked

While solving the puzzles even if you don't get the right answer do not worry just tell
them about your approach and thought process. They will try to confuse you many times
but if you are confident about your answer stick to it.
Prepare the standard questions like introduce yourself, why finance etc.

HR Round
The round began with my introduction. Seeing one of my courses the interviewer asked
me what do you understand by the term "Portfolio Management". Then I was asked to tell
a scenario in which I optimized the result of a project using a better dataset something on
these lines actually I forgot the exact question. Then the interviewer explained a bit about
the JPMC work culture and asked me of my understanding of the role and what I expect
my day-to-day work would be?  Then I was also asked that why I was not going for an
MBA. Then I was asked a bit about my family background.

Process had a total of 3 rounds, before that there was a resume-based shortlisting.

1. Round 1 : SQL Round [46 candidates appeared for this round]

The round was conducted in offline mode but on a gmeet with 1 interviewer in the panel. This was based
purely on SQL for me and went for about 30 mins. Firstly, the interviewer introduced herself and than
asked for mine. Keep it short, not more than 45 secs.  An Excel sheet containing two tables (customers
and orders) and their schemas was shared with me. I was asked to solve 7 queries, ranging from easy to
medium LeetCode questions. After solving each question, I explained my logic and approach, during
which the interviewer either cross-questioned or asked for modifications. The questions primarily involved
joins, aggregates, and subqueries. Do practice and understand MySQL functions (datetime, string, math),
CTEs and window functions (lag, lead, row number, rank, dense rank, etc) and make sure you know the
differences between them (also get a small example ready with you to explain the differences just in case
if required).
Initially, some of us faced internet issues, so keep your laptops connected to given WiFi and even if things
like these happen do not stress out, just let your interviewer know about the same.
Additionally, got to know that some of the interviewers in other panels were asking resume-based
questions as well as tableau if mentioned so be prepared with that as well.

2. Round 2 : Problem Solving Round [Around 24 candidates appeared for this round]

The panel had two interviewers, each with 5-6 years of experience. The round started with some SQL
questions, but this time, I only needed to provide the logic rather than the complete query. Some
questions required MySQL datetime functions and it was more of real life questions.
In some panels, they conducted guesstimates, but in my case, it was a root cause analysis based on
Swiggy. Specifically, the question was: "The ratio of the number of orders placed to the number of
active users is decreasing every month (i.e., the order rate is declining monthly). What could be the
possible reasons for this?" They let me brainstorm and asked me to open the app if needed. After each
reason I gave, they acknowledged but asked for another reason. This happened about 3-4 times.

Eventually, I couldn't come up with more reasons at the moment so I let them know about the same, so
they switched the question and asked, "If the discounts given on Swiggy are reduced, what type of users
will be most affected?" (This was a sort of follow-up question since I mentioned greater discounts on
competitors like Zomato as one reason. The answer involved age groups and income levels.)
The last segment of the round was puzzles. I was asked 3-4 questions (resources mentioned below). I
got the correct answers for some on the first attempt. For the others, I was initially wrong, but they asked
me to reconsider and provided hints, which helped me arrive at the correct solutions.
Overall, this round lasted about 45-50 minutes.

3. Round 3 : Culture Round [10 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was supposed to begin at 6 pm, but since I was scheduled first in every panel and had already
completed the first two interviews by 3 pm, my turn came around 5:15 pm. The interviewer started by
introducing himself but paused midway to ask if I had attended the pre-placement talk. He then asked
for my introduction and went through my resume, focusing on one of my data-related projects. I
provided an overall brief of the project, and discussed a new project I was considering that was similar
and related to one of my achievements listed in my resume, thus highlighting the same.
Next, he asked whether I was more interested in the business or product side. We then discussed my
hobbies and whether I am still pursuing them. He also inquired about where I live, why I would prefer to
move to Bangalore, and what I like about Mumbai.
Finally, he asked why I wanted to join WorkIndia, what specific and unique qualities I liked about the
company, and how my values aligned with theirs. Overall, it was not a typical HR round but more of a
discussion to understand my personal opinions. However, remember not to get too carried away, as
they are evaluating you from the moment you enter the room. The round lasted about 30-35 minutes.
Total 5 candidates were shortlisted including me for the role.

--- PAGE 2 ---

Accounting & Corporate Finance section had questions related to bonds, ratios etc.

3. Group Discussion [72 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

This was an offline round scheduled on 10th July. The topic for the Group Discussion was given a day
prior. Our theme was "India - the fifth largest economy". It was a very broad topic so it was difficult to
understand what kind of sub-topic would be asked. Try to research properly and make sure you have
covered all the important points. Students were divided into 6 panels. The moderator was changing the
topic in every 10 mins. Try to make at least 2-3 entries, but also make sure you add real value to the
conversation and don't repeat any points. Try to remember the major talking points and think of a
general outcome for a conclusion in case the moderator asks you in the end.

4. Interview Round 1[36 students were shortlisted for this round]

The interviews started at 11:30 am. The interview started with an introduction and as I had mentioned an
IB course that I had undertaken, they enquired about my learnings from the course. They asked me about
the Case Study Competition that I had won, I wasn't able to recollect every fine detail, so make sure to
revise everything that is mentioned in your resume in detail. Then the other panelist asked me a series of
questions on accounting fundamentals. As I knew that I didn't have in-depth knowledge in the field of
accounting, I made sure to answer all the questions to the best of my abilities and also tried to let them
know that I am much more proficient in Investment Banking concepts. Thus, they asked me a lot of
questions related to IB and to test my knowledge of the field. They also asked me questions on Index,
Inflation, Repo Rates, and yesterday's market closing price. They also asked me if I knew what valuation
is to which I answered yes and then they asked me to explain the DCF Model, WACC, and Terminal
Value. Thereafter they asked me a few puzzles and the interview ended with me posing a question to the
panelists.

5. Interview Round 2

The round was scheduled after only about 5 minutes from the completion of my Interview Round 1. Like
the previous Interview, it started with my Introduction. Coincidentally he asked me a lot of the same
questions from the last interview. Concepts like Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Cash Flow Statement,
Index, Inflation etc were asked. He then enquired about the latest current affairs in the field of Finance
that I was aware of. There wasn't any major news at that time, but I recalled reading that Nifty had
recently crossed a historical benchmark and so I mentioned that. He then asked me if I invest in Stocks
or do I follow the stock market to which I replied No, but he still asked me to name the top 5 biggest
stocks in India by market cap. He also wanted me to list the top 5 economies by GDP barring India. He
then asked me the reason behind the growth of India's markets, why Investments in India had increased,
and also asked about India's and USA's Inflation rates. He then asked me a puzzle to which I gave the
correct approach but he wanted me to give him the definite answer by doing the maths behind it. The
interview ended with me asking a question to the interviewer.
--- PAGE 3 ---

6. HR Round

It was a very chill round and lasted for not more than 5 minutes. The interviewer asked me to introduce
myself and then asked me what I think my job would entail if selected. Then she enquired about where I
stay and also asked about my further education plans to which I said no, but I mentioned that I had plans
to obtain the CFA certificate. Finally, she asked if I had any questions for her.

Placement process consisted of 3 rounds:

1. Online assessment (was to be taken from college)

2. Technical interview

3. Techno-HR round

A minimum CGPA of 7 or above was mandatory to apply for this job.

1. [Online Assessment] [11/09/24 ]

The Online test was of 1hr 30 minutes duration. It consisted of CS fundamentals mcq(guess the
output(Java based), DBMS, OOPS), a 20 marks sql query and a 50 marks coding question. The
coding question was similar to: String generation
The SQL question was straightforward, with no questions involving joins or subqueries. Make
sure to practice questions involving date as a column (extracting the day, month, and year from a
date column), as this was required in the question.
I believe I answered most of the MCQs correctly, solved the SQL question accurately, and passed
5 out of 10 test cases in the coding question.
35 students were shortlisted for the next round.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. [Technical Interview] [ 12/09/24 ]

There were 9 panelists, each with 3 or 4 students assigned to them. In my panel, there were 4
students, including me, and I was interviewed last. My interview took place after the lunch
break, so don't worry if your interview starts late.
The interview didn't begin with the typical 'introduce yourself' question. Instead, the interviewer
asked, 'What do you think is unique about Barclays that makes you want to join?' I gave three
answers (always try to include the RISES values of Barclays in such questions), but after each
one, he said, 'Every tech company has that or does that.' I think he was testing my ability to stay
confident. Even though I mentioned some of the tech stack that Barclays uses, like Java, he still
asked, 'You don't have experience with the company's tech stack, so why are you applying for
this job?' Don't panic at such questions. Answer confidently-- they're just testing how well
you handle pressure and stand by your reasonsạẠại
After that, he moved on to the 'Introduce yourself' question. Then, he asked about my first
project, where I had built an ARIMA model (a time series prediction model) and he asked me to
explain it. He also asked about all the keywords I had mentioned in that project.
I had also listed a data analytics project involving SQL and PowerBI, so he asked if I was
proficient in SQL. I said yes, and he then asked if I knew about triggers and views in SQL. While
I understood the concepts, I wasn't familiar with the exact syntax, so I explained the concepts
and also mentioned stored procedures. He then asked me to write a stored procedure that takes
three parameters and returns a result, which I was able to do. Next, he handed me a blank sheet
of paper and asked me to write everything I knew in SQL (primarily syntax) and explain it to
him. I somehow forgot about joins at that moment. He then asked, 'Do you know about joins?' I
said yes, and he asked me to explain the ones I was familiar with, so I described inner, right, left,
and full outer joins.
Next, he asked about OOP concepts and told me to write a skeleton structure on paper explaining
the four pillars of OOP. I explained each pillar with examples by writing code. He allowed me to
choose any programming language.
Then, he asked basic DSA questions, starting with the selection sort algorithm and then merge
sort. He asked me to explain both algorithms and write pseudocode for each. After that, he
moved on to a project I had mentioned that involved ReactS. He asked me some questions about
ReactJS concepts. I didn't know some of the terms he mentioned, so I confidently told him I
wasn't familiar with them. Then he asked me to differentiate between props and state(a standard
question of react), which I had prepared for in advance.
Finally, he asked about my major project (a hardware project) and told me to explain what we
were doing in it. After I explained, he confirmed for clarification and said, 'Okay, you're doing
--- PAGE 3 ---
this in your project, great.' He then said, 'I'm done with your interview, do you have any
questions for me?' (Make sure to prepare two good questions for the interviewer, as it shows your
interest in the company.)
After this round o total of 22 students were selected for the 2nd round.

3. [HR round] [ 12/09/24 ]

This round was a mix of technical and HR questions. It began with my introduction, followed by
questions about my project, such as where I got the dataset and why I chose to do the project.
Then, he asked why Python is mostly used for data analytics over other languages. Since I had
mentioned pandas in my project, he asked how to join two dataframes using pandas, and what a
numpy array is.
Next, he indirectly asked about normalization by giving an example of a table with student id,
student name, course_id, and course_name. He asked if we could add a course without any
student opting for it. I said no, explaining that it would cause an insertion anomaly, so we would
need to decompose the table. I suggested creating two tables- one for students and one for
coursesso we could add courses independently. When he asked how to access both tables
together, I explained that we would join the tables and use a primary key and foreign key to
reference between them. He seemed satisfied with my answer.
Then, he asked a situational question: 'If your team lead proposes an idea, but you have a better
one, how would you suggest it without offending the team lead?' He asked another similar
question. Finally, he noticed I had mentioned GitHub on my resume and asked, 'What is
GitHub?' which I answered.
At the end, he said, 'I'm done with my questions, do you have any questions for me?' (Make sure
to have two questions prepared, which don't necessarily need to be technical, to show your
interest in the company.)
A total of 19 grads were selected for the job.

gather your thoughts, don't hesitate to politely ask for a couple of minutes before answering. This shows you're
thoughtful and considerate in your responses.

you faced, and how you overcame them.
