The company's Pre-Placement Talk was on the same day as the test. The PPT took place at 1:30 pm, followed
by the test at 3:00 pm.

Round 1: Coding Round [177 candidates appeared for this round]

The test duration was 2 hours.

The test consisted of -
7 Aptitude MCQs: You can practice these from Indiabix
4 coding questions (3 DSA + 1 SQL):

1. First question was similar to https://leetcode.com/problems/process-tasks-using-servers/description/

2. Second question was just to determine if the given address is Ipv4 or Ipv6 using the given constraints

3. Third question was  similar to https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-profit-in-job-

scheduling/description/

4. SQL query was comparatively hard. It consisted of 3 tables - Shape, Color and a Relation table. Query

was to find the shapes having exactly 2 colors and its given percentage and print the output in such
format - "Circle Yellow Red 100"

I completed 2 coding questions having all the test cases passed.
And I was only able to print "Shape name and Percentage" as the SQL output.

Practice Leetcode medium questions, and focus on topics like 2 pointers, priority queue,  stack, dynamic
programming.

Round 2: Technical Interview 1 [28 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was 40-45 mins long.
First, the interviewer asked me to introduce myself
Then a simple question on string. A list of strings was given, and the question was to segregate the strings into
two different lists based on the length of the strings.
The next question was to c reate schema for Books and their respective Authors . Make sure to correctly
create the schema and include the necessary primary keys and foreign keys, since the interviewer will
ask further queries on the same schema that you created.
Easy to moderate SQL queries starting from simple ORDER BY to JOIN and subqueries, on the same schema
I created.
Then he asked me what I knew about object -oriented programming and what its characteristics were . I
explained to him about classes and objects and told him the 4 pillars of OOPS. On this, he asked me to explain
the meaning of "Encapsulation". I explained this to him by giving an example. He was satisfied with my
answers, and I was selected for the Interview Round 2.

Round 3: Technical Interview 2 [20 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was 35-40 mins long and a tough one.
I was only asked 3 questions. An SQL Query, A Leetcode 2 pointer problem, and the last which I had no idea
how to solve - A question regarding File System using object-oriented programming.
SQL Query - Two tables were given Order and Customer. A simple query which required the use of JOIN,
GROUP BY and HAVING clause. I gave him two queries, one using subqueries and one using JOIN.
Leetcode Problem - The question was similar to . I first explained to him my approach with a pseudo code.
Then he told me to write the entire code using any language of my choice. I wrote the entire code in python
and he was satisfied with my answer.
File System Problem - There is a class named 'File' and a class named 'Directory'. The class File has a
method getsize() that directly gives us the size of that file. But the class Directory doesn't have any such
method that could give us its size. So, the question was to write a code in oops using your preferred language
to give any directory's size. The first thing that came to my mind was to check how many files are there in the
directory, then call the getsize() method of all those files and then sum it up and return the answer. So, while
writing the code for it, I realized that a directory can also have multiple directories, and those can have more
directories and so on. My mind completely went blank. After 15 -20 mins, the interviewer told me that this
was hardly a 3-4 lines code. At that time, I gave up and apologized to him, and told him that I am not able to
find the desired solution for the question and asked him to explain how to solve it. The way to solve this
question is using Recursion. Recursively go through the directories until a file is found then return the

getsize() method of that file. But it's not like I was silent the entire time. I explained how I would design this
File System; I told him my approach whether right or wrong.
And finally, I was selected by the company as an SDE. A total of  6 were selected (4 were for internship +
placement and 2 were selected for internship only). I was selected for both internship and placement.

1. Resume Shortlisting

2. Aptitude

3. Group Discussion

4. Technical + HR Round 1

5. HR Round

6. Technical + HR Round 2

Round 1: Resume Shortlisting Round [100+ candidates had applied.]

The students who wished to appear for KPMG's process had to fill out the form provided by the
company on their platform, which was HirePro. We could choose only one role between IPCG and
Digital Trust; I chose Digital Trust. We were asked details regarding our active backlogs (those who had
active backlogs weren't allowed for the further process) and our CGPA's (strictly above 6.0 throughout
the engineering tenure). Other than the aforementioned restrictions, all the students who applied and
filled out the form correctly were allowed to continue the process.
Note: Having a high CGPA opens a lot of doors, especially during placements and, to some extent,
higher studies. Be consistent in your academics, and it'll pay off in the long run. If you have any
pending backlogs while you're reading this, please make sure to clear them as soon as possible because
they'll cause you a lot of trouble during placements. There isn't a single company on campus that
entertains poor academics.

Round 2: Aptitude Round [93 candidates appeared for this round.] [Time: 55 minutes]

The aptitude round was conducted in online mode on the HirePro platform. It lasted for about 55
minutes, the test had a total of 45 questions which were divided into 3 sections which were: Analytical
Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Verbal Ability. We were able to navigate between sections and
there was no time limit per section. In my opinion, the quality of the questions asked was of medium
difficulty.
I'd prepared for the aptitude round using the following materials:

1. CareerRide's Quantitative Aptitude Playlist:

[https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLpyc33gOcbVA4qXMoQ5vmhefTruk5t9lt]

2. IndiaBix: [https://www.indiabix.com/]

3. Quantitative Aptitude by R.S. Aggarwal. [Link for the same.]

Following any one of these resources would be more than enough vis -à-vis aptitude tests for on-campus
placements. Companies only ask basic questions in their filtering tests.

PPT: We were called at 10:30 AM on the 1st of October for the pre-placement talk; a few candidates
didn't show up for the process, which was noted by the TPC's, and those candidates were given
demerits.
The pre-placement talk lasted for 30 minutes, as we'd been asked to attend IPCG's PPT too, so we
already had an idea about KPMG and the role for which we're applying. The PPT was taken by the HR
and partner; the partner talked about the role for a while and then asked us if we had any questions. I
asked a few questions regarding the responsibilities and career growth.
I was taking notes, and since I kept interacting with the team during the PPT, I was noticed by all of
them.

Round 3: Group Discussion [29 candidates appeared for this round.] [30 seconds of ideation time + 10

minutes of group discussion + 1 minute for conclusion]
The candidate pool was divided between IPCG and DT after the test; the division was done on the basis
of the candidate's preference and their resume. The IPCG group had their process a day before ours.
For digital trust, we were divided into 3 panels of 10 candidates each. My panel had very active members;
the topic given to us was "Phenomenon of Influencer Marketing." The panellists/judges for this GD were
the same partner who took the PPT at KPMG with over 14 years of experience and a director. I took a
total of 2 entries and h ad very good points and referenced with real -life examples (which is the most
important aspect in a GD). Firstly, I talked about the loyal fan base of an influencer and how greatly it

affects the sales of any product that they market. Then I talked about the fact that start-ups are able to get
great exposure due to the same and how it has given the start-ups the much-needed platform early in their
business and that they can target the fan bases who would genuinely be interested in their products by
talking with the influencers. I also talked about a few negative aspects of the same: many influencers have
started buying followers in order to reach fame quickly, which has negatively affected the overall social
media space and has opened up a lot of attack vectors for threat actors. I also referenced the recent (Beer
Biceps) Ranveer Allahbadia's case that, due to fame, there's also the over looming threat of being victim
to a cyberattack.
Points to remember : Apart from your content, your performance and approach  to group discussions
leave an impression on the panellists. As the panellists are the ones to take your interviews, it's important
to actively participate in the GD, communicate your thoughts, listen to your peers, and always be
supportive and positive during the GDs. If someone is struggling to recall any phrases or words, do help
them out, as it leaves a very positive impression and is also a sign that you're actively listening to them.
If, perhaps, you happen to disagree with any points, have a very res pectful tone during the same; also, if
you try to enter and happen to be interrupted, let the other party go first. As this happened to me, I said,
"I'd like to hear your point first and would like to go after you." This shows respect and politeness.
After the GD, the panellists asked us to conclude; he pointed out 2 people to give the conclusion; they
hadn't spoken much or at all during the GD, hence the reason. Everybody in my panel performed pretty
well. Since my colleagues were struggling with English, they switched to Hindi/Marathi during their
entries, which is absolutely fine. The panellists pointed out as well that it's nothing to be ashamed of if
you're not fluent with English and if you'd like to speak in Hindi or your regional language instead. Your
voice modulation/enunciation, GD etiquette, and poise matter more during a GD than your control over
English.
Note: Before the GD began, the partner/panellist had asked us for our resume, and after the GD ended,
he immediately pointed out two people whose resume, in comparison to the rest of the participants, was
extremely lacking, their resume formatting was poor, and that he isn't happy with them at all. He tried
to reason with them further but gave up after their casual responses.
This set the tone for the further rounds that the team is not here to mess around or have fun.
A total of 17 candidates were shortlisted for the further processes. Four candidates from IPCG were
further added to the list on the recommendation of their interviewers, which had happened a day before.

Most of my interview rounds were skipped due to my GD performance. Keep this in mind and do well in
your GD itself.

Round 4: Technical + HR Interview 1 [21 candidates appeared for this round.] [20 minutes]

My interview was conducted by the same partner I mentioned earlier, along with his colleague, a director. I
entered the room and put my hand forth for a firm handshake; this again leaves a good impression. I
asked to take a seat, and they started the interview by asking my introduction. In the introduction, I
emphasized more on my cybersecurity skills and the relevant industry experience which I'd gained during
my internships, as well as the soft skills I'd developed through both work and extracurricular activities.
My interview was mainly taken by the director; he was focusing more on my resume and the wordings
that I'd used and told me to elaborate on them. Throughout the duration of the interview, I remained
calm and composed, focused on the questions, and answered them promptly. As I knew the inside out of
the resume, I was able to understand the terminology that they were using (the terms that they used were
specific to cybersecurity only, such as "hardening guidelines," "configuration management," and
"improving the security posture.") The director further grilled me on the technical aspects of my
resume; he wanted to know the kind of work I did during my internships down to the minute details.
He also asked me, why not continue on with that company and why KPMG? I'd prepared extensively
for this question, so I confidently answered it. They liked that, and they also wanted to check if I'd leave
KPMG after the duration of my internship. I answered the same as well, that I'd definitely continue with
KPMG after my internship.
Overall, they only wanted to take a gander in seeing how well I maintain my composure during serious
situations and how this would translate into my work once I joined. Finally, they asked me about the
people whom I worked with during my internships and if it's alright to call my manager and ask him for
my review. I confidently told them to go ahead; they liked that too. After which they asked me how
confident I am about this interview. I told them that I'm pretty confident that I'll make through; they
appreciated that very much and then asked me to go for the HR interview.
The director was solely focusing on my resume throughout the interview, I'd been told by my seniors
that they wish to see how well you perform under pressure, as consulting is a stressful job.
Note: A few of my improvement areas: I could've been calmer and registered each question first before
answering it, all of which only comes through rigorous practice.
There was no formal list sent out for the further shortlists; I'm not aware of how many were shortlisted
for the further rounds. Many of the candidates did not perform well in their interviews, which was
highlighted by the team to the TPCs. Around 4 were instantly rejected after their first round.
The first Techno-HR round was pretty easy for the rest of the people, as all of them were asked CCN
fundamentals and basic cybersecurity questions; practicing the same a few days before the interviews
would be sufficient.

Study material for Cybersecurity:
Computer Networks:
Atul Sharma's playlist. Focus more on Cisco Packet Tracer and OSI layers as both shall build your
fundamentals.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2mvn4eOOVZo
NetworkChuck's playlist for CCN fundamentals. He makes studying CCN very fun.
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLIhvC56v63IJVXv0GJcl9vO5Z6znCVb1P

Cybersecurity: Study OWASP Top 10, basic attack vectors like CORS, XSS, CSRF and so on. Also,
study viruses, botnets, malware and ransomware attacks. Be up to date on current events for
cybersecurity.
Practicing DVWA Labs and Metasploitable2 Labs shall give you an in-depth idea about the attacks.
OWASP Top 10: https://www.hacksplaining.com/
DVWA Labs: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLHUKi1UlEgOJLPSFZaFKMoexpM6qhOb4Q

Round 5: HR Interview [~12 candidates appeared for this round.] [25 minutes.]

I was told by the HR manager that this would be my last round and that they're happy with my
performance so no further rounds would be conducted for me, but she'd asked me to stick around if I'm
free for the rest of the day, that is.
After my Techno-HR round wrapped up, I was immediately called for the HR round. The HR manager
who was taking my interview was very chill, and she asked me about my day, how my previous
interview went, and the toughest question that they'd asked. I responded in a formal manner though, and
she seemed pretty satisfied with my answers. She then proceeded to ask me about my family, where I'm
from, and which location I'd prefer.
After which she proceeded to ask me about my weaknesses and what went wrong in my previous
interviews, which was holding me back from being placed. I realized that this was one of the deciding
questions for this interview, so I gave a very humble and serious answer: Throughout this placement
journey, I had to do a lot of self-introspection; hence, after each interview I started listing out what went
wrong and what I should improve on, following which the most recent interview that I couldn't crack
was of Barclay's Bank, where I believed that one of my improvement areas should be confidence, so I
practiced for the interviews to improve my confidence. I gave more interviews to my friends and in
front of the mirror in order to be more fluent during the interviews. She seemed very happy with this
answer; furthermore, she asked me if I'm interested in higher studies, to which I replied that I'm more
interested in pursuing the cybersecurity certifications rather than the MBA or MS. She seemed satisfied

with the answer and told me that I'm done for the day and if she needs anymore details, she'd call for
me, and whether I'd have any questions for her, I asked her about the career growth in my role, and she
answered it.
Overall, the interview was very chill, and I was the one driving it; this led to me being much more
relaxed than my previous one. This was the end of the entire process for me.
A few of my friends were being interviewed late into the night; the entire process lasted till 8 PM. I
stayed around to accompany my colleagues and asked them about their experience. The third round,
which was the Techno-HR 2, was the hardest for the rest; the interviewers were grilling them a lot, and
hence no one was confident about the results, but we kept our heads high and hoped for the best.

The results were announced two days after the process, a total of 6 people were selected and I was
one of them!

Pointers for Placement Processes:

1. Try to attempt seriously for the processes of most (or all) the companies, regardless of the role.

You'll get an idea of the interview processes and the kind of pressure that you'll be under during
the entirety of the process which shall prepare you for the next process or your target company.
KPMG was my 4th interview and the 1st company with my dream role, the role for which I'd
prepared extensively for about a year.
Once you start giving more interviews, you get an idea about the kind of questions are asked and
how you should tackle such questions and what kind of answers they're expecting on their end.
After participating in the interviews, try to write down a similar transcript as this, so you'll
understand where exactly you went wrong and where exactly you require more improvement.
Not everyone is born perfect, the more your practice the closer you shall get to cracking
interviews.

2. Do participate in national level competitions. A lot of my interviewers focused on my case study

competitions and extra-curricular tournaments which I'd participated in, rather than my
internships which was pretty surprising but understandable as they're more familiar with their
area of expertise rather than mine. The same opens up different dialogues during your interviews
which may result in your favor.

3. Do not lose hope. Placements are draining but you should never lose hope. You'll definitely get

placed, luckily for me I had a lot of well-wishers consisting of my family and friends and they

were always backing me up during my journey. Please do not hesitate to call up your family
members or friends during placements, as placements take up most of your mental space, we
must let lose sometimes and hence go for a couple of outings as you'll feel lighter and more
motivated for the next process.
Further pointers for placements in general:
Placement season is quite taxing, mentally and physically as well, but they're part and parcel of
engineering. You can treat them as a part of your development/improvement journey which was what I
did or look at them as a line item and try to tackle them as soon as possible.
I tried my level best for a few companies but their requirements were different. I still didn't lose hope
and neither should you. Being selected and getting placed on-campus becomes one of your highlights in
your engineering tenure, if you do not get selected in your dream company or your dream role, it's
absolutely fine because we still have our entire lives ahead of us to strive for the best and we must
always reach for the stars.

If you wish to call me, please send me a message on WhatsApp.

All the very best! You can do it.

journey.howSecured:
The placement process had 4 rounds consisting of resume shortlisting, test-based shortlisting, interview-1
and interview-2. There was no separate HR interview, but HRs from the company were present in both the
interviews and asked some HR-type questions. There was an online pre-placement talk by the company
prior to the entire process where they detailed what the company does, its growth, industry position and
values, as well as what the job role would demand and offer. It is important to pay attention here, as you can
then modify your resume/ interview answers to be better aligned with the job role and company. It is also
useful in answering HR questions.

1. Round 1: Resume Shortlisting (Candidates: roughly 200)

The resume shortlisting is generally done based on the company's requirements and job roles. The most
important thing here is to prepare a job-role and company specific resume. Highlighting more
development projects/skills in a data science role or vice versa will not be much helpful. It is unclear
whether CGPA was a criteria. It is always good to keep a CGPA above 8.5. I had worked on machine
learning and data science projects, which was very relevant to this role. For each project explain what the
project did, the methods it used, the technologies used, and results obtained. Do NOT lie about something
you didn't do, as you are grilled on the projects in further rounds. It is also good to have 1 extracurricular
activity showing yourself as team player/leader. I used 2 ML projects, 3 data science projects and my
experience as an HOD Creatives at Oculus in my resume. Lists of relevant skills are given at the end.
124 candidates from 200 were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Written Test (Aptitude, SOL) (Candidates:

124) Interestingly this test was conducted by pen and paper. It had 10 questions to be solved in 25 mins. There

were 6 aptitude type MCQ questions, 3 SQL questions and 1 very simple coding question. The questions
were very much doable. Because of the time constraint you had to do them fast. Almost all students could
solve most of the questions, and hence only 2-3 questions became the deciding ones. Only students who got
9/10, 10/10 were probably shortlisted. The questions covered mathematical and logical aptitude, SQL
aggregate functions, sorting and joins. The coding question was to simply sum numbers from 1 - N.
However as the papers were checked manually by the recruiting team, using the formula (N(N+1))/2 could
be an edge over recursion/loop. Only Python/ pseudocode was allowed. Keeping a calm and focused head
will easily let you pass such a test.
--- PAGE 2 ---
38 candidates from 124 were shortlisted for the next round.

3. Interview Round 1 (Candidates:

38) This round started with the recruiters asking me to introduce myself. Keep an introduction prepared

beforehand (company and role-specific of course) highlighting the relevant coursework, skills and passion
for the field. The panel consisted of 3 recruiters, one of them was an HR.
They took my resume and one by one started covering my projects. They picked up keywords/concepts
from my project descriptions and asked me to explain it/ asked me related questions. Some questions that
they asked are: difference in HAVING and GROUP BY. These are not actually differing but are keywords
that are used together. I explained how they worked and also gave an example. (HAVING lets you put
checks on aggregate results obtained by GROUP BY) They asked me to explain how window functions
worked, and list some of them. I again gave an overview of the concept and followed it with an example.
(Window functions calculate values in a running fashion over rows, assigning the values to each row while
keeping each row intact. Most aggregate functions can be used as window functions. Others are: RANK,
DENSE_RANK, NTILE, ROW_NUMBER, etc.) Mentioning OVER, PARTITION BY, and window
function aliases could be a plus. Mention only those words/ terms you can explain, as you could be
cross-questioned. This was followed by a simple Python question to explain difference in sets and lists,
and explain some of their characteristics. (Sets are like a bag, sets can't have duplicates, sets are
unordered, lists follow the order they are subjected to, etc) Next they asked what is a confusion matrix. I
explained its structure and usage as a metric for classification models. Then they asked about false positives
and what does it mean when there is a high number of false positives. (False positives are results
classified as positive class by a model when they were actually of the negative class. More false positives
indicate uneven distribution of classes in the training dataset, it could have more positive class entries
leading to biased training of the model. I should have also detailed that another reason could be using an
erroneous threshold while classifying.)
Next they asked a case study type question: What factors will I consider to decide a suitable location
for a Zudio store. Here your knowledge of current trends comes handy as it is important to know Zudio is
focused on making fashion affordable and cheap. I first highlighted that Zudio targets middle class and
lower middle class populations so those areas must be recognised. For this I first thought of collecting
incomes of residents in an area but then realized that it was personal to collect such data and the collection
will also prove to be difficult. Then I suggested collecting the housing prices and rent prices in the area to
gauge what kind of area it was. I also suggested analyzing local shops and the prices they provide, especially
clothing shops, and whether any branded/ top end entities existed. After recognising a suitable middle/lower
middle class area, I further noted that Zudio is much more popular in the youth. Hence I must find a
road/junction where there is a constant stream of young people such as near a college, mall, movie screens
etc. This will make the shop more visible to its target market. (Note: I had never prepared for such
non-tech questions before, I was focused only on SDE or data science kind of roles. I just went ahead with
what I thought was logical at the moment and kept explaining my thought process clearly.)
The recruiters seemed satistied with my answer. Lastly, the HR asked me to explain one of my hobbies. I
am very passionate about graphic designing, so I explained what I do, the tools I use, and where I have used
them. (Maybe I went a little overboard:)). The interview ended in a happy/friendly mood due to this.
15 students from 38 were shortlisted for the final round.

4. Interview Round 2 (Candidates:

15) --- PAGE 3 ---

This interview was much more serious-toned than the previous one. They only asked one case study
question: How will you diagnose delays in loan repayment in tier-2 cities and what methods could you
undertake to avoid them. I literally used the first 5-7 mins to understand what they were actually asking
me to do. The interviewers were helpful and explained how loan repayment works and that reminders are
sent via telecom centers in Mumbai to loan bearers in tier-2 cities regarding their installments. I fumbled a
bit in the start and then slowly narrowed down to various points which I noted on the pen and paper
provided. Firstly I stated that some borrowers are incurable, that is they are taking ibad loans' which cannot
be supported by their income. We should avoid such customers by analyzing their income before giving a
loan. Next I surmised that people delaying repayment are already lacking ethics, hence they can only be
made to repay by threatening them with their own loss. They should be made aware of the consequent effect
on their CIBIL score, increasing interest rates, and possible legal action. (Effect on collaterals is another
possible threat). The interviewers were satisfied, and further asked how this awareness could be created if
the current telecom system mentioned is not being effective.
One interviewer suggested thinking around a system where loan repayment reminder teams can be sent
to the borrower's homes. I suggested two approaches: I had heard about third party companies which
provide the services of collecting loan repayments using their own mechanisms. So such a company's
services can be hired. Secondly a team based system design could be made where each team is assigned
certain households to visit in a day. Upon visiting, they meet the borrower, familiarize him with his situation,
remind him about the repayment and list out the threats. They also do a OTP/QR based two-way verification
with the borrower. This will be a consent on the borrower's side that he has recognised what could be the
consequences of his delay in repayment and a confirmation from the team's side proving that the household
was visited. This verification's location could be tracked in the centers located in Mumbai. Failing to do the
verification on the customer side would result in one of the threats being implemented, and failure from the
teams' side would count against the teams' performance. This will prevent any malpractice/bribing. The
interviewers were satisfied with this.
Some of my friends were asked guesstimates. Guesstimates are absolutely essential for data science/
non-tech roles and they can't be overlooked. Most of the case studies/guesstimates asked were in a way
related to services that InCred provides. Hence skimming through the company's website and gaining
more information about their services/products is helpful.
5 candidates from the final 15 were selected for the job role.

problem of medium difficulty and another that was quite challenging.

Questions with Solutions

¡Technical Round (Projects, OOP, Brain Teasers] | No of candidates who appeared for this round =>

Polymorphism, Abstraction, and Encapsulation. I was asked to implement these concepts in Java using pen
and paper and to elucidate their practical applications. Following this, I was asked to delineate the
differences between Hash Set and Hashmap, including their implementation in Java, typical use cases, and
the time complexities associated with various operations performed on them. I was also provided with a
scenario and had to discern which data structure would be most efficacious.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Subsequently, the interviewer presented a diagram and asked me to identify the number of squares within it.
This was followed by a similar task involving the identification of triangles. Later, I was instructed to
rearrange some triangles to form the maximum possible number of squares.
The interview then shifted focus to my resume, where I was questioned about my projects. The questions
revolved around the problems I aimed to solve with these projects, the benefits to others, the most arduous
challenges encountered during development, and the solutions I devised. I was also asked about potential
optimizations, the rationale behind choosing particular technologies, and alternative technologies that could
have been employed. Finally, the interviewer inquired about REST APIs and their alternatives, and asked me
to compose two SQL queries.
[Technical and HR Round(DSA + HR)I [ No of candidates who appeared for this round > 19]
The interviewer began by asking me about the programming language of my choice, before delving into the
fundamentals of Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA). Initially, I was asked to elucidate the structure and
representation of both singly and doubly linked lists. Following this, I was tasked with rotating a linked list
by k positions-- Link to the code. Next, I was questioned on the representation of trees using linked lists
and the distinctions between trees and graphs. The interviewer also probed into the practical applications of
trees and graphs, asking me to choose the appropriate data structure for a given scenario.
Further, I was asked which traversals are necessary to construct a unique binary tree-Link to the code. I
was also asked to print the top view of a binary tree - Link to the code. For all these questions, I was
required to write the code on pen and paper.
The interview then moved to the HR segment. I was asked to "Tell me about yourself," followed by the
question, "Why do you want to work for Oracle?" The interviewer also inquired about my hobbies. Having

which I responded with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. I shared an anecdote about him - here's the link, and
with that, the round was concluded.

Process had a total of 3 rounds, before that there was a resume-based shortlisting.

1. Written Assessment [ No of candidates who appeared for this round - 123 - after resume shortlisting]

The assessment was divided into three sections: SQL, Python, and Aptitude (Quants), lasting 25 minutes.
The Aptitude section involved multiple-choice questions, while the SQL and Python sections required
writing SQL queries and Python code, respectively.

• SQL Section: This section included two queries focusing on joins, GROUP BY, HAVING, and

WHERE clauses, along with an output-based question on different types of joins. The difficulty level
ranged from easy to medium.

• Python Task: This task involved writing a program to calculate the sum of n numbers, which was

straightforward. Using the formula instead of a loop might give an edge.

• Aptitude Section: This section contained logical questions of easy to medium difficulty,

emphasizing speed and accuracy.
To prepare for the Aptitude section, practicing questions from IndiaBix should suffice. For the SQL section,
a solid grasp of the basics is crucial, as the questions are typically not too challenging.

2. Interview Round 1 [ 38 students were shortlisted for this round]

The interview began with a self-introduction. The interviewers then reviewed my resume and focused on my
project, particularly my contributions to the machine learning aspect. I discussed my work on the diet
recommendation part using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) with cosine similarity. They asked about the
algorithm, how it works, the dataset used, and the preprocessing steps involved.
Next, I was presented with a guesstimate question, estimating the number of Pepsi bottles sold in a year. I
clarified doubts with the interviewers, such as the type of bottles considered. It's important to articulate your
--- PAGE 2 ---
thought process aloud during these exercises. If you need time, it's perfectly acceptable to ask for a moment
to organize your thoughts.
At the end of the interview, always ask questions about the company or role to demonstrate your interest and
preparation, leaving a positive impression.

3. Interview Round 2 [15 students were shortlisted for this round]

This round involved three panelists, including an HR representative. They began with a self-introduction and
then asked about my native place. Since my projects had already been discussed, they moved on to case
studies.

• Case Study 1: I was asked to assume the role of the India head of Amazon and propose strategies to

increase the company's profitability. I suggested identifying areas where Amazon might be losing
profit, such as issues with damaged goods, and addressing these sources to reduce returns and
enhance profitability. Additionally, I proposed reducing delays in shipping and addressing higher
costs and longer delivery times for international goods.

• Case Study 2: I was asked how to increase the profits of InCred, focusing on personal loans. I

suggested identifying the primary reasons people seek personal loans and targeting these segments
with tailored marketing and sales campaigns.
The round concluded with me asking the panelists about InCred's future initiatives and plans, which shows
interest in the company's direction and long-term goals.
5 students were offered the job.

A total of 3 rounds were conducted as a part of the placement process, before any rounds could be
conducted, there was a resume-based shortlisting. 46 students were shortlisted for the role of DA after the
resume round. Below listed are the 3 rounds:

1. SQL Round

2. SQL + Guesstimates Round

3. HR Round

1. Round 1: SQL Round [ 46 students ]

In the first round, I was interviewed by a panel of one full timer. This was a SQL round, first the interviewer
asked me to introduce myself.
Pro Tip #1: Make sure your introduction is not more than 30-40 seconds long, if the
interviewer still wants to ask something he/she will. Do not over answer.
The interviewer picked up a SQL project from my resume which caught his eye, it was a Data Analytics
project. I was told to explain what I did in that project and what all could I conclude, later he built up on the
same project by adding two more tables to the original dataset. All the 3 queries asked to me later in the
round were based on the additional tables.
The queries ranged from leetcode easy to leetcode hard level problems. The first one was a simple join
query, the second one was a bit tricky and also involved calculations on date. The third was a complex
query involving subqueries, the interviewer was pretty chill and helped me by providing hints for the third
one. (Although he asked me to drop the question because he wanted me to ask another theory question)
--- PAGE 2 ---
Pro Tip #2: Whenever you are solving the question, make sure you first discuss the
approach with the interviewer. Keep explaining as you continue to write the solution.
The final question was a theory question on the different types of window functions and the difference
between them. The round lasted for about 50 minutes.

2. Round 2: SQL + Guesstimates [ 24 students ]

For the second round, there was a panel of two full timers. This was a guesstimates round, so after asking
me to introduce myself, they asked me to find the number of ACs in Mumbai city. (The resources for the
same have been provided at the end). The first part of this question was to find the number of ACs in
households while the second part involved public places.
Pro Tip #3: Ask questions related to the problem statement. For example, do we also
need to consider ACs in the buses and metros?
The second question was a case study based question about Swiggy, they provided me the avg. rating Ra
and Rb for the two verticals of Swiggy (Two verticals are food delivery and instamart). The two questions
on this case study were based on the concept of weighted avg. and distribution of weight in a normal
gaussian distribution. (Both were pretty easy if you have basic knowledge on probability and statistics).
And the final question of this round was a SQL query to find out the cumulative sum of a column without
using the inbuilt function, I was not able to recollect the approach, but was provided with a hint from the
interviewers. This round lasted for almost an hour.
Pro Tip #4: Voh log bhi bore ho jaate hai interviews lete lete, to keep them interested, ask
them some good questions at the end. Questions can be related to work culture, technical
questions, etc.

3. Round 3: HR Round [ 9 students ]

The HR round was the last round. It started off with introducing myself, then the interviewer asked me the
reason why I chose to apply for this role and what excites me about data analytics. The mistake I made in
the HR round was over answering, because of which the topic shifted from data analytics to something
else. I realized this at the end of the interview when I asked him one good thing and one bad thing about my
interview, and he replied, "You went a bit off topic, keep that in mind the next time". I tried to cover it up by
explaining things from a different perspective. (Which I thought would not work, but did :)). This round
again lasted for an hour.
Pro Tip #5: Again, DO NOT make the same mistake as me. Jitna pucha hai utna hi jawab
do. Every question the HR asks is related to the job profile, toh thoda profile and thoda
apna point mix karke jawab do.
A total of 5 students were finally offered the job including me.
--- PAGE 3 ---

journey.prep:
The most important thing about placement season you need to understand is that there is a large
amount of luck involved here. You can increase your chances by practicing as much as possible but in
the end you really need good luck (only once ;)).
I did not get through 5 companies before landing this offer. All that went wrong was pure bad luck. My
resume was not shortlisted for Work India even though I prepared a lot for it and I verified it from one of the
senior employees itself, it was purely random. Same thing happened with JPMC and there was nothing I
could do about it. So be ready that even though your resume is great and according to the JD it could not be
shortlisted.
When I finally landed my first interview for MSCI, it went horribly wrong as the interviewer was very
difficult to impress and was asking the toughest of questions, it was least likely to qualify for the further
rounds though him (hardly anyone could). Same thing repeated for IDFC too!. Be ready that you might get
a tough interviewer and your interview might go completely different from others and in a bad way.
Then I was not selected after the HR round of InCred even though everything went as perfect as they
could've just because the seats were limited. So be ready for rejections even if you have answered
everything perfectly well.
These are mentally tough times to process as it takes a lot of effort from some to achieve it while it happens
in the first for some. What is important is to not give up and embrace the process instead of stressing about
it. Have trust in yourself, and it will work out, just keep grinding consistently till it happens and it will
happen !!
--- PAGE 4 ---
Resources.

1) DSA: Striver Sheet (Make sure to do only sufficient amount depending on the companies you are

targeting, for eg PhonePe requires a lot of DSA, others comparatively lesser so don't utilize your
entire time doing DSA)

2) C++: Saurabh Shukla Playlist is a 10 year old playlist but it is still a goldmine when it comes to

explaining OOPs concepts.

3) SQL: LeetCode Top 50 SQL questions are enough.

Feel free to contact me for any help on my LinkedIn profile.
journey.howSecured:
There were 3 rounds for this process all within the span of two days. Make sure you are prepared beforehand
as you will be notified a day prior to the OA Test and the Interviews of shortlisted candidates is on the next
day itself.

1. Round 1: Online Aptitude Test [ 208 students appeared and it was conducted in college]

There were 30 MCQS: 15 Technical - Java, SQL, DBMS and 15 Aptitude.
There was 1 coding question and it was important to solve it fully to get through.
My Question was after simplification of the word problem into a basic question, it would look something
like this : Given an input string consisting of characters 'a', 'b', and 'c', determine the minimum number of
insertions required to transform the string into a sequence of "abc" repeated multiple times, without
changing the order of existing characters.

2. Round 2: Technical Interview [36 Students appeared in College the next day]

The Round started with Introduction (By this time I had mentioned this already in 4 interviews and I was
well versed in it). Make sure to keep your introduction simple yet elegant, mention those things and
achievements in which you are confident if questions are asked about. The interview started with the
Interviewer going through my Resume and asking me about the mentioned Projects. There was in depth
discussion on the projects
Tip 1: Now you need to understand that asking about your projects is a blessing in
disguise because it is your playground to play with as anything can be asked in core
subjects or DSA but Projects is what you have done and accomplished, so make sure you
know everything about your projects. (Be ready with questions like why you did it? What
problem did you solve? Try to include such projects which are solving real world
problems. Then make sure you have an idea of the tech stacks used and the alternatives
to them and why you chose what is implemented in the Project. Some may even ask to
write code of a particular function)
--- PAGE 2 ---
Then they proceeded to ask about the database schema for my project. They gave me tricky situations
and how I would handle the database. They were satisfied with my application of concepts.
Tip 2: The answers to these questions lied in basic applications of concepts of
Normalization, Candidate Keys, using Relational Database. So make sure when you
study core subjects you understand the concept rather than the theory so as to
understand where they are applicable and what kind of problems they resolve.
Then they asked me to explain about types of Joins in SQL. Now the answer to this question is simple,
but I made sure that I was explaining each type with clarity by communicating and simultaneously
drawing a diagram on the page. So they are satisfied with the answer enough to change the topic.
Then the interviewer asked me about OOPs concepts, what is overriding and give a real life example of
when would you implement it. They expected Java, however I said that my primary language is C++. I
was able to convince them that I possess fundamental conceptual clarity and can easily switch to Java if
necessary. They were very pleased with my answers.
Tip 3: All the Banks majorly use Java so it's a plus if you are already familiar with
it. Make sure to know all the concepts OOPs including real life examples of
applications of each pillar and subtypes. And if you use C++, make sure you know
the difference between them.
Then they asked me about the different types of databases, are you familiar with mongo db? What are
key value pairs? Which is suitable for your project?
Then they asked about my ML project and they wanted to know what was done after the results were
achieved. I explained the purpose of the project and whatever lies beyond the results is out of scope of
the problem.
Tip 4: Here I could've given a simple no as an answer that nothing is done after the
Data Analysis and Model building, but I made sure that the interviewers don't get
disappointed by the limited scope of the project by explaining the procedures I
followed and learning them was the main purpose. This way the interviewers
understand that you have a learning attitude and you learnt something valuable from
the project implementation.
Then they asked me to explain Data Structure and Algorithms in layman terms to someone who doesn't
know anything about it. Then I gave them a detailed explanation using easy to understand terms and
basic understanding of why Data Structures are used and what are they used for and then what is
Algorithms and what are they used for
Tip 5: These types of questions can be answered only when you study concepts with
conceptual clarity. So a tip would be to make sure whenever you are learning
something to constantly ask why? Why is something used, what is the need for it?
Then they asked me a medium- hard DSA question on how will you reach a root node from a leaf node
given that it is a directed acyclic graph pointing from parent to children. This is a tricky question, so
give it a thought !
Then they asked me about my leadership position as Head of Finance and how I manage finances and
did I automate the process.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Then they asked me if I had any questions for them. I asked them two questions. The first one was if
there is a Role in Research and Analytics working on AI/ML engines of the company? They explained
that first you have to work for 18 months before switching to a role and then depending upon the
requirements. Then I asked what if someone faces an unfamiliar technology while working on the
project what are the opportunities provided for upskilling the employee at UBS?

3. Round 3: HR Round Around 20 students appeared for this round

I was called within 15-20 minutes of my first round for HR. This was a very short round which hardly
lasted for 5-10 minutes. Make sure you are well prepared for the generic HR questions on Strengths,
Passion, Future Plans, Family Background. Work preference. Attending ppt is a must and making notes.
Tip 5: HR rounds may seem easy but you have to play safe here, as this is also the
round where you have a lot to lose if something goes wrong as you have worked
hard enough and the luck was in your favor to have qualified till here. So don't take
it lightly, be well prepared with your answers, create an impression. Don't ask for
feedback (never), don't talk about negatives or anything. The atmosphere at all
times should be positive.
12 students were offered the role and I was one of them !!!.

journey.prep:
• Read their requirements and thoroughly prepare your resume to fulfil their requirements as it is an

ATS based selection process.

• Remember to always ask at least 3 questions after the interview is close to a conclusion; this would

let the interviewers know your interest in the process as well as in the company.

• Read gfg logical reasoning problems to prep better for OA as well as interviews.

• Know as much as possible about the company from their website or via the ppt

• Finally remain calm do not get baffled if you answered a question incorrectly just moveon to the

next, remember the interviewers knows only as much as you know.

• Answer as honestly as possible. Consider these rounds more of a behavioral test wherein your every

single gesture is being monitored and evaluated upon. Try not to be nervous or anxious

• Have in depth knowledge of your projects and all the skills that you have mentioned in your resume.

Learn the topic well before mentioning it on your resume.
journey.howSecured:
The selection process consisted of 4 rounds: 1 aptitude test and 3 interviews. Around 100 people had applied
for the application. Out of which only 40 people were selected after the resume shortlisting round. A day
later this was followed by an online quiz that was heavily based on logical reasoning as well as probability
and numerical questions along with code snippets and MCQ. After this round around 14 people were
selected to the interviews.

1. [Tech/Business Round] [14 candidates appeared for this round]

This round consisted of 2 panels. They expect you to have a good knowledge of data structures and
algorithms particularly in python. I was asked questions based on arrays, tuples and concepts of oops like
encapsulation and multiple level inheritance. Then I was asked to write down code on a sheet of paper, the
question was to write a function to calculate the factorial of the given number. The interviewer was
particularly interested in how I would be dealing with any possible errors thrown by the system(try and
catch). Later i was asked about one of my projects followed by a detailed guesstimate round, i would
recommend to memorize the guesstimate sheet given below:
https://180dcsrcc.in/guesstimate-cheat-sheet-2023/
Later on i was asked some questions on basic calculation of probabilities and basic maths. At the end of the
interview they asked me if i had any questions, i asked them 3 questions primarily about work culture and
job position. The interview lasted for about 30-45 mins
2.
Lech/Business Round] [4 candidates appeared for this round]
--- PAGE 2 ---
This round was very different from the earlier one. First I was asked to introduce myself. Later on I was
thoroughly asked about my AIML project and research paper which I was able to explain in depth. I was
asked about image processing and CNN used in my projects along with its model design. Then the topic
shifted to my research paper and my possible motivations for writing the same. I was able to convince
him that it was not a product of my plans for higher studies. Then the topic shifted entirely to ML
wherein I was asked to explain a detailed workflow of how I would approach an AIML problem given
10 parameters. The follow ups were very thorough as the interviewer dealt with AIML on a daily
basis. We talked about how I would clean data using plots and contours along with suitable regression
models for contiguous and non-contiguous data. Next I was asked about how I would optimize a model
now after making it .We dealt in the concepts of mean error and adjusted mean error along with
examples and formulas for calculation of the same. Furthermore I was asked about my knowledge in
automation using VBA which I didn't know about so I explained how I would approach the problem
using Selenium and Pandas. Later I was asked about my ability to maneuver through a new problem
without any external help or support like stackoverflow or chatgpt, i was able to walk him through the
process ( after these questions I asked him 3-5 questions about his role in JPMC along with possible use
of AIML Furthermore I asked about my role in the company) . He was satisfied with my answers after
which I proceeded to the next round.
An in-depth knowledge of AIML and automation would be required at this stage. The interview lasted for
about 45 mins and after 25 mins I was selected for the HR round.

3. [HR Round] [2 appeared for this round]

The HR interview was conducted by 2 female panelists. Both made me comfortable and I was asked
general questions about myself, my family and my interest in the fintech industry. I was asked about the
role and if I understood what it entails. I was asked why JPMC, which I was able to answer based on
their company values and ideas. I was asked questions on my resume as well as I was given a scenario
wherein I had to resolve a conflict. The questions were basic although read through their ppt and
company values on their website. After this I asked 3-5 questions about the work balance, values and
about the role as well as my designation.
2 candidates were selected after this role.

journey.howSecured:
1. Online MCQ (14/08/2024 - 15/08/2024) on HackerEarth

2. Machine Coding

3. Interview

1. MCQ Round [Around 150+ students applied] [Online]

There was a criteria of 7+ CGPA for applying at BrowserStack and everyone got the HackerEarth MCQ test
link which was valid for 2 days and I have given the test on the 2nd day i.e., on 15th Aug.
There were around 20 MCQs which we have to solve in 50 minutes (can be solved within 10 min) consisting
of HTML, CSS, JS, OS, DBMS. If you have basic to moderate knowledge of these fundamentals then you
can solve these MCQs pretty easily.
And a very important point, they not only see your MCQ score but also shortlist based on the resume as well
so make sure you have decent development skills mentioned in your resume. (my resume link)
After this round,
34 students shortlisted for BrowserStack and 22 for EdraLabs (sister company of
BrowserStack). I don't know on what basis they divided the students because the test was common. I was
among 34 students.
There was a clash between JPMC - CR and BorwserStack interview process and hence 14 - 16 people who
got shortlisted for both the companies were asked to choose one just a day before the interview and only 4
students chose BrowserStack including me.
I don't know about the EdraLab process but it was online.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Machine Coding Round [24 people appeared for this round] [Offline] [ 2hrs ]

This round was conducted in their office at Goregaon. We were divided into 6 batches, 3-6 people per batch
and then they sent a problem statement which was the same as last year. They have been using the same
problem statement for the past 2-3 years which you can find on gfg, github, etc.
This was the PS:
https://medium.com/@ibrahimanis/implement-log-watcher-similar-to-tail-f-command-7b0674d4b767
Sometimes they also ask this PS:
https://github.com/harssRajput/browser-stack-round/tree/main/browser_controller
I was prepared for the Log watcher problem as I have already read the GFG interview experience of this
company. We were given 2 hours to build the solution and there were 2 mentors for each batch. Basically
they will help you build the solution but make sure you clearly communicate your ideas and tell them about
the approach bes this will help you in case your solution doesn't work properly. And they will visit you in an
interval of ½ hour to help you guide the solution.
This problem involved using Socket. IO and Node.js file structures, which aren't commonly used by students
when building projects. However, practicing and incorporating these into your projects can give you an edge
in this round. Although they allowed the use of Google and ChatGPT, not being able to explain your code is
seen as a significant red flag. They were more interested in your thinking or approach to solve the problem
rather than seeing the results. You can use any tech stack python, node, java, etc.
After building the solution, my mentor asked how I would optimize it if the log file were several GBs or
larger. I started detailing my approach, and he provided hints whenever I veered off track. Unfortunately, due
to the limited time left, I wasn't able to fully implement the optimization despite having a clear direction.
And in the final evaluation he was satisfied with my approach and asked me to submit the code.
After lunch, students began receiving calls for the interview round, with only one student per batch being
selected. Four people had already been called, and I was getting really tense because no one from my panel
had received a call yet. Finally, after some time, I received a call for the interview. (fat gayi thi)
Be honest with your mentor. Tell him everything that you're trying to do with a clear approach.
Only 5 people received a call. But after some time one more person got a chance for the interview.

3. Interview Round [6 people appeared for this round] [30 - 40 mins]

There were three panels, each with one panelist. My round was conducted by a Senior Engineering Manager
who had been with the company for 6-7 years. After introducing himself, he immediately asked me to
explain the projects I had worked on. After giving a brief overview of one of my projects, he started asking
in-depth questions about my role, the backend development, and the reason for choosing the tech stack. For
instance, I used MongoDB to store data, and he questioned why I chose it over SQL. He also asked why I
created the project. These questions were focused solely on that one project.
Participating in Hackathons can help you build these projects so you don't have to spend time building them
alone. And try to talk about hackathons experiences as well.
--- PAGE 3 ---
He then asked me to explain another project, focusing on why I built it, what I learned, and the new tools
and technologies I used. For this project, I had utilized Redux Toolkit (RTK) so he asked me what I achieved
by using RTK .
I also gave details about Redux Toolkit (RTK) and RTK Query, explaining how I manage the overall state of
the application. I discussed the store, custom hooks, dispatch, and selectors to give him a clear
understanding of the state management in my project.
If you have in-depth knowledge of a particular tool or technology, you should definitely mention it and
explain it thoroughly. Sharing the ins and outs can leave a strong impression and create a positive impact
during the interview.
After that, he inquired about my major project. I explained every detail thoroughly, providing proper
examples. He then asked, 'If this already exists, why are you building it?' I responded by explaining the
technical challenges, why previous efforts in this area weren't successful, and how our approach is different.
My major project was related to machine learning, and while I only had upar - upar ka knowledge of some
aspects, I was able to clearly explain the idea and how it worked. It's always beneficial to have a good
understanding of your major project because many companies tend to ask questions about it.
He then asked me about threads and processes in the operating system, followed by the difference between
the WHERE and HAVING clauses in SQL. I explained it with a real-world example, and he seemed
satisfied. Next, he gave me a technical scenario: 'If you type www.google,com in your browser and the page
doesn't load, how would you debug it?' I walked him through my troubleshooting steps, and he asked
counter-questions along the way.
He then gave me a new scenario: 'You have a ITB file and need to find the count of a word, for example,
"interview." How many times does this word appear in the file?' I suggested dividing the file into chunks and
searching each chunk simultaneously. However, he pointed out this might fail when a word is split between
chunks. I then mentioned using MapReduce for handling such big data problems (thanks to GFG interview
experiences), but I admitted I couldn't fully explain its working. He appreciated my honesty and said, 'It's
fine.'
After that, he asked about my hobby projects. I mentioned that my web development projects were my
hobby project bes he didn't know I was from EXTC. When I revealed that I was an EXTC student, I
explained the projects we work on are completely different compared to these dev projects. Initially, I was a
bit scared because this company originally wasn't allowing EXTC students to sit for their process-only CS
students. But a heartfelt thanks to the TPO team for convincing them.
That wrapped up my interview when he asked if I had any questions for him. I inquired about what I should
learn from now to make the most of my internship.
Always remember to ask genuine questions at the end.
This was the final round, after which HR gave feedback to everyone. When it was my turn, I felt a bit
anxious about whether I had been selected or not. To my relief, HR informed me that they were happy with
my performance and would be pleased to extend an offer. Only 3 people got the offer.
That was it!
--- PAGE 4 ---

journey.howSecured:
IDFC visited around the end of July, conducting their PPT between the 25th and 27th. It was announced that
the recruitment process would include:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Two Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

However, due to the tough decision of selecting between the final eight HR candidates, two additional
technical rounds were conducted with higher technical positions and a Senior Managing Director. In total,
there were six rounds:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Four Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

Round 0 - Online Assessment (160 Candidates)

Over 160 students appeared for the online Assessment. The test was online but was strictly proctored via
camera,microphone, etc on hirepro. The test had three sections: section 1 Aptitude and data interpretation,
section 2 was SQL+Excel + Computer Fundamentals+Math and section three was DSA. Each section was
separately timed and the test was overall 90 mins. First two sections got locked after 45-50 mins and the
remaining time was for coding questions.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The coding section was pretty easy. The two questions asked were:
Question 1 was similar to this :
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/find-duplicates-in-an-array/1?itm_source=geeksforgeeks&itm_me
dium=article&itm_campaign=practice_card
Question 2 was similar to this:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/check-if-a-number-is-palindrome/

2. Round 1: Technical Round 1 35-40 students |

This round was all about my resume and the projects I have done. The interviewer took one of the projects
and scaled it to a large level and told me to tell how I would handle the project at such a large scale and also
asked me questions about dev ops because it was on my resume. I was slightly grilled due to my lack of
experience in frontend development but I covered it by convincing the interviewer about my backend and
dev ops skills. It is advised to always keep a smile on your face and have confidence while speaking. If you
don't understand the question do not hesitate to ask the interviewer to repeat it. The round went on for 40-45
mins and was taken after the lunch break.

3. Round 2: Technical Round 2 [12-15 Students]

After my round 1 some applicants were giving round 3 and as I was slightly grilled I thought I was not
getting past round 1 but I was shortlisted for round 2. So never lose hope even though you were grilled
you will get shortlisted. Round 2 was very calm and the interviewer asked me to explain my projects in
depth and asked me about some libraries which were used in them. In short IDFC needs a developer and
they intend to find one via their resume and their experiences. So be very clear about your resume even
though you have lied on the resume make sure you do that concept before the interview.

4. Round 3: HR Round [8 Students]

The HR round was taken online on microsoft teams. In this round I was asked to give my introduction now
in the HR round do not make your intro too technical. After that I was asked about my family
background so I told them about how both my mom and dad are from the commerce field and their
dream was to work in a bank and my dream is to become a software engineer and how IDFC is bringing
it together. Then she told me to convince her why tech is important in the banking sector. I started from a
real life incident about how I used UPI to transfer 3Rs to a XEROX guy in the morning and
everything. She said she was convinced then asked about my future plans. Then she asked if I had any
questions and I asked about the work culture. Pretty Ironically I was slightly grilled over this but as
always I kept my smile and went on.

5. Round 4 Tech Round 8 students|:

So as mentioned above there was a tough decision to select among 8 students. They decided to take one
more tech round on the next day. I was just boarding the metro to watch Deadpool and Wolverine when I
came to know about this interview so I rushed home but then it was conducted the next day T_T. It was
technical and I was asked about my resume and I was also asked to explain the most complex algorithm
I know. I explained Kruskal's Algorithm (MST using disjoint sets).
--- PAGE 3 ---

5. Round 5 Tech Round 8 students:

Again they were not able to shortlist the candidates T_T so they took one more round. In which I was asked
about the difference between SQL and NoSQL. When to use which one. Also about data structures used
at different applications like front and back buttons in media player or navigation in browser, searching
phone contacts. But then the unbeatable 8 candidates made it and all 8 of them were selected for the role.

journey.howSecured:
The company first conducted a pre-placement talk, which was followed by an online assessment 2 days later.
After that 3 interview rounds were conducted on 30 July followed by 2 interview rounds later.

1. Online Assessment [ 167 students appeared for this round]

The test consisted of 3 sections and each section had a time limit. The first section had 15 questions and was
aptitude based wherein general questions on logical reasoning were asked. The second section had 20
technical questions based on Programming, Excel, SQL and Basic Statistics. The third section had 2 coding
questions which were very easy.

1. Check whether given number is positive and a palindrome

2. For a given array of integers, find an output array which contains the AND operation of every integer

in the original array. After this check whether elements in the new array are repeated.
I fell short of time in the aptitude section, however the technical section went very well for me and I was
able to solve both of the coding problems. I would suggest focusing on the technical part more especially for
the test. I referred to articles on GFG and interviewbit for the topics mentioned.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 38 students appeared for this round]

The interviewer first asked me to introduce myself and elaborate on my college experience. He asked me to
tell about a positive and a negative experience. He then asked me a few questions on a project mentioned in
my resume. He gave some situations and how I would manage them in my project. I had ML projects in my
resume so he questioned about the accuracy mentioned and how I achieved that, the model used, etc. I had
mentioned python as my primary programming language so he then asked questions on python such as
Walrus operator, swapcase function, what does pass do, exception handling in python, docstring, slicing in
python, concatenations, variable types, etc.
(For this part, I would suggest referring to the GFG article on "python most asked interview questions", a
lot of the questions were mentioned in the article. I couldn't answer all of the questions and just told him
that I had not worked previously with this and so did not know about this however I think it is similar to this
thing I worked with. It's okay if you don't know the answer to a question just be honest with the
interviewer.)
--- PAGE 2 ---
He then asked me a few questions on numpy and pandas as I had mentioned them in my resume. He then
gave me a situation where I had to build a food service app and asked me to build a schema of the app and
what considerations I will take while building the app. He then asked me how I would handle excess traffic
on the app. I told him about nginx and how I used it in a project before. He then asked me what architecture
I would use to build the app and to explain the architecture. I asked him if he was referring to MVC to which
he said yes and then I went on to explain to him what MVC is and how different components work together.
He then asked me why I chose python and not Java. He then asked me a few questions on Java based on
syntax and then asked why is Java more used and what are the benefits of Java. He then asked me about the
4 pillars of OOPS and asked me to give applications for 2 of them. He then asked me a few questions on
DBMS. He then asked me about another project I had mentioned in my resume and asked as to why I had
implemented it in a certain way and what is the future scope for it. I explained to him the entire process of
that project and he seemed very interested in it. At the end, I asked him a question regarding the ML used in
features in IDFC and he went on to explain how they use it in various applications. The interview lasted for
around 40-50 minutes.
(Firstly, I would suggest being honest on your resume and making sure you know about everything in your
resume. Try to list projects which are a bit innovative/different and have some unique features. Read up on
your projects before the interview and make sure to know every detail about it/how it is implemented
because they will try to test you majorly on your knowledge on various aspects of the projects.)

3. Technical Round 2[12 students appeared for this round]

The interviewer first asked me to introduce myself and then asked me what skills I was planning to learn in
my remaining year of college and how I would go about learning them. He then asked me the reason for
choosing AI/ML and not going for Comps. I was upfront about it and told him I had no idea about the course
while joining and it was the best I could get based on my percentile. He then asked me about a project and
why I chose it. Then he gave me various scenarios wherein he tried to complicate things and asked me
questions as to how I would solve them. I had a project based on LLMs so then he asked me about my
understanding of LLMs and how they work/function. He then asked me if I had to make a project which
would solve a large-scale problem in India utilizing my current skills, what would I make. I told him about
an app designed for women's safety that I was familiar with. He then asked me to suggest improvements and
if I had limited resources, how would I optimize the app and track well-lit areas. He gave me hints which
helped me arrive at the solution. He then asked me how I would go about implementing some specified
features. He then asked if I had any questions for him and I asked him a similar question that I had asked in
the previous round. He explained on a deeper level how various factors at IDFC work. This round lasted
about 25-30 mins
(What I felt from talking with some fellow interviewees was that they were asking questions based on the
answers given. So be honest and ask for hints if you cannot think of something and explain whatever idea
comes to mind.)

4. a) HR Round [ 8 students appeared for this round ]

This was an online round. The panelists first asked me how I was finding the process and how I felt in the
earlier interview rounds and who had interviewed me earlier. They then asked me to introduce myself and
tell them about my family background, hobbies, etc. The next question was what I knew about IDFC Bank
and what I thought was unique in the bank. They then asked me to elaborate on one of my projects, what
was an experience I gained from it and how I used ML in it. They asked me if I had ever faced a conflict in
--- PAGE 3 ---
my team and how did I resolve it. They then asked me to list 3 of my weaknesses and strengths. The last
question was why should they hire me and what unique qualities did I have. They then asked me if I had any
questions. The interview lasted for about 15-20 minutes.
(Do not forget to ask the interviewer their name after every interview as it might be brought up in HR
rounds. Read up about IDFC bank in advance and note some pointers/take screenshots in the pre-placement
talk when they talk about their vision and values. Prepare sample HR questions and rehearse their answers
beforehand. The ones asked to me were very basic HR questions which I had prepared beforehand and I
advise you to do the same. In weaknesses talk about how you have a weakness which you are improving
on.)
IDFC first planned on selecting 5-6 students however later they wanted to hire all 8 students and therefore
conducted 2 more virtual interviews in the coming days.
b) Techno HR Round [ 8 students appeared for this round]
The interviewer was a senior manager in the company. He began by asking me for my introduction and as I
from it. He asked me what I knew about IDFC. He then asked me what I had studied in college apart from
normalization is used and if I could list all forms and apply it in a real life example. He then asked me to
explain the 4 pillars of OOPS and give an example where OOPS can be used in a real life application. He
asked me some questions on Operating Systems and what is virtual memory and why do we have virtual
memory, etc. He then asked me why Python and not Java and asked the benefits and drawbacks of both
Python and Java. He then asked me if I knew about red-black trees which I did not know about and told him
so. He then asked me to explain to him how a BST works and how BSTs work when alphabets are involved.
He then asked me to list how BST can be applied with an example. He again asked me why they should hire
me and what unique qualities I have that made me stand out. He then asked if I had any questions to which I
asked him his role and what a day looks like in his life. He explained what his exact role was and the
responsibilities he has. This round lasted for around 20 minutes.
(Practice CS fundamentals thoroughly approximately a month or 2 before the placement season. I referred
one shot videos on youtube and tried to solve mcqs on different sites. DBMS & SQL > OOPS > OS > CCN
in that order)
c) Technical Round - 3[8 students appeared for this round]
The interview was conducted by 2 senior developers of the company. They first introduced themselves and
asked me to introduce myself. They then asked me to explain a project I had done and the tech stack used.
They then asked me why C or C++ have a lower execution time than python and if python was an
interpreted or compiled language and why did I prefer python. I answered the same as earlier rounds as it
has more support for ML and DS and has a lot of libraries and is easy to read and understand. They asked a
few more questions based on my resume and then asked application based questions on DSA. They asked
me how would I implement forward and back buttons in chrome, how would I implement panels in Netflix
and how can I implement contact searching. On naming a data structure he then asked more detailed
questions and how it works, etc. I asked them the same questions as the last round and they were very
friendly in replying and interacting overall.
8 students received the offer.
--- PAGE 4 ---
