journey.howSecured:
A total of 3 rounds were conducted - 1 Online Assessment Round, 1 Tech Interview Round & Finally 1 HR
Round. All were conducted on the same day. The CGPA Criteria for SDE was 8.5, later reduced to 8. Only
for testing role it was further reduced to 7.5. May not be the case for next year if they don't want more
applicants in testing so it is preferable to maintain a pointer of 8.5 and above

1. [Online Assessment] [155 appeared, ~ 49 selected] Invigilated by Company Officials

The Online Assessment had 70 Questions in total & lasted for 90 mins. 40 Technical Questions (18 Java, 17
Python, 5 SQL) & 30 Aptitude Questions (primarily quantitative questions). There was 1 correct mark for
every right answer & -0.25 for wrong answer. There was no specific weightage to any section as such and all
questions had equal marks. Physical Calculators were not allowed but on screen you could use what your
laptop OS provided.
Tech Questions in Java were mainly around the actual application of language in industry & snippets were
given for which output was asked in majority of the questions. There were things like ConcurrentHashmap,
Consumer objects & stuff which I had never even heard of as a part of our curriculum & other things such
as. I first attempted those questions around OOPS which I was confident of. Did a couple of questions by
eliminating options & left the rest. I also attempted two questions based on their extreme similarity to
javascript. One was somewhat similar to resolving Promise and another one based on filtering & a sort of
then syntax. I was okay with losing 0.5 marks just in case they were wrong.
I then moved to the next section on Python. It was very heavy on OOPS in python. I had only done OOPS in
Java & C++ in detail & only knew the basics in python so was slightly taken aback. I still attempted the
questions which involved concepts common to all languages. Skipped a question which involved multiple
inheritance because I was not aware it was allowed or not. Other questions were around lists, sets & strings
and were very easy.
Next I moved to the SQL section. Here questions had given the schema & the task to be performed & we
were asked to select the correct query among 4 options. Questions were of easy level but they were listed as
--- PAGE 2 ---
continuous sentences & not written line by line in indented form so it was difficult to find the differences
between them.
I completed the above 3 rounds in around 30-32 minutes.
Finally I went to the Aptitude round with 1 hour in hand. It has questions primarily around permutations &
combinations, ratio proportion, simple & compound interest & interpretation & calculation based on
bar-graph and equation based questions on speed, time, distance. Boat moving upstream, downstream type
of Questions. I attempted the easy questions first, then went over the questions which would require more
time in calculation in the second iteration. I was able to do almost ~80% of the questions here.
Tip: Don't attempt questions you are not very sure of in tests with negative marking. In mcq tests which do
not have any negative marking don't leave any questions unanswered.
Resources :

• Aptitude - IndiaBIX

• Java Theory - Java Tutorial | Learn Java Programming - javatpoint

• Java MCQs - 300 Core Java Interview Questions (2023) - javatpoint

• Java OOPS, Generics etc. - • OOP 1 | Introduction & Concepts - Classes, Objects, Constructors,..

• SQL Theory - • MySQL Full Course for free

(2023) (You can use any video to learn syntax, I

already had it as a part of syllabus)

• SQL Questions - Problems - LeetCode (do many easy questions first to get a hang of syntax)

• Python - • Python Full Course for free

• (you need not go through the whole video)

2.
[Technical Interview] [49 appeared, 17 shortlisted] 2 panelists in my interview panel
(For me it lasted for 35-40 ish minutes, in some panels the interviewer only took interviews for 6-7 minutes)
I was asked to wait some time before I went after the next candidate (I later found out that they went through
all the links of my projects and my github profile) They asked me to give my introduction in brief
mentioning my academic background, projects & explain the project I am most passionate about mentioning
the team size, my role & my contribution in the project. Then they asked me a few cross questions around
our approach & since it involved chatbot, how did we train it etc. I answered about my role in front end so
the second panelist asked questions such as Why React? Framework vs Library, Is NextJs a framework or
library with reason & then it clicked to me that he was using words from my answer itself to move on to the
next question, for subsequent questions I was careful of not using tech terms that I was unsure of. He then
asked me about my MongoDB over SQL databases, what is scalable, what is not, how is data stored in
mongodb, if i could redesign in hindsight would I use SQL or NoSQL. What benefits one provides over the
other, ACID properties in databases. Then the first panelist asked me how confident I was in java & other
languages. I told him we had some of it as a part of our curriculum but for DSA I used C++ & Javascript for
webdev. He gave me his laptop with a java file and asked me to code solver function for a problem -
Q. Given a string like "Hii, today is the greatest day ever with balloons giggling" and asked me to find the
word for which max characters are getting repeated. I thought the answer should be "giggling" as g repeats 4
times but he clarified that "greatest" should be the answer as two characters 'e' & '' are repeated & that the
frequency/ no of times individual characters repeated did not matter.
--- PAGE 3 ---
I proceeded by writing my approach on paper & basically thinking out loud as I was writing it. He then
asked me to optimize my approach by moving from set to map. I did so & when he was satisfied he asked
me to code it. I acknowledged that I am not able to recall the Java syntax of inserting into a map but I am
confident that I could do it in cpp & asked his permission to do so (This is where on his laptop I saw all my
profiles & links were opened in new tabs). He agreed & I coded it quickly in cpp & when I ran the code I
got an error saying map[character] cannot be accessed. He said maybe you aren't able to do it in cpp too but
I quickly figured out that I had written map[character] instead of frequency[character] (simple mistake in
cpp) & ran it and it worked. He then asked the other panelist to ask questions. The panelist asked me
questions about OOPS in Java & I realized that he was asking the same questions that were there in the OA
in the morning. I explained my approach to those questions & MCQS. Here is where he asked about the
question which has syntax similar to javascript & how I was able to do it. I honestly accepted that I did not
know it & I used common sense & some simple programming logic to do it. He then asked about a Question
on ConcurrentHashMaps which I had earlier left in the test. I said I did not know what they were but also
added that I knew what hashmaps were. We discussed some things about hashmaps in general & then he
proceeded to ask the first panelist to ask me questions. Panelist asked me how comfortable I am with SQL
& I told upto joins, aggregate functions & subqueries. He then asked me a simple Question
Q. Find employees with max salary in each city
I started writing the query but midway asked for clarification if multiple people could have the max salary.
And then wrote it accordingly, he told me that there was a simple syntax error which I was not immediately
able to resolve so they pointed it out. I said yes I overlooked it by mistake as I was focusing on only the
max(salary) part instead of the group by clause. One last thing they asked was a very famous puzzle similar
to Chicken, Fox and Grain Riddle (Solution Using Original Images) - DigiNo I gave a step by step approach
in a diagram form. They then asked me what questions I had for them. I asked them about the projects
interns work on & tech stack they use & which dept. is allotted to them etc.

Tips:

• Do not lie on your Resume but you can smartly change phrases so that your resume looks good.

• Do not throw the sheets/papers in which you did your OA questions. They can be asked in an

interview.

• Make sure if you are adding any links then they are clickable in your resume

• Prepare well around your resume projects & its tech stack. You can ask your friend to keep on cross

questioning you on them

• Prepare a couple of scenarios (even if fake) about disagreement in the team, or any times that you

have shown leadership/ team spirit. These questions are very common too.

• If you don't know the answer or you are not able to recall it, try to put it across politely instead of

saying something wrong

• Think out loud when solving a DSA problem/ SQL query but when saying a theory answer try to sort

of structure it in your mind first. Make use of technical terms & examples where possible

• If possible have examples of OOPS in a different setting, not those regular Animal or Car Inheritance

sort of things. This makes your answer slightly novel & interesting.
Resources :

• For Languages: Same as in above section

• For Project Related: Depends on your Tech Stack. Go through GFG and Interview Experiences

across all drives, see what all questions they have been asked.

• Technical Interview Questions - A Complete 2023 List

--- PAGE 4 ---

• The Ultimate Guide to Acing Your Technical Interview - InterviewBit

3. ¡HR Round] [17 appeared, 12 Selected] 1 HR & 1 MD in panel

(For me this lasted 15-17 ish minutes, for others it was around 25-30 & event 35 mins in some cases)
This was the last round where they first introduced themselves & then asked me to introduce myself stating
my academic background, some information about my family & my most favorite project. Then I was cross
questioned on my Minor Degree in Management & why I was doing it etc. Then there was quite some
discussion on my project, what I learnt from it. What was the team like, how I resolved any conflicts etc.
After that they pointed out that I had a great academic record so why not go for masters. I answered by
stating that I need to support my family & my focus is completely on doing a job. Post that some discussion
around where I live & will I be able to commute to Nesco to their office. I said I travel to college daily &
Nesco is also almost at the same distance & assured them I will be able to do so. The MD then asked about
my preference in technology & I answered that I did not have preference as such & tried to showcase that I
can wear multiple hats by telling him that I do DSA in C++, web dev in javascript, have done Java, Python,
Blockchain programming as a part of curriculum & electives. He then asked if I was okay with
programming in. Net or app dev, I showed my enthusiasm & assurance that I will learn it if the project needs
it. Post that they asked if I had any questions for them. To the MD I asked what training is provided to
interns & what projects/tech they work on. To the HR I asked that I had gone through their website and
wanted to know more about the ISS University program that they have.
Around 10 PM the results were announced & 12 people were selected across all roles.
lips :

• Keep a Smile on your face when answering questions & Listen actively

• If asked about masters/further education say that you want to focus on job whatever be the reason

that suits you

• Go through the company website & understand what the company does

• Find something interesting & of interest to a fresher & ask questions about it to the HR

• Make sure you know the names of HRs/panelists in general, if not ask the TPCs

• Some general etiquettes like greeting when you enter, putting the chair back to its place when you

are about to leave.

journey.howSecured:
The pre-placement talk was scheduled online on 2nd July. Try to ask questions and give answers if you can.

1. Resume Screening: Deadline 4th July

2. Online Aptitude Test : 6th July

3. Group Discussion

4. Interview round 1

5. Interview round 2

6. HR round

Rounds 3-6 were scheduled on 10th July.

1. Resume Screening

We had to submit all details and resume via the JPMC portal. You are also allowed to attach a cover letter,
although not mandatory, try to submit one.

• Use latex template and add only things you are confident about. Keep it single column, one page.

• You can take a slightly modified resume on campus which may contain 2 columns, you will need

around 5 to 6 copies as your panel may have more than one interviewer.
97 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Online Aptitude Test

The test window was 11-11:30 am and the duration was 45 mins. It had 4 sections, with no negative marking
and navigation was allowed.

• Basics of Finance and Accounting : 10 questions

• Market awareness: 10 questions. Questions were not necessarily finance based but general current

affairs.

• Quantitative Aptitude : 15 questions.

--- PAGE 2 ---
Questions based on Profit and Loss, Workers and Time, AP GP, Probability, etc. (Normal Aptitude
questions)

• Verbal Skills: 10 questions.

Passage based, rearranging, standard questions.
The test was lengthy so try to attempt things you know and equal parts from all sections rather than acing
one section.
72 students were shortlisted. The result was announced only a day before the interview so be prepared.

3. Group Discussion [ 72 selected students were divided into 6 panels of 12 each. We had Around 30

mins]

• The topic was revealed on 9th July, a day before the process, and it was 'India the 5th Largest

Economy'

• We were allowed to take notes with us for reference.

• We had 2 panelists. They told us to start with an introduction of the topic and the general idea we had

about GDP and the growth over years.

• After 7-8 points were discussed, they started introducing subtopics like which states were

contributing more, which were lacking behind, how the global scenario and decline in the China
market was affecting our economy. Lastly they asked us what could go wrong and prevent the
economy from rising. They asked me to conclude.

• Make sure you have at least 3-4 entries. The duration you talk for is not imp as long as you have

good points. Try using numbers to elevate your points. They were taking names and making sure we
all had chances to speak.
The better you perform in GD, the earlier your interview will be scheduled. I was the last person called for
round 1, so don't give up hope as it will be a lengthy process.
31 students were shortlisted for round 1
9 more were waitlisted but were not given a chance to give the interview.

4. Interview Round 1 [ My round lasted for about 25-30 mins]

There were 5 panels. My interview being scheduled last happened after lunch. I had only 1 panelist but some
people had 2 panelists.
I was first told to introduce myself, keep these basic answers ready as I was asked this in each round. He
started by asking me what I thought my role would be. Then he asked about stock markets so I told him
about Sensex and Nifty. Do see the previous day's closing for both. He asked me if I invested and then about
which sectors I would invest in. Then he asked about RBI and its policies, inflation and the name of RBI
governor. If you don't know something do not guess, just say you haven't read about it. Then he moved on to
financial statements. He gave me scenarios and I had to create the balance sheet and income statement, cases
like buying inventory, selling for revenue, all basics. He asked me about Enterprise value and market
capitalization. Then he moved on to puzzles. He asked a sum on avg speed, puzzle on probability (10 teams
against each other, find no of matches) and a puzzle on work and time.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Only a few students weren't taken for round 2, all others were given a second chance.

5. Interview Round 2 [ This round was for 15-20 mins]

There were 3 panels. I was called for the second round immediately after the first round so do not assume
you will get time to prepare between rounds.
I had two panelists. They asked me to introduce, and a few things from my resume. Then they told me to
explain financial statements and how they were interlinked. Then they gave a case with profit and tax which
was a little tricky. In between they asked about line items on IS, cash flow types and working capital. I could
not solve it completely but I explained the approach at every step and they were satisfied. Then they asked
about enterprise value and if it could be negative giving scenarios. They also asked about valuation methods
and told me to explain the multiple based approach. Then they moved on to the overall Indian market
scenario and just needed a generalized overview.
Around 16-18 people were selected for the HR round.

6. HR Round [ Around 10 mins ]

This was the easiest round. She asked me to introduce myself and to tell about my family. Then she asked
me why I was opting for a finance role and if I wanted to go for higher studies or any certifications in the
future. She also asked me what my plan was if I didn't get selected. Always say that you still want to do
something in finance and show you are passionate about it. Do not say you have higher studies plans even if
you do. Praise the company as much as you can and show how eager you are to join. She asked me if I had
any questions so I asked her about the growth opportunities and how to work for them. I think that
impressed her because then she asked me another question regarding any unethical scenarios I had come
across and how I dealt with them, which I could answer from committee experiences.
My HR round was also towards the very end so you never know who they will select.
The process on the 10th started around 9 and we got the results by 5:

30. 11 students were selected for the Banking role.

journey.prep:
• Always be honest with your answers: The interviewers are highly experienced, and they can easily

tell whether you are being honest or not. If you don't know the answer, politely tell them that you
don't know or are not able to recall it. Don't beat around the bush.

• Be thorough with RISES: Either you will be asked about it in the interview, or you will be judged

based on your answers. If asked in an interview, try to explain how you have followed it during your
projects or hackathons.

• Drive the Interview: Sometimes, you have the opportunity to guide the interview in the

direction you want. Use this to your advantage.

• Resume: Be honest with your resume and know it very well. Prepare for every word in it and

every technology used by you.

• Projects: Try to add projects related to Java and Spring Boot. Based on feedback received from

panelists, they are looking for students who have worked with Java. Since Barclays is a bank, they
suggested having a project in Java. Though they do consider projects in other domains as well, it's
better if you have a project in Java.

• OOPs: The most important topic. Try to answer OOPs questions using real-life examples. Be

prepared for questions like where you have implemented OOPs concepts (for example, inheritance)
in your projects. If you code in C++, prepare for questions comparing Java and C++. For Java,
prepare topics like multithreading, exception handling, and core Java concepts. For C++, be
well-prepared with topics like STL, differences between operator functions, virtual functions vs. pure
functions, etc.

• DSA: Start practicing DSA at least 6 months prior. Participate in contests on LeetCode or any

other platform. Even if you haven't prepared, start participating. It helps in online tests. • SQL:
Practice SQL from LeetCode's top 50 questions. I will be adding useful links below. • React:you
can prepare react from interview bit

• Read Previous Experiences: It helps a lot.

• Rejections: Don't get disheartened if you don't get selected. I, myself, faced 4 rejections before this.

Don't lose hope if your interview didn't go well compared to others. Sometimes miracles happen
(My Round 2 was not that good). Learn from your rejections, analyze what went wrong, and prepare
accordingly.

Placement process consisted of 3 rounds. Online test (Test was to be taken from college only), 2 Interview
rounds

1. Online Test(11/9/2024)

The Online test was of 1hr 30 minutes duration. It consisted of cs fundamentals mcq (variable marks), a
10 marks sql query and a 50 marks coding question. The coding question was about string generation
similar to this:
https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
SQL was basic group by and orderby query where we had to group by according to a month. Make
sure to practice SQL of date and months questions.
I was able to solve 5 / 10 test cases ,sql and mcqs.
35 students got shortlisted for the next round.

2. Technical Round 1 (12/9/2024)

Before the interview rounds, a Pre-Placement Talk was conducted. Then, from around 11:40 AM, the
interviews started. My interview was the last in my panel. It's good to know your panelist's name, it shows
that you were attentive during the PPT. My interviewer was Assistant Vice President at Barclays, with over 7
years of experience. The interview started with the question, "Tell me about yourself." (Make sure you
prepare this question very well, as it forms your first impression.)
Thad secured a scholarship, which I had mentioned in my resume, and we discussed it for a couple of
minutes. Then, he asked, "If the company that offered you this scholarship were to give you an offer, and
Barclays as well, whom would you choose?"
Then came the technical part. He asked me which data structures I knew. I replied, "Stack, queue, linked
list, string, array, trees, and graphs" (I mentioned I knew graphs but hadn't revised it). Then he gave me a
paper and asked me to write the code for insertion of a node in a doubly linked list, where a position is
--- PAGE 2 ---
given.
For the next question, he gave me his laptop and told me to write the code for reversing a string. I did it
using two pointers. Then he asked if reversing a string is possible using a stack. I said yes, and then he told
me to code it as well. After that, he asked about the difference between struct and class in C++.
Then he asked questions regarding OOP concepts: "What is Object-Oriented Programming, and how is it
different from other paradigms? What is encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, and polymorphism? What is
the difference between abstraction and encapsulation? How can you perform encapsulation?" (Using private
variables and getter/setter methods.) "What are abstract classes, and can abstract classes have concrete
methods?" Can we create object of abstract class. He asked me to code abstract classes in Java. He then asked
if multiple inheritance is possible, if not, why? "If we want to achieve it, how can we do it?" (By using
interfaces).
Then he asked me to name any completely object-oriented programming language. I said I didn't have an
idea about it. He then asked, "Is Java a completely object-oriented language?" I explained that Java is not a
completely object-oriented language as it has primitive data types.
After the OOP questions, he asked more questions on DSA. He asked me to name any shortest path-finding
algorithm, to which I replied, "Dijkstra's algorithm." He then told me to explain it. After explaining it, he
searched for a graph question on the internet and asked me to find the shortest path between two given
nodes. Then he asked a few more questions on it.
First, he asked, "How would you store a graph?" (Using an adjacency matrix/list.) Then he asked me to tell
him all the data structures and their uses in this algorithm. He then asked me to code it, but later he said just
explain him the algorithm thoroughly.
After that, he asked a few questions about my projects. The interview ended with the question, "Do you have
any questionsạẠạPrepare few nice questions as this shows your interest in this company)

3. Techno-Hr Round 2(12/9/2024)

For few panels, this round was an HR round, but for my panel, it was completely technical. As soon as my
Round 1 was done, I was called for Round 2. The interviewer directly handed me a few prints with Java
code snippets and asked me to answer and explain them. There were around six questions. After discussing
those questions, he asked about React: What is React? What are components? What are useState hooks, and
what are they used for? What is the virtual DOM? What is the shadow DOM in React? What are controlled
components and other types of components? He also asked me to explain the lifecycle of React components.
Then, he asked me to write the code for merge sort and explain how the time complexity is Onlogn). He
asked about the difference between SQL and NoSQL, followed by SQL-related questions. He asked me to
create two tables: "departments" and " students, " and then write a query to find the department-wise
highest
salary (this was solved using a subquery). After asking for a hint, I was able to solve it.
Next, he asked about OOPs concepts. He asked if multiple inheritance is possible in Java and C++ (it is
possible in C++ but not in Java) and why it is not possible in Java (due to ambiguity). Then, he asked why
C++ can handle it but not Java. Then he asked how a HashMap is implemented internally. Finally he
--- PAGE 3 ---
asked regarding DevOps, what it is and could explain devOps lifecycle?

4. Round 3 (PRANK round)

We all interns + grads were told to sit in the conference room except few. Then we were told that now
they will be calling out a few names who will not be selected for further process and have to leave the
conference room immediately. Everyone was very tensed. Then they told this was a PRANK and all of
you have been selected !!!!!
A total of 19 grads were selected!!

journey.howSecured:
Initially they had kept a cutoff of 8.5 CGPA for applying to any of the 4 roles, which was
further lowered to 7.5/8 . For software testing role it was reduced to 7.5, for other roles it was
kept 8.

1. Online Assessment [Approx 155 students appeared]

The assessment was conducted offline in college, and was on google forms. There were approx. 70
questions which had to be completed in 90 minutes. The marking scheme was +1, -0.25 and there
were 4 sections- Java based (18 Q), Python based (17 Q), SQL based (5)  and Aptitude questions
(30).
Java questions were related to enums, multithreading, filtering, streams, scope of variables, OOPS
etc. Python questions were mostly OOPs related and some basic but tricky ones. Both these sections
involved code snippets to determine the output. Aptitude involved CAT type questions on  volume,
distance speed, simple compound interest, graphs, etc.
For Aptitude use a bit of guesstimates and elimination methods . For some questions just by looking
at options you could figure out what could be the possible solution and that would save some of
your valuable time. There were a few tricky questions which were difficult to understand, leave
those questions for later. I solved dsa questions in C++ so Java and python sections were a little
tricky for me but you can solve all the logical questions and some questions were syntax and
functions related for that you can refer to 1000 python questions for an interview on Sanfoundry.
Remember that not all students are familiar with both python and java and so even if you are unable
to solve their questions dont panic and focus on logical questions from all the sections.

2. Technical Round [49 students selected]

After the OA, 49 students were shortlisted for the technical round. There were a total of 8 panels,
with distribution based on role preference. My panel included 9 candidates, and I was the fourth
one to be interviewed. The interview began with an introduction, followed by questions about my
projects, why I applied for the Analytical Verification role, how I became interested in analytics and
when and how I started studying data analytics. Try to answer this question passionately and show
genuine interest in the role. I shared about how I watch a lot of sports like Cricket and Football and
there is a lot of data analytics involved over there. I also talked about data analytics while investing
in stock market.  Then I talked about my projects and my internship experience which were mainly
about database design and data analytics.
While talking about projects don't reply in a monotonous tone as it will appear memorized and
may not seem genuine. Prepare for questions about the Tech stack, what problem you solved by
the project, real life use cases etc.
He also asked me to rate my proficiency in SQL and Pandas on a scale of 1 to 5. After that, the
interviewer handed me a laptop with a question and asked me import an excel file in Pandas. I
logged in my colab account and imported the file. Then he asked me to describe the excel sheet. I
used df.describe and df.info function. He then asked me to once see the excel file to know about
the columns and then asked a query about the file. Instead of opening in excel I used df.head
command and opened the file in colab itself. He then asked me to return count of number of
matches held at each venue. I didn't remember the syntax so I explained him the logic and talked
how I leverage AI technologies for syntax and to know about different functions faster and get the
task done efficiently.
Then he asked me to write a SQL query on an online compiler. The question was easy; I had to
identify the relevant tables from a large set and solve the problem using joins and group by
functions ( The question was to find the best product for each company and the number of sales
for that product ). Towards the end, the interviewer asked about my future plans, my family
background, and my understanding of the role. The interview lasted for about 30 minutes.
The one who went just before me was asked 7 to 8 coding questions and his interview went for 1
hr. So if you are not confident about your technical skills you can still drive the interview to projects
side.  Also don't panic if your interview was for a shorter duration as how long your interview goes
doesn't determine your selection. Also remember to at least ask one question to the interviewer. I
had prepared a staple question that I had asked in all my interviews about integration of AI tools in
their tech stack and day to day operations and based on their answer I more often then not asked
another follow up question.

3. HR Round [17 students selected ]

There were 2 panellists in this interview, the MD of ISS and the HR. They first asked me about my
family background, if I had any plans of higher studies?. After that the MD asked me that why did u
decide to apply for this role, what do you know about data analytics, etc. I explained how I have
observed data in sports and stock market. I also mentioned my internship experience and about my
projects which were based on data analytics. Then he asked about data pipeline of my project. I
explained how I obtained my data, how I made changes etc. Then HR asked about my greatest
academic achievement. Other generic HR questions were asked, this was a pretty chill interview

For the placement process, three rounds were conducted. There was a resume shortlisting round before any
of the actual rounds happened. 182 students were shortlisted after the resume round.

1. [Case Study Round] [20 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

About : The Case Study Round started at 8am sharp and we were given a time of 2 hrs for making PPTs for
the cases. Students were provided with a case study each based on product designing, and were supposed to
study the challenges associated, suggest new features and define success metrics for each feature. My
case-study was regarding GooglePay, others got Healtifyme and Olx. From this round, 15 people were
shortlisted ahead together for APgM/APM/AGM roles.
How I prepared for this round: I started participating in business-case competitions (mostly organized by
IITs/NITs/IIMs) almost a year before placements (5th Semester). My experience helped me a lot in this
round, because I knew the template of how case-studies work . It was all about understanding the problems
associated with the product and providing solutions.
Suggestions:
a) Try and make your resume strong in terms of internships and competitions, because skill set is all
that matters.
b) Always mention numbers in your resume to show the impact you caused by the positions you were a
part of. For eg, during my tenure as a social media & marketing intern at ABC company, our
engagement shot up by 60%.

2. Interview Round 1:1 [15 students shortlisted for APgM/APM/AGM)]

About: In this round, each of the 15 shortlisted candidates had a one-on-one interview with the industry
experts of the domains. My interview lasted for around 1 hr 30 mins. I was asked about my case study, 1
guesstimate question, 1 RCA question and why I wanted to go into Product Management. Lastly I was
asked if I had any questions for the interviewers. I think one mistake that everyone should avoid in this
--- PAGE 2 ---
round is not listening to the interviewer. Always keep communicating, keep asking the interviewers if
your approach is correct, if the values and assumptions are correct etc.
How I Prepared : Guesstimates & RCA - https://www.youtube.com/@technomanagers/playlists

3. ¡HR Round] [ 6 candidates were shortlisted for APgM/APM/AGM]

About : In this round, the interviewer asked me to introduce myself followed by questions like why I wanted
to do product management, Proud moments in my experience, About my plans for masters etc. The
round ended with me asking the interviewer a few questions.
How I Prepared: What I did was first get an idea about questions that can be asked in the HR round. You
can easily find videos on Youtube about the same, or just ChatGPT the questions for your role. Once I
had the questionnaire ready, I started building answers about them based on my interests and role applied
for.
Suggestions: My technique for answering the questions in HR round is as follows:
First, tell the interviewer about the number of points you are going to talk about.
b) For each point, use a key-word and then explain each point in brief.
For eg: Why should we hire you?
Ans. - I think you should hire me mainly because of these three reasons. Firstly, I have a proven track
record, as in I have experience in this domain.......(Brief explanation). Secondly, I have a
customer-centric approach, which means that....(Brief Explanation). And lastly, I am really
adaptable, that is I understand.... (Brief Explanation)
c) Your Introduction in the HR round should be brief, try mentioning your experience more than talking
about your technical skills and always end the introduction with telling the interviewer why you are a
good fit for the role.

The entire process consisted of 3 rounds :

1. Technical Test

2. Technical Interview

3. Techno HR round

1. Technical Test [138 appeared for this round]

The test consisted of technical MCQs, 1 coding question and 1 SQL query with a time limit of 90 minutes.
MCQ section consisted of 12 questions which were based on core subjects and guess the output type of
questions. For this section I would recommend going through GFG guess the output questions (language
specific). Important thing to note is that each question has different weightage so make sure you solve
questions with more weightage correctly.
The coding question was a medium difficulty question and was based on string. The question was on a
constructive side rather than requiring any kind of data structure or algorithm to be solved. I was able to pass
all test cases.
Link to Question:https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
SQL query was a very basic one and included only one table.

2. Technical Round [ 34 students appeared for this round]

Students who correctly solved the MCQ section and were at least able to solve coding question partially
were shortlisted for this round.
--- PAGE 2 ---
This was a pure technical round. The interview started with the interviewer introducing himself after
which he asked for my introduction. Make sure you have a precise and concise introduction (aleast 30
seconds and specific to the role).
The interview proceeded with the interviewer asking me for one of my favorite projects. Since I had
worked on a College Portal in my 4th semester, he asked me how I would go on restructuring the entire
project if I were to start it from scratch. He then asked me to explain and draw the architecture of the
system and how I would improve the performance of the system.
I explained that we can deploy load balancer to distribute the incoming traffic across multiple servers
and create a cluster of databases to increase reliability. However he did not seem satisfied with my
answer and said that this won't improve the performance of the system in terms of response time. I later
provided him with a caching and message broker solution which he approved and we discussed it for
about 20 minutes.
Later he asked me how I would decide on the tech stack for this project. Since I had developed this
project using MERN he asked to choose different tech stack and reason for choosing specific technology.
After deciding the tech stack he asked how and which design principles I would use in my project.
Since I wasn't completely aware about all the design principles, I explained about which I was familiar
with. The interview ended with him asking me if I had any questions. I asked him about his role and how
would he utilize my skills if I were to work in his team. Make sure you ask questions at the end of
interview as it shows your interest in the company and the role.
The interview lasted for around 1hr 15 minutes.

3. Techno HR round [22 students appeared for this round]

For some students this was a technical+HR round and for some just HR round.
The interview started with the interviewer asking for my introduction. After which he asked me if I had
worked on any project that was used in real-life. Since I was part of IPL auction (Oculus) tech team I
explained to him about the application which was used on the day of the event. He asked to list 5-6
limitations of our applications and the solutions to overcome them. We talked about this for about 30
minutes. Later he asked me some scenario based questions like for example if my team leader asked me
to work on the latest requirement by the client without providing any concrete information, how would I
deal with the situation. Later he added that if the work was humanly impossible to do within a given time
how would I deal with this situation. I told him that in this case I would be honest with the client and tell
them what he/she should expect till the deadline. Through this I was able to highlight one of the barclays
core value which is Integrity. Make sure when answering such question you try to incorporate the core
values of the company. He kept on asking me scenario based questions for the next 25-30 minutes. The
interview ended with him asking me if I had any questions. I asked him about Barclays cloud platform
and why they prefer their own cloud platform and not any other public cloud service like AWS.

4. PRANK round

All the interviews for round 2 finished around 5:30 pm and all were eagerly waiting for the final
results. Later we came to know that there would be another round and were asked to assemble in the
conference room. They said that it would take another 2 hours for the entire process to conclude as they had
decided to take another round and asked us if we were comfortable with staying in college till late night.
--- PAGE 3 ---
They started calling out our name one by one after which they said that we all have been selected and there
won't be any further rounds. Everyone in the room was relieved and happy .
Total 19 grads were selected for full time role.

Process Date:

(All the processes were offline at the college)

- 11th July (PPT + OA)

- 12th July (2 Technical Rounds + 1 Hiring Manager Round)

Online Assessment/Coding Round [291 students appeared]:
This round was conducted on DoSelect platform. Questions: 4, Time: 90mins

1. Given an array, print the number of subarrays where XOR of all elements in the subarray, should

have an even number of divisors.
Eg. arr = [1 2 3]
Output: 3
Subarray [1, 2] has XOR value 3 (1, 3 are the divisors)
Subarray [2] has XOR value 2 (1, 2 are the divisors)
Subarray [3] has XOR value 3 (1, 3 are the divisors)

2. Given an array, print the lexicographically smallest array possible by swapping elements any number

of times but you can only swap 2 elements with each other if their XOR is strictly less than 4.
Eg. arr = [5, 2, 1, 4]
Output: [4, 1, 2, 5]
You can only swap (1, 2) and (4, 5) among themselves
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Given a binary string of length 'n', and 'q' queries having ranges L to R(1 based indexed and both

are inclusive). For every query, you have to sort the elements in the range L to R on the original
string to obtain a new string. Output the number of unique strings that would be obtained after all q
queries.
Eg. s = "11001»
Queries = [(2, 4), (3, 4), (3, 5)]
Output: 2
First query will result in : 10011
Second query will result in : 11001
Third query will result in : 11001

4. Given a directed graph and q queries related to it. The queries could be of 3 types. Add a dependency

(add edge A->B), remove a dependency (remove edge(A->B), query for checking a transitive
dependency (is there any we could reach B from A).
All the problems were solvable with brute-force approach. Most of the people who were shortlisted solved 2
problems completely and the other 2 partially. The total test was worth 400 points (each problem was worth
100 points, partial scoring was also counted), and your final score would be considered out of 400. Try to
read every problem first and attempt easier ones first. Keep trying to solve it till the last minute, wrong
submission doesn't have any penalty.

1. Technical Round 1[30 students]

There were two interviewers for my panel in this round. It started with the standard "Tell me about yourself"
question. I mentioned that I enjoy working on the backend, and they asked me why. Based on my answer,
they then asked me to describe a situation where I scaled or optimized a backend system.
The first technical question was Number of Flowers in Full Bloom - LeetCode. I initially explained the brute
force approach, then moved on to the difference array technique. They asked if we could optimize the space
complexity. For that, I suggested a different approach using sorting and two-pointers. Both approaches had
trade-offs in terms of time or space complexity. They then asked me to write the code for one of the
approaches on paper.
The second question was Lexicographically Kth smallest way to reach given coordinate from origin -
GeeksforGeeks. At first, I approached the problem using mathematical observation but it seemed too
complicated, and then I suggested that we keep generating the next permutation of the string k times but that
also had very bad time complexity. After seeing me struggle they gave me a hint, and I was able to figure
out the correct approach. I did a dry run on a test case, but as time was running out, they didn't ask me to
write the code for this one.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Tip: Even if you are not sure of your approach share it with them, they will help you point in the right
direction. Keep trying till the end maybe you figure out the approach at the last minute it matters a lot

2. Technical Round 2[13 students] (there were 3 of us whose round 2 happened after HM round)

In this interview round, there was one interviewer. First, he asked about the online assessment (OA) and my
day. Then he went straight to the first question: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully
Traversable - LeetCode. I mentioned that type 3 edges are always preferable. I explained my approach of
creating a minimum spanning tree using disjoint sets. He asked about the time complexity of the find_parent
function in a disjoint set union. I said it would be O(n), but with memoization, it could be reduced to O(1)
amortised time complexity. However, he pointed out that we should still consider the worst-case time
complexity as O(n). Then, I was asked to write the code on paper.
Next, he asked the second question:
"Given an N*M matrix initially set to 0 (where 0 indicates land and 1 indicates water), each day, a piece of
land at some (i, )) will turn into water. Given this input and the number of rows and columns, we need to
find the last day on which we could still reach the last row from the top row."
Since the previous question was about disjoint set union (DSU), my thoughts were making me think about a
solution using a similar approach. I observed that we could flip the problem to find the first day a river
would be formed; the day before that would be our answer. I explained my DSU solution, which had a time
complexity of O(N^2 * M^2) in the worst case. He asked if we could improve the time complexity and
hinted not to invert the problem and to optimize how we add water each day. I realized the approach should
involve binary search. After a few minutes of thinking, I provided a BFS + binary search approach with a
time complexity of ON * M * log(N * M)). The round ended with me asking him two questions.

3. Hiring Manager Round [9 students]

This round lasted over an hour, and the interviewer was an Engineering Manager at PhonePe. On the way to
the interview room, we had a brief chat about where I live and other small talk. The focus of this round was
mainly on my resume. It began with the usual "Tell me about yourself" question, followed by a detailed
discussion about my internships and projects. The questions were not very technical; they were more about
how I would implement additional use cases.
He asked about my final year project. I explained that it was only halfway completed, which is why it wasn't
on my resume. I described what was done so far and our plans for the next phase. He followed up by asking
how the project could be adapted for use at PhonePe and asked for a basic system overview. He then gave
me feedback on how to proceed in the next phase.
Next, he asked some behavioural questions. I initially didn't realize they were non-technical and should be
answered accordingly, so don't make this mistake. He asked what I would do in my first three months at a
new company and how I would handle a situation where the code I'm trying to understand is written by
--- PAGE 4 ---
someone who is very busy. He also asked about a situation where I had any conflicts with friends or
teammates.
He then asked if I had explored PhonePe app. I said I had only used it for making payments and hadn't
explored other features. He asked me to explain the process flow for scanning and making a payment to a
merchant's QR code and encouraged me to use paper if needed. I gave a brief explanation of what I thought
happened behind the scenes but didn't draw a proper architecture or process flow.
At the end, I asked him a few questions. Taking the stairs to the fourth floor had left me out of breath and
made me nervous initially, but the interviewer was very friendly and made me feel comfortable.
6 students received the offer (Intership+FTE).

Useful Tips:

1. For OA don't panic and read the problems carefully (giving coding contests might help)

2. For Technical Rounds

a. Try practising "thinking out loud" while solving problems
b. You should be able to solve leetcode hard level difficulty with hints in 20-30mins, so try
practising with a similar time limit
c. More than the optimal solution they are looking for how you approach a problem, try to break
it down into smaller problems and keep sharing your ideas with the interviewer.

3. For HM Round

a. Be transparent while answering the questions (avoiding unnecessary details)
b. They want to assess your attitude and behaviour in this round
c. Try to show that you are passionate about what you do and always keen to learn

4. Remember, it's not over until it is, so keep trying until the end, even if you least expect things to go

your way.
All the best!
You can contact me on LinkedIn

Process Dates:

- 11th June (Pre-placement Talks + Online Assessment (DoSelect)

- 12th June (Interview Rounds - 2 Technical Rounds, HR Round)

Coding Round:

- 90 Minutes - 4 Questions (Almost 300 students appeared for this test)

1. Given an array, return the number of subarrays where xor of all elements in the

subarray, should have an even number of divisors.

2. Output the lexicographically smallest array, where you can perform array

swapping operation (any number of times) on index i, j (i<j) where arrli]^arri] < 4.

3. Given a binary string of length 'n', and 'q' queries having ranges I to r. For every

query, you have to sort the elements in the range I to r on the original string to
obtain a new string. Output the number of unique strings that would be obtained
after all q queries.

4. Given a directed graph and q queries related to it. The queries could be of 3

types. Add a dependency, remove a dependency, query for checking a transitive
dependency.
I was able to solve the first 2 questions completely and partially solved the third
question. Expertise in problem solving is required to clear this round.
30 students were shortlisted for the interviews on the next day.
Round - 1 (Technical Round) | 30 Students
There were 15 panels that were going on simultaneously for Round - 1
interviews.
The round started with the panelist introducing himself, and he explained about his work
at PhonePe. I was curious about it so I asked him a few questions related to it. The
interviewer then asked me for my introduction. In my introduction I mentioned that I was
--- PAGE 2 ---
a specialist on codeforces and then we had a discussion on codeforces rounds. We
then started with the questions.

1. Given n ranges of time period (start day and end day) during which a flower

blossoms in a garden, followed by q queries, where i-th query represents the day
on which a person would come to the garden. The answer to the i-th query is the
total number of flowers blossomed during those days.
Almost immediately, I gave him the brute force approach of it, moving to the
optimal prefix summation technique. He then increased the constraints of the
ranges to 1e9, so we won't have an array that huge. Since I had solved some
similar range type questions on CSES, I had some intuitions for a better
approach. During the discussion to improvise time complexity even further I
suggested a segment tree approach, to which he said that would work with the
given time complexity constraints but to think of another approach that wouldn't
use a complex data structure. Using a hint I was able to solve this question, and I
was asked to write the complete code of it on paper.

2. Given a matrix of MxN size, we can move to right or down, we want to reach

some arbitrary point (x,y) and for every move we append H for right or V for down
in a string. Of all the possible strings, we want to give the k-th lexicographically
smallest string. He was expecting a mathematical solution to it rather than a
graph. Took a few hints to reach the mathematical solution from a graph based
approach. There wasn't enough time left to write the code for this question but
the interviewer was satisfied with our discussion of both the questions.
I asked him a few questions that I was curious about after the pre-placement talk. 14
students were shortlisted after round.
Round - 2 (Technical Round) [ 14 students ]

- All the 14 selected candidates were being interviewed simultaneously.

There were 2 interviewers in my panel. The round started with both of them introducing
themselves. The interviewers clarified in the beginning that they expect me to write code
of both the questions on paper and take minimum hints for the 2 questions that they
would ask me. (But I'm guessing that it was just to try and put me under some pressure
situation even before giving me the problems)

1. Given a grid of NxM size, initially all the boxes would be filled with 0, and another

array of pair of integers which mention that on i-th day, (x,y) box would be
flooded with water (can be represented with 1, and 0 would mean that the grid
isn't flooded). Find the maximum 'i for which I can travel from top to bottom (one
--- PAGE 3 ---
can move in all 4 directions) and I can only step on non-flooded grid at a time. At
first I gave them a tricky, new approach, to which they both were quite intrigued
and all 3 of us were working on some test case on which my approach would fail.
Eventually I could come with a test case that my solution would fail on. And then I
asked for a hint, to which he told me that a monotonic function is being
developed on the days array. I was able to gather from this hint that it is a binary
search solution. I then gave him the binary search + bfs solution to it. We
discussed the time complexity of it and I wrote the code for it on paper.

2. We are given a graph and it consists of 3 types of edges, type -1 edge can only

be traversed by alex, type -2 edges can only be traversed by bob and type -3
edges can be traversed by both of them. So how many maximum edges can be
removed so both of them are able to traverse all vertices present in the graph. In
almost no time I could come up with the optimal approach to solve this problem
using 2 DSU's. I explained to them the structure of a DSU. This was the optimal
approach they were expecting. They made me write the code for this problem
first assuming that I have the DSU class implemented, and after I wrote the code
for this, they asked me to implement the DSU class. I wrote all the codes on
paper.
By the end of this interview, I was too exhausted and thirsty so I didn't ask them any
questions, but in both the technical rounds I had some amazing conversations with the
panelists (so basically it became fine for me to not ask any question I believe XD). 9
people cleared this round (of which 3 of us had our HM round taken before round - 2
because they wanted to optimize the interview process, I was one of them).
Round - 3 (HM Round) | 9 students ]
I was called for this round right after my round - 1 interviews. Going to the room I was
expecting a technical round. But it was only after I sat down I got to know this was a HM
Round. The interviewer started reading my resume. And asked me questions on
everything and anything that I had written in it. He asked me questions related to my
projects, on what was my learning, or if something that could be added. He asked me a
few questions related to my competitive programming skills, like why giving more
contests on these platforms makes me a better engineer and not just a better coder. He
asked me questions relating to my experience and work in CSI-SPIT. He asked me a
few behavioral questions and gave a few situations and how I would respond to those.
For all such situations he also wanted me to give some personal examples. He asked
me if I had used the PhonePe app. I told him that I didn't use any UP service but I do
know in's and out's about the app as my elder brother and parents used it. He asked me
if there is something missing in the app. He asked me for a start up, (they expect some
--- PAGE 4 ---
ideas that solve some real problems, also think of the business expect of it, on how it
would make its revenue and all). He asked me a few system design questions for the
most frequent app that I used on my phone. This interview focuses on your critical
thinking on different situations and interests towards the system design aspect as
PhonePe is a product based company.
Finally, 6 candidates received the job offer. All of our offers were i+p.

1. Stay calm and confident throughout the interview process. Focus on your

individual progress for the entire preparation phase and to not compare yourself
with others.

2. PhonePe interviews focus a lot on DSA. The only way to master it is to solve

more and more questions. There is no shortcut to it. Give more and more
contests. CP isn't a must, but it helps a lot.

3. Think out loud during the technical interviews. It's fine to ask for hints, when stuck

(hints are to get closer to the optimal approach, hints give ideas to go for which
approach, solve more questions to build that intuition).

4. Be well prepared for any format of the interviews, you can never expect only DP

or Graphs questions to be asked in the OA's, have a well understanding of other
topics as well. My round-3 was conducted right after my round-1 and before
round-2, so be prepared for all rounds beforehand, as some reordering might
happen.
All the best! Feel free to reach out!

IDFC visited around the end of July, conducting their PPT between the 25th and 27th. It was announced that
the recruitment process would include:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Two Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

However, due to the tough decision of selecting between the final eight HR candidates, two additional
technical rounds were conducted with higher technical positions and a Senior Managing Director. In total,
there were six rounds:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Four Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

1.
Hechnical Round 1] [ around 36 students appeared this round]
This round was one of the main rounds of the process, lasting around 40-50 minutes. It focused primarily on
my resume, core knowledge, and problem-solving approach. The flow of the interview was as follows:
--- PAGE 2 ---

1. Introduction and Skills:

• The interviewer asked me to introduce myself and outline my skills.

• Based on my introduction, he chose my main programming language (C++) and asked

questions about its concepts, such as pointers, virtual tables, OOP in C++, and the reasons for
choosing C++.
o Despite being more familiar with Java, the interviewer had a solid understanding of C++.

2. OOP Concepts:

• He asked about polymorphism, the reasons for using polymorphism, multiple inheritance, and

its availability in both Java and C++.

• I answered smartly, explaining the concept and the diamond problem associated with multiple

inheritance, which demonstrated my strong foundational knowledge.

3. Project-Based Questions:

• The interviewer inquired about one of my projects, specifically the stock data analysis project

using Kafka and AWS services.
o Questions included why I made the project, its purpose, how it works, and the technologies
used.

• He asked me to explain the project's step-by-step process and architecture.

4. DSA and Real-Life Scenarios:

• The interviewer presented real-life scenarios and asked how I would solve them or which

data structures I would use for efficient solutions.

• There was also a question that you know sql stores data in form of tables, So in physical

memory will that be in tabular format only or how is it stored and retrieved.
Throughout the interview, he emphasized the importance of understanding how things work on a physical
level, such as data storage on databases and hard disks, rather than just knowing the concepts superficially.
Pro-Tip: It's crucial to handle questions you're unsure about effectively. Instead of simply saying "I don't
know," try to relate the topic to something familiar. For example, you can say, "I am not sure/unaware about
this, but as I can relate this to certain CS fundamental concepts, it could be this or that." Moreover, you can
ask the interviewer for help if you're unable to recall something.

2. [Technical Round 2] [ 12 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was more of a technical + HR kind of round. It was pretty relaxed, and the interviewer was very
friendly. Here is a breakdown of the interview:

1. Introduction and Background:

o The interviewer asked me to introduce myself.

• He inquired about my background, specifically how I, being from Jammu, chose to come this

far for my education.

2. Resume Grilling:

• The interviewer asked about my internship, requesting a brief summary of what I did during

that time, how I got the internship, and what benefits I gained from it.
--- PAGE 3 ---

• He asked about my projects and various tools mentioned in my resume, such as Postman and

Docker.

• For Postman, he asked me to explain its usage, what it does, the protocols involved, the

differences between GET and POST requests, what the requests look like, and other related
concepts.
The purpose was to verify that my resume was accurate and to check my conceptual knowledge. This part of
the interview lasted about 20-30 minutes.
Pro-Tip:

• Be calm and do not lie on your resume.

• In your introduction, emphasize the topics you are well-prepared for, as future questions will likely

be based on this.

• If you are not fully prepared about something, remove it from your resume or avoid mentioning it in

your introduction.

3. [HR round] [ 8 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was like a typical HR round. The interviewer asked me to introduce myself but then suddenly
stopped me and gave me around 10 questions to be answered in my introduction, such as:

• Where are you trom?

• Your schooling background

• Your grades

• The games you play

• Extracurricular activities

It was a bit confusing at the time, but I tried to stay calm and answer the questions appropriately. I managed
to answer most of them but forgot a few, so I asked the interviewer what else he needed to know.
Here is how the rest of the interview went:

1. Games and Interests:

• He asked which games I play. I mentioned that I used to play basketball but later got into

online games and now focus on coding.

• He then asked about online games and how I would make or structure a game like PUBG.

• I explained that games are developed on Unreal Engine, which I haven't used, but I

described the basic flow: first, creating the action figures, relating everything to
classes and objects with certain values and methods, and making the arena a real-time
collaborative environment.

2. HR Questions:

• Three strengths and three weaknesses: I ensured my answers were professional and aligned

with the company's needs and my strengths.

• Where do you see yourself in the next five years? Another typical HR question that I

answered thoughtfully.
--- PAGE 4 ---
The interview was conducted online and lasted about 20-30 minutes. My key advice for such rounds is to be
friendly with the interviewer, stay calm, and handle questions effectively.

4. [Technical round 3] [ 8 candidates appeared this round]

This round was not initially planned. Interviews were completed, and the results were supposed to be
announced that night. However, the next day, we received a notification about an additional round. The 8
selected candidates were among the best in the college, and the company initially intended to recruit 5-6
candidates based on their HR head's discussion with the TPO. Since they couldn't decide, they conducted
one more round to finalize the selections.
This additional round was taken by their senior manager to test our technical skills rigorously. It involved an
in-depth grilling on our concepts and projects. Here's how it went:

1. Primary Language Focus:

• The interviewer emphasized my primary language (C++) and asked deep questions about its

concepts such as pointers, memory addresses, virtual tables, template classes, etc.

• I handled this well due to my strong knowledge of C++.

2. Secondary Language:

• He then asked for my second language, which I mentioned was Java.

• He asked about the difference between generics in Java and templates in C++. I couldn't

answer this as I wasn't deeply familiar with Java, but it worked out fine.

3. Project Questions:

o He asked why I chose my projects and what problems they solved.
o Questions on React and JavaScript were also posed, including why I preferred that tech stack.

4. Final Question:

• The last question was why they should prefer me over others. Instead of saying I am better, I

highlighted my strengths and aligned my answer with the job description.

5. [Technical Round 41 [ 8 candidates appeared for this round too ]

This round was conducted by their senior Managing Director (MD) and focused more on technical
knowledge and problem-solving approach. The atmosphere was quite relaxed. Here is a breakdown of the
interview:

1. Introduction and Final Year Project:

• The interviewer asked me to introduce myself.

• As I am currently in my 4th year, he inquired about my major final year project. I mentioned

that I was using a Large Language Model (LLM) in my project.

• He then asked how I would solve the problem if there was no LLM available.

2. Data Structures and Algorithms:

• The interviewer moved on to a DSA problem and asked which data structure I would use to

solve it.

• I explained that I would use a TRIE and illustrated the basic structure on OneNote.

3. HR Question:

• He concluded the interview with a single HR-type question.

--- PAGE 5 ---
The interview lasted about 15 minutes.
Finally, after all these rounds, all 8 students were selected for the Application Engineer position.
Tip: Give mock interviews and practice interviews with your friends. This will help you be prepared for
anything that can be asked in an interview.

question. Do not just solve the problem; the interviewer wants to understand your approach. Take a
moment to think before you start answering to avoid giving a rushed impression. If you do not know
the answer, be honest about it. If you know the approach but cannot reach the final answer, explain

For the placement process, three rounds were conducted. There was a resume shortlisting round before any
of the actual rounds happened. 182 students were shortlisted after the resume round.

1. Round 1: SQL [46 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

The first round of my interview, conducted online via Google Meet, started with a brief introduction of
myself and lasted about 30 minutes, focusing on SQL. A single interviewer asked me questions ranging
from very easy to hard Leetcode SQL queries, with the difficulty level increasing after each correct answer.
I tackled five questions in total: a simple WHERE query, a straightforward JOIN query, a more complex
query covering aggregate functions, joins, the GROUP BY clause, and window functions, and finally, a
question about the difference between DENSE_RANK() and RANK().  I was able to provide correct
answers to all the queries.

2. Round 2: Problem Solving [24 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

The second round of my interview lasted about 45  minutes. After introducing myself again, I was asked
to solve two guesstimates. The first question was to estimate the number of Maggi packets sold in India
in a day. Although I initially got stuck and confused in my approach, the interviewer guided me to solve
it using a different method. The second question was quite unique: I had  to estimate the number of liters
of alcohol required at a middle-class Punjabi wedding. I asked preliminary questions to gather necessary
details and estimated the number of guests to be 500. I categorized the guests into kids, adults, and senior
citizens, further dividing adults and senior citizens into low, medium, and high drinking capacities. After
receiving the values in milliliters for each category from the interviewer, I performed the calculations and
provided an answer. The interviewer appreciated my approach and showed interest in my response. It
is crucial to ask preliminary questions to ensure your assumptions are correct and to communicate your
thought process to the interviewer throughout the problem -solving. He then asked if I have any
questions for them.

Also, my panel did not ask me puzzles and some advance SQL, but students from other panels were asked
so make sure you prepare that too . Some students were also asked about root cause analysis of a certain
company.

3. Round 3: Culture Fit [10 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

The final round of my interview began at 7:30 pm and lasted approximately 45 to 50 minutes. The interviewer
started by introducing himself, and when it was my turn, he interrupted my prepared introduction, advising
me to avoid a rehearsed response. As our conversation progressed, it maintained a relaxed and informal tone.
The interviewer asked about the places I have visited in India and requested that I highlight the most underrated
one. He also inquired about my extracurricular activities and my ac hievements, the committees I was
involved in, and the Position of Responsibility for the college fest mentioned on my resume. He asked about
my learnings from that role and why I chose to be part of it for three years.
The interviewer then asked about my plans for further education, specifically whether I intended to pursue an
MBA or a Master's degree, suggesting that a Master's degree would enhance my profile. He wanted to know
why I believed I was a suitable fit for the role  and what unique qualities I brought to the table .
Additionally, he asked about my knowledge of WorkIndia and which of their mission values resonated with
me. Although the interviewer maintained a casual tone, it was clear that the evaluation began from the outset
of the interview.
Towards the end of the session, I had the opportunity to ask questions. Just as I did in the previous round, I
used this chance to pose well-researched and unique questions  about the company. This final interaction
was crucial for creating a lasting impression and demonstrating a genuine interest in the organization.
Total 5 students including me, were selected, and offered the I + P offer from Work India for the Data
Analyst role

1. Keep engaging with your interviewer by thinking out loud and explaining your logic when given a

question. Do not just solve the problem; the interviewer wants to understand your approach. Take a
moment to think before you start answering to avoid giving a rushed impression. If you do not know
the answer, be honest about it. If you know the approach but cannot reach the final answer, explain
your thought process.

2. It is essential to have a strong understanding of all SQL concepts. Use resources like w3schools to

reinforce your knowledge and challenge yourself by solving 50 SQL questions on platforms like
LeetCode. These problems will test your problem -solving skills and deepen your understanding of
SQL.

3. Enhance your learning by working on real -world projects related to data analysis or data science.

Applying SQL in practical scenarios will improve your logical thinking and show you how SQL fits
into larger data-driven processes.

4. Develop your critical thinking and puzzle-solving skills by engaging with challenges on platforms like

GeeksforGeeks and Brainstellar. These exercises will sharpen your problem-solving abilities.

5. Boost your confidence and refine your communication skills, as these are crucial for effective

interaction during interviews.

6. If you still have any questions or need guidance, feel free to contact me on LinkedIn

journey.howSecured:
1. Round 1: Resume Shortlisting (All students above 6 CGPA were shortlisted)

Before Resume Shortlisting we were asked to fill the registration form on their website, make sure
you stick to any one resume format and use the same email address everywhere you apply and make
sure you fill all applicable fields.

2. Round 2: Online test

Test Duration: 1 Hour
Platform: HirePro
Test information: 3 Sections (Aptitude, Reasoning, Verbal skills, 2 Coding Questions) Each section
was having definite time (no switching between sections), MCQ's were mostly easy and solvable.
And last section was coding, coding Questions asked were so easy to solve. More weightage was on
solving aptitude reasoning and solving MCQ.

3. Round 3: Online Interview (Technical + HR: 30 min) [35 Students]

A day before the interview we were assigned specific time slots for the interview. Each slot was 30
minutes and my interview was scheduled from 10.00 to 10.30 AM.
My interview began with the interviewer introducing himself, followed by my introduction. I had
prepared an impressive introduction, which included details about my experience, projects, skills, and,
most importantly, my achievements. Preparing a strong introduction is essential because it allows you to
steer the direction of the interview. After my introduction, he asked me in detail about my internship at a
startup. This was followed by some technical questions and one HR question: "How has this internship
helped you grow?" Another question was related to my work and coordination with the founders, though
--- PAGE 2 ---
I don't remember it exactly.
He then asked me three in-depth questions about the frontend, mainly regarding React. I answered two of
them but couldn't answer the third one correctly. When he asked if I was sure about my answer to the
third question, I was honest and explained that I had been more focused on backend work and hadn't
worked on the frontend in several months. Never lie in your interview.
He also asked detailed questions about Docker. Since I had mentioned AWS in my resume, he asked
about where I had used it and my experience with it. Later, he asked if I had taken on any leadership
roles, to which I mentioned leading a team of four developers in building the Oculus event website, as
well as leading my team in the National Hackathon at Barclays.
I had also noted my activity as a problem solver on LeetCode and my strong ranking in their contests. He
asked me an HR question about how participating in contests on LeetCode helps me upskill. Then he
asked what language I prefer for contests, to which I answered C++. He followed up with questions about
different types of data structures, asking me to provide real-life examples. Afterward, he gave me three
DSA questions (focused on string manipulation, stack, and recursion) and asked me to explain my
approach, to which I provided three approaches for each. Then, he asked two SQL questions and one
query.
He also asked if I'd be comfortable working with unfamiliar technologies. I told him that I would be,
sharing how I had learned AWS, Docker, and other tools during my internship, demonstrating my
"learn-as-you-go' attitude.
Finally, he concluded by asking if I had any questions for him. Make sure to prepare plenty of specific,
interesting questions about the company-avoid generic ones. He didn't ask me about my projects,
likely because there was already so much information on my resume. I had designed my resume in a way
that ensured specific questions would come up.
I had only one interview, while some students attended two. In the evening, the results were announced,
and 15 students were selected for the opportunity-I was one of them.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Important tips:

1. Prepare an well-crafted introduction

2. Make notes during pre-placement talk

3. Solve striver's A2Z DSA sheet at least once; you don't need to be a knight on LC or a pupil on

CF to clear the interview rounds

4. Solving LC top 50 SQL sheet will give you enough ideas about different types of possible sql

questions

5. Dont panic in the interview, simply ask for help-interviewers are very helpful

6. Practice mock interview with friends

7. Thinking aloud might help you a lot

8. After every interview, prepare genuine questions and avoid generic ones. The notes you made

during the pre-placement talk might assist you here. Prefer asking follow-up questions and
engage in a conversation

9. Don't mess up with your CGPA. It will kill your chances and it hurts :)

Linking resume for reference: Resume
Kuch doubt toh puch liyo:) LinkedIn
All the best for your placements!!!
