journey.howSecured:
3 Rounds were conducted in total, 1 Online Test and 2 Interviews

1. Online Test [138 candidates]

The test was of 1 hour 30 minutes, it consisted of CS fundamental MCQS (variable marks), a DSA question
(50 marks) and an SQL query (10 marks).
The DSA question was similar to this:
https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
The SQL question was a basic aggregate query.
I was able to solve 5/10 test cases for DSA, SQL and MCQs.

2. Tech Interview [34 candidates]

The interviews were scheduled for the next day, after the ppt. Be attentive during the ppt as it will be helpful
in answering certain questions in the interviews.
My first interviewer was a Vice President at Barclays. He did not ask for an introduction and started
discussing my first project for a few minutes.
After that I was asked about OOPs concepts (Polymorphism and Inheritance in Java). The questions on
polymorphism were about differentiating between overriding and overloading and whether function return
type should be different for overloading. Next, I was asked to give an example of inheritance, then he asked
if there are 2 classes, SUV and Truck, what relation would be among them (siblings, as they will be derived
from a parent class Vehicle as inheritance is an IS-A relationship).
Next I was asked an SQL query where I had to find the second largest value in a column (offset).
Then I was asked 'Why Barclays?', to which I responded that I had an interest in the fintech domain. He
followed with asking about topics on finance (which I did not have as much knowledge on and mentioned
it). I was given a question where I had to calculate the compound interest, given 1000R as principal, rate of
10% and duration of 3 years. I could not recall the formula for it so he said that I could use the formula for
--- PAGE 2 ---
simple interest. Using that, I calculated the final amount compounding it annually. Then he asked me to
derive the formula for compound interest using the obtained series.
Next I was asked a puzzle similar to this:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-the-burning-candles/
In the end he was open to questions so I asked about general projects that Barclays does and projects that he
has done as a part of Barclays.

3. Tech+HR Interview [21 candidates]

Generally these interviews were HR only, but for me it was a mix of tech and HR. The interviewer first
asked me for an introduction (tech stack, hobbies and family background). Then he asked how my day had
gone so far, and how my first interview went and an overview of it (I gave a brief recollection of it,
remember the name of your interviewers as it creates a good impression). He asked when I had started
preparing for Barclays and what achievements did Barclays have that made me interested in it (paying
attention to the ppt helped out a lot here) and when had I become interested in the CS domain.
After that he moved on to asking why I chose web development and my tech stack (MERN), more details on
my project and that if I was selected, which role would suit me best (again it was important to have had paid
attention to ppt as six roles were mentioned for which they were hiring). Then he asked me whether I knew
what accessibility features were (in regards to UI/UX).
Next was a scenario based question where data was classified as secret, internal, external and unrestricted
and that I had to classify it. First was data from a customer who had submitted it to the company (I answered
internal, as the customer had trusted the company with their private information), next if I was a manager
what type of data would be my employee's salary (I answered secret).
Next I was asked situational questions. First, if I were part of a team whose project is to be launched the next
day and I encountered a bug the night prior, what would be my response? Next, a meeting is called with the
developers and testers, how would I relay information about the bug in that meeting? Eventually he asked a
question on unit testing and I said that I was not familiar with it, so he moved on to the next scenario, which
was more related to ML models.
In the end he asked me for any questions to which I asked what was his favorite part of working at Barclays.
In the end 19 candidates got selected (following a prank round 3 :))

journey.prep:
1. Preparation Resources:

• Aptitude Questions: IndiaBix

• Guesstimates/ RCA:

→ The Consulting & Strategy Club, IIM Lucknow - YouTube: Initial understanding
→ Case Interviews Cracked - YouTube: Initial understanding

• [Case_Interviews_Cracked_Case_Interviews.pdf](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LbGkz-cPT_lqWW3s9Op7C23bDBWwGKmS/view?usp=drive_link): To practice Case Studies (this level is

higher than that asked in interviews).

• Puzzles: Top 100 GFG

• SQL:

→ SOLBolt: Use initially to get a hang of the basics
→ GFG SOL Articles: For theory/ better understanding
→ Leetcode SOL 50: For practice (sufficient for InCred rounds)

2. Resume Shortlisting:

• Make sure to tailor your resume according to the role. If you don't have a particular role in mind or

want to try out for multiple roles, I suggest keeping 2 projects per role handy and then changing the
projects in your resume according to the role.

• Use a single-column ATS-friendly resume. (Overleaf or Resume Worded)

• Always check your Resume score using a resume checker. (Resume Worded)

• If you're using Resume Worded, a score of 65+ is great!

3. Interviews (general tips):

o In interviews, questions often arise from the conversation flow and your responses. Use this to your
advantage by steering the discussion towards your strengths and preferred topics.

• Prepare some standard HR questions before the interview.

• Research the company thoroughly and keep a few questions ready to ask after the interviews.

• If you mess up during the interview, it's completely fine and normal. Don't get nervous because of it

and try to laugh it off and correct yourself as soon as possible! Smile and try to seem relaxed.

• Always be humble. HR representatives are really good at detecting overconfidence or

underconfidence, so try to be neutral.

• Lastly, just be yourself and let your personality shine!

For any further questions, feel free to reach out to me on Linkedin
Keep at it and believe in yourself! All the best!
journey.howSecured:
- Pre-Placement Talk (Online) - 24th July

- Resume Shortlisting - 25th July

- Written Assessment and Interviews - 26th July

The process consisted of a resume shortlisting, a written pen-and-paper test and 2 interview rounds. There
was no distinct HR interview. One HR representative from the company was present in each round to ask
relevant HR questions.

1. Round 1: Written Test (Offline) (124 students)

Highlights: Aptitude, SOL, Python
We had 25 minutes to solve the test. It was given on a printed paper where we had to tick correct options for
MCQs and write answers for other questions. The test included 12 Aptitude questions, 3 SQL questions, and
1 Python programming question. I solved the Aptitude section first as it was easier, then the Python
question, and finally the SQL queries.

• Aptitude (MCQ format)

This section had easy questions on topics like Profit and Loss, Time and Work, and Simple Interest.
It's important to solve these quickly since the SQL section usually needs more time. About 10-12
minutes should be enough for this part.

• SQL Questions (Write query on test paper)

We got 3 easy-to-medium SQL questions. They involved writing SELECT queries, JOINing tables,
and creating output tables for different types of JOINs. This section needs careful thinking, so I
suggest using about 10 minutes for it.

• Python Question (Write solution on test paper)

This was an easy question about summing N natural numbers. I spent about 2-3 mins on this section.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The test aims to test both speed and accuracy. To move to the interview rounds, you need to get almost
all questions right. Do not underestimate the test after looking at the difficulty of the questions! While
the questions are easy, you will need to use the allotted 25 mins wisely to clear this round.
38 students progressed after this round

2. Round 2: Interview Round 1(38 students)

Highlights: Resume-based questions, SQL, Guesstimates (Duration: 45 - 60 mins)
For this round, there were 3 interview panels, each consisting of 2-3 panellists. My panel had three
members: one HR representative and two technical experts.
Upon entering, I was first told that I had answered 15 out of 16 questions correctly in the written test and
asked to guess which one I might have gotten wrong. Next, I was asked to introduce myself. Following that,
they inquired why I chose InCred and a BA role. I shared a few personal experiences, along with my interest
in participating in case studies to support my response. Afterwards, I was asked to name one Data Analytics
project I had completed, describe it, and state the top 5 analytical conclusions I drew from the project. I
could only recall and name 3. They asked a few follow-up questions before moving on to guesstimates.
While discussing one of my case studies, we started talking about OTT platforms and their relation to my
case study topic. One of the panelists then asked me to estimate the number of Netflix subscribers in India. I
asked some preliminary questions and made a decision tree to estimate. My number was too high. In such
situations, it's crucial not to get nervous and to try to build upon your previous logic. I hadn't considered
rural/urban and age factors, so I explained this and recalculated. The interviewer wasn't fully satisfied but
decided to move on to technical questions. For the technical part, I was asked a few resume-based techstack
justifications, different types of keys in SQL and execution sequences for statements in SQL.
Finally, I was asked if I had any questions for them. I asked two questions related to the company and the
role, after which we concluded the interview.
15 students progressed after this round

4. Round 3: Interview Round 2 (15 students)

Highlights: Case Study Question (Duration: 45 - 60 mins)
My panel had two panellists. My case study question was to add a loan function to the PhonePe app. When
facing case study questions, always ask relevant preliminary questions to fully understand the problem and
requirements. I took about 10 minutes to understand the PS and asked around 8-10 questions.
After taking the interviewers' input I concluded that I had to look at 2 major points: Data analysis of the
target audience (to analyze what features we should have) and Basic UI or input parameters. I classified
people according to different parameters to understand who would be eligible to take a loan.
--- PAGE 3 ---
For most of the interview, I focused on providing a detailed analysis of the target audience. This part lasted
for about 30 minutes. It's important to keep this round as conversation-like as possible. Talk to the
interviewers, take their feedback regularly and keep them engaged. Once the interviewer was satisfied with
my analysis, he told me to move on to the UI/ Input parameters part and I drew a basic Wireframe for the UI
and listed 6 major parameters that should be taken as input from the user before considering giving a loan.
The interviewer was satisfied with my responses. Finally, I was asked if I had any questions for them. I
asked two questions related to the company and the role, after which we concluded the interview.
5 students were given the offer after this round

Process Date: 30 August 2024

1. OA Round - DSA Computer fundamentals and Aptitude (Criteria min 7 CGPA)

There were 3 sections - Problem Solving 1  problem, Technical MCQ -20 Q and General Aptitude and
Communication MCQ-15 Q
I got a substrings dynamic programming problem which was very much easy as it was similar to the ones I
had practiced.
Technical MCQs were on code snippets, OOPS, CCN, OS and DBMS.
General Aptitude was of the Indiabix level.
So total 36 questions in 2 hrs.

2. Preplacement Talk

3. Technical Interview (40 students appeared for this round.)

The interviewer began by asking how many interviews I had previously attended, ensuring I was comfortable
with the interview process. The first question was an introduction. Then, he inquired about my proficiency in
Java. When asked if I had experience with backend development in Java, I honestly mentioned that I didn't
have direct experience but explained the general flow of how backend development is typically done in Java,
which I had prepared for a prior Java-based role. He then asked about Spring Boot, and I admitted that I wasn't
familiar with it. However, I assured him that if it was required for the role, I would make it a priority to learn.
The conversation moved on to OOP concepts, where he tested my understanding of the basics.
Next, he asked me to write a basic "Hello World" program in Java, expecting me to explain each part of the
code as I wrote it. After that, we discussed exception handling in Java, focusing on the try, catch, and finally
blocks, and the Throwable interface. He posed a tricky question about the execution order when multiple catch
blocks are present, essentially testing my understanding of the exception hierarchy. The interview then shifted
to SQL, where I was asked to write a basic query, which was straightforward. He also asked me to explain
different types of joins, which I did using Venn diagrams, similar to those found on GeeksforGeeks.

We then moved on to system design and various design patterns. Although I couldn't recall all the patterns, I
mentioned the ones I knew. I chose to explain the Singleton pattern in detail. When I struggled to articulate it,
I asked if I could demonstrate with code, which I did, and he seemed satisfied with my explanation.
Finally, he asked some CSS-related questions, including what typically goes into a CSS file (classes containing
key-value pairs) and about Tailwind CSS.  He also asked me about basics of Machine Learning . There were
no DSA questions in this round.
This round lasted for around 35 -40 minutes . Throughout this interview, it's crucial to provide thorough
explanations for your answers, using examples , codes, diagrams, and detailed concept explanations. This
approach helps avoid tricky follow -up questions that could potentially lower your confidence.  If you don't
know a concept, politely admit it, and emphasize your willingness to learn.

3. HR Interview (25 approx students were appeared for this round.)

This interview also began with introduce myself. Following that, the interviewer inquired about my internship,
focusing on the platform's users, my role, the current status of the website, the tech stack we chose, and the
challenges I faced during development.
He then asked me to explain a recent project, so I chose to discuss a blockchain project I had worked on. He
mentioned recent news about data breaches in blockchains and asked why these occur. I didn't have any idea
of data breaching in blockchain, I didn't have an immediate answer, I asked which specific blockchain he was
referring to and guessed it might be Hyperledger. I then explained how Hyperledger works and guessed and
identified potential vulnerabilities that might not be fully explored during smart contract development. I also
described a vulnerability that had occurred in a smart contract I developed earlier. He then asked how these
vulnerabilities could be identified  beforehand. I responded by sharing a past scenario where I had handled
similar work.
The conversation then shifted to the software development lifecycle (SDLC). He asked about various models,
specifically the Agile model, and inquired about the scaling factors used to measure development progress.
Since I had mentioned software testing on my resume, he delved into that as well, asking about different
testing levels, including black box and white box testing, as well as static and dynamic testing. I was well -
prepared for these questions and provided detailed answers . He then asked my about Data migration about
which I didn't know anything but I did have basic understanding what it was and explained in layman terms.
He then asked about the process which goes behind that,  And I politely replied that I didn't have knowledge
about it. He then asked about jdk, jre why is Java a plateform independent language.
Finally, he asked about the most challenging project I had worked on and why it was difficult, which I had
also prepared for. Since I mentioned my leadership role on my resume, he asked in -depth questions about it,
including the marketing deals I managed a nd how I balanced those responsibilities with my studies.  Finally
he asked if had any question.  I asked him about how a role shift process occurs at Oracle and about Oracle
institute.

This too lasted for around 40 minutes. Overall, this round focused heavily on the experiences and skills I had
mentioned in my resume. Confidence in your answers, maintaining a positive attitude, and good posture are
key to succeeding in this round. This is a round where in you should be ready to answer the questions which
you haven't prepared. If you don't know a term completely then polite tell or if you know it a bit try to guess
or explain it with your similar past experience examples.

Eligibility criteria was 8.5 CGPA which got lowered to 8 for Software Engineer, SQL developer and 7.5
for Analytical Verification and Software Testing roles
Hiring Workflow:

● Pre-placement talk

● Online Assessment

● Technical Interview

● HR Interview

1.     Online Assessment (155 students appeared for the test)

The test was conducted in College on Google Forms. 70 questions - 90 minutes. It had +1, -0.25
marking scheme.
Test was divided into 4 sections -
Java 18 questions
Python 17 questions
SQL 5 questions
Aptitude 30 questions
Java and Python part were mostly predicting the output from given code, OOPS concepts, collection
framework, lists, exception handling, etc.
In SQL, we had to predict the correct query for each question
Aptitude section was very lengthy. It had speed, distance, probability, interest rate, etc type
questions

2.     Technical Interview (49 students were shortlisted for this round)

Students were assigned to 8 different panels based on the role preference they had filled. In my
panel, all SQL students were present. My interview lasted for around 30 minutes.

- He saw my resume and asked me about my work experience and what was my day-to-day

task during my job.

- Next, I was asked why I choose SQL role

- Then he started with some theoretical questions like how many unique columns can be

The eligibility criteria for all four roles initially required a CGPA of 8.5 or above, but later they lowered it to
8.0, and for Software Engineering in Test and Analytical Verification, it was further reduced to 7.5 and
above.
There were 3 rounds: Online Assessment, Technical Interview and HR Interview
1.
Online Assessment [Around 150 students appeared for the test]
It was a 90 minute assessment and was conducted on Google Forms. It consisted of 70 MCQ questions, and
there were four sections - Java(18 questions), Python (17 questions), SQL (5 questions) and aptitude (30
questions). The correct answer would give you 1 mark, -0.25 for incorrect answer and 0 for not attempting.
The Java section consisted a lot of finding the output of the code kind of questions. Make sure you have
OOP concepts clear, especially how they are implemented in Java. I recommend practicing from websites
such as GFG, Interviewbit, Javatpoint, etc. There were questions about streams, filters, multithreading,
concurrent hashmaps, anonymous functions, enums etc but if you were familiar with the basics, you could
guess the answers. However, it would be better to be sure so, if your main language is Java, look into all
those concepts and how they work.
Similarly, python questions were also of similar kind, make sure you know all the python specific concepts
such as slicing, mutable - immutable data types, shallow copy - deep copy, OOPs in python (they're
implemented differently than in java), list comprehension, which functions are in-place and which return a
new lists, etc.
SQL questions were about choosing the right query out of four options, so make sure you know SQL queries
and which can be used with which and not with others, what can give errors, etc.
Aptitude questions were mathematical, some were easy but tricky, while others involved solving. You were
allowed to use the desktop calculator but not the physical calculator, for some reason. Only attempt what
you are confident in this section and scroll through all the questions once because some are dead easy
--- PAGE 2 ---
compared to others. Don't worry if it doesn't go as well as others, if your technical score is good, you should
be fine.
You were allowed to switch sections, but make sure you use the next and back buttons on the form and not
the browser back button. Also, to be cautious, make sure to submit the test at least 5 minutes before the time
runs out as the answers won't be auto submitted.

2. Technical Interview [Approx. 50 students shortlisted]

The panels were formed based on the first role preference you were eligible for. My interviewer was
probably in a hurry, everyone in my panel completed their interview in about 15-20 min, while other panels
were going for about an hour for each student. The interview started with my introduction and not even two
lines in the introduction, when I mentioned backend development, he asked me what backend development
is and the questions began.
Explain the four pillars of OOP, what the final keyword in Java means (explain all 3 cases when used with a
variable, method, and class), can an abstract class be final, what is immutability, if there is a variable A =
"Dheeraj" and another B = "Dheeraj," how many objects are created (only 1, because of string pools in
Java), what will happen if A is set to "Muppineti" (another string is created, and now A points to it), what is
the difference between Left Join and Inner Join in SQL, and finally, he asked me to explain my most recent
project and my role in it.
I sensed the interviewer didn't want long answers, so I kept my responses short and concise, refraining from
giving examples, and it went quite smoothly. He didn't ask me if I had any questions for him, so I said thank
you and left.

Tips :-

• I got lucky and your case most likely would be different, so prepare a good introduction and only

mention things you know really well, as the next questions would probably be from those.

• Don't over explain things, keep concise answers with good examples.

• Know everything you mentioned in your resume really and make sure you can explain every word in

it.

• If you're not sure about something, it's okay just to tell the interviewer upfront so they can move on

to the next question.

• Be ready for some easy DSA questions and definitely be ready to write SQL queries. Do SQL really

well, especially joins and group by.

• Be calm, take your time and answer confidently.

3. HR Interview [17 students shortlisted]

I was the first person for this interview and there were two panelists. It was a short interview and it began
with a tricky question, what do you know about us? The context is, I didn't pay attention during the
Pre-Placement Talk, and these two were the ones who gave it, so I was supposed to know them. So, don't
make this stupid mistake - pay attention and take notes on everything. I just answered what I knew about the
--- PAGE 3 ---
ISS (which was not much, please do your research) and luckily they didn't make any notes for this. And
then the interview began.
They asked me about my family background, education, why I chose my degree and to explain any one of
my projects. Use the STAR method of answering, especially for the projects. They asked me if I was looking
for AIML in my job, and for such questions make sure you read the JD carefully and answer accordingly. I
said I am more interested in overall backend development. And to which they asked if I would be open to
work also in frontend. What I did remember from the PPT was that they wanted someone who was flexible
in terms of technology, so I said yes, even though it's not my strongest asset, I am open to it. They asked if I
had any plans for further studies (in most cases, you want to say no, as they are looking for loyal candidates
who will stick with the company, so prepare a good answer). They asked about the disparity between my
technical and aptitude scores. They asked where I lived, and whether there would be any travelling issues.
Finally, they asked me if I had any questions, so I asked about the team structure and how the projects were
assigned to the teams.
In the end, 12 students got the offer!

Each round is an elimination round

1. Resume Screening

2. Aptitude Test(Online)

3. Group Discussion (Group size 12)

4. Interview Round 1

5. Interview Round 2

6. HR Round

1. Resume Screening:

General tips with regards to resume:

• Make single column resume using Latex (might as well use other one but this is the standard one)

• Do add your photo when it comes to submitting resume to JPMC

• Make sure you have some keywords related to finance in your resume.

97 students were shortlisted for the aptitude test.

2. Online Assesment:

45 Questions (No negative marking) - 45 minutes

1. Section 1 - Corporate finance and Financial Accounting (10 questions)

2. Section 2 - Market Awareness (10 questions)

3. Section 3 - Quantitative Aptitude (15 questions)

4. Section 4 - English Usage (10 Questions)

72 students were shortlisted after the round. Shortlist given a day prior to the interview process.
Preparation: https://www.indiabix.com/

3. Group Discussion:

Topic: India - The 5th Largest Economy
Divided into groups of 12 candidates each. The GD topic was given a day prior with the shortlisted
candidates, but the groups were allotted just before the interview started.
The given topic is just the theme for the GD. During the GD they gave topics one by one and asked to
discuss the same. The discussion started with what is GDP. Then the topic shifted to what factors have
worked for the uplifting of our economy. Then there was discussion around what are the challenges India
faces going ahead or what could go wrong. Lastly the topic shifted to the GDPs of other countries.

Tips:

• Have adequate and impactful points related to the topic.

• Try to bring in new points that would create an impact on the discussion.

• Having some numbers or examples to support your views would be a plus (but not too many).  You

should reason on the numbers and examples.

• Do memorize the points as your panelists may or may not allow you to carry any material for the

GD.

• Panelists were quite chill and made sure everyone got a chance to express their views.

4. Interview 1:

Duration: 1 hr approx. (much shorter for others)
The interview began with how was your day did you have your lunch etc to calm you down. Then the
questions started with "do you invest in the markets?". Name a stock you invested in, how you identify
where to invest. Here I mentioned some financial ratios so was asked about the same. Also mentioned
about revenue and profit growth yoy so I was asked what would be considered as a good profit or sales
growth in percentage. Then there were questions related to financial statements. If a pen is
manufactured and it is sitting in the inventory, how will it affect cost of goods sold  and how would
depreciation affect EBITDA.  Then I was asked about the nifty and sensex price just before the
interview and then what is nifty and sensex . Do check this before going in for the interview. Then I
was asked about recent IPOs. I mentioned about an IPO in which JP MC itself is a book-runner. He
then asked me for a second IPO and I mentioned the to be biggest IPO that is Hyundai (JPMC was
book-runner in this too). He then asked me about the valuation, amount they are raising and also why.
I was then given 2 guesstimates and one question related to calculating average speed. I was asked
about any masters plans or any certifications plans like CFA or CAT etc.  Then I was given a set of 3
companies: a mature manufacturing company, a tech startup which is not yet profitable and another
mature company and was given a set of 4 financial ratios and told to match them as to what would be
the best ratio to analyze which company. I was able to match 2 companies but gave wrong answer for
this third one. Then what beta is and sectors having beta less than and greater than 1. I was able to say
for greater than 1 but wasn't able to answer for less than 1 (answer was FMCG sector).

5. Interview 2:

Duration: 25-30 mins
Just in 5 mins time of my first interview I was called for a second interview. This one was pretty chill
and started with the same as the previous question which is do you invest and how do you analy ze
companies to invest and tell some other company you would recommend  to invest in and why. Then
the financial ratios for analyzing the company. I was asked about the valuation methods. Then what I
understand of the job role and about the tasks to be done in the role. After that questions around
WACC, what it is, why and where is it used . Then a question about the paper I had presented and
mentioned in my resume. Lastly about any plans for CAT or CFA or masters.

6. HR Round:

Duration: 15-20 mins
Do carry a special resume prepared for JP. This did help me in the HR round. The HR noticed that I
had made a separate resume and looked happy with that. Started with an introduction, then about the
job role and what I understood of it. I had mentioned about the forage investment banking simulation
in my resume on which I was asked how was the experience and did I do it gradually or in one go.
Ended with asking about where I was based out of.

Process had a total of 3 rounds, before that there was a resume-based shortlisting(123/200)
1.

Round 1: OA Round [123 candidates appeared for this round]

The assessment consisted of three sections: SQL, Python, and Aptitude (Quants), and it was conducted over
a duration of 25 minutes. We had to reach college by 8:45 AM, and the assessment started at 9:00 AM. A
question paper was given, and we had to tick the answers for the aptitude section like MCQS, and write
down the SQL queries and Python code.
The SQL section included 2 queries related to joins, group by, having and where clause and one was an
output based question where we had to write down the output for different types of joins. I would classify
the questions as easy to medium level. For Python, the task was to find the sum of n numbers, which was the
easiest question. The aptitude section featured easy to medium level questions, mostly logical type
questions. It tests your speed, so try to maintain a good pace.
To prepare for this round, understand how to write pseudocode, build logic for Python, and be proficient in
SQL queries. They won't ask very hard Python and SQL questions, but it's important to have a solid grasp
of the basics. Do not neglect the aptitude section. More than testing your Python and SQL skills, they want
to assess your critical thinking and your ability to think logically.

2. Round 2: Interview 1[39 students were shortlisted for this round]

There were three interview panels. My interview was scheduled after lunch, around 2 PM, and lasted
approximately 30-35 minutes. The panel consisted of three experienced interviewers. They began by asking
how my day was going and then inquired about my family background. Then they told me to introduce
myself. They also asked why I was interested in a Business Analyst role.
When answering this question, I shared some personal experiences to provide a realistic and authentic
response. It's important to be ready for such HR questions and prepare for them before the placement
process begins.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Then they asked me to rate myself out of 10 in SQL. I said 8, and they proceeded to ask SQL questions
based on this rating. They asked about the difference between the WHERE clause and the HAVING clause,
the purpose of the GROUP BY function, and the execution sequence of SQL statements. I correctly
answered all their questions.
Next, they delved into my resume and asked questions related to my projects. One of my projects was
related to machine learning, so they inquired about my choice of algorithm, how it works, and any
challenges I faced during the project.
Afterward, they asked about my hobbies. Initially, I mentioned sports, but since many candidates were asked
guesstimates related to sports, they requested I share another interest. I mentioned Yoga, and they asked me
to estimate the number of people practicing Yoga in Mumbai. While answering the guesstimate, keep
explaining your approach to the interviewer, as they are often helpful and may provide hints. Even if your
estimate is much higher or lower than what they expect, it's important to stick to your answer and justify it
with examples. They might cross-question your estimate, but remain confident and provide proper
explanations.
Usually, interviewers ask if you have any questions at the end, but in this case, they didn't. I took the
initiative to ask them some questions I had prepared based on my research about Incred Finance. They were
quite impressed by this. If you have any questions, do ask them, as it shows your interest and preparation.
If you have tech projects in your resume then just make sure to justify why they should still select you for a
non tech role.
Be prepared with some guestimate and case study questions. I will list down the links at the end of the
document.

3. Round 3: Interview 2 [ 15 students were shortlisted for this round. ]

This was essentially a case study round lasting around 20 minutes, where the interviewers posed questions
on various case studies, primarily related to lending terms. The session began with me introducing myself,
followed by questions about my first interview, including the name of the previous interviewer. It's
important to be attentive and remember the names of your interviewers.
I was given a scenario where, as a bank manager, I needed to determine if a borrower would be able to repay
a loan. The catch was that I would not have information about the borrower's income. I had to consider
other factors to assess their repayment capability. The discussion on this question lasted 20 minutes, during
which the interviewers were very helpful and provided hints. I answered the question as expected, and the
interviewers were quite impressed.
In the end 5 students were offered the job.

companies may use it. CGPA above 8 looks impressive on the resume.

2. Make a good resume. Use a standard template , I used :

Check the ATS score of your resume on:

3. Please do not lie on your resume. Add only those projects/technical skills in your resume that you are

completely sure about. Keep 4-5 points ready for every experience/achievement you have mentioned.

4. Do a thorough research of the company and the role that you are applying for. Based on your research

prepare some good questions that you can ask to the interviewer after the interview.

5. Read the job description carefully. You can form some of your answers using keywords mentioned

in the JD.

6. Prepare for some standard HR questions  beforehand. So that you do not panic one day before the

interview. Please do not use too much AI for this. First, note down your points, and then you can use
AI to help refine them.

7. For DSA:

 Please focus on understanding each question thoroughly rather than just trying to solve as many
as possible. Even if you have successfully solved a question on your own , review solutions
shared by others to learn different approaches.
 Do standard questions first. Try to solve POTD on Leetcode or GFG  everyday.
 Giving contests helps to improve time management which is very important in DSA rounds of
companies.
 Always check the constraints  carefully. If you can't come up with the most optimal solution
right away, write the brute force solution first to secure partial marks.

8. Take core subjects seriously. If you are from EXTC background like me :

 I would suggest taking DBMS as your 6th Sem open elective. Since it is a very important subject
for placements plus it is very easy to score in exams.
 Also make sure to focus on CCN in Sem 6. This will help you in placement preparation for this
subject, as it is often part of the technical questions asked during interviews.

9. Have a good understanding of the programming language that you use the most. Get all the basics of

that language clear (if you are not able to answer them in an interview it creates a bad impression.)

10. Keep discussing your approach with the interviewer whenever you are solving a question. If you get

stuck somewhere they will help you.

11. If you and your friends share the same goal, motivate each other, take regular follow-ups on progress,

and push one another to stay on track.

12. Please do not get demotivated by rejections  , treat them as learning experiences to identify and

improve upon your weak areas. Many aspects of the placement process involve luck, so don't doubt
your capabilities. I faced rejections from JPMC (FinTech) and PhonePe interview rounds just 5 and 2
days before my MSCI interview. What helped me was focusing on what I could control--improving
and preparing for the next company.

13. Everything falls into place eventually! Do not stress about the results , give your best whenever you

get an opportunity.

1. Pre Placement Talk

2. Online Test

3. Technical Interview 1

4. Technical Interview 2

1. Pre Placement Talk

The Pre Placement talk was organized on Microsoft teams platform by MSCI on 8 th July. It was
compulsory for everyone who applied for MSCI.
They gave us a brief introduction about MSCI's work , values and cultures. I would suggest make
notes or at least take screenshots during this presentation as you will be questioned on this in further
rounds.
If you have genuine doubts get them cleared.

2. Online Test [Everyone who applied was eligible for this round]

This was an online test on Hackerrank Platform. Duration of the test was 75 mins.
There were 3 questions : 2 DSA and 1 SQL based.

i) First question was similar to: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/maximum-people-a-person-can-see-
while-standing-in-a-line-in-both-direction/
I solved this question using two pointers and 14/15 test cases passed.

ii) Second question was easier: There where 2 arrays : projects and bid of size n. Every element in
projects had corresponding element in bid. We had to return the sum of minimum bid for each
project. Project ids would be from 1 to n. If any project id is missing,return -1.
I solved this question using unordered_map and passed all 15 test cases successfully.

iii) I do not remember the exact question but it was a bit challenging. Different concepts like Self Join,
Concat() function and group by were applicable in the same query. I was not able to solve this.

49 students were shortlisted for the next round but only 46 gave interview as 3 got placed in PhonePe.

3. Technical Interview 1  [46 students appeared for this round] (45 minutes)

First question interviewer asked me was "What do you know about MSCI ?"
After which she scanned my resume and asked me to explain my final year project which I had
mentioned in it. Then she moved on to another project and since I had used MongoDB as a database
in it she asked me "What are different types of databases and in what format are you passing data to
the database?"
Then she asked me to explain ACID Properties  of database transactions and gave me 3 SQL
questions to solve. I had to write these queries on a paper. They were easy and could be solved with
basic understanding of joins, subqueries and aggregates.
Questions:
There were two tables employee and departments. Department id was used as foreign key in employee
table.
i) Find the employees who are either in HR or Engineering Department. (Solved  using inner
join and OR/IN keyword).
ii) Total salary of employees in each department. (Solved using sum() and group by).
iii) Employee with the second highest salary (Solved using order by and limit keywords then
suggested another approach using subqueries and third approach using dense rank function).

After this she moved on to ask DSA questions:
i) First question asked was : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/top-view-of-binary-
tree/1 .
I had done this question before but wasn't able to remember the approach initially. I kept
on talking with the interviewer and explained her my understanding of the question. Then
I asked her for a hint.
After the hint I was able to form the entire solution. So I took a sample test case and
explained her my solution with a dry run. She asked me to write a pseudo code for the
same and explain its time and space complexity.
ii) She gave me a scenario : There are two classrooms A and B and her aim was to keep
number of students in both classrooms same. If excessive students enter one class she
would shift them to the other class to keep numbers equal. In this way lot of students keep
coming in and going out.
Her question was: In this scenario which data structure should be used?
Since there are lots of insertions/deletions so I suggested that linked list can be used.
Then she asked what if there are N classrooms. I tried to answer the question but she
explained me why my approach was wrong and told me the answer she expected was B+
Trees.
iii) She asked me if I know about AVL Trees, to which I admitted that I don't.
Moving on to OOPS she asked me questions revolving 4 pillars of OOPS. To be precise the questions
were:
i) What is encapsulation?
ii) What are types of inheritance?
iii) Difference between multiple and hierarchical inheritance.
iv) What is meaning of overloading?
v) Can constructers be private?

Interview ended and she asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her about the women leadership
forum community in MSCI and some questions related to what tech stack do freshers work on.

4. Technical Interview 2 (30 Minutes)

Interviewer asked me to introduce myself. Then she directly moved on to the projects that I had
mentioned in my resume and asked few questions about each of them . This included general
questions about the projects as well as on the tech stack used. She also asked me to write a specific
piece of code that was used in one of my projects.
Then she asked me which was my favorite subject and why. After I answered this , she directly
moved on to OOPS.
Questions:
i) What is the need of object oriented programming?
ii) What are classes and objects?
iii) If  I asked you to design a hospital management system using classes and objects what
all classes will you include in it? How will you implement appointment booking
functionality? I was asked to define the classes and its data members by writing a pseudo
code for them on a paper.
(I got stuck at few places while answering this but I kept on discussing my approach , with
her guidance I was able to come up with a valid solution.)
After this she asked me to write a C++ code to check if a string is a palindrome or not.
Then she asked me few non-technical questions:
i) Tell me something that is not on your resume.
ii) What are your interests and hobbies?
iii) Who is your role model?
iv) Where do you see yourself in next 5 years?
Interview ended and she asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her how does MSCI provide
risk management tools and services to its clients and are they customized for the client ? Follow up
question to that : Since MSCI provides solutions as both services and tools ,  is MSCI a product based
or a service based company? She answered everything in detail.

5. HR Interview [17-18 students appeared for this round] (15-20 minutes)

My panelist was really sweet and this round felt more like a conversation than an interview.
Questions asked were:
i) What do you know about MSCI?
ii) Give me a brief introduction about yourself as a person, as a student, a little bit about your
academic journey and the projects you have worked on. ( Please keep your points short
and crisp for such questions so that the interviewer doesn't get bored.)
iii) What will you bring to MSCI if you get selected ?
iv) What are your plans for further studies?
v) Is there any particular domain in which you want to peruse your career?
vi) Preferred job location

Interview ended and she asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her about different employee
engagement activities at MSCI. I also asked her for advice on building a successful career, as I am a
fresher and this would be my first corporate job.
6 students were offered the internship.

1. Online Assessment (around 120 students applied)

The OA round happened on 10th August. The round consisted of 3 coding questions out of which you had to do 2, and 1 sql query question. 40 people were selected who could do at least 2 coding questions correctly. It was proctored and on HackerRank.
The time of the test was 70 minutes. I had solved 2 questions and the sql question. The questions were pretty easy and if you have done some DSA and problem solving you will be able to do these as these were implementation based questions and not very logic oriented. For eg. One question was where the date was given as '27th July 2017' and you had to output it as '2017-07-27'. Time was a key factor so keep that in mind.
My tips would be to manage your time well, koi question nahi aa raha toh usko tab chod do, move on then come back to it. Don't spend too much time on a question if you're not able to solve it. This goes for all OAs in general.

2. [Round 2 Name] (around 40 candidates got shortlisted)

This round happened on 12th August. This was a tech round.
There were 3 panelists. In this round mainly the questions revolved around your projects and your resume.
Each and everything which I put in my resume was asked to me. Each skill, each project. One of my projects was discussed at the start of the round and i had made it in MERN stack. The interviewer asked me why did  I use MongoDB for this. Then he asked me to tell me some of the schemas i had implemented and asked me to make tables in SQL corresponding to those schemas. Related to those tables he asked me 3 4 sql queries involving group by, aggregation, and joining tables.
After that he tried to grill on each skill written in my resume and the interview ended with him telling me to send in the next candidate.
In the end he also showed me one of my submissions in the OA for a coding question and asked me to explain my approach and the code.

Some important points to note:-
Keep calm during any interview, sit back straight(posture and body language is very important) and smile.
My interview was the shortest in my panel and I had thought that I wouldnt make it but I actually was the only one to get selected for next round in my panel. So dont worry, just give your best.

3. [Round 3 Name] [Around 5 to 6 people were selected for this round]

This was an HR round.
The interviewer was very friendly and didn't ask any typical HR questions. It was more of a conversation, pretty chill.
She asked how were the previous interview, what did you like about it, could we change some things in our process etc. Then she asked, that had you sat for IDfy's PPT. I said yes, then she asked what things did you like in them, why did you apply for IDfy. Why did you take up engineering in SPIT.

But of course, frame your answers properly and dont get carried away. Since this is a startup you need to show them that you are actually passionate about this field, tell some instances to prove it as well.

journey.howSecured:
The Placement process consists of 4 rounds. 1st round is resume shortlisting followed by Case
Study Round followed by the Problem Solving Interview and the last round is the Culture Fit
Interview.
For the role of APM/AGM/APGM: 45 Students were shortlisted post resume screening for the
case study round. 15 were selected for the problem solving interview and 6 were shortlisted for
the Culture Fit Interview.
It was an offline process with some interviews being held over G-Meet.

1. Resume Shortlisting Round]

Make sure your resume is of 1 page and proper formatting is maintained. Include and highlight
relevant internship experiences and courses which you have undertaken. I had made my resume
on MS Word.
[Case Study Round] [45 students appeared for this round]
The Case Study Round started at 8am sharp and we were given a time of 2 hrs for making PPTs
for the cases. Students were provided with one of 3 different case studies each based on product
design, user retention, and solutions for betterment of the product, and were also supposed to
define success metrics for each feature. My case study was regarding HealthifyMe, and
following was the problem statement:
--- PAGE 2 ---
"Healthifyme aims to increase user retention and encourage long-term usage for its users.
Despite a high number of downloads, the app struggles with retaining users beyond the first
month"
You have to be innovative and practical while suggesting the solution,it will help to stand out
amongst the rest. Allot sufficient time in understanding the problem statement,the app and the
solution which you are proposing. The content is more important than the aesthetics. There was
not a strict slide limit but try to keep it as concise as possible.
I have participated in various case study competitions and marketing competitions since the
onset of my second year which helped me a lot to understand what was expected in the solution.

3. [Problem Solving Interview Round] [ 15 candidates appeared for this round]

My interview was taken by the VP of Growth. I had prepared for this round by practicing
guesstimates and root cause analysis questions which are generally asked in this round to
check how can you solve a problem in a structured manner. To my surprise,my interview did
not consist a single question on guesstimate or RCA.The interviewer asked me questions
regarding my case study solution. Questions revolved around what problems are existing in
the app currently and as the PM how would I solve it? What features would I implement to
tackle it? The entire interview was heavily product focused and I was put in the shoes of PM
to solve situation based problems. The interview questions were very close to the real world
scenarios..It checked my problem solving skills and how differently does one think. I was
given situational based questions on Spotify and G-Meet as well. Whatever feature I
suggested as the solution, the interviewer asked few follow up questions to it. My interview
lasted for 45 minutes
Few tips:

• It is okay to ask the interviewer to give you 30-90 seconds to think about the answer.

• Make sure you have 2-3 supporting reasons for the feature you are suggesting to be

implemented

• Give mock interviews, this helps a lot.

• Expect the unexpected.

4. [Cultural Fit Interview Round] [ 6 candidates appeared for this round]

--- PAGE 3 ---
My Interview was taken by the CTO of the company. He asked me how could they improve
on their recruiting process,post which I was asked about my biggest achievement and the
lowest point in my life. Don't try to pretend to be someone which you are not. The interviewer
shall recognise it immediately. All the questions asked to me were very behavioral and
specific in nature. I could answer them easily as I responded by first thinking what would
have been my natural response if I was put in such a situation. I tried not giving an ideal
answer but an answer which resonated the most to me. I was also asked questions on the
concept of greater good and what would I do if I had 100 cr. Most of the interview revolved
around my life experiences and my actions in certain hypothetical situations. This interview
went on for an hour.
Few tips:

• Be yourself and confidently tell the values which you believe in.

• In this round the interviewer genuinely wants to know about you,so do share your

life experiences which have moulded you.

• You might be asked about company specific questions,researching about the

company would be beneficial.
Resources that helped me:
1)I referred to the casebooks by IIM A,B,C for my preparation on guesstimates along with
the videos on the Exponent Youtube Channel.
2)The course by Google on Project Management aligns significantly with this role.
3)The Product Management Books by the Product clubs of HIM A and HIM B helped me to
understand about PM in general.
LASTLY,
"BELIEVE IN YOURSELF BECAUSE IF YOU DON'T, THEN WHO WILL!"

Given 2 arrays named as serverLoad & serverCapacity, the goal is to minimise total cost of the server.
For Example,
serverLoad = [7, 2, 7, 3], serverCapacity = [4, 1, 5, 6],
The total cost of server is calculated as -  7 * 4 + 2 * 1 + 7 * 5 + 3 * 6 = 83 (dot product of 2 initial arrays)
In order to minimise the cost of server , the problem statement mentioned that you can swap the position of
elements in serverCapacity only. The objective is to find the sequence of serverCapacity that results in the
minimum total cost. In case multiple sequences result in the same minimum total cost, return the sequence
that is lexicographically smallest.
In the above example, elements of serverCapacity can be arranged in a order [4, 6, 1, 5], and the dot product
with the serverLoad (elements of serverLoad are not altered)  - 7 * 4 + 2 * 6 + 7 * 1 + 3 * 5  = 62 (total cost).
But note that there is also 1 possible sequence which could minimize total cost which is [1, 6, 4, 5].
(7 * 1 + 2 * 6 + 7 * 4 + 3 * 5  = 62).
Now for sequence s1 [4, 6, 1, 5] and s2 [1, 6, 4, 5], s2[0] < s1[0]
So the output would be sequence - [1, 6, 4, 5]
Approach that came to my mind - Greedily, dot product of 2 arrays will be minimized if larger numbers
from one array are multiplied with smaller numbers from the other array and vice versa. . So I sorted
serverCapacity array and mapped the maximum value with minimum value of serverLoad.
Elements of serverLoad mapped with serverCapacity -
7 -> [4, 1]
3 -> [5]
2 -> [6]
Now for each key, I sorted the list in ascending order.
7 -> [1, 4]

3 -> [5]
2 -> [6]
After that I created an array of size serverLoad and assigned each value by iterating over the map.
I thought this would give me TLE, because for each key I was performing sort on the corresponding values,
but to my surprise it passed all the test cases.

Technical mcqs were straightforward, which contained questions on -

1. 4 - 5 questions on MySQL queries, normalization.

2. 4 - 5 questions on guess the output of the given code, output of bitwise operation ( &, | ), type casting

(all ques were based on C++).

3. 2 - 3 questions based on Data structure. (3-Ary Tree, map interface, dynamic list)

4. Questions on Java classes, package and synchronized keyword.

Aptitude mcqs were bit tricky and time consuming. It contained questions on -

1. 4 - 5 questions on probability, PnC, sets, intervals.

2. 3 - 4 questions on complete the series / find element in the series.

For Example -

1. ABC, ABC2,  AB2C2, A2B2C2, ? (guess the next element)

2. A10, A12, B18, B42, __, C882 (fill the blank)

3. 1234, 1024, 78, 1556, ?

3. 2 - 3 questions on Letter and Symbol series.

4. 3 - 4 questions on Diagramatic reasoning.

5. 1 question on mirror image of given sequence.

Tip -
In my opinion, when weightage is not assigned to each component, it is best to start with the coding questions
first, followed by the technical mcqs, and finally the aptitude questions.
Also even if you are not able to think the optimal approach, just code a brute force soln and submit it, because
some of them were shortlisted  for interviews based on aptitude and technical mcqs  even if they didn't clear
all the test cases of the problem.

3. Offline Technical Round - 1 [36 candidates appeared for this round]

I had 2 interviewers on my panelist which were very friendly and chill. At the start, they were just having fun
with me, although I was nervous (don't know why) but they made me comfortable. They began the interview
by asking me to tell them about myself . Based on my introduction, they started to ask me why I only knew
JavaScript only and not TypeScript (TS), as I had mentioned JS as one of my primary language s. To this, I
answered that I have use TS in my projects, but I am not as proficient in it as I am in JS. Then they asked why
one should use TS over JS. I responded that TS is more stricter version of JS, most of the github repo I looked
upto where in TS, and the community support of TS is excellent.
After that, they asked me if I knew React, to which I replied yes, but they didn't ask any further questions on
it.
In my resume, I had mentioned about implementing virtual stock market  (vsm) using Paytm Websocket, so
they asked me why WebSocket and not traditional HTTP request - response can be used for vsm. I broke the
question into 2 parts by explaining what WebSocket is and how does it work and same for HTTP. I explained
that if HTTP is used in place of ws then the client needs to request each second to server because the share

price of any stock keeps on fluctuating in seconds. They then asked how do you call an api from the frontend.
I explained them that I can use fetch method which return s a promise. Then they immediately asked what is
promise, promise status - pending, fullfilled / resolved  or rejected. Then I was asked to write the code for
same.
fetch(api).then((res) => { // logic }).catch((err) => { // log error })
Then they asked me about HTTP status code that I have used in my projects , and what do you mean by the
error 'resource not available'. Then they moved on to explain left join, right join, inner join, outer join, self
join in MySQL. They indirectly asked about normalization by inquiring why should one create multiple tables,
why not to keep data in one table only. To which I replied by giving an example and told that 3 anomalies
would arise - insertion, deletion and updation. Then they asked me to tell one use case where developer should
not normalize the table / relation !. I replied that if a table is decompose into more tables, then the query would
take more time to process as it would required join operations to retrieve data. Then they asked me to name
sorting algos, and which one I would prefer all the time. I replied that I would use Merge sort over other
because the worst case TC of it is O(n * log(n)).
Then they asked me some typical HR questions about my strengths, weakness, role model, why I joined SPIT,
why did I chose CE department.
The entire round took duration of around 30 - 40 mins.

4. Offline HR Round [around 20 candidates appeared for this round]

Like the technical round, the HR round was also relaxed and informal. I was asked about my family
background, where I see myself in two years, my interests outside of academics, whether I plan to pursue
higher studies, how many interviews I had before UBS and why I want to join UBS. At the end, I asked her a
few questions about idea sharing and internal hackathons.
The entire round took duration of around 15 - 20 mins.
At the end of the day, a total of 12 candidates received job offers.

1. Know your resume inside out. Thoroughly review and understand every detail listed in your resume.

2. For the interview , prepare 30 - 40 seconds of concise intro. You should be able to explain your

projects, your motivation behind the project, what problem is your project solving,  your choice of
technology stack over the other ones.

3. Start participating in contest hosted by Leetcode , Codechef, Codeforces. Doing cp is not mandatory,

but it really enhance your problem solving skills. Also before 1 month the placement starts, focus on
practicing aptitude questions  of major companies like Gol dman Sachs or any ot her. Don't
underestimate aptitude skills.

4. OOP and MySQL are frequently asked in OA as well as in interviews. Try to implement your projects

using OO P principle and if your project involve s DB, then practice drawing relational diagram
beforehand. Also you should be familiar with the basic conepts of OS and CCN, although they are not
frequently asked.

5. Prepare standard HR questions beforehand.

6. Avoid panic, nervousness and overconfidence. Even you are stuck at a challenging question, try to ask

for a hint, interact with interviewers, they will definitely help you out because they spend so much of
their hours, money in finding the right candidate.

1. Aptitude Test ( 2nd August 2024)

2. Technical Round 1

3. Technical Round 2

1.     [OA(Aptitude Test ] [ 155 Students  ]

This was an aptitude round consisting of three sections: verbal, analytical, and quantitative , with 20
questions in each section. The total duration was 60 minutes, so you need to be fast and quick to solve the
questions. You can practice from IndiaBix aptitude questions. 32 candidates were selected for the next
round of the ITM role.

2. [Technical Interview  1] [ 32 Students ]

For students selected for the ITM role, the interview started directly at 9 am. For other roles, there was a
group discussion and a technical test. I got called in for the interview.
The interviewer introduced himself, and then he asked me to introduce myself. Towards the end of my
introduction, I mentioned my involvement in sports, particularly Kho -Kho. He mainly asked about Kho -
Kho, as I had mentioned it, with 2 -3 questions related to it. Then, he asked me about the expected total
medal count for India in the 2024 Olympics.
Next, he asked me about my projects. He specifically asked about the keywords that were bolded in my
resume, so it's important to be sure of what you add in your projects section. You should know each word
you include there.

He then gave me an SQL question and a pen and paper to write a query. He first asked about equi join
(inner join) and then about all types of joins in SQL. He gave me three questions, asking for the output
for different types of joins between Table 1 and Table 2.
Afterward, he asked about the differences between NoSQL and SQL, as I had highlighted MongoDB in
my projects. Then he asked me about AWS and some other languages and tech stacks that I didn't know,
so I honestly said I didn't. He then asked me to rate myself in different languages. I rated myself 8.5-9
in Java, which I'm good at, and the same for SQL. I also mentioned C++ on my resume, but he didn't ask
me to rate C++.
(If you have good time for placements, try to learn Java and do coding in Java on LeetCode , as most
companies prefer Java over C++.)Then he switched to OOP concepts in Java and asked some questions
about Java OOP.At the end, I asked 2-3 questions related to Nomura.
Total duration was 30-40 minutes.16 selected for next round.
This round was mainly focused on the resume.

3. [Technical Round 2] [16 students ]

The interviewer asked me for a quick introduction. After that, I was given a series of puzzles(Gfg) .
Next, I was asked to write SQL queries for a given schema. There were 5 -6 questions, with one related
to another. Out of the six, two were medium level, and the others were easy. You should refer to LeetCode
SQL 50 series for practice.
After that, I was asked about normalization, sharding concepts, and indexing . I explained these
concepts with some examples using pen and paper. If you're good at explaining with pen and paper, make
sure to do so.
Then we switched back to my resume. I thoroughly explained each project, addressing questions like why
I chose that tech stack, why I selected that language, and what other alternatives could be used for the
project.
As I mentioned that my primary language is Java, the interviewer then shifted towards core Java
questions, such as the volatile keyword and synchronization in Java. There were also questions about
triggers in SQL and the final keyword in Java. After that, the focus shifted to OOP concepts, discussing
the four pillars of OOP. I was asked to provide real -life examples for each. Then there were questions
about interfaces and abstract classes. The interviewer wrote some OOP code and asked me to predict the
output.
Next, the interview moved towards DSA. Questions were asked about the difference between HashSet
and TreeMap and when to use each. Then, I was asked to explain sorting algorithms. There was a task
to sort objects (consisting of various attributes) based on certain conditions. Also Asked windows function
inn sql .For example, objects of employees were given with ID, name, and age, and I was asked to output
the names of people having an age > 20. This could be solved using the comparator function . The
interviewer also provided an alternative approach using the stream() function in Java.

After that, I was asked about a case study and a competition mentioned in my resume. The interview lasted
for around 1.5 hrs. Eight students were selected for the HR round.

4 )HR Round -:
Again, there was a quick introduction. The interviewer asked, " What else should I know about you that
isn't mentioned in your resume?" Then, I was asked to explain some of my projects. I also had to explain a
case study and competitions I had participated in. The interview lasted for about 10 minutes.

Finally 8 students got offer for ITD role.

Initially they had kept a cutoff of 8.5 CGPA for applying to any of the 4 roles, which was further
lowered to 7.5/8

1.     Online Assessment [Approx 155 students appeared]

The assessment was conducted offline in college, and was on google forms. There were approx. 70
questions which had to be completed in 90 minutes. The marking scheme was +1, -0.25 and there
were 3 sections- Java based, Python based and Aptitude questions.
Java questions were related to enums, multithreading, filtering, streams, scope of variables, OOPS
etc. Python questions were mostly OOPs related and some basic but tricky ones. Both these sections
involved code snippets to determine the output. Aptitude involved JEE/CAT type questions on
volume, distance speed, simple compound interest, graphs, etc. Java is my core language so I was
able to solve almost all the questions in that section. I was not very familiar with the Python syntax,
a few questions were asked on that too like Syntax error etc, so I only marked for those questions I
was completely sure of because it had negative marking. I had not practiced for aptitude separately
at all, but if your core math concepts are clear then I feel it'll be quite doable. If you think you need
practice then you can refer to IndiaBix for aptitude questions.

2. Technical Round [49 students selected]

After the OA, 49 students were shortlisted for the technical round. In my panel all the students had
applied for the software testing role and they were asked very basic java oops questions, printing
star patterns, difference between joins, etc and nothing on projects.
As soon as the interview began, he first asked me how my test was and how many I think I answered
correctly. He asked me questions related to my project which was completely using Java. I was asked
a lot of questions on the data structures I had used, why I chose them, what are the alternative data
structures that could be used. I was not able to answer the alternatives. After that he asked me what
happens when you enter a url in the browser. To this I answered everything confidently from DNS,
http requests to the Client Server Architecture in detail. Then he cross questioned me on the types
of servers, and I named 2/3 of them. He asked me about inheritance, its types, if multiple
inheritance is allowed in java(no), how will u execute multiple inheritance if u want to?(interfaces).
Then he asked me a few questions on that and store procedures, triggers in sql. He asked me real life
example of a linkedlist. Then since this was a testing role, he asked me what do u know about
testing, tools used, real life example of testing, why is it necessary, etc.
While I was waiting for my interview outside, I read about all the above because I had no previous
knowledge of testing tools like Selenium etc. A basic question was asked, turn the string "Harshey
Kaur Soi" into "Harshey$Kaur$Soi", he mentioned you cant use StringBuilder. I used the .split(" ")
function and solved it. And then he asked me which package is used by this function(java.lang).
I was also asked about my family background, and if I would be flexible with the changing work
timings because as ISS is an MNC it has a lot of US based clients.

3. HR Round [17 students selected ]

There were 2 panellists in this interview, the MD of ISS and the HR. They first asked me about my
family background, if I had any plans of higher studies?(always say NO) but they were quite stuck on
this question given my answer for my family background. After that the MD asked me that why did u
decide to apply for this role, what do you know about testing, etc. They asked me if I could learn a
few testing tools before joining since I had absolutely ZERO experience in them.

Finally 12 students got the offer!!!(Including MCA candidates)

WI campus Drive lasted for a day and consisted of 4 Rounds. The day before, we had a PPT in which we
were briefed about their values and work culture. Following that we had to submit our resumes for
shortlisting. We could only apply for only one of the 5 roles. 92 students were shortlisted after the resume
round.

1. API/Frontend Round (92 candidates appeared for this round)

We had two choices for this round in which we had to code out any one option. They were:

1. Front-end round: Create a website frontend in 2 hours. They had given a Figma mock design which

we had to replicate in any frontend framework. We were provided with APIs to load data to our page
and were evaluated based on the quality of code and the quality of UI and UX.
OR

2. API dev round: This was the one that I chose. I had to create APIs for a car rental platform

(ZoomCar) in 3 hours. They had given a problem statement and the details of 6 API endpoints we

needed to create. The details for each API included the type of request, the request data, query
parameters, the expected output, and access type (user/admin access).
After submission, I was asked to demonstrate the endpoints. Then they asked me questions about my
database schema, code structure, how I would perform some changes in the code and some theoretical
questions based on jwt/encryption. This interview lasted for 1 hour.
25 Students were shortlisted for the next round.
Tips for this round:

1. Prepare on topics like jwt and hashing since these are required almost every time. Also have some

experience in role based access.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. It is compulsory to use SQL as the database. So have some practice so that you can build the schema

and prepare APIs within the time constraint.

3. You are allowed to use google. But using Al tools and copying an existing project is not allowed.

4. Use different folders for routes, controllers and middleware. Ensure that you are following proper

coding conventions.

5. Have the postman or curl requests ready so that you can quickly demonstrate it to the interviewers.

2. Technical Round 1[18 students appeared for this round]

This round primarily focused on DSA. I was asked 2 DSA questions. The first question was a
straightforward question in which I had to find the 3 least performing Engineers in the current year. I
initially suggested a brute force approach by sorting and then I gave him the optimized approach using max
heap. The second question was to partition the array into k parts so that the max sum of the partitions is
minimum.
This question was same as :
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/split-the-given-array-into-k-sub-arrays-such-that-maximum-sum-of-all-sub-a
rrays-is-minimum/
Initially I gave him the brute force approach, but he was not satisfied. After some thinking, I realized it was
a binary search problem. I was required to share my screen and write the pseudo-code. The interviewer also
asked me to perform a dry run and tell him about the time and space complexity of each solution.
This round lasted for around 1 hour.
Tips for this round:

1. Be as interactive as possible with the interviewer, and let him know what you are thinking.

2. If you want any clarifications, be sure to ask since the interviewer expects and welcomes it.

3. Ensure you communicate the meaning of your pseudo-code properly along with the reasons for your

decisions.

3. Technical Round 2[10 students appeared for this round]

This round primarily focused on SQL. I was asked to prepare a schema for an e-commerce website. The
interviewer was really helpful and I ran all my ideas through him while building the schema. In case I was
going in the wrong direction the interviewer nudged me to the right path. I was also asked some standard
questions like differences/advantages/disadvantages of NoSQL over SQL databases. Then I was asked to
perform database queries on my schema which was easy to medium level questions on leetcode.
This round also lasted for around 1 hour.
Tips for this round:

1. Prepare for SQL questions using platforms like leetcode, w3 schools, etc. Ensure you complete at

least one of the SQL sheets: (the one that I did was https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/).

2. Do prepare for concepts like schema normalization, types of relationships and other standard

concepts as they will surely ask about it.
--- PAGE 3 ---

3. HR/Culture Round [ About 6 students appeared for this round]

I was interviewed by a former SPIT student and core team member of WI. He began by asking me to
introduce myself. He asked me about my college experience, and we had a brief chat on how it was different
from his time there. He proceeded to ask me about my internships and projects that I had built. Then he
asked personal questions like:

1. What's the most valuable thing for you that you currently have?

2. What's the most valuable thing for you that you are yet to receive?

3. What was the lowest point & the highest point of your life and how did you learn/improve from it?

4. What would you do if you had infinite resources (100 crs)?

5. What mistakes did you make in your college years and how did you improve on them?

6. You had the privilege to study at the prestigious SPIT. What did you do with this opportunity?

7. Why did you choose this career path?

8. Why did you choose to work in a startup like WorkIndia?

9. Would you prefer a stable work environment or environment with lots of highs and lows?

There were some more questions of the similar sort.
I was given time to think on how to answer these questions. The interviewer was really chill and encouraged
me to be honest and candid. At the end,the interviewer asked me if I had some questions for him. I asked
him about the features his team was working on as well as some questions about the business model and
advertising strategy. This round lasted for around 45 minutes.
Tips for this round:

1. Be honest. Answers that are insincere or contradict at any point will be caught by the interviewer.

2. Do take some time to think before you answer. Also add some information/evidence to support your

answer.

3. Learn about the values and goals of the company beforehand.

4. At the end, prepare a well thought out question that genuinely interests you.

Three students were offered the opportunity at WorkIndia for the role of SDE.
