journey.howSecured:
Barclays had hired students prior to this via Hack-O-Hire and the CyberShala course, and it came pretty late
for the on-campus hiring. It was a two-day process consisting of:

1. Online Assessment (OA)

2. Technical Interview Round

3. Techno-HR Interview Round

4. A prank, yes you read that right, a prank (disguised as a 3rd Interview Round)

An in-depth description of everything is given below:

1. Online Assessment [138 students appeared for this round]

The OA was scheduled on 11" September at 8 am, and only those students who had a CGPA above 7 were
allowed to sit for the same. The test was conducted on HackerEarth, consisting of 12 MCQS, 1 coding and 1
SQL question.
A crucial point to note, make sure that you have a fighting CGPA, for reasons I'll explain below.
Now, a fun fact about this test, it was 1 hr 30 mins long and IT WAS THE SAME TEST AS THE ONE I
HAD GIVEN FOR THE BARCLAYS SUMMER INTERNSHIP ROLE!
--- PAGE 2 ---
The 12 MCQs were on CS fundamentals, code snippets for which you had to mark the correct output, SQL
fundamentals and queries, all-in-all consisting of 40 marks. I'll add my resources for the same towards the
end. Do not take these lightly as they contribute a good chunk to your score.
The SQL question was worth 10 marks, where you were given a table and you had to figure out the
compensation a person would get. Just read the question properly and you can easily solve it using a
WHERE clause and a bunch of AND operations.
Now comes the fun part, the coding question on strings, which could be categorized as a Leetcode medium
but the edge cases make it seem much harder. The question states:
You are given 2 strings S1 and S2, S1 will consist of a string of characters and S2 will consist of just two
characters 'T' and 'F' in any order, such that the order of 'T'/F' will map to the answer string you return in
such a way that if a character in S2 at some index is 'T', the answer string should consist of characters from
S1 starting from that index, and if it is 'F' at least one character from the substring of length S1 starting from
that index shouldn't match. And your objective is to return the lexicographically smallest such answer
string.
For example, consider S1 = "ABCA" and S2 = "TFFF", whose answer string is "ABCAAAA".
Now you may very well start off with the same thought process I had, that is to consider an answer string of
length S1 + S2 - 1 consisting of all A's and then just copying the string characters of S1 from the index of
'T' till length of S1. Yes, that will do the job for 5 of the test cases, for the next part you had to ensure the
string was lexicographically smallest, that meant changing the substring starting at 'F', now this will get you
to 8 test cases. Now, for the infuriating part, to completely pass all the test cases, you simply had to run a
loop to check the validity of the string (which I missed).
The bottom line being, your logic for the code may be correct but the test cases may not be so kind, so
bear that in mind.
Now as I mentioned before, to have a fighting CGPA, that may come in handy for you as some students just
managed to pass 2 test cases but their CGPA came in clutch and pulled them through, for others it was the
MCQS which was their saving grace, so do the MCQs diligently. The results were announced in the evening
and 34 students were shortlisted for the interviews.

2. Technical Interview Round [34 students appeared for this round]

The interviews were scheduled for the next day, 12ạiSeptember, and prior to this, a PPT was organized
They were going to start at 10 am but all the members hadn't arrived so it was a long wait, so a good night's
sleep is a must before the interviews. A tip here, keep yourself busy during this span, have a chat with your
friends, go eat something, anything to keep yourself fresh.
The interviews began at 11:30 am. There were 9 panels for the Grads and 6 panels for the Summer Interns
which were taking place simultaneously. I was the first in my panel. As I sat waiting in the TPO lobby, my
interviewer Mr. Rahul Garware himself came to call me into the cabin to begin the interview. Side note
about him, he is an alumnus of our college, which I learned during the PPT.
He created a very comfortable environment before commencing the interview, asked me about my day, to
which I responded and asked him about his. He told me to have a seat, while he himself stood for a few
--- PAGE 3 ---
minutes, examining my resume before seating. My entire interview revolved around one project in my
resume - my major project for a Multimodal Depression System and we conversed the entirety of 30
minutes on it. He asked me to explain it, and was particularly interested in its practical application in a
company like Barclays. He switched to BERT (which I had used in my project) and asked me to find a use
case where it could be used to find typos in trade data, to which I responded I hadn't heard of BERT being
used for numeric data evaluation, but I did manage to explain my thought process to him. After that, he gave
me an 'assignment' to be done at home, regarding the same, and said he was done and whether I had any
questions for him. I asked him what prerequisites we are required to have before joining - to which he said
whatever you have learned throughout your curriculum, is enough and that most of the learning process
happens on the job. He also asked me whether I had any feedback for how the interview was conducted, to
which I responded this seemed more like a discussion than an interview, to which he laughingly said, that
was the point.
A word of advice here, remain confident and maintain a positive attitude, one of the main things to keep in
mind while answering questions for Barclays is their RISES principles - Respect, Integrity, Services,
Excellence, and Stewardship. If you feel you do not know the answer, just say it, try to mention something
which you do recall around the same question, like I said about BERT not being used for numeric data and I
mentioned how BERT works, they are just testing how much you know, so just tell them what you know.
This was how my interview went, but a few of my friends were asked questions on OS, OOPs, SQL along
with projects in their resume. Know your resume inside-out, be prepared for any curveballs on the
same.
Post-lunch, around 3 pm, a list of 17 students were called out to go for the next round, while some students
still had their first ones left. Five more were shortlisted for the next round, while my next round was going
on.

3. Techno-HR Round [22 students appeared for this round]

Like the round before, I was the first one in my panel. For some students it was a techno-HR round, but for
me it was purely HR, though I didn't know it at the time. The interview started off with questions on my
resume and as I was about to explain the flow of one of my projects, the interviewer cut me off saying that
won't be necessary, this isn't a technical round anyway.
So, right then and there, I switched gears into HR mode. I was asked situation-based questions - what would
you do if you're in a conflict with one of your colleagues, what would you do if your colleagues are in a
conflict, what would your process for pitching a new idea be, what would you do if you found your
colleague doing something unethical.
I replied keeping the RISES principles in mind, and also, I was asked to reiterate my responses given a new
problem, so answer all of these without fail, even if you take some time to think about the same.
At the end, when asked if I had any questions for him, I asked the same question I asked in the previous
round and another one - how can one change departments? Funnily enough, he asked me you're asking all
of these questions like you know you've already been selected, who told you this, there is still an asterisk
after your name. I apologized saying that this wasn't mentioned in the PPT so I was curious and he smiled
and said it's standard for almost all companies but I'll tell you since you asked me this. So yeah, that
happened :)
--- PAGE 4 ---
This round lasted approximately 30 minutes, though it's hard to keep track of time during the interview.

4. The Supposed 3 Round

My interviews were done by 4 pm and then came the brutal waiting game. To kill time, I sat and chatted
with my friends, had a snack in the canteen, and went for a walk. In the middle of my walk, I was informed
that there may be another round. Now bear in mind it was 6:30 pm, I was mentally drained, just wishing for
the day to be over, so I got a bit worried that I wouldn't be able to perform well. We waited till 7 pm, and
then 19 out of the 22 students were called into room 105, for the next round.
It was a grim environment designed to fool us all. We were asked whether we would be comfortable staying
late, as it will take some time, given Mumbai traffic and Ganpati on top of that, to which we grudgingly said
yes. Then our names were read one by one, and it was declared that these names..., are all selected! That
was quite possibly the tensest 10 minutes of my life, then turned into the best minute of my life. We were
then given general feedback and called below for a photo shoot.
19 grads and 13 interns were selected finally.

journey.prep:
1)Start your placement preparation as soon as possible. Focus on core subjects such as DBMS, OS,
Computer Networks, and OOPS. Make concise notes for future revision. Additionally, rescarch common
interview questions to get familiar with frequently asked topics and concepts.
2)Prepare your resume well. The resume should not include things that you may not be able to answer if
asked about in the interview. Listing things you can't explain may come across as dishonest and leave a poor
impression. At Least be aware of the basic concepts of the technologies mentioned. Also, fine-tune the
resume with minor changes according to the role.
3)The first step of the placement process is usually the company's presentation. Be attentive and note key
details about the company's history, products, and services. Clarify any doubts regarding roles and
responsibilities to make an informed decision and position yourself as a good fit for the role.
3)For OA's,practice makes the most difference. Start giving contests/timed-tests to improve your
problem-solving approach and identify areas where you need improvement.
4)For interviews, it's important to demonstrate your strengths and walk the interviewer through your
approach rather than rushing to get the correct answer immediately. Stay calm and confident, as it reassures
the interviewer that you can handle stressful situations effectively.

5) Don't lose hope, just focus on identifying how you can improve your chances of getting selected.

Understand your strengths and weaknesses, and continue to work on them throughout the process.

journey.howSecured:
A total of 3 rounds were conducted- 1 Online Assessment Round,1 Technical Interview, and 1 HR
Round. All were conducted on the same day. The CGPA Criteria was 8.5,later reduced to 8,Only for testing
role,it was further reduced to 7.5. But make sure that your CGPA is at least 8 to be eligible for applying for
all 4 roles in the future for ISS-STOXX.

1. [Online Assessment] [155 appeared, ~ 49 selected] Invigilated by Company Officials

The test was conducted in College on Google Forms. 70 questions - 90 minutes. It had +1, -0.25
marking scheme.
Test was divided into 4 sections -
Java 18 questions
Python 17 questions
SQL 5 questions
Java and Python questions focused on OOPS concepts, frameworks,exception handling, and Lists. In Java
section, there were questions where output of the code was expected and most of them were based on
Streams. A basic understanding of map, filter, flatmap functions was enough to solve them.
For SQL Section, queries were asked for the given table and the required output. The queries covered
various topics like joins, date functions, subqueries. The questions were on easy to medium level but they
were listed as continuous sentences, making it slightly time-consuming and needing a double check.
The Aptitude round consisted of the normal Quantitative Aptitude questions such as Percentages,
Ratios, Time-Distance, Boat upstream-downstream, Probability etc. The questions were on an easy level with
few medium ones. The key was to identify questions were you are most confident and are well versed with
required formulae or logic.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The key point to note for the online assessment is to identify the questions where you can maximize your
score while minimizing risk due to negative marking. However, for assessments without negative marking,
attempt all questions.
Also, start preparing for Aptitude before the placement season. Keep a journal with important formulae or
time-saving techniques so that you can attempt maximum questions in a limited time frame. For the Java and
Python section,just keep your basics clear along with a routine of solving MCQs to discover new topics or to
revise the studied topics.

2. [Technical Interview] [49 appeared, 17 shortlisted] 2 panelists in my interview panel

The students were divided into groups based on their first preference. My panel consisted of 9 students and
initially one panelist, but a second panelist joined during my interview. All the students in my panel were
applying for the SQL Developer role.
The interview began with the panelist asking me for my introduction, followed by why I chose the SQL
Developer role. Then, I was asked to solve a question and write the output on paper. Although I can't recall
the exact table values, the problem was focused on left and self joins, with the challenge being the presence
of duplicate entries and their impact on the joins. The conversation then shifted to questions about different
types of keys, their distinctions, and SQL constraints.
Then certain scenarios were presented to me and was asked about my initial approach. On further discussions
with the panelist, we arrived at an optimal way to approach the scenario. One of the scenario was:-
1)There's some data in T1 - i) Copy all data from that in T2. ii) Copy only the latest data (last row).
2)There's a table present with multiple records already. Add a new column with a NOT NULL constraint.
The interviewer also gave me a series of SQL questions, where I had to write queries for calculating the
highest salary in each department, dropping a column, and updating the salary column by adding a 10%
bonus.
For this round, a solid understanding of SQL constraints, keys, subqueries, window functions, and stored
procedures was essential. Additionally, clearly communicating your thought process helps the interviewer
understand how you approach problems. This can guide them to offer hints if you get stuck..Practice as
many sql questions to consolidate your understanding of these topics and their nitty-gritty.
3.[HR Interview](17 students were shortlisted for this round)
This round had two interviewers: an HR representative and the MD of ISS. This was the final round,
beginning with them asking for my introduction. We discussed my academic background, whether I plan to
pursue a Master's degree in the near future, and my reasoning for opting for a Minor in Management. Next, I
was asked to elaborate on one of the projects listed on my resume. They then inquired if I had read the job
description for the SQL Developer role and whether I was comfortable with the responsibilities. When asked
if I had experience working with databases, I referred to one of my projects where I used MySQL. This led
to an in-depth discussion about the database aspects of the project and whether its objectives were
--- PAGE 3 ---
business-oriented. Following that, there was a conversation about where I live, how I commute to college,
and whether I would be comfortable commuting to Nesco. Afterward, they asked if I had any questions. I
asked the MD about the governance solutions they provide to clients, and I asked the HR about what a
typical day would look like if I joined ISS Stoxx.
Around 10 PM the results were announced & 12 people were selected across all roles. However,I was not
selected.

4. 4th September 2024

Nearly a month after the process date, I received a message from the point of contact for the ISS Stoxx
process, that the company had asked whether I had been placed or not and was ready to extend the offer.
Later that night, I received a message confirming my selection.

Round 1: Online Test

The test had a duration of 60 minutes and was divided into three sections:

1. Verbal Ability - 20 Questions

2. Analytical Ability - 20 Questions

3. Programming Ability - 20 Questions

There was no specific time limit for each section; you were free to solve any section at any point during the
test. Additionally, there was no negative marking for incorrect answers.

• The Analytical Ability section was generally solvable.

• In the Programming Ability section, most questions involved being given an output, and you had to

select the correct code from the provided options that would generate that output. Some questions
were related to DBMS (Database Management Systems).

Round 2: Interview (Tech + HR)

Betore the interview began, we were asked to write code for three questions based on strings. These
questions were relatively easy. After the test was completed, candidates were called one by one for the
interview.
The interview began with me introducing myself, followed by the HR asking about my family background. I
was then asked to explain how I solved the string-based coding questions and what the optimal solutions for
them would be. After that, I was asked to write the code for binary search. The conversation then shifted to
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts, where I was asked about the four pillars of OOP, with a
specific focus on how abstraction is implemented, leading to further questions on related topics. We also
discussed the projects I had worked on and how I implemented them. In the next segment, I was asked to
solve SQL queries. One of the SQL questions involved a self-join, which I found confusing and struggled to
solve completely. Finally, they asked some HR-related questions, including my long-term and short-term
goals.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Important Tips:

• Make sure you know everything about your projects. Spend a good chunk of time explaining the

deatils.

• Practice DSA on leetcode/Hackerrank.

• Know the four pillars of OOP (Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction), and be

able to explain and apply them.

• If you encounter a challenging question, don't panic. Try to explain what you understand about the

problem, even if you can't fully solve it. Interviewers appreciate effort and problem-solving mindset.

• If you have done any internship it will come handy.

The following rounds were conducted in order:

1) Pre-placement talk

2) Online Assessment (on Hackerrank platform)

3) Interview Round 1

4) Interview Round 2

1.     Online Assessment [~240 students appeared]

The first round was the online assessment, conducted right after the pre-placement talk. Around
240 students appeared for this round, as students from both SPIT and SPCE were eligible to
apply.
The assessment was for 1 hour on Hackerrank platform and consisted of 18 questions covering
logical reasoning, aptitude, basic supply chain concepts, programming and SQL. The
programming and SQL questions were straightforward, as were the supply chain questions if
you had a basic understanding of the concepts of supply-demand, inventory, process planning,
graph interpretation etc. Having pursued a minor in management at SPJIMR, I was able to
answer all the supply chain-related questions. The programming question (1 question only) I
got was to find the sum of numbers from 1 to n using a loop. The SQL questions were simple
as well (2 questions) and could be solved using just SELECT statement with WHERE
condition.
22 students were shortlisted for the next round based on resume and the online assessment
score. (Make sure you attempt most questions accurately and submit the assessment as quick
as possible as shortlisting was also done based on speed).

2. Interview Round 1 [22 students appeared]

This was a personal interview round. There were 4 panels and each panel had 1 interviewer.
My interview lasted about 30 minutes. The interviewer first introduced himself and his position
in the company and then asked for my introduction. After the introduction, we moved to
questions.
The questions consisted of guesstimates, puzzles, basics of supply chain and some were resume
based as well. I was asked a guesstimate question to find/estimate the number of ATMs in
Andheri. I could reasonably solve the question and the interviewer was satisfied with my
approach. Next, I was asked a puzzle of 5L, 3L water containers - you have a 3L and a 5L
water container, and neither one is marked aside from the total volume. In order to measure out
exactly 4L of water, we must utilize the containers in the right way. How is this possible? I had
read this puzzle beforehand and so could answer easily.
For guesstimate questions, practice a wide range of scenarios to improve your estimation skills.
Focus on breaking down complex problems into smaller, manageable parts and making
reasonable assumptions. Familiarize yourself with common guesstimate frameworks like
market sizing, population estimates, and resource distribution. This will help you approach
these questions with confidence and structure during interviews.
For the puzzles, go through and practice Geeks for Geeks puzzles for interviews. Almost all
types of puzzles asked during the interviews of any company are from here.
Some other questions I was asked:

1) What is supply chain, who are the stakeholders in a supply chain, what are the different

stages of supply chain and what moves from one process to another in a supply chain
(answer - money, goods, information).

2) My understanding of the role

3) Describe your internship as a web development intern

4) Describe your BTech major project and how you are planning to go forward

5) One SQL question to find the count of IDs grouped by country and ordered

alphabetically in a table having columns - ID, country

6) One programming question to find and display all prime numbers between a given

range (num1 to num2)
10 students qualified for the next round.

3. Interview Round 2 [10 students appeared]

This was the final round of the process. There were 2 panels, first panel had 1 interviewer and
the second panel had 2 interviewers. My interview was taken by the second panel and lasted
about 40-45 minutes.
The questions asked in this round were similar to the ones asked in the first interview round.
There was one guesstimate question - find/estimate the number of cups of tea consumed in
Mumbai in a month and one puzzle - two people went to a cafe together and both ordered iced
tea. One person drank ten of them in 30 minutes, and the other drank just one in the same time.
The person who drank one was poisoned, while the other who drank ten was fine. But, all of
the drinks that were served turned out to contain poison. Why did the person that drank more
iced tea survive? I took a little longer than expected to reach the final solution but was able to
get hints and convince the interviewers about my approach and solution.
Keep asking clarifying questions about the guesstimate/puzzle if you are unable to recall or get
to the solution right away. The interviewers often give some important hints to guide you to the
right solution. Also keep them informed about what you are thinking and how you are
approaching the problem instead of just solving on a paper silently. This lets them know about
how you approach problems, how you think, how you apply logic, etc and they can correct you
if you go wrong in some step.
Some other questions I was asked:

1) Are you good with handling pressure and what are you doing to get better at it?

2) If given an easy task and a difficult task, which one will I do first and explain why?

3) Are you good at multi-tasking, how do you prioritize things?

4) How did you work on improving your weaknesses?

These were some basic HR questions. You can go through some general HR questions asked
in interviews that are available on the internet and prepare general answers for them
beforehand. These questions are asked in the HR rounds of almost all companies.
5 students, including me were offered the internship/placement.

1. Coding Round (291 students appeared for this round)

Platform: DoSelect || Time: 1hr 30min || Questions: 4

1. Given an array, print the number of subarrays having XOR of all elements that have an even

number of divisors.
Approach:
i. I used the brute force approach for this question of calculating the XOR for each
subarray on the go in O(n^2) complexity after which I calculated the count of divisors for the
XOR.
ii. The brute force solution worked for this question.

2. Given an array, provide the lexicographically smallest array possible by swapping the

elements any number of times if arr[i] ^ arri] < 4.
Approach:
i. I used the selection sort algorithm for this question as sorting would lead to the
smallest possible array. The only change made was adding the additional condition as mentioned
here.
ii. The brute force solution worked and the time complexity was O(n^2)
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Given a binary string of length 'n' and 'q' queries having ranges 1 to r. For every query, you

have to sort the elements in the range 1 to r on the original string to obtain a new string. Output
the number of unique strings that would be obtained after all q queries.
Approach:
i. I used a set to store the strings being generated and could only partially solve this
problem. 5/10 test cases passed.

4. Given a directed graph and q queries of three types could i.e. Adding a dependency, removing

a dependency and checking if dependency exists between two different nodes.
Approach:
i. I used an adjacency matrix for this as the queries involved addition and removal of
edges which can easily be done in O(1) time complexity.
ii. To check the presence of the dependency, I performed DFS which has O(V+E) time
complexity. The solution worked and all test cases were passed.
Overall I was able to solve 3 problems completely and 1 partially. 30 students were shortlisted
for the interviews after this round.

2. Technical Interview - 1(30 students appeared for this round)

The offline interviews were just on the next day after the OA. The interviews started at 9 am and
15 panels were going on simultaneously. The round started with me giving my introduction to
the panelist and then 2 DSA questions were asked.

1. Given n number of flowers having their blooming period as (start, end) inclusive. If a person

arrives in the garden at i time provide the number of flowers that the person would see.
Approach:
i. I started with the brute force approach of creating an array and incrementing the
number of flowers at a particular time by traversing through the provided flowers. But this
solution failed at some edge cases.
ii. The panelist provided me some hints to approach the solution through sorting the start
and end time of flowers. I finally used the prefix method to maintain the number of flowers at a
point of time.
ili. Further I was asked to provide the space and time complexity for the given solution.
The panelist was satisfied with my approach and we moved on to the next question.
--- PAGE 3 ---

2. Given a matrix of r rows and c cols we need to move from the (0, 0) to the (r-1, c-1) cell. We

can only make 2 moves, 1 towards right and 1 downwards. Each move is represented by an
alphabetH for horizontal and V for vertical move. The result of the program should be the kth
lexicographically smallest possible path out of all the paths.
Approach:
i. I started with the brute force approach where all the paths would be generated using the
dfs and then sorting the strings and returning the ith value.
ii. The panelist told me to improve this so after some discussion I tried to find a
mathematical way to reach the output but was not successful. So finally I decided to generate the
next permutations from the smallest possible path for i times.
ili. The panelist asked me to explain the implementation of the next _permutation function
and we discussed the same for 10 minutes.
Finally the panelist told me that time was up. The interview lasted for around 1 hr. Finally, 13
students were shortlisted for the next round.

Tips:

1. Always be vocal about the approach you are thinking about even if it is wrong.

2. Always make sure about all the conditions mentioned in the problem and ask doubts to the

panelist about the same.

3. Knowledge of time complexity and space complexity is a must.

3. Technical Interview 2 (13 students appeared for this round)

The second technical round at around 2 pm and 13 panels were going on simultaneously for the
same. The interview started on the similar lines with me providing my introduction to the
panelist. Then he introduced himself and gave some information about the overall process for
this round. Then we started with the DSA questions.

1. Given a grid of size mxn, suppose a person is standing at the top of the grid and he needs to

reach the last row of the grid. An array of indexes (i, j) A is given where on the kth A[k] cell of
the grid is filled with water and blocked. Return the maximum number of days after which the
person is still able to reach the last row of the grid
Approach:
--- PAGE 4 ---
i. Initially I was a bit confused with the problem statement and spent some time clearing
my doubts regarding the same. After which I instantly provided the brute force solution of filling
one block at a time and then performing dfs to check the possibility of reaching the goal.
ii. The panelist told me to improve the same and after that I discussed different
approaches but they provided no significant improvement. After a hint from the panelist I was
able to arrive at the binary search based maximization + dfs based approach.
ili. I was told to write the complete code in my preferred language and the time and space
complexity for the same.

2. Given a graph with R, G, B colored edges where Alice can walk on R colored edges, Bob can

walk on G colored edges and both of them can walk on B colored edges. Return the number of
edges that can be removed from the graph such that Alice and Bob can still reach all the nodes.
Approach:
i. As it was needed to reduce the number of edges I approached this problem using a
Minimum Spanning Tree. The panelist told me that I was in the right direction.
ii. After some discussion I arrived at a modified Prim's algorithm solution where two
different visited arrays would be used to mark the arrival at a particular node.
ili. I was told to write the pseudocode for the same as the remaining time left was less.
Finally after the interview I got to ask the panelist what all tasks were normally a part of his role.
The interview lasted for around 1 hr 25 min. 9 students were shortlisted for the last round.

4. Hiring Manager Round (9 students appeared for this round)

So I was overall confident about this around as having read all the interview experiences of the
seniors I had a lot to talk about in my resume. As I had been actively participating in hackathons
, I had work experience as well as experience of working in a committee.
The interview started at 5pm. The interviewer was the Head of Engineering and led around 17
teams. I gave my introduction to him after which he started asking me questions based on my
resume.
Initially, he started by asking about my internship experience. So I have been working at the
same startup for 1 year. He was curious to know what was the reason behind the same. I
explained each and every project which I had developed and the overall growth that I
experienced in using different tech stacks.
--- PAGE 5 ---
After which he asked me about my experience with hackathons as I had mentioned my
achievements regarding the same. I explained some of my projects which I had made during the
hackathons.
Then he asked me about my experience as the Technical Head of CSI where I explained about
my role and responsibilities. The overall experience is about the same.
He asked me about my favorite application, which I told as Instagram and then he asked me how
the stories feature is implemented in the same. I explained about the priority based sorting which
he verified himself by checking the app on his phone.
He asked me some situational questions about resolving conflicts, working in a team. The criteria
that I used for shortlisting people for the hackathon. A tech based startup I would like to build if I
was provided funding and time for the same.
He also asked me about a feature I would want PhonePe to have. Here the conversation with the
second panelist helped me understand how the PhonePe SDK was still under development for
TypeScript. I discussed the same and how I would have used it instead of other options.
Finally, he asked me about my weaknesses to which I answered based on the facts that were
quite evident from my resume. I asked him what all tasks were a part of his role.
Finally 6 students were offered the I + FTE role and I was one of them.

1) You can start with CAT-level questions from  https://bodheeprep.com/free-cat-quant-

practice-questions

2)  Please read the instructions before the test and see if they have mentioned

anything about negative marking on the test window.
Focus on improving speed and Manage time wisely. Make sure before the actual test
you have practised enough to know your strengths n weakness.

4. Interview I  [39 students were shortlisted for this round]

This round was based on resume. Know your resume  A to Z. For me the first question
was "Tell me something that's not mentioned in your resume". So just be prepared for
surprises. BE CONFIDENT in whatever you say. The Next question was "do you know
what JP in JP Morgan is and what is the history of JP Morgan Chase & co."
Know the company its work policies, lines of business and history. The rest interview
revolved around the basics of risk management: "What is risk management"," What are
different types of risks", and "Can you elaborate on Credit Risk and Market Risk". The
one question which was asked in all interview rounds (at least to me) was "Why risk
management and finance, Why not core/tech". Also, Read the Job Description (JD)
before the interviews, I was asked questions based on JD. Also, they ask you which role
you prefer and why. (we had Projects & solutions and middle office & reporting as two
different roles.)

Useful Tips:

1) You are the one who decides the flow of the interview. So answer what you know

and be ready for cross-questions. Do not say anything that you have absolutely no
idea about. In fact do not mention anything in your resume that you can't explain.

2) CONFIDENCE IS THE KEY. BE CALM.Be clear while you speak and Be precise. Do not

talk a lot, if they want you to elaborate about something they will let you know.

3) Have real-world examples prepared, especially regarding risk types and risk

management failures. For instance, be familiar with the Lehman Brothers collapse,
its role in the 2008 financial crisis, and the associated risk type.

4) When asked why you chose JPMorgan Chase, don't simply state "The company has

an excellent reputation or the company culture aligns with me." Instead, provide a
specific example, such as how the firm navigated the 2008 crisis, and then elaborate
on your reasons.

5) Have an brief idea about the current market situation in India and the world. Be

aware of all major financial n risk-related news.

6) READ JOB DESCRIPTION. Know your strengths and which role you prefer and why.

5. Interview II  (2 panalist) [15 students were shortlisted for this round]

This round was a complete scan of my resume. They asked me about the case study
competition and the solution I had pitched. They later asked me to explain my projects
and inquired about the basics of Python and a few questions on SQL. The courses I had
listed on my resume made up the majority of the interview. I had 4-5 courses and was
asked 2-3 questions on each. There were a few risk management questions as well.
"Why not core/tech? Why risk and finance?" was a repetitive question from the
previous round. I had a few co-curricular activities, so there were questions related to
that too. They asked me to rate all my skills mentioned out of 5 and asked 1-2 questions
on each

Useful Tips:

1) Be as thorough as possible with everything mention in resume.

6. HR interview   [8 students were shortlisted for this round]

This was the most chill interview. They asked me questions about my location
preference, my job role preference, and again for the third time " Why not core/tech?
Why risk and finance?".

Useful Tips:

1) BE YOURSELF. The round will test your behavior and mindset, so do not try to

overshow or lie.

Courses

management/25809

https://learn.corporatefinanceinstitute.com/course/excel-fundamentals-formulas-for-
finance
Reading Financial Statements (optional)
https://learn.corporatefinanceinstitute.com/courses/take/learn-to-read-financial-
statements-free-course/30734

Few Important Topics

Basel Norms:
https://www.drishtiias.com/to-the-points/paper3/basel-norms

Lehman-Brother Case :
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BnDbdQa_r38

Credit Sussie Case:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sAslAvRaYfo

Silicon Valley Bank failure:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=430axupwty4

How JP Morgan Chase & co. become biggest bank in world
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Rb2TsOm3Kw

Just be OPTIMISTIC. Luck plays a part, but in the end, it's hard work that takes you the long
way. Give your best. BE CALM and PATIENT throughout the process.

Wish you all the very best!!

1. Pre-Placement Talk [All applicants]

One of the most important rounds, this will be the first time you'll interact with
JPMC's hiring team. They give an overall view of the company's work culture, future
goals, etc. I say this because the presenter for this PPT was also my interviewer for the
first round. So I was already familiar with the person, and he also asked me what I liked
most about the PPT.

It was an interactive presentation so Be Interactive. Ask Relevant questions, Kindly
refrain from asking repetitive and irrelevant questions.

Screening is mostly based on C.G.P.A, so anything above 8 is safe. Make sure you add
your projects and a few achievements. Since the whole process was online the Resume
you submit while the application is the only one used throughout the process. So do not
lie about anything on your resume. Keep your resume diversified apart from your
projects and technical internships, add sports achievements, Hackathons, case study
competitions, and any committee work.
For your resume keep in mind:

1) Single Page Resume on Latex

2)Add relevant Risk Management & Finance Certifications.

3) Check the ATS score on https://resumeworded.com/.  (If possible  try and take ATS

score above 60)

3.  Online assessment  [108 students were shortlisted for this round]

Test Pattern: 30 questions  in 45 minutes
With negative marking of +2 for correct answer and -1 for wrong answer
Section 1: Quants  (27 questions)
CAT level questions based on topics such as : profit loss, ratios & percentages, number
series, number systems, work time distance ( train problems, work done by x men in y
time), clocks, geometry.

Section 2: Data Interpretation (1 set of 3 questions)
It was a moderate set : Probability and Permutation combination

journey.prep:
- The entire interview was revolving around "what, when, where, and why" for each topic.

- Be honest with the interviewer and with your resume as well (as a fresher, they don't expect you to

know everything).

- In my case, Tech Round 1 was 80% DSA and Tech Round 2 was 80% Dev.

- During Dev rounds, it's a plus point to use fancy development terms in your answers, as the next

question may be related to them. However you should be familiar with these terms before using them.

- Having Internship experience helped me a lot they didn't focus on the project section of my resume.

- Thankfully I was not asked questions on aptitude and puzzles, as I was not well-prepared for them.

- Do prepare for Java because most companies work in Java.

- For DSA, Striver's A2Z is more than sufficient. First, try to understand the basics of all the concepts,

and then go in-depth into each one. In my case, I had solved 65% of the sheet, but I covered the
basics of all the topics. Most of the time, I repeated the videos multiple times if I felt that I hadn't
understood the concept properly.

- In an interview, your way of explanation and your approach to solv e the problem >>>> just providing

the correct ans. ( Focus on discussing multiple approach and explaining why some of them may not
work)

- Prepare for OOPs, DBMS, SQL, OS, and Dev concepts (including basic system design, as interviewers

often ask about basic system design nowadays, so don't neglect Dev).

- Participate in company hackathons it is a plus point during interviews.

If you have honestly put in the effort from your end, you will surely get what you deserve.
Best of luck!

Following are rounds that occurred after applying:

1. Resume Shortlisting (63 students shortlisted for CDO Role)

2. Technical Round 1

3. Technical Round 2

4. HR Round

1.     [Written Test] [ 63 candidates appeared for this round]

In this round you will be given 1 hour(8:15 AM to 9:15 AM) to solve 1 MCQ, 2 Coding question, 1 SQL Query on
paper.

1. MCQ

2 MCQs were provided and we had to solve one of them

1) The first was based on the Left Shift (<<) operator

2) Second one was based on python scope variables

I solved the second one

2. Coding Question

We just had to write down function code in a format similar to LeetCode.

1. https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-k-sorted-lists/description/

I wrote optimal solution of this using priority queues.

2. https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-window-substring/description/

Solved using brute force approach

3.   SQL Query

https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sql-query-to-find-the-highest-salary-of-each-department/
I solved this query using 2 approach

1. Using GROUP BY with MAX()

2. Using ROW_NUMBER() Window Function

Tips: Try to write clear code. Avoid excessive edits or messy code (it should be easy for them to

understand and evaluate your approach, and also at each round your interviewer will have this paper in their
hand).
Write down comments at imp steps and proper naming for variables.
Keep a copy of your resume ready, as you will need to attach it with your answer paper during submission.

2. [Technical Round 1] [ 19 candidates were shortlisted for this round ]

This round lasted for more than an hour, and there were two interviewers present.

- The interview started by asking how many questions I solved in the test. They inquired about the

approach for each question, starting from the MCQs to the SQL query. For the first coding question,
they asked about the different approaches to solving the pr oblem, including their time and space
complexities, (I answered all brute, better and optimal) and why I ch oose the particular approach I
used. They also wanted to know why I selected a specific data structure and what would happen if the
conditions were changed. Additionally, they asked a few questions about linked lists, focusing on how
pointers worked in this question.

- They asked how a hash map works internally and what happens if there are collisions.

- They asked about sets and multisets, including when to use each, and the internal implementation of

priority queues in the C++ STL.

- I was asked to create a data structure similar to a hash map where the key is an element of an array,

and its value contains multiple indices where the element occurs in the array. I proposed using a linked
list for the value portion. The interviewer then asked how to retrieve the smallest and largest index
values from the linked list in less than O(n) time. I initially suggested a doubly linked list approach, but
noted that it would work for either the smallest or largest index, but not both efficiently. The interviewer
suggested to think for tree data structure instead of a linked list, which would reduce the time
complexity to O(log n). I was then asked to derive the time complexity mathematically  and plot the
graph for TC.

- They then asked further questions about Binary Search Trees.

- After this, he moved on to the second coding question and asked me to describe all the approaches

that could be applied to solve the problem, including their time and space complexities. I covered the
approaches from brute force to the optimal one using a sliding window. He then asked me to identify
various edge cases for the optimal approach.

- After this, he provided me with an array and asked me to find a particular element. I identified that it

was a rotated sorted array, so I suggested using binary search. He then asked me to explain condition
statements needed to write the code

- https://leetcode.com/problems/search-in-rotated-sorted-array/description/

- Further, they asked me about REST APIs what they are, the various types, methods, and the difference

between PUT and PATCH.

- They asked about abstraction, how it can be achieved, and the concepts of abstract classes and

interfaces, how to implement them and the differences between them.

- Difference between Having and where clause

- They asked about SQL and NoSQL databases, including what they are. They inquired about which

database to use for scaling, whether MySQL or MongoDB

- They also asked about indexing, database partitioning, and the criteria for partitioning a database.

- Lastly they asked about my role in the major project. I mentioned that I handled the entire web

development part while the rest of the AI/ML work was done by other team members.

They asked if I had any questions, so I inquired about the day-to-day work of the job role because I didn't
get a chance to attend the PPT.

3. HR Round

After being shortlisted from Technical Round 1, I was called for the HR round. This round lasted 20 to 25
minutes.
The questions asked were:

1. How was my day?

2. Where do I stay, how much time I spend in travelling, my daily schedule, and how I manage my time.

3. Work done during internships.

4. He asked me about hackathon s and  fortunately I had cleared Round 1 (Executive Summary) of the

Nomura KakushIn hackathon. He then asked about the solution we proposed for that hackathon. He
also inquired if I had participated in any other hackathons like this, to which I responded about Barclays
Hack-o-Hire. He then asked for details on the problem statement and the solution we proposed for
that hackathon.

5. How I was when I joined SPIT and how I have changed or developed since then.

6. He asked me to tell him something about myself that is not mentioned in my resume.

4. Technical Round 2

After the HR round, I was called for Technical Round 2. This round also lasted for more than an hour,
and there were two interviewers present, both of them are currently working under CDO at Nomura.

1. Tell me about yourself

2. What are the sorting algorithms and the time complexity (TC) of each of them?

3. Explain Merge Sort in detail.

4. Given a sorted array in ascending order, how would you sort it in descending order? Which algorithm

is most suitable for this, and which algorithm is the least suitable?

5. They gave me a SQL query that was an advanced version of the one provided during the coding test.

6. What are the pros and cons of using Arrays and Linked Lists? When should each be used? Provide a

real-life example.

7. In my resume, I had mentioned multiple AWS services, so they asked me about them, what work I did.

What is the AWS CLI?

8. What are REST APIs?

9. What is SOAP?

10. Different HTTP status code and their use?

11. What are WebSockets? When should they be used? Provide real-life examples. (The interviewer was

delving deeper into this, but then I told them that I have a basic understanding and haven't
implemented it yet, so they stopped asking further in-depth questions on this concept.)

12. Scenario-based question -> Given a 30 GB file, how would you find the frequency of words in it,

considering your system can process only 10 GB at a time? (I initially thought he was asking about the
concept of virtual memory, so I explained how high -end games like PUBG can run on 8 GB of RAM by
our OS, but he was looking for a different answer. He provided a hint about "Streams," which I caught
and explained how data streams can be used in such cases and how queries are performed on
streams.)

13.   What are MySQL and MongoDB? When should each be used? Provide real-life examples.

14. What is Polymorphism (including the meaning of the word)? What are its types, and provide a real -

life example.

15. What is Microservice architecture and Monolithic architecture?

16. When should Microservice architecture be used?

17. He gave me a scenario, "We usually see that the IRCTC app remains down. How would you solve this

problem?" I suggested deploying multiple backend applications and using load balancing. Then, he
asked me to explain this concept in detail.

18. Design a database schema for Amazon. I started by considering all types of users, but since it resulted

in a very large schema, he asked me to focus only on the user perspective (as it is already a bit difficult
question).

19. Lastly, they asked if I had any questions, so I inquired about the day-to-day work of the job role (same

question asked in Tech 1 also      ).

Total 13 students were selected: 3 for CDO, 8 for ITD, and 2 for the GM role.

customSections.content:
- The entire interview was revolving around "what, when, where, and why" for each topic.

- Be honest with the interviewer and with your resume as well (as a fresher, they don't expect you to

know everything).

- In my case, Tech Round 1 was 80% DSA and Tech Round 2 was 80% Dev.

- During Dev rounds, it's a plus point to use fancy development terms in your answers, as the next

question may be related to them. However you should be familiar with these terms before using them.

- Having Internship experience helped me a lot they didn't focus on the project section of my resume.

- Thankfully I was not asked questions on aptitude and puzzles, as I was not well-prepared for them.

- Do prepare for Java because most companies work in Java.

- For DSA, Striver's A2Z is more than sufficient. First, try to understand the basics of all the concepts,

and then go in-depth into each one. In my case, I had solved 65% of the sheet, but I covered the
basics of all the topics. Most of the time, I repeated the videos multiple times if I felt that I hadn't
understood the concept properly.

- In an interview, your way of explanation and your approach to solv e the problem >>>> just providing

the correct ans. ( Focus on discussing multiple approach and explaining why some of them may not
work)

- Prepare for OOPs, DBMS, SQL, OS, and Dev concepts (including basic system design, as interviewers

often ask about basic system design nowadays, so don't neglect Dev).

- Participate in company hackathons it is a plus point during interviews.

If you have honestly put in the effort from your end, you will surely get what you deserve.
Best of luck!

Following are the four rounds that occured after resume shortlisting:

1) API Round

2) Technical Round 1

3) Technical Round 2

4) Hr Round

1. API Round [ 92 students appeared for this round]

In this round, you will be given 3 hours to create an API for a problem statement. You can use any web
server of your choice, but the database should be MySQL or PostgreSQL. At the end, you need to fill out a
Google Form and submit the GitHub link for the API.
I got the problem statement of creating an API of dining reservation system for Zomato, where I had to
implement the following requirements:

1. Register a User

2. Login User

3. Add a New Dining Place

4. Search Dining Place by Name

5. Get Dining Place Availability

6. Make a booking

After submission, you will explain your API to the panel, where they may ask you to write code for a
different functionality in front of them. They asked me to write code to search for a dining place by address
and to delete the dining place.
Tips for this round:

1. Practice creating 1-2 APIs beforehand

2. Have a template ready where the server is connected to the database, and the login and register

functions are working with JWT Authentication.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Decide the libraries you will be using beforehand to avoid wasting any time during the round.

4. Have clear understanding of how Authentication using JWT works

5. Your first priority should be to complete all the functionalities; once implemented, you can improve

them and adjust the output format as required.

6. Ensure that all backend code is not in the same file.

7. Keep your explanation short and effective, as the panel may be short on time.

8. If possible, prepare a few extra points to distinguish yourself from other candidates. For instance, I

described how my API is secure against various types of attacks and can be scaled.

9. If the Google Form requires you to submit the GitHub link, do not wait until the last moment. Push

whatever code you have written and ensure your last commit is before the deadline.

2. Technical Round 1[18 students appeared for this round]

In this round, the panel asked me to share my screen and open a Google Docs document, where they had
pasted a DSA question. They explained the question to me and asked how I would approach it. I initially
shared a brute force approach and discussed its time complexity. They then requested optimization, which I
explained within 30 seconds due to my familiarity with the question. Subsequently, I was asked to code the
solution in the document.
The interviewer then remarked, 'Now that you're warmed up, let's increase the difficulty,' and presented me
with a LeetCode medium-level question. I explained the brute force approach, then within the next 30
seconds, I formulated a DP approach and discussed its time complexity. Thinking the solution couldn't be
further optimized, the interviewer provided hints that led me to realize the question could be solved using
binary search. I proceeded to write the code accordingly.
The exact questions that i was asked are:

1) Find the Engineer who has kth lowest score this year

Productivity : [5, 6, 7,7, 8, 8, 9]
Engineers: 7
Quarter wise performance
Q1: [1, 5,6 ,8, 8, 8,9]
Q2: [4,6,7,3,8,9,1],
Q3: [6,8,1,6,5,4,4]
SCORE: productivity * performance

2) partition tasks into X parts such that the maximum sum out of all partitions is minimum

Sprint - eg: 14 days - n days
X engineers team
t tasks
I just know about t tasks and i know for every task how much time will it take as x y z tasks
Tasks -> [2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 3] 6 tasks
X = 2 engineers
--- PAGE 3 ---
N - sprint days
Sprint = 11 days
Constraint

• You can't divide/break tasks

You have assign tasks sync to same engineer

• Order of tasks can't be changed

Tips for this round:

1. If you don't understand the question, ask the interviewer to explain it again.

2. Before diving into the solution, clarify the question's constraints with the interviewer

3. Test your approach with an example to validate its correctness

4. Always begin with the brute force approach, stating its time complexity, and iteratively optimize the

solution

5. Vocalize your thought process so the interviewer can guide you effectively and save time

6. If you feel stuck, don't hesitate to ask for hints; they can be very beneficial

7. Reviewing standard questions thoroughly is usually sufficient to succeed in this round

3. Technical Round 2 [ About 10 students appeared for this round]

This was my first round where I had to answer the common question 'Introduce yourself.' I had prepared a
response to keep the interviewer interested. I mentioned that I'm in the top 5% of global coders and shared
how I reduced task completion time by 75% during an internship, saving over 200 hours each year. After
that, I explained the task in detail and we discussed how the project's architecture works with the database.
Next, I was given the task to design a database for an Instagram-like platform. I asked questions to fully
understand the requirements and avoid making assumptions. I discussed my thought process out loud,
explaining why I chose certain solutions and considering potential problems that might come up as the
database gets used more.
During the database design, I suggested several solutions and asked for feedback on whether they were
practical for an SQL database. Whenever I got stuck, I asked for hints to help me move forward. After
finishing the database design, I was tested on writing SQL queries using aggregate functions and joins. I
managed to answer all the questions and even suggested improvements for the last query.
The interview ended with me asking a question and having a short chat with the interviewer.
Tips for this round:

1. Emphasize the reasons behind your solution choices. They want insight into your thought process.

2. Learn from my mistake: Prepare by considering how you would design databases for common apps

like Instagram, Twitter, WhatsApp, YouTube, and blogging platforms beforehand.

3. Practice sql questions before the interview

4. HR Round [ About 7 students appeared for this round]

The interview started at 11 PM and lasted about 30 minutes with the co-founder. He asked me to introduce
myself within 30 seconds, so I focused on highlighting important achievements and kept my introduction
--- PAGE 4 ---
concise, about 3-4 sentences. It's advisable to prepare multiple versions of your introduction for such
situations.
We then briefly discussed my internship experience, particularly focusing on the quantifiable results I
achieved. Since I mentioned leading a team, I was asked about delivering negative news to team members
and how I would handle various leadership situations.
This round primarily aimed to understand my thought process and assess whether I would be a good fit for
the company culture. I was asked personal questions such as the lowest point in my life in the last 3-4 years,
why it happened, what might have occurred if things had gone differently, and what I learned from the
experience. They also inquired about any regrets I might have.
Additionally, we discussed what global issue I would choose to solve if given the opportunity, and why. I
was also asked what I had learned if I didn't secure the internship today.
The interview concluded with me asking several questions about the company's core values
Tips for this round:

1. Take your time to consider your answers. Speaking impulsively can lead to difficulties when

discussions delve deeper into the topic

2. Frame your life experiences as a narrative. Be prepared to explain why things happened as they did

and what lessons you've drawn from them

3. Approach this round as a conversation rather than a formal interview. Use it as an opportunity to

discuss your life and experiences
Three students were offered the opportunity at WorkIndia for the role of SDE.

journey.prep:
1. In the Digital Interview (DI) round, I had prepared my answers and written them down beforehand,

which helped me deliver a smooth interview. If you're an introvert, practicing your answers in front
of a mirror can significantly improve your speaking skills.

2. For the Technical Test, I just revised the concepts on OOPS, SQL, Java, CN, OS.

3. For the GD, I made sure to stay updated on the latest world affairs. My experience with the online GD

wasn't the best, as these can sometimes be challenging, but I focused on making one strong
contribution. Even if you don't get another chance to speak, that one entry should be impactful enough
to make you stand out. Start by greeting everyone, th en present your point. Ensure that your point is
unique and carries significant weight.

4. For the tech interview, be thoroughly familiar with your resume. You should be prepared to answer

questions about the "how," "what," and "why" of everything listed. Have an in-depth understanding of
the topics you know. Don't stay silent --ask questions and engage with the interviewers; they'll
appreciate your curiosity and will help if you try. Make sure to practice well -known DSA questions
and SQL queries.

5. For the HR rou nd, focus on clear communication and maintaining good body language. Share your

thoughts, ideas, and real-life experiences. Talk about non-technical activities you've been involved in,
and be prepared for common HR questions.

Important: Be thorough with your resume and know every detail. Don't stay silent for more than 20 seconds.
If you need time to think, ask for a moment. If you don't know the answer, it's okay to say, "I'm don't know
the answer." Please, don't lie.

For any queries, feel free to ask me at https://www.linkedin.com/in/shubham-solanki-6376221a3/
Wishing you all the best! Hopefully, you'll succeed, and if not, an even better
opportunity is on the horizon!
journey.howSecured:
Rounds Date & Time
Digital Interview 1st August - 3rd August
Technical Test 7th August, 7:30 PM - 8PM
Group Discussion 10th August, 7:30 AM - 9 AM
Technical Round
9th August, 10 AM - 4 PM
Leadership Round

1.     Digital Interview - HireVue

This was the first round of the placement process, it was a 15-minute interview on HireVue, with 6 basic HR
questions about my background. Those not familiar with HireVue, it's basically a virtual interview, the
question will be displayed on screen and you will be given 30 seconds to prepare and then 3 mins to record
your answer. The 6 questions were same for everyone:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Don't rely on scripted responses or read from any material. Just speak naturally, looking directly at the camera.
Although the maximum time limit is 3 minutes per question, you don't need to use the full time --stop the
recording whenever you feel you've answered thoroughly.

2. Technical Test - Online (120 Candidates)

Platform: Microsoft forms (No proctoring)
Time: 30 minutes
Format: 25 MCQs
Topics Covered: DSA, OS, SQL, Aptitude, Java and Python

The test was MCQ based so not that hard, do java/python/os/ccn guess-output questions beforehand as
they are asked, don't get stuck on a question, time management is key.

3. Group Discussion - Online (80 Candidates)

The group discussion was held online on Microsoft Teams, we had 2 choices either give the GD from
home and reach college in-case of selection or go to college early and sit there and give the GD (depends
how far you stay from the college), choose accordingly . The Actual GD didn't, time is less overall only
30 mins, of which 2 mins are given after topic reveal to prepare a bit.

Remember basic guidelines for GD -

1. Listen Carefully: Pay attention when others speak to understand their points.

2. Avoid Arguments: Remember, it's a discussion, not a debate--don't fight or interrupt.

3. Introduction: Only introduce the topic if you're 100% confident in your understanding.

4. Conclusion: Aim to make the conclusion as inclusive as possible within the limited time.

Some topics:

1. Challenges/Opportunities for India in the Indian Subcontinent (Political)

2. Digital Twins (Technical)

3. Gen AI / Chatgpt (Technical)

4. Future of EVs (Hardware, Economical)

5. Complete Cashless Society

Tips: While in 2-min prep time, try to make your own points, don't search here and there, write down what

you can think of, they will come to know if you have searched online. A night before sit down and go through
current affairs in all the most common domains.  If you don't understand the topic well, listen properly
what others are speaking based on that, try to find out some valuable points.

4. Technical Interview (30 Candidates)

The Technical Interview was conducted by a panel of two senior developers, and they focused heavily on
my resume projects. It was essential to be completely confident about each project, including the
technology used, the reasons for choosing it, and the implementation details.
When I entered the interview room, we exchanged greetings, and one of the interviewers complimented
the quality of my resume, noting that it was a color copy. After introducing myself, the interviewers began
their in-depth questions about my projects.
One of my projects was a client facing project so that went on in detail about each and everything. They
asked why I built the project and what made it unique compar ed to similar ones. They were interested in

the challenges I encountered during implementation and how I overcame them. Additionally, they wanted
to know whether it was a team or personal project and what my specific contributions were.
Next, they moved on to a project where I used Oauth 2.0. They inquired about some advance terms such
as SAML etc. which I was not aware about so I honestly told them about having no knowledge about them.
Being honest is better than saying anything irrelevant.
Later they moved to docker and went on in depth about docker its working and commands. Later they
moved to Ubuntu as it was mentioned in m y resume. They a sked about chmod and other commands in
depth
After discussing my projects, the interviewers shifted to topics related to computer networks and operating
systems. They began by asking about the OSI model. They wanted to know what it is, its layers, and the
function of each layer. They also inquired about the differences between the OSI model and the TCP/IP
model.
They then asked about TCP and UDP --what they are, their uses, and their differences. They wanted to
know which one is better and asked for real-world examples of where each might be used.
They then asked me a basic Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) question:

1. reverse a string - first I explained brute force approach using stack and then moved to optimal one by

swapping characters

2. how to find the middle node of a linked list. I explained the solution using the slow and fast pointer

technique.
They also asked me the internal representation and working of hash map and how it is different from stack.
Later they moved on to java, multithreading, thread synchronization, pass by value and pass by reference
concept.

At last, they asked me what Baker Hughes do and If I had any questions for them. I asked them about the
most fascinating project they have worked on till date at Baker Hughes.
I tried to answer nearly all of their questions, and they seemed satisfied with my responses.

5. Leadership Interview - Techno HR (15 Candidates)

The final round was a mix of technical and HR questions. The interviewer  started by asking me to introduce
myself. Then, she asked about my weaknesses and how I plan to overcome them.

She also asked some managerial questions, like what I would do if I were in a team with three people and two
of them weren't working properly.  Another question was about what I would do if a project deadline was
approaching and the project wasn't completed yet.

Next, she asked about the app I spend the most time on my phone. She wanted to know why I like that app,
what the best thing about it is, and what I would change if I could.
She also gave me a situation where they are going to reduce time size of 5 to  team size of 2  because of AI
takeover and why should she keep me in top 2 employees and what is it that I can do and AI cannot. She also
asked me my favorite food delivery app from swiggy and zomato and the tech issues of both.
Then, the conversation shifted to why I want to join Baker Hughes. She also asked if I had gone through
previous interview rounds, and when I said yes, she followed up by asking why the other company didn't hire
me.
Finally, she asked if I had any questions for her.
(TIP: Stay calm and answer confidently during the interview. Remember, your body language, facial
expressions, and speaking skills will all be closely observed.)

After a long wait, the results finally came in, 7 students were selected, and I was one of them 😊

journey.howSecured:
1. Coding Test:

This was conducted on the HirePro platform. It consisted of 15 aptitude questions, 20 technical questions
(SQL, MS Excel, Programming Basics, and Basic Statistics) and 2 coding questions (Both Easy) -

- Question 1: Given an array of numbers and a value k, we first had to find the corresponding AND

array by getting arr[i]&k for every element in the array and then

- Question 2: Given an array of stocks, each stock was represented by a number and the person will

buy the stock if that stock is palindrome and non negative so print yes else print no.
Eg: - stock = [121, -11, 23], output = Yes, No, No
I was able to solve both the coding questions but my aptitude didn't go as well but the technical questions
went well.

2. Technical Round 1: [38 students appeared ]

This round lasted around 50 minutes to an hour. My interview was online, and it began with a short
introduction and from there the interviewer asked me some situational questions on React.js as that was my
primary skill. After this he asked me to explain the OOP concept and the 4 pillars along with the question on
why multiple inheritance is not possible in java using classes and how we will implement it using interfaces.
Then he asked me about try catch and why we use it. After this he asked me to explain authentication and
authorization. I explained with the example of a login page and then for authorization I explained JWT
tokens and how we use middleware for auth. Then he said what if we have dynamic user roles and we want
authentication for each role (Eg user1 should not be able to use user2 apis and user2 should not be able to
use user3 apis and so on) I answered by saying that since we have their roles in the Database we can include
user role in the token and for every api we will check in the middleware if the appropriate user is accessing
that api. After this he moved on to DSA, only my panelist was asking DSA questions. They were the
following -

- Given a linked list and two variables m and n, you have to delete n nodes after every m nodes. I

explained using two pointers and keep in mind the edge cases as well when m and n can be null.

- The second question - Valid Parentheses

At the end he asked me a simple aptitude question where I had to find the angle between the hour and
minute hand when the time is 1:30 (135 degree).
--- PAGE 2 ---
Tip: Remember to stay calm and answer the question with examples like when explaining abstraction you
can give an example of abstract class car and an abstract method engine (since every car will have its own
implementation of engine). Also whenever you want some time just ask the interviewer that you need some
time to think it's completely fine and while solving DSA questions keep talking about what you are trying to
do and while writing the code explain the interviewer as you write the code.

3. Technical Round 2: [ 12 students appeared ]

This round was offline and lasted around 30 - 35 minutes. The interviewer began by asking for an
introduction and then he asked me questions about my freelance project which I was working on and asked
why that particular tech stack. I was using MySQL there so he started asking questions about that, like how
are you using Node.js to run SQL queries, how many connections can you keep, are you re creating the
connections for every query or you have established one connection and keep it as it is. He grilled me quite a
bit here but I was able to answer decently. Then he asked about my second work experience and then some
questions about it as well like what was my contribution there etc. Then he said that he was satisfied and got
everything so the interview was done. This scared me a bit since the person before me was interviewed for
more than an hour. So I asked if he had any feedback for me. He said they give the feedback to HR and
based on feedback of every interview they decide if they want to proceed with the candidate but he told me
not to worry as he was happy with the interview. Another question I asked was about the crowdstrike issue
and if that affected the bank.
Tip: Keep a smile on your face throughout the interview. The interviewers are very friendly and you just
need to show them that you know everything that is on your resume.

4. HR Round: [ 8 students appeared]

This round was online and lasted for 30 - 40 minutes. There were two HR's and they started by asking how
my day has been up till now. Then they asked me to introduce myself followed by questions like what is my
family background, what are my hobbies, what I do for fun, which was the last book I read and what lesson I
learnt from it (since I said reading books as one of my hobbies). Then they asked me in what way do I think
technology will affect the banking sector in the coming years. My initial answer was the offline processes
getting automated and making use of Al to improve customer services but they were not satisfied with my
answer so I asked for some time to think and then said that we still manually add cash to ATMs when they
run out of cash so making Smart ATMs which print appropriate amount cash if they run out and the Offline
KYC being done online with document verification done online as well and they said they liked this answer.
Then they asked me why I want to join IDFC and strengths and weaknesses and then asked me if I had any
questions for them. I asked for some information about the role and again the crowdstrike question.
Tip: Keep smiling and think before answering. Also when saying weakness say something and that you are
working on it and pay attention in PPT because you might get the answer of why you want to join the
company from there.
--- PAGE 3 ---

5. Techno HR Round: [8 students appeared ]

So this round took place one day after the HR round took place (on 1st August). The interviewer was a
senior manager. He began by asking for my introduction. Since I mentioned that I had won a hackathon in
my introduction he asked me about that hackathon and what we created and what was my contribution. He
then asked me about React.js and why use it instead of vanilla JS. Then he asked about state management in
React and what is redux. After this he asked me to explain any one DSA algorithm. I explained Binary
Search. He then asked me about the Time and Space Complexity. I don't remember the other questions but
he asked some more questions about CS fundamentals. Then he asked why I wanted to join IDFC and if I
had any questions. I again asked the crowdstrike question and asked that due to that issue have you
reconsidered using third party services because of it. He really liked my question and answered it and the
interview was done.

6. Technical Round 3: [8 students appeared]

So just when we thought (and were told) that everyone was selected, we got a call again and got told that we
have another interview with the senior MD. But when I joined the call, there were two senior engineers who
were going to take the interview and the senior MD was just present in the call (audio and video off just
listening ig). This round also began with an introduction after which just like the previous round they asked
me about the hackathon and what was the project, what was my contribution, what were the issues we faced
while creating the project. They then asked which language I use, I said for DSA I code in python to which
they asked me the difference between cpp java and python and why python. I said that it was interpreted and
why because I was doing a DA course and the youtuber who I followed for DSA coded in python as well
and it was easy to code and better to understand. Then he asked about javascript whether it was a compiled
language or interpreted to which he asked then what is the difference between js and python. I answered that
python was more readable and in python we don't declare the data type whereas in js we have to use var, let
and const. Then they asked which data structure can be used for the forward and backward button in the
browser. I said we can use stack. Two stacks, one for the backward and another for the forward and then I
took some time to check it and then explained to them my approach of using them. They then asked what
other data structure we can use, I took some time and said doubly linked list or even a graph and they were
satisfied with the answer. They then asked if I had any questions and I asked the same questions as the
previous round and they liked the question too and answered it and the interview was done.
At last after giving 5 interviews the next day, we were informed that all 8 of us got the offer.

get nervous

the company and find stuff to ask them.
