with a constraint that you can swap any two values only if their XOR is less than 4
→ Approach: I used a brute force approach of O(N^2), all the test cases passed using this approach.

3. Unique String with sub-string sort queries

Given: A binary string of length n consisting of O's and 1's and k queries consisting of a pair (l,r),
sort the substring(between 1 and r) in the original string and return the number of unique strings after
performing the operations k times.
→ Approach:

• I used a brute force approach where I extracted the substring from the given string for each query.

• Instead of using the sort function for substring, i used counting sort since the string contained only

1's and O's.

• I was partially able to solve this question. For a few cases I faced TLE.

4. Dependency question

Given: N number of initial edges (transitive dependencies) of a directed Graph, Perform three types
of operations given k operations
Types of operations, Given k operations,
--- PAGE 2 ---
Type 1: Insert a new dependency i.e. add a new edge u,v to the pre-existing graph
Type 2: Delete a dependency i.e. edge u,v
Type 3: Given u,v check if a path exists between them
→ Approach:

• I used Disjoint set approach Onlogn)

• However the answers to few test cases were wrong. After understanding the problem was in the

remove function. I tried to correct it, however was out of time.

• This question could have been solved using simple DFS as well.

• I was able to partially solve this.

Tip:

• Do not hesitate in using the brute force approach, for most questions the brute force approach will

work.

• Each question was of 100 marks, if you are stuck at one question, move to another. Partial marks also

count.

• If you are able to solve 2 complete questions/ 1 complete and then partial questions the chances of

selection are still quite high.

2. [Technical Round 11[30 students were shortlisted]

This round was a complete DSA round. The interviewer asked me 2 questions.
Ist question: There is a list of events given, where each event had the start time, end time and value of the
event. The question was to select any 2 events and maximize their value.
→ Initially I gave a greedy approach, but the interviewer gave me a test case from which i understood that
the greedy approach won't work here.
→ So then I gave the recursion approach and then optimized it using a memoized solution and the tabulation
solution. The dp solution i gave was correct but the interviewer was looking for a more optimal solution.
→ So after the help of the interviewer I was able to give a binary search solution with memoization, which
was indeed the most optimal solution. He then asked me to write the pseudo code for the same.
Then he moved on to the next question
2nd Question: A grid of n*n is given. The grid has 1: Number of Fruits, 0: Empty cell, -1: Blocked cell.
The start position is 0,0 and initially we can move in the right and bottom direction to reach the bottom most
right cell. After that we move towards left and in upward direction to again reach the starting position. While
moving from top to bottom and then bottom to top again, we collect fruits and then they replaced by a 0. We
need to collect the maximum fruits.
I started with a dp solution and a traversal technique, but wasn't able to reach the correct answer, however
after the help of the interviewer, i was able to reach to a solution.
--- PAGE 3 ---
The interviewer was happy with solution and the round ended.

Tips:

• The interviewers are very friendly, even if you start with a wrong approach, or aren't able to reach a

solution keep talking to the interviewer and try to explain them your solution, and after listening to
their hints, try and reach to a solution.

• They dont see if you are able to answer every question correctly but they focus on the way you are

thinking and how you are reaching a solution.

3. [Technical Round 21 [ 13 candidates were shortlisted]

The interview started at around 2pm. Again this round was solely DSA based.
Initially the interviewer asked me for my introduction and then a jist about my resume and then the DSA
question started.
The 1 st question was:
https://leetcode.com/problems/remove-max-number-of-edges-to-keep-graph-fully-traversable/descriptio
This question was quite tricky, I knew this question and the name of the algorithm (Union-Find) that
is required to solve this question as it was part of this year's LC Daily questions.
So I was easily able to provide the solution to this question. The interviewer then asked me about the time
complexity and told me to write the pseudo code of the solution.
The 2nd Question:
Given N*M grid initially with all 1's in it. We can start from 1st row and can move in any direction. The
goal is to reach the last Column. Each day a coordinate will be provided, and a blocker will be added to
the given coordinate. The question was to find the day from which we no longer will be able to reach the
last column.
I started with the brute force approach of using dfs for each case and then finding the answer. Later i tried to
optimize it but the interviewer was looking for a much better solution. After thinking a lot i was still not
able to reach a solution.
The interviewer then told me that we could binary solution for this question.
Hater understood the reason and then the interviewer asked me to write the pseudo code for it. Which i did.
The 3rd Question:
This question was a medium leetcode question: https://leetcode.com/problems/decode-ways/description/
I quickly gave the recursion solution for it and then optimized it by giving the memoization solution and
then the tabulation solution for it.
Then I wrote the pseudo code and explained the time complexity for the same.
The interviewer then asked if i had any questions for him, I asked about the technical challenges the
company was facing. We had a discussion about it and the round ended.

Tips:

• Don't lose your confidence if you aren't able to answer, keep trying but once you know you wont be

able to reach the solution let the interviewer know, don't beat around and try to fool the interviewer.
--- PAGE 4 ---

• Know about the time complexity and how it works, because after each question you will be asked to

explain their time complexity and space complexity.

3. Hiring Manager Round [9 students]

This round lasted over an hour, and the interviewer was an Engineering Manager at PhonePe.
The interviewer was very chill and it mostly was a discussion round, Initially he started with my
introduction and then he asked me about my preparation for the placements.
Then he asked me about how I developed skills and balanced academics along with it. Later he asked me
questions on one of the projects on my resume which he liked and we had a little discussion about it.
He then moved on to ask me questions about my hackathon experiences and how do I go about forming
a team about the same. This discussion was followed by a question as to what would be my approach to
learning if I joined Phone Pe as a full time engineer. He then asked me a feature I would like to
implement on any of the UPI apps.
He was quite impressed with the answer I gave. Lastly he asked me about any conflicts i have faced while
working in teams, and how i resolved them and also a few questions on my committee experiences.
In the end I asked him about his experience after joining Phone Pe.
6 students received the offer (Intership+FTE).

Tips:

• Keep your calm while giving your interviews. The interviewers are there to help you, keep

conveying your thoughts and approaches to them, do not stop talking.

• The interviewer is looking for how much you are willing to learn and not how much you

already know.

• Try and relate your answers to real life experiences, those give you an edge and shows the

interviewer your skills to learn from your environment.
All the best for your placements!
Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.

journey.prep:
1. In the Digital Interview (DI) round, I had prepared my answers and written them down beforehand,

which helped me deliver a smooth interview. If you're an introvert, practicing your answers in front
of a mirror can significantly improve your speaking skills.

2. For the Technical Test, I just revised the concepts on OOPS, SQL, Java, CN, OS.

3. For the GD, I made sure to stay updated on the latest world affairs. My experience with the online GD

wasn't the best, as these can sometimes be challenging, but I focused on making one strong
contribution. Even if you don't get another chance to speak, that one entry should be impactful enough
to make you stand out. Start by greeting everyone, then present your point. Ensure that your point is
unique and carries significant weight.

4. For the tech interview, be thoroughly familiar with your resume. You should be prepared to answer

questions about the "how," "what," and "why" of everything listed. Have an in-depth understanding of
the topics you know. Don't stay silent --ask questions and engage with the interviewers; they'll
appreciate your curiosity and will help if you try. Make sure to practice well -known DSA questions
and SQL queries.

5. For the HR round, focus on clear communication and maintaining good body language. Share your

thoughts, ideas, and real-life experiences. Talk about non-technical activities you've been involved in,
and be prepared for common HR questions.

Important: Be thorough with your resume and know every detail. Don't stay silent for more than 20 seconds.
If you need time to think, ask for a moment. If you don't know the answer, it's okay to say, "I'm don't know
the answer." Please, don't lie.

For any queries, feel free to ask me at https://www.linkedin.com/in/shahvarshil
Wishing you all the best! Hopefully, you'll succeed, and if not, an even better
opportunity is on the horizon!
journey.howSecured:
Rounds Date & Time
Digital Interview 1st August - 3rd August
Technical Test 7th August, 7:30 PM - 8PM
Group Discussion 10th August, 7:30 AM - 9 AM
Technical Round
9th August, 10 AM - 4 PM
Leadership Round

1.     Digital Interview - HireVue

This was the first round of the placement process, it was a 15-minute interview on HireVue, with 6 basic HR
questions about my background. Those not familiar with HireVue, it's basically a virtual interview, the
question will be displayed on screen and you will be given 30 seconds to prepare and then 3 mins to record
your answer. The 6 questions were same for everyone:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Don't rely on scripted responses or read from any material. Just speak naturally, looking directly at the camera.
Although the maximum time limit is 3 minutes per question, you don't need to use the full time --stop the
recording whenever you feel you've answered thoroughly.

2. Technical Test - Online (120 Candidates)

Platform: Microsoft forms (No proctoring)
Time: 30 minutes
Format: 25 MCQs
Topics Covered: DSA, OS, SQL, Aptitude, Java and Python

The test was MCQ based so not that hard, do java/python/os/ccn guess-output questions beforehand as
they are asked, don't get stuck on a question, time management is key.

3. Group Discussion - Online (80 Candidates)

The group discussion was held online on Microsoft Teams, we had 2 choices either give the GD from
home and reach college in-case of selection or go to college early and sit there and give the GD (depends
how far you stay from the college), choose accordingly . The Actual GD didn't, time is less overall only
30 mins, of which 2 mins are given after topic reveal to prepare a bit.

Remember basic guidelines for GD -

1. Listen Carefully: Pay attention when others speak to understand their points.

2. Avoid Arguments: Remember, it's a discussion, not a debate--don't fight or interrupt.

3. Introduction: Only introduce the topic if you're 100% confident in your understanding.

4. Conclusion: Aim to make the conclusion as inclusive as possible within the limited time.

Some topics:

1. Challenges/Opportunities for India in the Indian Subcontinent (Political)

2. Digital Twins (Technical)

3. Gen AI / Chatgpt (Technical)

4. Future of EVs (Hardware, Economical)

Tips: While in 2-min prep time, try to make your own points, don't search here and there, write down what

you can think of, they will come to know if you have searched online. A night before sit down and go through
current affairs in all the most common domains.  If you don't understand the topic well, listen properly
what others are speaking based on that, try to find out some valuable points.

4. Technical Interview (30 Candidates)

The Technical Interview was conducted by a panel of two senior developers, and they focused heavily on
my resume projects. It was essential to be completely confident about each project, including the
technology used, the reasons for choosing it, and the implementation details.

When I entered the interview room, we exchanged greetings, and one of the interviewers complimented
the quality of my resume, noting that it was a color copy. After introducing myself, the interviewers began
their in-depth questions about my projects.
For one of my projects involving a video transcoding service, they asked why I built the project and what
made it unique compared to similar ones. They were interested in the challenges I encountered during
implementation and how I overcame them. Additiona lly, they wanted to know whether it was a team or
personal project and what my specific contributions were.
Next, they moved on to a project where I used SHA-256 and AES-256. They inquired about the differences
between these two technologies and whether one could be used in place of the other in certain scenarios.
Finally, they discussed my project based on a NodeJS API. They asked about pagination, its necessity,
and the type of authentication I used. They also questioned why I chose a particular database and did not
use MongoDB on AWS instead of MongoDB Atlas.
After discussing my projects, the interviewers shifted to topics related to computer networks and operating
systems. They began by asking about the OSI model. They wanted to know what it is, its layers, and the
function of each layer. They also inquired ab out the differences between the OSI model and the TCP/IP
model.
They then asked about TCP and UDP --what they are, their uses, and their differences. They wanted to
know which one is better and asked for real-world examples of where each might be used.
Next, they asked about what happens when a user types "www.google.com" into a browser. I explained
that the browser first checks its cache to see if it has the IP address for the domain. If not, it queries the
DNS server, which then contacts the root DNS server and the .com top-level domain to find the IP address.
Finally, a request is sent to the server, and the HTML document is displayed on the screen.  Lastly, they
asked about virtual memory--what it is and its purpose.
After covering computer networks and operating systems, the interviewers moved on to SQL. They asked
what SQL is and how to retrieve data from a database. Initially, I answered with "SELECT * FROM
table_name." The interviewers seemed disappointed, but I qu ickly added that instead of using "*," it's
better to specify the table's attributes to reduce computation and save bandwidth. This response satisfied
the interviewers.
They then asked me a basic Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) question: how to find the middle node
of a linked list. I explained the solution using the slow and fast pointer technique.
At last, they asked me what Baker Hughes do.
I tried to answer nearly all of their questions, and they seemed satisfied with my responses.

5. Leadership Interview - Techno HR (15 Candidates)

The final round was a mix of technical and HR questions. The interviewer started by asking me to introduce
myself. Then, she asked about my weaknesses and how I plan to overcome them.

She also asked some managerial questions, like what I would do if I were in a team with three people and two
of them weren't working properly. Another question was about what I would do if a project deadline was
approaching and the project wasn't completed yet.
Next, she asked about the app I spend the most time on my phone. She wanted to know why I like that app,
what the best thing about it is, and what I would change if I could.
Then, the conversation shifted to why I want to join Baker Hughes. She also asked if I had gone through
previous interview rounds, and when I said yes, she followed up by asking why the other company didn't hire
me.
Finally, she asked if I had any questions for her.
(TIP: Stay calm and answer confidently during the interview. Remember, your body language, facial
expressions, and speaking skills will all be closely observed.)

After a long wait, the results finally came in, 7 students were selected, and I was one of them

get you. They will help you through the process, so do not be afraid of making mistakes or asking questions
if you need any help. They just want to see your way of thinking and approaching problems, even if you
may be incorrect, they will guide you towards the correct solution until you grasp it. So always keep talking
and let them hear what you are thinking, and even if you think you are incorrect just say that you are not

There were a total of 3 rounds conducted for the role of data analyst. All of these rounds were in the form of
interviews. 46 people had been shortlisted by resume to appear for the first round.

1. SOL Round [46 candidates ]

The first round took around half an hour. The interviewer introduced herself and then asked me to introduce
myself as well. In all three rounds my introduction was very basic and only included my name, branch, and
my interests in the aspect of data analysis which led me to apply for this position. After that we began the
SQL evaluation. I was provided with an excel sheet which had two tables and there were 7 questions based
on the data provided in those tables, for which I was asked to write queries. Most of these questions
involved joins, some involved the group by - having clause and one involved using a window function. Then
I was asked to explain the logic behind the queries, and modify them according to certain conditions. I did
make a mistake in one question, but then I was given a hint and I was able to correct it. I only completed 6
out of the 7 queries because of a bit of network delay which took up a lot of time, so we skipped the last
question. Then I was asked if I had any questions, and then we were done with this round.
I had prepared for this round by only doing two things - watching a comprehensive video of SQL from
basics to advanced, paying special attention to joins, group by - having, and window functions; and then
searching for difficult sql questions asked in interviews and practicing them. I feel that if you get the essence
of how these clauses and functions work, you will be good to go.

2. Problem-Solving Round [24 candidates ]

In this round the panel had two interviewers. They introduced themselves and asked me to do the same.
After that the first question I was asked was on guesstimates: - estimate the number of cars in Mumbai. I
took some random estimates about the number of people who would be able to afford a car and then
mentioned multiple factors which would affect the same, this led me to an estimate about the number of
privately owned cars. I thought my answer would end here, but then the panel hinted on the fact that I had
missed something out, and I realized I had to estimate the number of taxis as well. Here too I took a very
--- PAGE 2 ---
wild guess as to the number of people who work as taxi drivers and made my calculations based on that, and
my approach seemed to satisfy the panel.
The second question was slightly on the mathematical logic side, as it was based on averages. The essence
of the question was as follows: -
Let there be 4 values x, a, y and b.
We have a value R = (xa + yb)/(xty)
If both a and b increase, is there any situation where R can decrease?
Here I gave an incorrect answer. I immediately said no as the value of R is directly proportional to both a
and b. But I was asked to take a minute to think and re-evaluate my answer. This was a pretty obvious sign
that my answer was incorrect. Even so, I was very unsure that such a situation was possible. Still I kept
talking and shared my reasoning so as to why I believed this situation was not possible. But then I was given
a hint about breaking down the equation and from there I realized how this question could be answered, and
I then explained what I understood and gave the solution, and the panel seemed satisfied. Again I was asked
if I had any questions, and then we were done with this round.
To practice for this round, I had searched up common guesstimate questions and puzzle-type questions asked
in interviews and gone through the common approaches for the same.

3. HR Round [10 candidates ]

The HR round was the only interview round conducted in-person. It was taken by Ranaq Sen sir who is the
Head of People at WI.
This round was very unlike typical HR interviews, none of the questions that were asked was something I
had a prepared answer for. I was first asked to introduce myself, there I had mentioned certain strengths and
interests which sir discussed a bit in detail. Then I was asked about my opinions on the field of data science.
I was also asked about my hobbies, which led to a bit of a relaxed environment as we discussed novels I had
read. Then I was asked what direction I would want my career to take in the future, or more simply, what I
would like to be doing for the next year or two. Here I emphasized the fact that I had a genuine interest in
the role of a data analyst, and for the future part I gave a pretty non-traditional answer and included the fact
that I was considering higher studies in the future along with other job prospects. I felt it was not correct to
do so at first, but at the end of the interview when I asked sir for feedback/advice, he complimented my
honesty on the topic and added how that is one of the core values of the company. I got a bit more general
advice from sir and here my interview ended.
A total of 5 students had been selected for the role of Data Analyst in the end.

confident, as it reflects your level of self-assurance or nervousness. Additionally, maintain
positive body language and wear a pleasant smile. Avoid shaking your legs or leaning on the
table during the interview. If the interviewer hasn't invited you to sit, always ask, "May I have a
seat, sirạbefore sitting down.
The interviewer reviewed my resume again and noticed a project I had mentioned, which was
based on Java and MySQL. This shifted the focus of our discussion heavily towards that
project. He asked me to explain the overall flow and architecture of the project and whether it
was a solo or group effort. Next, he inquired about the database connectivity, including the
libraries or dependencies I had used. He also presented some technical situational questions
related to the project, asking how I would handle specific cases. Finally, he asked how I would
approach making the project scalable, including the adjustments to the tech stack and the
step-by-step process I would follow to meet this requirement.

in a project. In response to such questions, it's important to focus on the positive aspects of
both options, highlighting how they differ and how they can be used according to the project's
needs. Additionally, consider the security implications of each option and explain which one
would be better in that context. After this the interview concluded with some HR questions and
then he asked me if I had any questions for him. As I had said earlier, be ready with 2-3
questions to ask the interviewer during the overall interview process. The HR questions were as
follows.

1. Tell me about a challenging scenario faced while working on a group project and what all

steps you took to handle the situation

Round 1:

1. Aptitude Round (55 mins)

The assessment took place online via the HirePro platform and consisted of 45 questions, divided evenly
across three sections: Analytical Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Verbal Ability, with 15 questions
in each section. Notably, there was no specific time constraint for each section. Overall, I found the
difficulty level to be moderate. Following this round, 21 candidates were shortlisted. For those who find
the Quantitative section particularly challenging, I suggest checking out the following playlist for
preparation: Quantitative Aptitude Playlist. Additionally, Indiabix offers a wide range of practice questions
that can be useful for preparation.

2. Group Discussion [21 students appeared for this round]

Our group discussion (GD) panel consisted of 9 -10 candidates. My panel was filled with good speakers.
The topic assigned to us was "EV in India". Since it was a bit common subject, we were given 2 minutes
to gather our thoughts. I quickly jotted down key points on paper, considering how EV impacts different

sectors and is used differently by individuals. I also touched upon the Benefits of EV in both Public and
Private Sector, while highlighting its positive contributions. I ensured that my arguments were backed by
real-life examples and statistics --one of which was about that now a days EV vehicles are becoming
affordable for middle class families by giving example of Tata Nexon EV model. A GD isn't just about
speaking, it's also about listening and engaging with the ideas of fellow participants. After about 10
minutes of a healthy discussion, each of us was given 1 minute to conclude, where we were expected to
summarize and state whether we supported or opposed the topic.
After this round, some students were selected for the next phase, with some candidates advancing from
my panel.
Here are a few tips that helped me succeed:

1. Participate in mock GDs: Make sure you engage in mock GDs conducted by  our Teachers in initial

semesters in soft skills sub jects and also by your Training and Placement Office (TPO) before
placements. These sessions give you valuable experience and highlight areas where you can improve,
based on evaluator feedback and self -reflection. The more you practice, the better you'll get.
Personally, my habit of reading and communicating regularly, combined with my experience leading
student organizations, helped me excel in this round.

2. Balance communication with substance : Communication skills are crucial in a GD, but they must

be backed by valid arguments and a well -rounded perspective. If you're not confident in your
knowledge of the topic, stay calm, listen to your fellow panellists, and build on their points rather than
staying silent.

3. Focus on listening and maintaining positive body language : Many candidates focus only on

speaking without truly listening to others or maintaining positive body language, which can harm their
performance. Most of the time, you'll be listening, so avoid turning the discussion into a heated debate.
Stay polite and maintain the group's decorum.

4. Clarify any doubts: If you're unsure about the topic or its scope, don't hesitate to ask the evaluator

for clarification before you start brainstorming.

This was an online assessment(from college). Consisted of 15 MCQ Aptitude Questions + 15 MCQ

• Aptitude Questions

The aptitude questions were easy to moderate. Questions were based on probability, sets, finding
missing element in series, mirror/water Images, and answering the question on the basis of a
given graph.

• Technical Questions

Questions were mostly asked on DBMS, SQL queries, JAVA basic concepts, code snippets. And
were Conceptual.

• Coding Question

server.
For Example, serverLoad = [7, 2, 7, 3], serverCapacity = [4, 1, 5, 6], The total cost of server is
calculated as - 7 * 4 + 2 * 1 + 7 * 5 + 3 * 6 = 83 (dot product of 2 initial arrays)
the position of elements in serverCapacity only. The objective is to find the sequence of
serverCapacity that results in the minimum total cost. In case multiple sequences result in the
same minimum total cost, return the sequence that is lexicographically smallest.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Java approach which i used - It was based on Greedy Algorithm. You just have to sort the
serverLoad array in descending order while keeping track of their original indexes by creating a
Pair class to store the server load and its index, then use a comparator to sort these pairs based on
the load and if loads are same then on the basis of index. Next, sort the serverCapacity array in
ascending order. Finally, create a new array to map the sorted capacities to the corresponding
loads: for each pair in the sorted serverLoad array, store the corresponding capacity from the
serverCapacity array at the original index of the pair.

2. Technical Round (36 students)

There were two interviewers in a panel and my interview lasted around 45 mins
The conversation began with a brief introduction where I shared a bit about myself and about my projects.
Following the introduction, the interviewers delved into an in-depth discussion of my projects, asking
detailed questions about the specific technologies and libraries I chose. They were particularly interested
in understanding the reason behind my choices, prompting me to explain why I opted for certain
technologies and how that benefited my projects.
The discussion then turned to the APIs I used, including how I integrated them into my projects and the
challenges I encountered. They also asked about the schemas of my project's databases, where I had to
justify my preference for MongoDB over MySQL. This led to a broader discussion about the differences
between SQL and No-SQL databases, including their respective advantages, disadvantages, and suitable
use cases.
Next, the interviewers inquired about how I implemented authentication and authorization in my projects.
I explained the strategies and technologies I used to ensure secure access control. The conversation then
shifted to front-end development, specifically React. They asked about the fundamental concepts of states
and props, their differences, and the use of hooks. This was followed by a discussion on Redux and its
role in state management within React applications.
They also explored my understanding of Java, questioning whether it is solely an object-oriented
language. To test my knowledge of data structures, they asked me to explain the internal workings of
HashMap, its differences from ArrayList, and scenarios where each would be appropriately used. Also
asked various sorting algorithms and their efficiencies.

experience and how I functioned within a team. To test my abilities to manage the dynamics of teams and

2. Being from an engineering background, we do not have in-depth financial knowledge. It is thus

important to prepare sincerely for this role. I would recommend CFI finance courses as they are free
and are very credible.

3. Please do not start your preparation at the last moment. I was preparing for both tech and non tech

profiles and hence had a lot of stress managing DSA, development, finance, EXTC subjects, etc. Do
not repeat my mistake. Ideally, I would say prepare for only one profile in depth and if you want to
try both then have a sufficient time window with you.

day at least a month prior to the placement start date. This won't take much time, 30 min everyday
while having dinner is enough.

you are not able to answer and at least let the interviewer know what approach you're thinking about.

course. In my case, we participated in a M&A competition without any knowledge, but we learnt and
researched for 15-20 days and won the competition.

study without worrying about external factors like market situation, recession, etc. Believe me, it

- Resume shortlisting

- Online Assessment - 6th July, 2024

Remaining rounds all happened on 10th July:

- Group Discussion

- Interview Round 1

- Interview Round 2

- HR Round

1. Resume shortlisting

> JPMC evaluated all resumes and sent the shortlist to the TPO.
> Use LaTeX to draft your resume and check the resume score on Resume Worded. In my opinion, a
score above 65-70 is good enough.
> Do not exaggerate things, keep it simple. Be sure that you know and understand everything
mentioned in your resume.
> Personally, I only mentioned non-tech projects and courses in my resume. If you have a tech project
that is finance-related, you can include that too.
(97 candidates were shortlisted for the Online Assessment)

2. Online Assessment (97 candidates)

> This was a 45-minute test with 45 questions to attempt without negative marking.
> There were four sections: Corporate Finance (10 questions), Market Awareness (10 questions),
Quantitative Aptitude (15 questions), and Verbal Reasoning (10 questions).

• The Verbal Reasoning section was easy, Quantitative Aptitude was moderate and lengthy, and

Market Awareness and Corporate Finance were moderate.
(72 candidates were shortlisted for Group Discussion)
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Group Discussion (72 candidates)

> One day before the GD, we were given the topic "India - Sth largest economy". It was a broad theme
with many points that could have been included.

• We were divided into groups of 12, and the discussion lasted about 20-25 minutes. There were two

interviewers present who constantly evaluated and guided the discussion in the right direction. They
also assisted those who did not get a chance to speak.
> Try to include numbers and examples in your points as it helps establish credibility and demonstrates
analytical skills and a statistics-based approach.

• Listen to what other people are saying and follow general etiquette.

• Remember, evaluation is based not only on your content but also on how you conduct yourself.

(31 candidates were shortlisted for interview round 1)

4. Interview round 1 (31 candidates)

> These 31 candidates were divided into six panels, each with one interviewer.

• I was asked to introduce myself and discuss things mentioned in my resume. The interviewer took

the resume, so be sure you know everything mentioned. He asked me about my Minor degree course
in Management from SPJIMR and the topics covered in it.

• He then asked if I knew financial accounting and the three financial statements. How are they linked

together? If we increase the depreciation cost by 'x' and the tax rate is 'y', how would it affect the
income statement and cash flow statement? I answered the question after providing an example and
solving it on paper. He tried to question my answers each time, but it's important to back your
knowledge and intuition in such scenarios.

• I did a DCF valuation project, so he asked about valuation methods and the steps in DCF valuation.

He asked for the formulas for calculating Terminal Value and Enterprise Value.

• We then moved to quick math questions like 97 × 103, 49 × 51, square root of 0.01, etc., and

obviously, using pen and paper was not allowed. These questions can be solved using basic math
formulas like a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b).
> He then asked me two puzzles. First, he asked me to calculate the total number of squares on a
chessboard (1x1 squares + 2x2 squares + ... 8x8 squares), and using pen and paper was not allowed.
The second one was about water in a lake doubling every day and the lake being full on the 8th day;
when was the lake 25% filled? Practicing GFG puzzles would be more than enough. It would help in
other interviews as well.

• He then asked about SENSEX and NIFTY and how their values are calculated. He also asked about

the current values of Gold, Crude Oil, SENSEX, and NIFTY, so be sure to check the closing values
from the previous day.
> Finally, he asked if I had any questions for him. Be sure you have 2-3 questions ready for different
rounds.
> Even if you are stuck on a question, be sure to talk about the approach you are trying. Do not pause
for an extended period. If you don't know the answer to a question, try for some time, and ask for
hints if you still do not get it. At the very least, show that you are genuinely trying.
> The interview lasted for about 40-45 min.
(Interviews were conducted simultaneously, so we lost track of how many advanced to round 2)
--- PAGE 3 ---

4. Interview round 2

• As soon as I finished my first interview round, I was called for the second round without even a

minute's break.
> This was a relatively relaxed round and lasted only about 15 minutes.
> The interviewer asked me to introduce myself and walk him through my resume.
> He asked about the selection process for the Minor in Management from SPJIMR.
> We had won a couple of national-level competitions in finance and consulting, so he asked about that
experience. The finance one was related to merger and acquisition, so he asked about the process of
an M&A deal.
> I was also asked about my internship as a React Developer and the reason behind shifting from
software development and electronics to the finance domain. This is a very standard question that
will definitely be asked. I explained how participating in non-tech competitions helped me make this
decision.
> In the end, he asked if I had any questions for him. Again, keep 2 questions ready for each round.
(15-16 candidates were shortlisted for HR round)

5. HR round (15-16 candidates)

> This round was more like a casual conversation and was pretty chill.

• I was asked standard HR questions: Introduce yourself, walk me through your resume, future plans

regarding higher studies, family background, and what do you understand about this role, etc.

• The interviewer then asked if there had ever been a scenario where someone was immoral or

dishonest and how I approached the situation. This question is to test your ethics. If you have not
faced such a situation, do not lie, and instead explain what you would do if it ever happened.
> In the end, I asked the interviewer a few questions about how different teams collaborated on
projects, job location, etc.
> Although I was not asked, remember the core values of JPMC.
> This round lasted about 15 minutes.
Finally, 11 candidates were selected for the internship.

Total 3 rounds: Online Assessment, Technical Interview, and HR Interview.

1. Online Assessment [90-100 students appeared]

The round consisted of four secƟons: Logical ApƟtude, QuanƟtaƟve ApƟtude, Coding, and a Verbal SecƟon. Everyone received two diﬀerent coding quesƟons, and the diﬃculty level was quite random. Some students received easy quesƟons involving HashSets or HashMaps, while others got diﬃcult Dynamic Programming (DP) quesƟons.

Thankfully, I received very easy quesƟons:

1. Remove duplicate elements from an array and return the unique elements.

2. Count the frequency of each character in a string.

Tips:

 PracƟcing apƟtude quesƟons from IndiaBix and GeeksforGeeks (GFG) is suﬃcient. Just remember the paƩerns and formulas to solve similar types of problems.

 These paƩerns are repeƟƟve in every Online Assessment, just presented in diﬀerent forms.

 For Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA), start pracƟcing as soon as possible. I regret starƟng only one month before placements.

 However, if you are starƟng late as I did, you can sƟll succeed. BeƩer late than never, but I sƟll recommend starƟng your DSA preparaƟon a minimum of six months in advance.

 There are students who get beƩer oﬀers without pracƟcing more than 10 DSA quesƟons, but this is an excepƟon and relies on luck, so don't depend on it.

2. Technical Interview [32 candidates appeared for this round]

My technical interview was unique. It's important to know that everything depends on the panel you are assigned to. There were three panels, with two panelists in each. The diﬃculty level and types of quesƟons were not standardized across all students. You will realize this aŌer a few interviews. My panel was very relaxed.

They didn't ask me for a formal introducƟon. Instead, they asked how my preparaƟon was going, how I had prepared for TransUnion, when I started, and if I had spoken with any seniors from my college who work at the company. You might think these are easy quesƟons, but your answers, where you might menƟon various technologies to impress them, will determine the direcƟon of the interview. I didn't menƟon DSA or SQL in my answers because I was not conﬁdent in my skills in those areas.

The interviewer then asked me to explain my projects. This is a quesƟon asked in every interview, so you should have 100% knowledge of your projects. Mostly, the interview will focus on the ﬁrst project listed on your resume, and someƟmes a second one. AŌer I explained my project, they presented some edge cases and asked how I would handle large amounts of data and improve the execuƟon Ɵme.

Then, they asked me how I would handle a Git conﬂict and what prompt I would give to ChatGPT to help resolve it. Next, they asked how I would run the project on another system. I answered with "Docker," which led them to ask more in-depth quesƟons about cloud compuƟng. However, I stopped them and explained that I haven't worked with cloud compuƟng technologies and don't have much knowledge about it. It's okay to admit when you don't know the answer to a quesƟon. Don't try to give a wrong answer; just be honest. However, you shouldn't say "I don't know" for every quesƟon.

They also asked about a hackathon I parƟcipated in: why my team placed in the top 10 and not ﬁrst, what went wrong, and what I learned from the experience. Then, they asked me to explain Docker to a layman with no technical knowledge. The interviewer was quite impressed with my analogy. Finally, he asked if I had any quesƟons for them. I asked them 3-4 quesƟons. The interview lasted for 27 minutes.

Tips:

 When you enter the room, greet them with a smile and a handshake.

 Give your introducƟon conﬁdently because the ﬁrst impression is the last impression.

 You should know the in-depth meaning of every word on your resume. It's not about the number of technologies you list, but how well you know them.

 There are standard quesƟons asked about projects, such as: how you would handle a large amount of data, how you would scale the system, why you used a speciﬁc technology, and how you would improve performance.

 You are the driver of the interview, so the conversaƟon will likely follow the direcƟon you set with your answers.

 I wasn't conﬁdent in DSA and puzzles, so I avoided menƟoning them. However, this completely depends on the panel. Other companies or panels will deﬁnitely ask more technical quesƟons on CS fundamentals like OS, OOPS, DSA, and DBMS.

 If there are two interviewers, try to maintain eye contact with both. Keep a smile on your face to show conﬁdence.

 They oŌen prioriƟze moƟvaƟon and a posiƟve mindset over just technical experƟse.

 Ask for their names at the end if they didn't introduce themselves at the beginning.

3. HR Interview [10-12 candidates selected for this round]

There was one panel with two panelists. Both were very relaxed. They started with small talk, asking how my day was going and if I'd had lunch. Then, they asked me to introduce myself, focusing on aspects not menƟoned in my resume.

When asked to explain my project, I didn't get too technical. Instead, I focused on storytelling: how I got the idea, my approach, how I collaborated with my team, and the project's future scope.

They then asked about my family background, if I had any issues with relocaƟon, why they should hire me, and if I had plans for a master's degree. Finally, they asked if I had any quesƟons for them. I asked a couple of quesƟons and made sure to shake their hands before leaving, as I had forgoƩen to do so at the start.

[8 students received an oﬀer including me]

Tips:

 I saw many people with good technical knowledge who were not selected aŌer the HR interview.

 Therefore, try to improve your English ﬂuency. I understand if you don't come from an English-medium background (Like me), but at least try to speak conﬁdently, even if you make a few grammaƟcal mistakes.

 Always smile during the interview.

 I feel that the HR interview is about engaging the interviewers with your communicaƟon skills, like telling a story about your projects and your learnings. Don't dive deep into technical terms; they are generally not concerned with those details.

 Try to show them what a good team player you are.

 Conﬁdence, a smile, and honesty are the keys to succeeding in the HR interview.

General Imp Question:

If you have AI in your resume learn about RAG, as interviewers generally know that in AI (asked in all 3 companies for me).

HashMap, HashSet, ArrayList internal implementation in java, JRE/JDK/JVM/JIT in java.

All types of questions on Palindrome(easy to hard), and sorting algos.

Indexing in dbms, have strong hold on sql mostly joins and subqueries are asked.

My Journey:

I completed an internship and a Data Analysis course after second year. Won a few DA competitions in November, but still in December I was really not confident of having a chance at getting a good placement, I did not have great dsa knowledge either. I effectively began my journey in first week of January. Earlier I used to practice very few dsa problems and that too in python. But my seniors told me about how important java is for companies so I switched to java. ( I did it because I was not too advanced in dsa then and was anyways going to start from scratch.) If you are solving in python/c++ pls continue, just do oops and java workings well theoretically.

January: began with java, close to 80 dsa problems, 1 hack participation

February: Gen AI course,close to 50-60 dsa problems

March: Gen AI course, 100 dsa problems, began trying lc contests

April: 150 dsa problems, completed the course, finalist in hackathon(first time)

May : 50-60 dsa, won here technologies hack(first time)

June: Did not focus on solving new problems, rather kept revising topics and solved problems, began with theory topics - java,oops,dbms,os,ccn

Resume: Do not lie about anything, first interview rounds are completely based on your resume. If you dont know about anything that is written it gives a bad impression. Know about every project in detail. Its ok to not know a lot of things, just know whatever you have written. My resume was completely AI/ML/DA/LLM/GENAI based, absolutely nothing about development as I did not know much about it. Also mention those things at the top which you want the interviewer to see, there is no specific order. 3-4 projects are enough, some skills. Pls do mention about any sports you would have played in your life. My MSCI and IDFC first round interviewers were very interested in my cricket skills and that really helped me. Just add one line but do add.

Projects:You dont need to have the best projects, you can have okish projects but need to know everything you did. You can take them from github, but again, know everything. If you can deploy them somewhere, that can be good as you can show it live to interviewer. But that is absolutely not necessary.

Interview: If you are asked something you dont know about, there are 2 ways,either you have absolutely now idea about it- just say sir i am not aware about it. Or you can relate it to some other topic. In that case mention that i dont know exactly, but i feel this is similar to the other thing i have worked on. First round is just resume based, no need to worry much. Also just to impress the interviewer dont speak fancy words which you are not aware of or have good knowledge about. It happened with me at MSCI, where I mentioned an advanced topic too early, so then he went a bit deeper into it and I was not able to answer all of it. The interviewers are mostly chill so they will calm you down.

DSA: DSA is necessary, but 500-700 problems are not, you can crack the best of companies even with less problems solved. But the more you solve, the more confidence you will have of solving unseen problems in oa or interview. Confidence is really important in dsa as in the pressure if you cant think of the right approach, it can get difficult. Codeforces, CP is absolutely not needed for any company other than PHONE PE. I still havent solved any problem on codeforces. If you like solving thats great but please ensure you are working on other aspects also. Also do ensure that you can take input in your language, as leetcode does not prepare us for that. Leetcode contests solving can be helpful, to get practice but dont panic if you can solve only 1 or two problems or even if you cant solve any problem in a contest. You can directly skip HARD problems on LC. Follow strivers A2Z Sheet. MSCI, Barclays and UBS had medium problems but idfc had easy problems. In interview mostly easy -medium are asked or they may not even ask. Even if you have not solved many problems, in june try to read through all easy-medium problems in strivers sheet. Having an idea can help you atleast come up with an approach in interviews.

OS/CCN/JAVA OOPS/DBMS/Aptitude/puzzles: I began with all this in June, You can start in May ideally. Java oops are extremely important, dbms comes next, along with sql, os is slightly important, while ccn mostly wont be asked, although its good to know basics.

Hackathon: Please participate in hacks. If you dont have the confidence, or no one is taking you in their team, find 3 others like you and participate. Because A- it gives you some impactful projects and B- if you sincerely give your best for 24 hours, for 4-5 hacks you will eventually win one for sure. It is helpful in interviews as it validates your skills for the interviewer. Also winning hacks dont require extraordinary skills these days. Just you need to be able to use open source tools well and present well. Please participate in company hackathons, if you win or even reach finale , they will select you for placement. Although if you are not able to win, that is not the end of the road, its not at all necessary.

Role: If you have certain preferences its ok to let go of some roles. But please be realistic, if you have confidence in your preparation, only then leave companies. Because it may happen that good companies might go away. Also please dont be too dependent on one role/company. MANY PEOPLE WERE WAITING FOR WORKINDIA DA, BUT IT DID NOT COME. At the same time it is important to have a few target companies and give it your all for it.

I wont say that placement is very much dependent on LUCK, It plays some part, but if you have not prepared well you have very little chance that luck would get you placed. But if you are well prepared luck can take you that extra mile. Overall if you have prepared well, You will do well eventually.

If you have given your best effort right from the time you decided to be serious (6/5/4/3/2 months) something good will happen, just keep going, Rejections can be tough, but eventually it will help you get something better. In my case I did not get MSCI, but rather got my preferred role,location and pay.

ALL THE BEST!!

Dont hesitate to reach out, 9372138292

Since I had given almost 10 OA's by now, I was confident (this really matters). The day before I gave practice tests for each of these sections on IndiaBix and realised that I was scoring maximum in Quants apti, followed by logical and then verbal. So in OA I began with Quants then logical then verbal, although the sections were in opposite ordering. Many students followed the given

(verbal-logcal-quant) order and thus had almost no time for many quants questions. So identify your strong area and begin with that. I practiced only from IndiaBix for this, I began practicing for Aptitude probably in July itself, focused more on Aptitude after MSCI.

Interview Day: I was in all the 3 shortlists, while this gave me more chances, there was a possibility of me losing focus, so ensure that you cut out all the noise and stay focused on the day of the interview. Now first the GM GD happened, topic- Is AI making us smarter or dependent, this did not go well for me and I did not go further. Then for ITD something unexpected happened, Due to suspicion of copying, all 28 candidates were asked to give another pen-paper OA, where they just shortlisted 7 for further rounds(no one knows what criteria was followed as most of us had solved all the questions correctly). So I did not get through in ITD as well. By the time my CDO Interview began I was already out of the other two.

2. [Tech Interview] [8-CDO, 28-ITD, 19-GM ]

So the interview began with them asking me to skip introduction and just give one line description of my projects and my role in them. I had 4 projects mentioned, all related to Data Analysis, ML and LLM, GEN AI. So my resume was highly aligned with the role. I had done an internship, so I also explained about my role in that and spoke about a few of my skills. There were 2 interviewers. One of them started questioning about one of my (Gen AI powered tool, that converts wikipedia topics into easy to understand comic strips) project. She first asked who is your target audience for this project. I answered that the younger students in age 12-20 who are inquisitive to learn about new things. Then she asked how will you control younger students from generating images of vulgar content. I tried explaining that firstly, wikipedia wont have much vulgar content, and secondly we were taking user's age as one of the user preferences and were passing it through prompts for our model. So we can ensure via structured prompting that the user does not get any vulgar images. She honestly was not convinced. The other interviewer then began by giving a problem. I have 1000 resumes, and want to perform searching in this, how can I do it(similar question was asked in IDFC as well), I explained the entire RAG framework and how it would make the searching very easy. Then he gave me another problem that, every morning he has to get up at 4 and mark a set of tasks as 0 or 1 based on the result, how would I solve it. Now just when he began writing 0 and 1 Logistic regression clicked in my mind. I explained to him the entire flow and working of logistic regression. He was satisfied with both my answers. Then he asked more about what I had done in internship. I spoke about flight price prediction (regression) model. I had mentioned R2 score as an accuracy metric in the resume. He questioned that we dont use R2 score to measure accuracy, I told him that since it was a regression model we cant use accuracy/precision, etc and rather we use mse/rmse/r2 score. He then asked me to explain what R2 score is. I knew about it and explained him with a short example. He then asked me to explain precision and recall. I answered that correctly as well. Then he asked me to give one line explanation about Encoder and Decoder and their examples. I gave a satisfactory answer to that as well. Now in the meantime, the other interviewer had left the room to take a call, this can be a bit distracting, but just try to focus on your answers. Also whenever interviewer asks u about a question, try to question him back, to get complete understanding of his question if you did not understand something. He then asked me to mention all ML algos I know about. I mentioned linear reg, logistic reg, random forest, decision trees,etc. He asked whether I knew about XGBoost. I told him that I had idea about its working but did not have experience working with it. He gave a remark that, did you just move to learning LLMS without completing all ML algos? I mentioned that I knew about them but had not worked with all the ML algos. He then asked me, how good am I in

python, I said 8 on 10. He then asked a DSA question, given an array of numbers find the minimum elements you need to choose to reach the target value. I thought for about 2-3 minutes,( greedy, dp,etc) but could not get an ans, then i just thought of using the brute force and told him for each element we will choose it and then check how many more we need to reach target and maintain a minimum count. So accepted the brute force (since this role did not require much dsa knowledge). Then they asked 2 sql questions 1 was a group by and count query (given document id and curr_status, count the no. of days that document is in the curr_status, each row denotes a day). Then next she gave 2 columns and asked me to explain all types of joins. They then asked if I had any questions for them. I did ask one about gen ai applications in nomura. And then about the diff in culture that nomura has as compared to other companies. They answered these for almost 5 mins. Overall, the interview went well, I was expecting to be called for next round.

3. [HR] [2- CDO ]

Only 2 candidates gave this round for CDO. It was a casual round. Interviewer asked me to give an intro, then asked me about the field I want to work in. Then she said that since I was shortlisted for all 3 roles, give me an explanation about all 3 roles. Then family background and higher studies preference(definitely no). And then I asked her 3 questions about what do u look for in a person not tech skills but general skills, one good thing about nomura and one not so good thing. She answered well for 5-10 mins. But then she left the room with me and when we reached the tpc standing outside tpo, she just said he is done for the day, he can go home. I was like what?? Nothing went alarmingly wrong in the interview, why am I being asked 2 go home, the tpc also said that you are not selected so you can go home now. I felt, I will have to start preparing for companies again from tomorrow. So both the hr round candidates were asked to go home. Then message came that every cdo candidate can go home and results will come later. So then there was some hope, given that only 2 gave the hr round. And finally the result came. 2 were shortlisted for CDO, 1 FOR GM, 3 FOR ITD.

SQL 20 minutes (10 questions) - Most were find the correct syntax, command as well as some theory based questions you should be ok if you practice a bit on geeksforgeeks

Aptitude I don't remember the exact time it was split in 4 sections like(6+8+11+9) mins or something like that 2 sections were like in you're average aptitude maths and logic I think, the other 2 I remember better cause they were unique

flowchart section - 2 flowcharts with blanks and 4 questions each to fill them they might look challenging especially given the time crunch but the first one had branches (switch case) so essentially you just had to compare the options for the blank cell with that spot on the other branches the second one had shorter variable names so it was much harder.

Reading section - I don't know what else to call it but essentially there was a table with construction material names and serial numbers, all questions were on matching them.

You can practice aptitude on geeks for geeks but I didn't find any questions like these 2 sections during my practice.

2. [Round 2 Interview 1] [ 35 candidates shortlisted]

The interview was held on webex in the TPO office itself. I was in the first morning slot so I consider myself lucky. I got a call from them and they told me they'll call again at time of joining and be ready. I entered the allotted room and set up my laptop and opened webex and checked my cam and mic, I also practised my intro out loud which I would recommend to you too if you have the time cause in the previous interviews I'd end up speaking in a low voice without noticing. I got the call and the interview started there were 2 interviewers my introduction went smoothly and they asked me about my projects, I had three projects all of which were all group projects, I went through them briefly after which they asked more in depth about each like my contribution in them, why python? Why next.js and not node.js? Is next.js worth upgrading to if you know react? Who made react? I had actually forgotten that one I said "I know a famous company made it but I forgot" even with this mistake the interview went pretty well like a normal conversation maybe because the interviewers chill and I was less tense. There was one question about if my website suddenly had a lot of traffic how would I handle it. Finally they asked me if I had any questions for them and I asked about their experience in the company.

3. [Round 3 Interview 2] [ 16 candidates]

Just as I stepped out of the room I got a call to join my second round of interview I rushed back and set up my laptop and joined the meet this time there was only one interviewer he also asked about my projects but mostly focused on one, what do you mean by scalable? How is your project scalable? How is it Accessible? Why do you call it easy to use? All these are the points I wrote about the project in my resume so only write the truth. I was able to explain all of his questions then he asked me to share my screen and open notepad and write a basic SQL code for inputting data from a source as I was typing there was a connection issue I switched to my hotspot and reconnected and explained what happened (Its possible unexpected things happen during an interview its important to keep calm and not panic) then he told me to stop typing and just explain there were follow up questions like what to do if there is no primarykey? How to choose if the data is coming form multiple sources? Finally they asked me if I had any questions for them and I asked about their experience in the company.(yes I asked the same question I didn't have a better one)

During the online interviews of blackrock sadly a few of our students had used ai it seems and even the company was angry so that day It was doubtful if anyone was going to be selected.

4. [Round 4 HR(not really)] [ 12 candidates]

12 of us were called by the TPO the next day through DMs we were told it's HR we were called one by one and had an interview with Vinod Sikka sir he asked me about how the interviews went and what could be done so the cheating incident doesn't get repeated. Then we all waited in the conference room and Sikka sir said the list had already been given to the college by the company of those who are selected and took the names one by one. I was overjoyed when I heard my name.

1) First of all be clear on your motto, mine was-To get placed in a good company which can help me kickstart my career and offer growth opportunities.

journey.howSecured:
This was a pool campus recruitment process so probably it took place simultaneously in other colleges too. Pre-placement talk was conducted along with VIT Pune students on Webex. Total 3 rounds took place after Pre-placement talk.

● OA (Technical and aptitude test)

● Tech Interview 1

● Tech Interview 2

1. Online Technical+Aptitude test [Approx. 100 students appeared for this round]

The CGPA criteria to apply was 7.5 and above. Having a proper resume format (Jake's preferably) and one good project with unique features(Can be Major project) along with a couple of basic personal projects is sufficient to make your resume get shortlisted in campus placements. Make sure to write the project description in the form of pointers(the various features). Also, don't completely rely on gpt instead list down in your own words and refine it using gpt. Try to keep the project that sells more at the top.

The test was conducted on the eLitmus platform and was proctored. As Blackrock visited for the first time, we had no interview experience to refer to. So, I searched the web for test formats/questions and prepared accordingly and the test format/topics were not different. Test duration was 1.5 hours , having 3 sections: Aptitude: Had 3 subsections - Quants ; Data Checking/Data Accuracy(was easy) ; Logical reasoning(pattern recognition,sequences,etc). Solving maximum without wasting time is key!

Programming : Had 2 subsections - Flowcharts. Given 2 flowcharts of some basic problem and contains 5-6 blanks which we were to identify and MCQs based on those. 1 was some string matching algo and the other was easy enough ; Pseudocodes. They gave 3 pseudocode based MCQs. Two were based on binary trees/BSTs(basic insertion,deletion,traversal,depth) and one on AVL trees(rotateLeft,rotateRight operations). I prepared on these topics beforehand and thus was able to solve this section confidently.

SQL: There were 20 MCQs on Oracle SQL and were mostly theoretical. Time given was more than enough. I was aware of most of the functions in mySQL and solved SQL50 on leetcode. Though Oracle SQL is a bit different syntactically, I tried to trust my gut and marked accordingly in some questions.

One thing I had learned about OA's in 2 months of placement season is that YOU NEED TO HAVE TRUST IN YOURSELF AND IN YOUR PREPARATION. This doesn't mean you have always prepared all the topics completely and have an overconfident attitude. Instead, you are well aware of what all you have prepared and what not and need to own that truth. Enjoy the test when the time comes. Breathe and take it slow , keep your mind focused in the present! THE MOST IMP THING: PLEASE PREPARE APTITUDE (Quants,LR,everything) properly from Indiabix. I fumbled a lot in aptitude tests till I was confident and became good.

2. Technical Interview 1[ 27 students appeared for this round ]

A total of 27 students (across all 3 roles) got selected for the interviews. 8 additional candidates were on the waitlist but they didn't get a chance for an interview at the end. For the SE role, 18 appeared for interviews. The interview process was conducted online on Webex. The interview started with a warm greeting followed by my introduction. After that he told me to walk through and explain my Major project(which was the highlight). I explained what it is, what problem we are solving (the need) and the main features of the project. Further, he asked me to explain the tech stack used which led to a detailed conversation about how the architecture of the project was, about the database used, about Next.js . He basically was testing the low-level implementation details and whether I have actually worked on the project. He also asked about any conflict which might have occurred while working on the group project. I was prepared for such questions. After that he asked me to explain what OOP is. I explained about how some languages are functional programming languages and others object oriented languages.gave an example - python being more on the functional side(i was wrong) and explained it further how python supports both upon intervention. Then he asked to explain encapsulation , Inheritance, polymorphism. Always remember to give examples! To end off , he asked me a very common puzzle. I was very aware of such common puzzles but I had never read the solutions :( Though I very well knew they were interested in the approach. So I was able to smartly handle this and come up with a solution. Then he gave a last minute effort to optimize it and was able to do so. Lastly, I asked him one question regarding the technologies used at Blackrock. Before leaving, he himself said that the HR will inform me about the next round shortly!

3. Technical Interview 2[ 16 students appeared for this round ]

The 2nd tech interview was a techno-HR for some of my friends. For me, it was completely a tech round. This round started with greetings and a short conversation on how was my experience of the 1st round to which I told him honestly how I tackled the last puzzle in the previous round. Then he asked me to explain one of my favourite projects. I explained my major project. Then I was asked about my contribution ;I spoke about the features I worked on. Then he asked me to explain the kanban board functionality which I built, supabase db used. Further he asked me to explain what is authentication and authorization which led to a to and fro conversation on how exactly it works behind the scenes. He was not interested in the token generation-cookies and session storage part but on whether the database is queried on each auth request and similarly for authorization. Further I was asked about enum in Java. I explained that it is a special class in java , where it is used (Gave an example of how I defined roles using an Enum in db schema. It is good if you bring up a concept which you have used in your project). Then as I spoke about

RBAC in my project he asked me to open notepad and design the Roles table and how authorization will take place. For this I designed 2 more tables to explain him properly about the end-to-end flow. Remember to be confident in what you explain and always keep talking! He then posed an open ended question: If you have data which is coming from multiple sources, what rules will you define to normalize/preprocess it and store correct data? I started with the use of python for data preprocessing and the different techniques used as I got a sense that he was not expecting 1NF,2NF,3NF. Then he clarified that I just need to give a rule to be imposed(low-level). For which I answered :A very general and straightforward rule would be to check matching data for each attribute. If it matches, there is high probability that the data is correct. Further for unmatched fields, I will check existing database and look for a match. I honestly did not know what he was expecting, but he was satisfied with my answer. The last part of interview was: A binary tree implementation and function to search for a value in tree. He told me to open notepad and code. It is a good practice to talk about each and every line of code on what you are doing. Further he gave 2 followups- finding the no. of occurrences of that element and the deepest level of that element. He wanted me to implement all 3 in the same function .I tried but afterwards, I used global variables and stored the value for each and explained. He told me it can be done without this but what I did was correct. At the end I asked for a feedback (he said good things!) ; asked him about some interesting project which he has worked on and a pleasant 2 min conversation went on.

4. HR Round(Prank round) [13 students]

We were told due to some unfortunate reasons, Blackrock is terminating the process but TPO is requesting them. 10 students were called the next day for an HR round. This was just a small unofficial 1 on 1 conversation with Sikka Sir after which the results were announced by Sir himself in the conference room along with some words of inspiration. He announced that 10 students were selected and 3 were on waitlist. (7 SE, 2 Aladdin data, 1 GM)

10 students were offered the job and I was one of them!

journey.prep:
1) It's never too late to start, but the moment you do, ensure you give your 100%.

2) Never compare yourself to others. Always remember, if someone is good at a particular thing, you'll be good at another.

3) Have your fundamentals and basics cleared and spend as much as time you can on improving those skills

4) DSA is a mandatory thing to learn, without saying.

5) You won't be able to survive just on your tech skills; you need your communication skills so you can portray yourself effectively.

6) Learn development properly, no need to gpt hamesha. There were instances where few of my friends were asked to write a part of their code that they implemented in their projects

7) In an interview, always be true to yourself. Don't fake anything you don't know. Know your resume in and out.

8) Companies prefer candidates who have interned before because it tends to give you an idea of how exactly you'll work in a larger organisation.

9) Trust the process. There will be times when you will be upset , you will self-doubt your skills, knowledge, and everything you've learned. During this time, stay motivated, have good friends around you, and talk to your family. No need to worry about things that haven't happened.

10) During your interviews, be confident in your answers. Your interviewer will try to trick you.

11) Overall you need to be good in Oops , DBMS , SQL , OS, CN and all those concepts and techstack you have mentioned in your resume. System Designing is a hot topic.

12) Don't neglect the Aptitude section. IndiaBIX is a good platform where you can practice it. Also, refer to GeeksforGeeks for puzzles; they might get asked sometimes.

13) Placement kaafi lamba process hai, and you will realise you are in a good college. Companies aayengi, guys, so eventually you will get placed.

Study material I referred to during my prep:

1) System Design : If you have good amount of time to study system design in depth

2) System Design : If you are short on time

3) DSA Striver's Sheet

4) One of the finest DSA based yt channels for concept clarity

5) CP Sheet by TLE Eliminators

6) Oops in CPP

7) Oops in Java

8) DBMS : Codehelp - Lecture Notes + Slides

9) Google Drive for necessary pdfs

10) Practise SQL questions

11) CPP secret

12) GFG and InterviewBits are the best platforms for referring any interview based questions on any topic and do give it a glance before you go for your interviews

You are your own warrior, and you are here to claim that one seat in your dream company.
